P01FA.en: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P01FA.desc: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FA is the general electrical fault that the module does not classify as low or high. Without a plausible actual pressure, boost control usually limits boost.

causes_en: Sensor drifting or stuck
Leaking charge air hose or blocked pressure port
Contact resistance at the connector
Fault in other model inputs (MAF, MAP)
P01FB.en: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Range/Performance
P01FB.desc: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FB is the plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit. After a long stop all pressures should equal barometric pressure; while running the value is compared with a pressure modelled from airflow, speed and throttle – GM flags its boost sensor at deviations of roughly 25–30 kPa.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted
Sensor faulty internally
P01FC.en: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low

For comparison, GM sets its boost sensor low code below 14.4 % of 5 V, Ford below 0.19 V for 5 s.

P01FE.en: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor B Intermittent/Erratic

causes_en: One sensor drifting
Leak or hose damage between the measuring points or on one bank

Uneven turbo output (twin-turbo, wastegate or vanes on one side)
P01FF.en: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
P01FF.desc: Turbocharger outlet pressure sensor B is a second pressure sensor at a compressor outlet – for example one per turbo on twin-turbo engines or a second measuring point; sensor A has the codes P00F8–P00FC. It is a separate family from the boost pressure sensor: GM and Ford report the pressure ahead of the throttle under the boost sensor codes P0236–P0238. No manufacturer using the sensor B codes was found; FCA documents sensor A and a second outlet sensor. P01FF compares sensors A and B: with the engine off both should read barometric pressure, and in comparable operation they must agree within a tolerance. If they disagree without either being electrically faulty, this code sets; which one is wrong is found by comparing with barometric and manifold pressure. On twin-turbo engines a genuinely weaker turbo on one bank can also cause it.

causes_en: Shared injector supply open (fuse, relay, harness connector)
Separate injector power stage or its wiring faulty (diesel)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
Ground fault of the module or power stage
P0200.desc: P0200 is the injector circuit fault without a cylinder assignment. The large US manufacturers do not use it – GM and Ford report injector faults per cylinder (P0201 ff) or as faults of the shared injector supply (P062D/P062E, P2146 ff). Saab documents it on the 3.0 V6 diesel of the 9-5, whose injectors are driven by a separate power stage behind the glovebox: there P0200 means an electrical fault in that power stage or its wiring, and the engine is shut down. Generally the cause lies in something all injectors share – supply, fuse, relay, ground or driver stage – so several cylinders are affected at once. CARB does not require separate codes for each kind of circuit fault.

causes_en: Connector at the cylinder 1 injector loose, corroded or with a broken or pushed-back pin
Injector coil open
Wire between module and injector open or chafed (heat, rodents)
Injector supply missing (fuse, relay) – then usually several cylinders at once
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P0201.desc: P0201 reports an electrical fault, mainly an open circuit, in the injector circuit of cylinder 1. The engine module watches each injector output: GM flags an open circuit at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more – on direct injection and diesel engines in 10 of 20 or 5 of 10 samples and with the warning light in the first trip, on some port-injected engines only after two trips. Ford's port injection reads a fault bit from the driver chip that covers open, short to ground and short to voltage alike; Ford diesels report only the open circuit here and shorts as P0261/P0262. On direct injection the affected injector is switched off; the cylinder misfires.

causes_en: Injector of cylinder 1 faulty (coil, armature, wear, deposits)
Injector wiring or connector: contact resistance, corrosion, chafing
Engine software sets the code falsely (update available for some models)
Injector driver stage or boost voltage in the engine module
Wrong injector code, contaminated fuel or loose injector clamp
P020A.desc: P020A reports a fault in the injection timing of cylinder 1 on a diesel engine. Unlike P01CB/P01CC ('over retarded/advanced', the result of the injector learning routine in overrun), this code has no direction, and what it checks is up to the manufacturer. GM uses it as an electrical check on a four-cylinder diesel and on the 6.6 litre L5P Duramax V8: at every injection the engine module measures how long the injector current takes to reach its pull-in level of 13 A. If on the V8 that time is outside 60–150 µs in 10 of 20 samples, the code sets and the warning light comes on in the first trip. FCA lists it for the 3.0 litre EcoDiesel V6 together with the learning codes: check injector coding, charge air leaks and the injector clamp, reset the zero fuel calibration and repeat the learning drive; if the code returns, the injector is replaced.

GM uses it as an electrical check on the 6.6 litre L5P Duramax V8: at every injection the engine module measures how long the injector current takes to reach its pull-in level of 13 A. If on the V8 that time is outside 60–150 µs in 10 of 20 samples, the code sets and the warning light comes on in the first trip. FCA lists it for the 3.0 litre EcoDiesel V6 together with the learning codes: check injector coding, charge air leaks and the injector clamp, reset the zero fuel calibration and repeat the learning drive; if the code returns, the injector is replaced.

P0210.desc: P0210 reports an electrical fault, mainly an open circuit, in the injector circuit of cylinder 10. The engine module watches each injector output: GM flags an open circuit at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more – on direct injection and diesel engines in 10 of 20 or 5 of 10 samples and with the warning light in the first trip, on some port-injected engines only after two trips. Cylinder 10 exists only on ten-cylinder engines; documented is Ford's 6.8 litre V10, whose check covers P0201 to P0210 with the warning light.

P0213.desc: A cold start injector is an additional injector in the intake manifold that sprays extra fuel for a few seconds while a cold engine is cranked. In classic Bosch systems a thermo-time switch on the block powers it directly, without the engine module – such systems cannot set a code at all. A code is only possible where the engine module drives the valve and monitors its circuit, as CARB requires for output components. From the 1990s the main injectors took over cold-start enrichment, so the code only fits early OBD II engines. P0213 concerns cold start injector 1. No manufacturer using it was found in GM, Ford or Saab documents.

causes_en: Shutoff solenoid faulty (open coil, sticking plunger)
Relay or fuse in the supply circuit faulty
Broken wire, corrosion or ground fault at the pump connector
Pump control module faulty
Engine module driver faulty
P0215.desc: The engine shutoff solenoid is the electric stop valve on older diesel injection pumps, mainly distributor pumps. It is energised with the ignition on and lets fuel into the pump; with no current a spring closes it, the pump runs dry and the engine stops – also as a safety backup if the governor fails. P0215 reports a fault in this solenoid or its supply, typically a broken coil, a sticking plunger, a blown fuse or relay, or a wiring fault. The result is either an engine that will not start or dies, or one that keeps running after switch-off. Newer diesels stop through the injectors or a fuel shutoff valve with its own codes P0005–P0007. No manufacturer document describing P0215 was found; the description rests on CARB's requirements for output components and a Bosch patent on the valve.

causes_en: Injector harness or connector (broken pin) – common rail
Engine module or injector power stage faulty internally
Distributor pump electronics or timing advance faulty

P0216.desc: P0216 is a diesel code for the control of injection timing. On 1990s distributor pumps with an electronic timing advance it meant that actual injection timing missed its target; today manufacturers use it for the electronic injector control, with different meanings. GM's Duramax diesels compare, inside the engine module, the summed injection pulse widths from the hardware driver with those calculated by the software; a mismatch in 30 of 124 or 60 consecutive checks sets the code with the warning light in the first trip. On GM's 3.0 litre LM2 it appeared together with P0202 from a broken pin in the injector 2 connector. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel uses it for a fault in the separate injector power stage. The result can be loss of power, rough running, smoke and limp mode.

causes_en: Low coolant (leak, head gasket)
Thermostat stuck closed
Radiator fan, fan clutch or water pump faulty, radiator clogged
Coolant temperature sensor or harness faulty (false reading)

P0217.desc: P0217 is a condition code: the engine module reports that coolant temperature has passed a protection threshold. The limit and the reaction depend on the manufacturer – Saab's 2.2 diesel sets it at 120 °C for over 10 s, limits fuel quantity and suspends EGR and boost diagnostics until the temperature drops; heavy-duty diesels cut power sharply and may shut down; Ford petrol engines use their own code P1299 and cut fuel to individual cylinders. Whether the warning light comes on varies, because CARB exempts overheat protection that only engages once the gauge reads red. Usual causes are low coolant, a thermostat stuck closed, a failed fan or water pump – but Ford traced some cases to a faulty coolant sensor or harness.

causes_en: High load (towing, hills, sustained full throttle, stop-and-go in heat)
Transmission fluid low or aged
Fluid cooler, thermostat or lines clogged, weak cooling system

Temperature sensor or wiring reading wrongly
P0218.en: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Over Temperature Condition
P0218.desc: P0218 is a condition code: the transmission or engine module reports that transmission fluid temperature sensor A reads above an overheat limit. Saab's Aisin automatic sets it above 170 °C for more than 10 s, or above 140 °C for two minutes at high speed, shows a 'transmission overheating' warning and shifts less smoothly; afterwards a fluid change is advised because the additives are spent. Ford uses its own code on diesels and lists P0218 without the warning light on other models. Reactions include earlier torque converter lock-up, a modified shift pattern and sometimes reduced power. Causes are real overheating – towing, hills, low or old fluid, a clogged cooler – or a sensor reading wrongly.

causes_en: Downshift at too high a road speed (manual gearbox)
Descending in too low a gear
Fault in the speed signal (crankshaft sensor, wiring)
Diesel runaway (oil drawn into the intake) or sticking injection
P0219.desc: P0219 is a condition code: engine speed has exceeded the overspeed limit even though the rev limiter already cuts fuel – so the engine was driven from outside, usually by downshifting at too high a road speed or descending in too low a gear, or the speed signal was wrong. Limits: Ford 6.7 litre diesel above 4,200 rpm, 3.0 litre above 4,800 rpm, after 0.1 s; GM/Saab 2.8 V6 petrol with manual gearbox above 7,000 rpm for 1 s; Saab 2.2 diesel above 6,200 rpm, although fuel is cut from 5,000 rpm. Many manufacturers store it without the warning light. Saab advises: together with a camshaft sensor code it was real overspeed, alone check the speed signal; after real overspeed inspect the engine for valve train damage.

causes_en: Throttle body or sensor B faulty (worn track)
Wiring or connector at the throttle body (corrosion, break)
5 V reference disturbed (short in another sensor on the same reference)
Engine module input or monitoring processor faulty
P0220.desc: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0220 is the general circuit fault of sensor B without telling low from high. GM uses it in a special sense on 2015–2016 V8 engines: the signal lies outside 0.25–4.59 V only in the monitoring processor while the main processor sees it as valid; this sets immediately with the warning light. Newer GM and Ford engines report sensor B faults as P0222/P0223. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

causes_en: Worn track of sensor B (signal jumps)
Contact resistance at connector or wiring
Throttle dirty or sticking
Mass airflow sensor fault or false air
P0221.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
P0221.desc: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0221 is the plausibility fault: the signal of sensor B is electrically valid but does not match sensor A or the throttle position expected from airflow. Bosch ME9 engines (Saab) set it at a deviation of more than 9 %, older Ford systems at more than 7 degrees between the sensors without the warning light; many newer engines report this only as P2135. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

causes_en: Signal or 5 V wire open or shorted to ground
Throttle body or sensor B faulty internally

P0222.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
P0222.desc: With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0222 means the signal of sensor B is below its lower limit – GM about 0.25 V, Ford below 0.25 V – typically a short to ground, an open signal wire or a missing 5 V reference. Both detect it within about a second and switch the warning light on in the first trip. If the shared reference fails, several sensors report low at once. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

P0223.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High

Both detect it within about a second and switch the warning light on in the first trip. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control.

P0224.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent

GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0224 reports brief dropouts or jumps of sensor B that do not last long enough for the steady fault codes. No manufacturer using exactly this code was found: GM counts intermittent faults within P0222/P0223, and Ford's digital sensors report intermittent faults as P0124 for sensor A and P0229 for sensor C – after more than 0.4 s, while a steady fault needs over 4 s. Depending on frequency the result is jerking or brief limp mode.

P0225.desc: Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position sensor whose role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors; with other makes it can be a further pedal or throttle channel. P0225 is the general circuit fault of sensor C without telling low from high (those are P0227/P0228). Ford sets it when the digital sensor of the second throttle body has been faulty for more than 4 s and switches on the warning light and the powertrain fault lamp; communication faults of the sensor line have their own codes. The result is reduced power.

P022A.en: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit/Open
P022A.desc: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P022A is the general circuit fault of the actuator drive, mainly an open circuit: the driver sees no current or an output voltage outside its window. The module then switches bypass control off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

P0230.desc: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0230 concerns the primary side. GM's output driver compares the commanded with the actual state of the relay control circuit and sets the code at 8 of 10 mismatches, after two trips; Ford checks for open or short circuits for 2–5 s. With a failed relay control the pump stays off and the engine will not start or dies; a short to voltage keeps the pump running and drains the battery. On Ford systems with a pump control module the code means its power relay circuit; on the Subaru-based Saab 9-2X it is the pump module's collective fault report.

causes_en: Power wire from relay or module to pump shorted to ground (chafing at tank or underbody)
Relay contact not closing, fuse or battery feed to the relay missing
Pump motor jammed or shorted (high current)
Connector at the tank flange corroded or burnt
Pump control module faulty
P0231.desc: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0231 means the secondary side reads low, and the meaning differs by system. Ford's relay systems read the voltage in the pump power circuit through a monitor wire: if it is missing with the pump commanded on – relay contact not closing, fuse missing, wire open or shorted to ground – the code sets after 2–5 s. GM pumps with their own power module report a short to ground as overcurrent at 18 A or more, setting the warning light in the first trip and switching the output off. The pump gets no voltage, so the engine will not start or stalls.

causes_en: Relay contact welded or sticking
Pump power wire shorted to another supply
Pump control module output stage shorted
Moisture or corrosion in the connector causing leakage current
P0232.desc: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0232 means there is voltage in the pump power circuit although the pump should be off – a welded relay contact or a power wire shorted to another supply. GM pump modules check this after switch-off or in the off phase of the PWM cycle; above about 4 V the code sets once per trip, with the warning light after two trips. Ford's relay systems see it through the pump monitor wire. Driving is usually unaffected, but the pump may keep running with the ignition off and drain the battery – and an emergency shutdown would not work.

causes_en: Loose contact at pump connector, tank flange or relay socket
Relay contacts burnt (intermittently high resistance)
Harness chafing at underbody or tank with intermittent contact
Pump motor with commutator or brush dropouts
P0233.desc: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0233 reports brief, recurring dropouts in the pump power circuit that count neither as steadily low nor high. The secondary circuit is the power side of the same pump, not a second pump. No manufacturer using this code was found – GM counts intermittent faults within P0231/P0232/P023F, Ford's relay systems only use P0230–P0232; the description follows CARB's output monitoring requirement and Ford's description of the power circuit. Symptoms are occasional stumbling, stalling or starting problems.

causes_en: Wastegate stuck closed, actuator or linkage sticking, control hose off or blocked
Variable turbine vanes sooted or stuck closed (diesel)
Boost control valve or electric actuator faulty
Boost or manifold sensor reading too high (drift)
Software or calibration, tuning
P0234.desc: P0234 is a function code, not a sensor fault: the engine module compares target and actual boost, and actual boost stays above target although the control is already lowering it (wastegate opened, variable vanes opened). GM petrol engines set it at 20–35 kPa over target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels with variable vanes at 7–10 kPa, after two trips; Ford EcoBoost at about 28 kPa (4 psi) over 5 s while the wastegate is already commanded fully open. Ford diesels instead use P0234 for exhaust back pressure above 4.0–4.5 bar. The engine limits boost or enters limp mode. Typical causes are a wastegate stuck closed, sooted variable vanes or a faulty control valve; Audi traced cases on the Q7 TDI to cracked exhaust parts jamming the turbo vanes. Check the boost sensor against barometric pressure first.

causes_en: Connector at the boost sensor corroded or loose, broken wire
Boost sensor faulty, often oily from crankcase ventilation
Charge air leak or jammed turbo vanes causing an implausible value
5 V reference shorted by another sensor
P0235.desc: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0235 is the general fault of sensor A's circuit or signal, for modules that do not split low, high and range. GM, Ford and Saab do not use it; Audi documents it on the Q7 TDI together with over- and underboost, so there it also marks an implausible boost value, for example from a charge air leak or jammed turbo vanes. No manufacturer threshold for this code was found. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.

causes_en: Charge air leak (hose, clamp, cooler) between turbo and throttle
Boost sensor dirty, oily or drifting
Contact resistance in connector or harness
Manifold or barometric sensor faulty (correlation partner)
Ice or condensate in the charge air cooler in cold weather
P0236.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0236.desc: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0236 is the plausibility fault: the signal is electrically valid but wrong. After a stop of at least 10 s boost, manifold and barometric pressure must match (Ford within about 7–9 kPa); while running, GM compares the sensor with models from airflow, manifold pressure and throttle and flags deviations such as more than 30 kPa from manifold pressure – with the warning light in the first trip. A charge air leak often triggers it too, because the model comparison drifts apart. VW traced a Tiguan case to contact resistance in a harness connector. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.

With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0237 means the signal voltage is below its lower limit: GM below 14.4 % of 5 V (about 50 kPa) for roughly 4 s with the warning light in the first trip, Ford below 0.19 V for 5 s, Saab's V6 below 0.30 V for 1 s. Causes are a signal wire shorted to ground, an open 5 V reference or a failed sensor. Saab's 1.6 turbo only lights a service lamp for this code. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power.

P0238.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit High
P0238.desc: Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0238 means the signal voltage is above its upper limit: GM above 86 % of 5 V (about 372 kPa) for roughly 4 s with the warning light in the first trip, Ford above 4.88 V for 5 s, Saab's 1.6 turbo above 4.8 V. P0239.desc: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P0239 is the general circuit fault of sensor B, the counterpart of P0235, without telling low, high or range apart. As with sensor A, boost control would be switched off, with loss of power.

P023A.en: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P023A.desc: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023A means GM's driver diagnosis has found an open circuit (more than 200 kΩ between output and ground with the low-side driver off). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited.

P023D.en: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation
P023D.desc: P023D compares the manifold pressure sensor (after the throttle) with boost sensor A (before the throttle): with the engine stopped both must read the same ambient pressure. Saab's 2.8 V6 checks this once per trip with the ignition on before starting and sets the code at a difference of more than 12 kPa, with the warning light and limp mode limited to 170 Nm. The code does not say which sensor is wrong – barometric pressure as a third value decides. Electrical faults of either sensor (P0107/P0108, P0237/P0238) block the test and must be fixed first. GM and Ford run the same comparison but report it as P0236, P0106 or P2227.

P023E.desc: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found – GM, Ford and Saab, even on two-stage and twin-turbo engines, use a single boost sensor; the description follows CARB and the documented sensor A codes. P023F.desc: The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P023F means the power circuit to the pump is open. GM pumps with their own power module, whose speed is controlled by rail pressure, measure the pump current: if it stays below 1 A (older modules 0.5 A) although the pump is commanded, the code sets with the warning light in the first trip, and fuel pressure diagnostics are suspended. The cause lies in the wire from module to pump or its return, the pump connector or the pump motor itself. The pump stops, so the engine will not start or dies – there is no limp mode.

P0243.desc: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0243 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. GM uses it for an open circuit: with the driver off, more than 200 kΩ between output and ground in 10 of 20 samples sets it with the warning light in the first trip (older modules: two trips). Ford uses P0243 on its electric wastegates as the collective code for open and short circuits (0.4 s), together with P2ABD for driver overcurrent or overheating. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.

Wastegate flap coked or sticking

P0244.desc: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0244 means the actuator does not respond as commanded although its circuit is electrically sound, and manufacturers implement it differently. Subaru engines (Saab 9-2X) set it when manifold pressure exceeds an altitude-dependent limit – about 220 kPa absolute at sea level – for over 2 s, with the warning light at once. Stellantis documented it with a wastegate rod that had come off for want of a retaining clip. Older GM modules (Saab LDK, LLU) however use P0244 for an open solenoid circuit; newer GM and Ford systems do not use it and monitor function under P0234/P0299 or P25B3/P25B4.

causes_en: Control wire to the wastegate valve chafed through to ground

P0245.desc: The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0245 means the control circuit of actuator A reads low – typically the ground-switched control wire shorted to ground, so the valve would be permanently energised. GM checks with the driver off for less than 0.5 Ω to ground, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip; Ford's driver chip reports it after 2–5 s, and on pneumatic wastegates Ford also includes the open circuit here. A shorted supply shared with the bypass valve can set it together with P0033/P0034. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.

P0246 means the control circuit of actuator A reads high – the control wire is shorted to voltage, so the driver cannot switch the valve to ground. GM checks with the driver on for less than 0.5 Ω to battery voltage, 10 of 20 samples, warning light in the first trip; Ford's driver chip reports it after 2–5 s, and Ford's functional check of the wastegate control pressure (P1015/P1016) only runs when P0245/P0246 are clear. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost.

P024A.en: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Range/Performance
P024A.desc: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024A is the functional fault: the bypass does not follow its command, judged from the position sensor or from the expected temperature effect – Bosch describes comparing the cooler's efficiency with the valve closed and open, using modelled air temperature before and measured temperature after the cooler. FCA documents P024A, together with P026E, on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo and fixed it with an engine software update, so check the software level first.

causes_en: Flap seized or coked
Actuator faulty (gear, motor)
Vacuum supply missing (pneumatic type)
Position sensor reading constant
P024B.en: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Stuck
P024B.desc: The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024B means the bypass flap does not move at all despite being commanded – the position signal stands still or the air temperature shows no reaction. Bosch's patent describes exactly the case of a valve stuck closed or a blocked bypass, which raises emissions during warm-up. Stuck open, the charge air gets hotter and power drops; stuck closed, warm-up takes longer. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve.

P0251.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0251.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve. Manufacturers use different codes for this part: Ford P0001–P0004, GM Duramax P0090–P0092. P0251 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel uses it for an open circuit of the pressure regulator on the high-pressure pump: if the control wire does not show the expected voltage with the driver off for more than 1 s, the code sets with the warning light at once. Depending on the system, rail pressure and power are then limited.

causes_en: Metering actuator with shorted turns, too low resistance (driver overheats)
Actuator mechanically sticking or dirty (fuel quality, wear debris)
Wiring with contact resistance
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P0252.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0252.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve. Manufacturers use different codes for this part: Ford P0001–P0004, GM Duramax P0090–P0092. P0252 is the range or performance fault of actuator A, and the meaning depends on the maker. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel sets it when the driver stage of the pump pressure regulator overheats – a sign of a shorted turn or excessive current – with the warning light at once; Ford checks the same under P0002 at a driver temperature above 170 °C. Generally the code can also mean the actuator does not achieve the expected effect.

causes_en: Control wire to the metering actuator chafed to ground
Connector or wire open (where makers include it under low)
Metering actuator faulty internally
Engine module faulty
P0253.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0253.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0253 means the actuator A circuit reads low. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel uses it for a control wire shorted to ground for more than 1 s, with the warning light at once. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel, whose pump has two metering valves, also includes an open circuit (over 2.1 s) and goes into limp mode: limited pedal response and injection quantity, rail pressure capped at 60 MPa, warning light if the fault recurs on the next trip. Ford's equivalent is P0003, GM's P0091.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to voltage
Metering valve with shorted turns (overcurrent)
Connector corrosion with leakage current
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P0254.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0254.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0254 means the actuator A circuit reads high or draws too much current – typically the control wire shorted to voltage. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel sets it after 1 s with the warning light at once. On Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel a short to voltage of more than 0.31 s stops the engine, because a permanently energised valve can no longer control quantity and pressure. Ford's equivalent P0004 sets above 3.7 A; GM uses P0092.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering actuator connector
Harness chafing intermittently (vibration)
Actuator coil with a temperature-dependent fault
Engine module
P0255.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0255.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0255 reports brief open or short circuits in the actuator A circuit that come and go – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. No manufacturer using it with exactly this meaning was found; a Ram 6.7 Cummins code list names it as a circuit performance fault instead. The description follows CARB's continuous circuit monitoring requirement and the documented A siblings.

causes_en: Metering valve B open
Connector or wire to valve B open
Engine module
P0256.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0256.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. Actuator B is a second metering actuator, for example on pumps with two metering valves such as on Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel. P0256 is its general circuit fault, the counterpart of P0251. No manufacturer using P0256 was found – Saab reports its two valves under other codes; the description follows CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and the A siblings.

causes_en: Rail pressure or metering target not reached (leak, relief valve open)
Poor low-pressure supply (filter, lift pump, air)
Metering actuator or pumping element worn
Software or diagnostic level
P0257.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0257.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0257 is the functional fault of actuator B: the metering does not achieve its target. It is documented on Mack and Volvo heavy-duty common-rail diesels of 2018–2020 together with rail pressure codes (P0087, P016F, P228F) and P2A17/P2A1F; the cause can lie outside the actuator, for example an electronic pressure relief valve stuck open, a leak or poor low-pressure supply, so those faults are fixed first. Engine power may be derated.

causes_en: Supply wire, fuse or relay of the metering valves open or shorted to ground
Connector at the pump corroded or loose
Metering valve shorted to ground internally
Engine module
P0258.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0258.desc: These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0258 means the actuator B circuit reads low. The only manufacturer found, Saab with its 3.0 V6 diesel of the early 2000s, uses it not for a second valve but for the shared supply of both metering valves: a short to ground or open for more than about 1 s triggers limp mode with limited pedal response and injection quantity, rail pressure capped at 60 MPa and idle raised to 1,000 rpm; the warning light comes on if it recurs on the next trip.

causes_en: Metering valve B shorted internally
Control wire to the valve shorted to voltage, chafing
Connector at the valve corroded or wet
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P0259.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0259.desc: Fuel metering actuator B is a second electrically controlled metering valve on a diesel injection pump; A has the codes P0251–P0255. P0259 means its circuit reads high or draws too much current – a short to voltage or a shorted turn. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel, whose pump has two metering valves, uses it for an internal short in one of the valves lasting over 2.1 s: limp mode with limited pedal response, injection quantity and rail pressure (60 MPa), and the warning light if it recurs on the next trip. GM and Ford use other codes for this part (P0090–P0092, P0001–P0004).

causes_en: Control line to the pump module open or shorted, often along the frame
Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame)
Pump control module faulty (input)
Module ground or supply poor
Engine module output faulty
P025A.en: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open
P025A.desc: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025A means the control line from the engine module to pump module A is open or faulty. On Ford systems the pump module itself detects the bad command signal and reports it on the monitor line (11–16 V, 2–5 s); Ford uses P025A for the shared line to modules A and B. GM's pump module compares the enable line with the request on the data bus and sets P025A after about 1 s, with the warning light in the first trip; on some Ford vehicles the code does not light it.

causes_en: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control line or connector distorting the duty cycle
Pump control module faulty
Interference or poor ground between engine module and pump module
Engine module software or output
P025B.en: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P025B.desc: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025B means pump module A receives a signal, but an invalid command – the duty cycle is outside the valid window or implausible. Ford's module signals this with a 20 % (±4 %) duty cycle on its monitor line; the check runs continuously at 11–16 V over 2–5 s. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the vehicle. Typical causes are contact resistance in the control line or connector that distorts the duty cycle, a poor ground or a faulty module.

causes_en: Control line chafed to ground at the frame
Water or corrosion at the pump module connector
Ground point loose or corroded
Pump control module faulty internally
Pump relay faulty (Ford 6.7)
P025C.en: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Low
P025C.desc: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025C means the control circuit to pump module A reads low, typically a short to ground. On Ford's 3.0 diesel the pump module detects it; on the 6.7 it means a short on the low side of the pump relay – both within 0.5 s. FCA documents it with the warning light on and sometimes a start followed by stalling, often together with P01C6 and P016F; the checks cover the pump module connector, the low-pressure sensor and a ground point for water, corrosion and pushed-back pins.

causes_en: Control line shorted to battery voltage or another wire
Moisture in the connector (leakage to voltage)
Pump control module faulty
Relay stuck or faulty (Ford 6.7)
P025D.en: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit High
P025D.desc: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025D means the control circuit to pump module A reads high, typically a short to voltage. On Ford's 3.0 diesel the pump module detects it; on the 6.7 it means a short to voltage on the low side of the pump relay – both continuously monitored and set within 0.5 s. Depending on the design the pump then runs all the time or not at all.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector
Wire or 5 V reference breaking from vibration or heat
Sensor faulty internally (erratic signal)
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor
P025E.desc: Boost sensor A measures the pressure between charge air cooler and throttle (Ford TIP, GM TIAP). P025E counts brief excursions outside its valid voltage range that are each too short for the low or high code P0237/P0238 – Ford's limits are below 0.19 V and above 4.88 V. Ford counts these events continuously and sets P025E after 10 in one drive cycle. Boost control then runs on a substitute value or is switched off, leaving only base boost. Typical causes are a loose or corroded connector or a wire breaking under vibration and heat.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Wire breaking from vibration or heat
Sensor B faulty
P025F.desc: Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on twin-turbo engines or a second stage. P025F counts brief excursions of its signal outside the valid range that are too short for the low or high code – the counterpart of P025E, which Ford sets after 10 such events in one drive cycle. No manufacturer using sensor B codes was found; the description follows CARB's input monitoring requirement and Ford's sensor A check.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering valve B connector
Broken or chafed wire in the harness to the pump (vibration, heat)
Metering valve B with internal dropouts
Unstable supply or ground
P0260.en: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
P0260.desc: P0260 reports brief dropouts or jumps in the circuit of fuel metering actuator B on a diesel injection pump that do not last long enough for the low or high code (P0258/P0259) – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. No manufacturer using P0260 was found; the description follows CARB's continuous circuit monitoring requirement and Saab's diagnosis of the same two-valve pump, which recommends a wiggle test with the valves activated.

causes_en: Control wire of the cylinder 1 injector chafed to ground in the harness
Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground
Injector shorted to its housing internally
Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too)
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P0261.desc: P0261 means the control wire of the cylinder 1 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground. Ford's 6.7 diesel has its driver chip report the short within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead.

causes_en: Control wire of the cylinder 1 injector touching battery voltage or another supply wire
Injector coil shorted internally (too low resistance, overcurrent)
Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P0262.desc: P0262 means the control wire of the cylinder 1 injector is shorted to voltage. GM detects this with the driver on: on direct injection by 25 A or more through the driver, on port injection and Duramax diesels by 0.5 Ω or less to the supply. On Ford's 6.7 diesel it means the injector's high side is shorted to its low side, reported within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead.

causes_en: Injector of cylinder 1 worn, coked or leaking
Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 1 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel
P0263.desc: P0263 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 1 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips. The code does not say whether there is too much or too little fuel – the correction value for cylinder 1 shows the direction: strongly negative means a leaking injector, strongly positive a weak injector or low compression. VW and Ram traced some cases to over-sensitive software, so check for updates before replacing injectors.

Injector shorted to its housing internally

causes_en: Charge air cooler clogged on the outside (insects, leaves, dirt) or fins damaged
Coolant-cooled cooler: pump faulty, air in the low-temperature circuit, low coolant
Charge air or ambient temperature sensor inaccurate
Charge air cooler bypass stuck open
Software or calibration
P026A.en: Charge Air Cooler Efficiency Below Threshold
P026A.desc: P026A means the charge air cooler is not cooling enough. The module compares the temperature drop across the cooler with the maximum possible (inlet minus ambient) or with a model: GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel sets it below 25 % efficiency, later GM diesels below 50 %, both after two trips; Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels when the measured temperature is 18–35 °C (3.0: 35–65 °C) off the model over about 10 s. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo petrol with a coolant-cooled charge air cooler sets it in the first trip when manifold air exceeds 110 °C or boost has been limited for a long time. Hot intake air costs power and raises NOx and soot.

causes_en: Engine module software (false setting)
Injectors coked or worn (changed start of injection)
Rail pressure or fuel supply problems (pump, filter, fuel quality)
Crankshaft or camshaft signal inaccurate
P026B.desc: P026B is the engine-wide injection timing monitor: CARB requires diesels from 2010 to detect injection that is too early or too late overall, or a timing control at its limit. Unlike P020A ff (per cylinder) it concerns the engine as a whole. It is documented on the Ram 6.7 Cummins, together with the per-cylinder timing and balance codes; FCA describes it as set falsely by software and fixes it with an engine module update, without publishing thresholds. GM and Ford handle timing with per-cylinder codes instead (P01CB ff, P2B11 ff).

causes_en: Injectors coked or clogged (too little flow)
Airflow or boost measurement wrong, NOx sensor lambda inaccurate
Weak low- or high-pressure supply (filter, pump, rail pressure)
Fuel quality or contamination
Software
P026C.en: Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
P026C.desc: From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets. P026C means the engine gets less fuel than commanded. GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel checks it at idle with the vehicle stationary and the engine warm, setting it at a correction of −20 to −35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s; later GM diesels use the learned correction value (10 of 20 samples); both need two trips. FCA lists it with an injector cleaning procedure for deposits. Ford diesels do not use it. Typical causes are coked injectors, wrong airflow or lambda measurement and weak fuel supply.

causes_en: Injector dripping or worn, or wrong injector type fitted
EGR valve not closing or EGR differential pressure sensor wrong
Boost sensor or turbo vanes faulty, intake leak
NOx or oxygen sensor reading wrong
Software
P026D.en: Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected
P026D.desc: From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets. P026D means the engine gets more fuel than commanded. GM's LML diesel sets it at idle at a correction of +16 to +35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s, two trips. Volvo trucks detect it as too little oxygen at the NOx sensors for the fuel flow and point to boost sensor, EGR valve and sensor, wrong injectors, turbo vanes and intake leaks. On GM's 2.8 litre diesel vans of 2020–2022 it could also be a software anomaly without driving problems. Symptoms are black smoke and more frequent filter regeneration.

causes_en: Air in the low-temperature circuit or low coolant (pump runs dry)
Pump faulty internally (bearing, impeller, electronics)
Software or calibration
Weak supply or ground, corroded connector
P026E.en: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Performance
P026E.desc: Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit with an electric pump. P026E means that pump is electrically sound but does not deliver as commanded – judged from feedback by the pump electronics or from the missing temperature drop. FCA documents it on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo, together with P024A, and fixed it with a software update; thresholds are not published. Air in the circuit or low coolant lets the pump run dry; hot charge air then costs power.

causes_en: Thermostat stuck open or opening too early
Thermostat stuck closed or opening too late
Map-controlled thermostat: heating element or control faulty
Coolant temperature sensor inaccurate
Low coolant or air in the system
P026F.desc: P026F is a general functional code for the coolant thermostat. CARB requires that the coolant reaches the temperature needed for other diagnostics in the approved time and comes within 11 °C of the thermostat's regulating temperature; from model years 2019–2021 petrol engines must also detect it dropping back below that temperature, and electric pumps or valves controlling coolant flow are monitored like a thermostat. The module follows coolant temperature against a heat model. No manufacturer using P026F was found – GM and Ford report thermostat faults as P0128, P01F0 or P2181 – so the description rests on CARB and the thermostat's function.

P027A.en: Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit/Open
P027A.desc: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. Module B is a second pump module, for example on dual-tank commercial vehicles. P027A is the counterpart of P025A: the control line from the engine module to pump module B is open or faulty. No manufacturer using P027A was found – Ford reports line faults of both modules together under P025A, GM only uses P025A; the description follows CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and Ford's module B check. If the second tank's pump gets no valid command, fuel may run short when running from that tank.

causes_en: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control or monitor line to module B

P027B.en: Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P027B.desc: On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. Module B is a second pump module, for example on dual-tank commercial vehicles. P027B means pump module B receives an invalid command or its feedback does not match. Ford's module signals this with a 20 % (±4 %) duty cycle on its monitor line, checked continuously at 11–16 V over 2–5 s; on Ford commercial vehicles the module B monitor line runs via the smart relay module and CAN to the engine module. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the vehicle.

P027E.en: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
P027E.desc: P027E is the cold-start counterpart of P026C: during cold start the engine gets less fuel than commanded, for example because a catalyst-heating injection does not arrive. The check probably works as in warm running, from airflow and lambda against the commanded quantity. The code covers only phases with the cold-start emission strategy active (extra injections to heat the catalyst, raised idle): CARB requires faults of elements also monitored elsewhere to be reported separately during the cold-start strategy. No manufacturer using this code was found; the description follows CARB and the warm-running counterpart.

causes_en: Wire or connector to the fan open or corroded
Fan relay or fan control module faulty
Fan motor open internally
Fuse blown
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P028A.en: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit/Open
P028A.desc: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler; a Deere patent describes such a fan that the module switches and reverses to blow out dirt. P028A means the fan's control circuit is open or has a general fault, detected by the driver stage. Without the fan the charge air is cooled less at low speed or in heat, which can lead to P026A and boost limitation. No manufacturer document using P028A was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement.

causes_en: Fan motor seized or worn
Fan blocked (debris, dirt, ice)
Fan relay or fan control module without output
Fan fuse or supply
P028B.en: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Performance/Stuck Off
P028B.desc: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028B means the module commands the fan on but sees no effect – no speed or current feedback from a fan control module, or the charge air does not cool – although the circuit is electrically sound (circuit faults are P028A, P028D and P028E). The charge air then gets hotter, which can limit boost and power. No manufacturer document using this code was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement.

causes_en: Relay contact welded
Driver stage or fan control module shorted
Control wire shorted (to ground on low-side, to voltage on high-side control)
P028C.en: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Stuck On
P028C.desc: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028C means the fan runs although the module has switched it off – speed or current feedback, or the voltage at the output, does not match the off command. Typical causes are a welded relay contact or a shorted driver stage. The fan runs continuously and can drain the battery; the charge air tends to be too cold, which favours condensate. No manufacturer document using this code was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground (chafing)

P028D means the fan's control circuit reads low – typically the control wire shorted to ground, detected by the driver stage. Depending on whether the module switches the low or the high side, the fan then runs permanently or not at all. P028F.en: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit Driver Performance
P028F.desc: Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028F concerns the driver stage that switches the fan: it reports an internal fault such as overcurrent or overheating, or its diagnosis does not match the command. A shorted fan motor or wiring can overload the driver; otherwise the driver in the engine or fan module is faulty. Cylinder 12 exists only on twelve-cylinder engines; no manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford documents stop at cylinder 8 – so the description follows CARB and the codes for cylinders 1–8.

causes_en: Control wire of the cylinder 12 injector touching battery voltage or another supply wire
Injector coil shorted internally (too low resistance, overcurrent)
Short between supply and control wire in harness or connector
Driver stage in the engine module faulty
P0295.desc: P0295 means the control wire of the cylinder 12 injector is shorted to voltage. GM detects this with the driver on: on direct injection by 25 A or more through the driver, on port injection and Duramax diesels by 0.5 Ω or less to the supply. On Ford's 6.7 diesel it means the injector's high side is shorted to its low side, reported within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead. Cylinder 12 exists only on twelve-cylinder engines; no manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford documents stop at cylinder 8 – so the description follows CARB and the codes for cylinders 1–8.

causes_en: Injector of cylinder 12 worn, coked or leaking
Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive
Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement
Low compression on cylinder 12 (valve, rings, injector seal)
Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel
P0296.desc: P0296 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 12 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips. The code does not say whether there is too much or too little fuel – the correction value for cylinder 12 shows the direction: strongly negative means a leaking injector, strongly positive a weak injector or low compression. Cylinder 12 only exists on diesels with twelve cylinders; GM and Ford documents stop at cylinder 8, so the description follows CARB and the siblings.

causes_en: Limiter speed genuinely exceeded (downhill, trailer)
Wrong tyre size or axle ratio programmed, larger wheels fitted
Wheelspin on the driven axle
Speed signal disturbed (loose contact, interference, tone wheel)
P0297.desc: P0297 is a condition code: the engine module detects that road speed – from the vehicle speed sensor or wheel and output shaft speed – exceeded the calibrated maximum. Electronic speed limiters cut fuel or throttle at that limit, and the event is stored. Ford uses the code on its petrol trucks and stores it without the warning light; no manufacturer publishes a threshold. Common triggers are descending with a trailer beyond the limiter speed, wheelspin on the driven axle, a wrongly programmed tyre size or axle ratio, or spikes in the speed signal. Unlike P0219 it concerns road speed, not engine speed.

causes_en: High load in heat (trailer, mountain pass, stop-and-go)
Cooling or fan problem (clogged radiator, fan, thermostat, low coolant)
Oil cooler clogged or oil thermostat stuck
Oil temperature or level sensor reading too high
Low oil level or wrong oil
P0298.desc: P0298 is a protection code: engine oil temperature – from its own sensor, often combined with the oil level sensor, or modelled – has exceeded the protection limit. Saab's 3.0 diesel limits injection quantity when the oil stays at 135 °C or more for over 10 s, until it cools down; a heavy-duty bus engine warns in two stages and then derates. Ford stores the code without the warning light, in line with CARB's exemption for overheat protection. Usual causes are high load in heat, cooling problems, a clogged oil cooler or stuck oil thermostat, and occasionally a sensor reading too high.

causes_en: Leak in the charge air path (hose off or torn, cooler leaking, clamps)
Wastegate faulty (rod off, preload lost, vacuum or solenoid, diaphragm)
Turbo vanes sticking or turbo worn (diesel)
Bypass valve leaking (torn diaphragm) or its control
Ice in the charge air cooler, boost sensor or connector, or software
P0299.desc: P0299 means actual boost stays below target for a period although the control already demands more. Thresholds: GM petrol 30–55 kPa below target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels 10–50 kPa, two trips; Ford EcoBoost more than 4 psi (about 28 kPa) for 5 s with the wastegate already commanded fully closed; Ford diesels 30–40 kPa for 10–15 s, with a further underboost code P2263. Typical causes from manufacturer bulletins: a charge air leak, a wastegate that lost its preload or whose rod came off, a leaking bypass valve, sticking turbo vanes on diesels, and ice in the charge air cooler in winter. A faulty boost sensor can also fake underboost. Many engines then limit power.

P029A.en: Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
P029A.desc: These codes belong to an individual-cylinder fuel correction: a diesel's cylinder balance control measures each cylinder's crankshaft acceleration and adjusts its injection quantity; on petrol engines a cylinder-selective mixture control does the same. CARB requires the system to report when such a correction has used up its range or one cylinder causes an imbalance. P029A means the correction for cylinder 1 is at its upper limit: the module keeps giving this cylinder more fuel and still cannot even it out – a sign that the cylinder receives too little fuel or builds too little pressure. GM and Ford use other codes for this (P0263 ff, P219A ff); no manufacturer document describing this code with thresholds was found, so the description follows CARB and published patents.

P02CA.desc: Turbocharger B is a second, separately controlled turbo – on twin-turbo or two-stage systems, or one per bank. No manufacturer using the turbo B codes was found; twin-turbo engines such as GM's 3.0 V6 and Ford's 3.5 EcoBoost report boost faults under P0234/P0299 with a shared boost sensor, so the description follows CARB and the turbo A codes. P02CA means actual boost of turbo B stays above target although the control is already lowering it; for turbo A, GM petrol engines use 20–35 kPa, Ford EcoBoost more than 4 psi over 5 s. Boost is then limited.

P02CB.desc: Turbocharger B is a second, separately controlled turbo – on twin-turbo or two-stage systems, or one per bank. No manufacturer using the turbo B codes was found; twin-turbo engines such as GM's 3.0 V6 and Ford's 3.5 EcoBoost report boost faults under P0234/P0299 with a shared boost sensor, so the description follows CARB and the turbo A codes. Typical causes are a charge air leak on that side, a wastegate stuck open or a worn turbo. Power is then limited.

P02CC.en: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
P02CC.desc: The engine module learns a small-quantity correction for each injector: on overrun it gives one injector a tiny test injection (GM about 1.5 mm³), measures the resulting crankshaft acceleration and corrects the injector's activation time per rail pressure step. P02CC means the learned correction for cylinder 1 has reached its lower limit at at least one pressure step: the injector needs much less activation time than nominal – it delivers too much at small quantities or opens early. GM diesels set it at limits of roughly ±66–182 µs after two trips. It is documented on GM's 6.6 litre L5P and 2.8 litre diesels – on the 2.8 a worn drive belt caused it to return after injector replacement – and on Land Rover's 5.0 V8 petrol, where a software update is the first step. It differs from P01CC (over advanced), which some systems derive from the same learning.

P02E0.en: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
P02E0.desc: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02E0 means the motor circuit is open – cable, connector or motor winding. GM diesels detect more than 200 kΩ with the driver off, after about 1.5 s (6.6 litre LML: 7 s), two trips. On a fault the valve is switched off and the spring opens it: driving is usually little affected, but EGR control is restricted and filter regeneration may be blocked.

P02E1.en: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Performance
P02E1.desc: The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02E1 means the valve does not follow its target position – GM's diesels set it when target and actual position differ by more than 10 % for about 1.2 s with a steady target, after two trips. Usually soot from EGR and oil from crankcase ventilation make it stiff, or the gear or motor is worn. On a fault the valve is switched off and the spring opens it: driving is usually little affected, but EGR control is restricted and filter regeneration may be blocked.

P02E4.en: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Open

P02EC.en: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - High Air Flow Detected
P02EC.desc: Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels control the air mass through the EGR valve and the intake throttle. P02EC means the measured air mass stays above target with the control at its limit – too little EGR, or the throttle cannot restrict enough – for 10 s (6.7) or 5 s (3.0). Typical causes are a stuck-closed EGR valve or clogged EGR cooler, a throttle stuck open or a mass airflow sensor reading too high. NOx rises; driving is usually unaffected. Other manufacturers using this code were not found.

P02ED.en: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - Low Air Flow Detected

P02ED means the measured air mass stays below target with the control at its limit – too much EGR, a throttle stuck closed or a clogged intake – for 10 s (6.7) or 5 s (3.0). Typical causes are an EGR valve stuck open, a clogged air filter, a sooted throttle or a dirty mass airflow sensor. The engine lacks air: loss of power, smoke and high soot load. Other manufacturers using this code were not found.

causes_en: Injector electrically aged (piezo capacitance, coil resistance)

Injector mechanically sticking (valve lift)
Injector driver stage in the engine module
P02EE.desc: P02EE reports an electrically implausible response of the cylinder 1 injector – not an open or short circuit (those are P0201, P0261, P0262), but a current or voltage pattern outside the expected range. GM's 8-cylinder diesel checks the time the current takes to fall from hold to zero (outside 20–50 µs in 10 of 20 samples, two trips); GM's petrol direct injection evaluates the voltage feedback of the opening and closing; Ford's diesels flag the injector's voltage or charge regulator at its limit (90 s), Ford's petrol direct injection its controlled-valve-operation adaptation at its limit. The injector may be shut off, causing misfire.

P02FA.en: Diesel Intake Air Flow Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
P02FA.desc: The diesel intake throttle learns the position sensor values of its end stops, as a Toyota patent describes for the closed stop at engine stop. P02FA means a learned end-stop value is implausible. Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels check it once after each learning run and set the code when the learned minimum offset is outside ±10 (6.7) or ±6.7 (3.0) – Ford only evaluates the minimum stop. Typical causes are soot and oil deposits at the flap and stop, a worn or shifted sensor, mechanical damage or a replacement part that has not been learned. EGR control may be restricted.

P02FB.en: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit/Open
P02FB.desc: Cold start fuel injection is an extra injection system for cold starts – for example on flex-fuel engines running on high ethanol blends, where a Hyundai patent describes a small auxiliary tank, a cold-start injector and a heater. CARB lists such heated fuel preparation systems among the monitored output components. P02FB means the control circuit of the cold-start injection is open or has a general fault – a broken coil, a loose or corroded connector or a broken wire. The engine then starts poorly or not at all in the cold; once warm it runs normally. No manufacturer document using this code was found; unlike the older P0213/P0214, these codes separate the fault types.

causes_en: Time source in another module (instrument cluster, body module) gives an implausible time after a reset or voltage loss
Software level of engine, transmission or instrument cluster module
Battery discharged or disconnected, voltage dips
Instrument cluster or timer in the engine module faulty
Coolant temperature sensor distorting the cooling check
P02FF.desc: Many diagnostics need to know how long the engine – or, on hybrids, the whole propulsion system – has been off: thermostat and evaporative checks and the cold-start strategy, for which CARB requires at least 6 hours of standstill. A timer measures this time, and the engine module checks its plausibility, for example against coolant cooling – a GM patent describes such a check. P02FF means that timer is implausible. Mercedes documents it on M256, M260, M264 and M274 engines of around 2020: after an internal reset the instrument cluster clock ran wrong; the fix is a software update for engine, transmission and instrument cluster modules. Readiness of standstill-dependent monitors may stay incomplete.

causes_en: False air (vacuum leak, crankcase ventilation, intake gasket)

P0300.desc: The engine module detects misfire from crankshaft speed: a cylinder that does not fire gives no acceleration impulse. At a catalyst-damaging rate (CARB: at least 5 % per 200 revolutions) the warning light flashes; at an emissions-relevant rate (at least 1 % per 1,000 revolutions – GM about 2–5 %, Ford 0.9–1.5 %) it comes on after two trips. Ford and GM may shut off a misfiring cylinder's injector to protect the catalyst. P0300 sets when the misfire cannot be assigned to one cylinder: several cylinders each account for more than 10 %, the cylinder changes randomly, or – at Ford – the cylinder cannot be identified at high speed. It often appears together with cylinder codes. Causes are usually systemic: false air, worn plugs on several cylinders, fuel pressure or fuel quality, valve timing – and false detection from a damaged tone wheel, rough roads or vibration. Bulletins name coils, cracked plug insulators and wrong plug gaps.

causes_en: Control line or connector pin open (corrosion, pushed-back pin)

P030A.desc: Ignition A is one of the control signal lines from the engine module to an ignition module, ignition output stage or group of coils; which cylinders it serves is defined by the manufacturer, not by the code standard. The code concerns the logic-level control signal, not the coil's primary current (that has its own codes, P0351 ff and P2300 ff). P030A means the control line is open – the module sees a voltage with its driver off that indicates high resistance. No manufacturer using these codes was found; GM reports coil control faults as P0351 ff (open above 30 kΩ, first trip), so the description follows CARB and that analogy. The affected coils fire wrongly or not at all, causing misfire; many modules then shut off injection to those cylinders to protect the catalyst.
