causes_en: Deposits at the throttle or bypass channel, or gummed idle valve
Extra load: stiff accessory drive, gearbox or converter
Intake or exhaust restricted (air filter, catalyst)
Idle valve or throttle actuator faulty, wrong learned value
Mechanical engine damage (low compression)
P0506.en: Idle Control System RPM - Lower Than Expected
P0506.desc: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0506 means the idle speed of the warm engine at standstill stays too low despite fully used control. GM uses more than 91 rpm filtered for 10 s (MIL after two trips), Ford petrol −100 rpm plus a correction above 1 lb/min, Ford diesel −100 rpm for 5 s, Subaru −100 rpm with the correction at its limit for 10 s three times. Typical are deposits, extra load or a restricted intake or exhaust.

causes_en: False air (vacuum hose, intake gasket, brake booster)
Crankcase ventilation leaking or wrongly routed
Throttle not closing fully (deposits, ice, stop misadjusted)
Idle valve stuck open
Wrong throttle learned value after cleaning or replacement
P0507.en: Idle Control System RPM - Higher Than Expected
P0507.desc: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0507 means the idle speed stays above target although the control is at its minimum – air bypasses the control or the throttle does not close. GM uses more than 182 rpm filtered (MIL after two trips), Ford petrol +200 rpm, Ford diesel +160 rpm, Subaru +200 rpm for 10 s three times; on the Saab 9-4X three overspeed fuel cut-offs at standstill also set it. False air is the classic cause.

causes_en: Idle valve coil faulty
Control wire shorted to ground or open
Supply missing (main relay, fuse)
Connector contact at valve or module
Driver in the engine module
P0508.en: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
P0508.desc: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0508 is an electrical fault in the drive circuit of a separate idle valve. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) feeds the valve from the main relay and pulses it to ground; the module counts signal edges and sets P0508 at 8 or fewer in 64 ms instead of about 160 – the output hangs at one level – with the warning lamp at once and limp mode without idle control. Many makers, Ford among them, report all circuit faults under P0511 instead.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to positive
Idle valve with shorted turns
Connector corroded or wet, interference
Engine module faulty
P0509.en: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
P0509.desc: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0509 is the counterpart of P0508: the drive circuit of the idle valve is shorted to positive or shows implausibly many signal edges – Subaru sets it at 225 or more in 64 ms, with the warning lamp at once and limp mode without idle feedback. It only exists on engines with a separate idle valve.

causes_en: Throttle or idle valve dirty or coked, not enough air when cold
False air or vacuum leak
Fault in the throttle or idle valve circuit
Extra load at cold start (alternator, A/C), stiff engine
P050A.en: Cold Start Idle Control System Performance
P050A.desc: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults. Ford collects data during the first 15 s after a cold start (coolant and catalyst 20–100 °F) and judges after 300 s, once per trip. P050A checks whether the raised idle speed or air mass commanded at a cold start is actually reached: Ford sets it when the average deviation between target and actual speed exceeds 200 rpm, with the warning lamp. GM does not use P050A as its own monitor and reports cold-start system faults under its manufacturer code P1400.

causes_en: Engine module software or calibration
Idle control takes back the retard because speed would drop (false air, dirty throttle)
Knock control or knock sensor intervenes
Extra load or alternator at cold start
P050B.desc: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults. Ford collects data during the first 15 s after a cold start (coolant and catalyst 20–100 °F) and judges after 300 s, once per trip. P050B checks the ignition part of the strategy – the retard for catalyst heating; CARB allows checking only the commanded value. Ford sets it when desired and commanded cold-start timing differ by more than 10°, for example because knock, torque or idle control take back the retard. FCA fixed P050B on the 2.0-litre turbo Wrangler of 2018–19 with software. GM has no separate monitor.

causes_en: Coolant temperature sensor drifting, wrong characteristic
Contact resistance or corrosion at the coolant or intake air sensor connector
Intake air temperature sensor reading wrong
Auxiliary heater or block heater not recognised, very short stop
P050C.en: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance
P050C.desc: P050C is documented only on Bosch ME9 in the Saab 9-3 V6 2.8 turbo: a cold-start plausibility check of the coolant temperature sensor. After a long stop coolant and intake air must read about the same; the code sets if coolant is more than 10 °C below or 15 °C above intake air, once per trip with the warning lamp. A wrong coolant reading distorts cold-start enrichment and can run the fan on a cold engine. The common reading 'coolant warms up too slowly' does not fit – that is P0125/P0128. GM, Ford and FCA do not use P050C.

causes_en: Injector with poor spray pattern or deposits, or injector circuit fault
Spark plug or ignition coil weak
Engine module software or calibration
Poor fuel or low fuel pressure
P050D.desc: GM's direct-injection petrol engines (from about 2016) split the injection into two pulses and retard the ignition after a cold start to heat the catalyst. P050D counts engine cycles with incomplete combustion via the crankshaft misfire detection during this strategy; if the rate reaches the catalyst-damaging misfire threshold, the code sets – once per trip, while the strategy is active (under 45 s running, coolant up to 66 °C). Mostly MIL after two trips, some calibrations without MIL. Ford and FCA do not use P050D.

causes_en: Idle or air control does not reach the cold-start target (dirty throttle, false air)
Ignition not retarded enough (knock or torque intervention)
Engine module software
Air mass meter reading wrong
P050E.en: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low
P050E.desc: After a cold start the engine module raises idle speed and air mass and retards the ignition so that much heat goes into the exhaust and the catalyst lights off quickly. CARB requires this cold-start strategy to be monitored with its own codes, separate from ordinary idle and ignition faults. Ford collects data during the first 15 s after a cold start (coolant and catalyst 20–100 °F) and judges after 300 s, once per trip. P050E is the system check of the strategy: does enough heat reach the exhaust and catalyst? Ford uses no exhaust temperature sensor but a catalyst temperature model – actual against target – and sets the code when the temperature deficit divided by the target rise exceeds 0.4, with the warning lamp. FCA uses P050E on the 3.0-litre EcoDiesel (Ram 1500, Grand Cherokee 2014), where it concerns heating the oxidation catalyst, fixed by software. GM uses its manufacturer code P1400 instead.

causes_en: Leaking vacuum hose or check valve
Leaking diaphragm in the brake booster
Vacuum sensor or its seal faulty
Electric or mechanical vacuum pump weak (where fitted)
P050F.desc: GM (from about model year 2017/18) monitors the brake booster with a vacuum sensor: with the pedal at rest and high intake vacuum the booster must hold its vacuum; a loss over time is filtered as a drift ratio, and above a threshold P050F sets, MIL after two trips. It runs with the engine on, during start-stop auto-stops and after switch-off. Without enough brake vacuum the module must throttle, restart the engine from auto-stop or request a pump – which affects idle and start-stop – and brake assistance can drop. Ford and FCA do not use P050F.

causes_en: Idle switch or throttle sensor misadjusted
Switch contacts worn, dirty or corroded
Wire or connector open or shorted
Throttle not closing (deposits, sticking cable, stop misadjusted)
Value not relearned after replacement
P0510.desc: Older engines with a mechanical throttle have a separate idle contact on the throttle or the combined throttle position sensor (Bosch Motronic throttle switch, Nissan and Toyota sensors with idle switch). The module uses it to recognise idle – for idle control, fuel cut-off on overrun and idle ignition timing – and as a substitute if the position sensor fails. P0510 flags an implausible switch: closed with the throttle open, or open at idle. Manufacturer thresholds were not found in accessible documents; with electronic throttle the switch no longer exists.

causes_en: Idle valve faulty (coil open or shorted)
Wire open or shorted
Connector corroded, pins pushed back
Driver in the engine module
P0511.desc: CARB requires the idle speed control to be monitored: petrol engines must flag a fault if the target idle speed is not reached within +200/−100 rpm, diesels within ±30 %. Older engines use a separate idle air control valve that bypasses the closed throttle; with electronic throttle the throttle itself controls idle and no separate valve exists. P0511 is the general circuit fault of the idle valve – open, short to ground or to positive – without separating low and high, which CARB permits. Ford (up to about 2012, engines with an idle valve) has the output stage report it via a diagnostic status bit, continuously. Valve types are PWM solenoid or rotary valves (two wires) or stepper motors (four wires, typical of GM). Without a working valve the engine runs on a fixed bypass or the mechanical stop and may stall.

causes_en: Ignition or start switch, or start button, faulty or sticking
Harness chafed, short to ground or positive
Selector or clutch switch in the start path
Starter relay sticking
P0512.desc: The engine module reads a start request – from the ignition switch, a start button via the body module, or start-stop – and drives the starter relay with it. P0512 flags a fault in this signal. Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X) checks plausibility: if the engine runs above 500 rpm and the start signal stays active for more than 3 minutes, a short or sticking switch is assumed, MIL after two trips. On a Jeep Cherokee diesel a chafed harness caused P0512 with a no-start. The starter then does not crank – or with a short to positive keeps running.

causes_en: Engine module replaced or reflashed and not taught to the immobiliser
Key or transponder not programmed or faulty
Immobiliser, body or RF hub module replaced or faulty
Software fault in the handshake
P0513.desc: The engine module receives a secret code from the immobiliser or body module (Chrysler SKIM/SKREEM/RF hub, Saab CIM); if it does not match the stored code, P0513 sets and starting is prevented – Saab cuts fuel and blocks the starter. The most common trigger is a replaced or reflashed engine module that was not taught to the immobiliser (FCA, Saab), less often handshake timing on FCA hybrids or a key not programmed. FCA lists it as invalid SKIM key. It is not emission-related; CARB does not require immobiliser monitoring, and no source documents a warning lamp.

causes_en: Engine module software (false trigger)
Battery sensor or NTC drifting
Corrosion at sensor or connector near the battery acid
Sensor fitted wrongly after a battery change
P0514.desc: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0514 is the plausibility check of the temperature signal. On FCA/Alfa Romeo the temperature comes from the intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal; P0514 means its value is implausible, and several cases on the Alfa Giulia 2.0 were fixed by engine module software. A fixed substitute temperature is then used; CARB requires plausibility faults to have their own code.

causes_en: Sensor or connector corroded (battery acid)
Wire open or chafed
Sensor not plugged in after a battery change
Module
P0515.desc: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0515 is its general circuit fault – open or short – without separating low and high; the charging voltage is then fixed or conservative. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules. A fixed substitute temperature is then used.

causes_en: Signal line shorted to ground (chafed at the battery tray)
Sensor shorted internally
Moisture or acid in the connector
Module
P0516.desc: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0516 means the signal voltage stays below its limit for a minimum time; with an NTC in a voltage divider a low voltage means very hot, or more often a signal line shorted to ground or an internal short. The module then assumes a hot battery and may charge too little. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules. A fixed substitute temperature is then used.

causes_en: Sensor unplugged or forgotten after a battery change
Wire or connector open or corroded
Sensor open internally
Signal line shorted to positive
P0517.desc: The battery temperature sensor – usually an NTC in the battery tray or inside an intelligent battery sensor on the negative terminal – lets the module adjust the charging voltage (higher when cold, lower when warm) and supports battery management and start-stop. P0517 means the signal voltage is above its limit, close to the reference; with an NTC that means very cold, or more often an open circuit – sensor unplugged, wire broken – or a short to positive. The module then assumes a cold battery and may charge too high. No manufacturer document available to us names this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules. A fixed substitute temperature is then used.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at the idle valve connector
Broken or chafed wire in the harness
Valve coil with shorted turns (temperature-dependent)
Driver in the engine module
P0518.desc: Older engines without electronic throttle have a separate idle air control valve bypassing the closed throttle; CARB requires its output to be checked but not the fault types to be coded separately. P0518 means its circuit fails sporadically – the signal or current briefly leaves its valid range and returns. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0518; GM and Ford report idle valve faults as P0505–P0507 and P0511. Engines with electronic throttle do not set it.

causes_en: False air behind the throttle (intake, gasket, vacuum hose)
Throttle or idle valve stuck open (foreign body, coking)
Throttle actuator motor faulty (follow-on P2101)
Follow-on fault of other codes (sensors, pedal)
P0519.desc: P0519 means the idle control fails functionally with an electrically sound circuit – the actual idle speed deviates strongly despite fully used control. It is documented only on Subaru (also in the Saab 9-2X, electronic throttle, around 2005): idle at least 1000 rpm above target with the control already at zero for 2 or 5 s sets the code with the warning lamp at once, and a fail-safe cuts fuel to cylinders to stop the engine racing. GM and Ford use P0506/P0507 instead; CARB's mandatory limit is +200/−100 rpm.

causes_en: Connector or supply, ground or SENT signal wire open or corroded
Sensor electronics faulty
Oil or moisture in the connector
Engine module
P051A.desc: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051A is the sensor's general circuit fault. Ford uses it only for the digital SENT sensor, when the module receives invalid messages or signal patterns (together with U060E for lost communication); analogue sensors report P051B–P051D instead. It is checked continuously with 5 s to fault.

causes_en: Sensor zero point drifting
PCV or blow-by valve sticking, ventilation blocked or frozen (real overpressure)
Engine module software (known false trigger)
Increased blow-by from engine wear
P051B.en: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P051B.desc: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051B is its plausibility check. Ford flags a zero-point deviation above 0.15 inHg (about 0.5 kPa) from ambient with the engine stopped, and in operation at low air flow a pressure above 5 inHg (about 17 kPa) or below −0.6 inHg – so Ford also reports a real excess crankcase pressure under P051B. Maserati and Alfa Romeo bulletins name blow-by valves or software.

causes_en: 5 V reference or signal line open or shorted to ground
Connector corroded or oily
Sensor faulty
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor
P051C.en: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P051C.desc: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051C means the signal of the analogue ratiometric sensor is too low – Ford sets it below 0.44 V for 5 s. Typical is a signal shorted to ground, an open or shorted 5 V reference, or an open signal line pulled down.

causes_en: Sensor ground open
Signal line shorted to positive
Sensor faulty
Engine module
P051D.en: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P051D.desc: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051D means the signal is too high – Ford sets it above 4.56 V for 5 s. Typical is a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage, an open sensor ground, or an open signal pulled up. A real excess pressure in the crankcase does not set P051D.

causes_en: Loose contact at the sensor connector
Chafed harness
Oil or water in the connector
Sensor faulty internally
P051E.en: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P051E.desc: The crankcase pressure sensor measures pressure in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) against atmosphere; Ford's EcoBoost engines use it for the disconnection check P04DB, which needs a sound sensor. P051E means the signal jumps or briefly drops below or above its limits – physically impossible changes, usually from a loose contact. No manufacturer document available to us uses P051E; Ford, Maserati and FCA use only P051A–P051D. The description follows CARB's input component rules.

causes_en: Separator or filter clogged with oil, soot or sludge
Icing in the separator or hose on short winter trips
Oil change intervals exceeded (sludge)
Pressure sensor reading wrong
P051F.desc: The crankcase ventilation has an oil mist separator or filter element that can clog; the crankcase pressure sensor then sees rising pressure at a given flow. P051F reports this restriction. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – Ford reports high pressure under P051B. BMW and GM bulletins describe the consequences of a blocked separator: oil pushed past seals, oil mist in the intake and charge air cooler, higher oil consumption. CARB requires the PCV system to be monitored.

causes_en: Sensor or switch faulty internally
Connector corroded or oily (oil creeping through a leaking sensor)
Signal line open or shorted to ground
5 V reference or supply faulty (usually with other sensor codes)
P0520.en: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0520.desc: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0520 is the general circuit fault, used differently: Ford petrol and diesel engines set it for the digital SENT sensor when it reports an internal fault, does not initialise or sends values out of range (lost communication is U0600), after 5 s. GM's 1.4 L turbo with an oil pressure switch sets it when the switch reports pressure although the engine has been off long enough to be pressureless – type C, without warning lamp.

causes_en: Sensor drifting or stuck (offset)
Oil pump control valve or two-stage pump stuck in the wrong stage
Wrong viscosity, low oil level or foaming oil
Worn oil pump or bearings
P0521.en: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Range/Performance
P0521.desc: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0521 is the plausibility check. With the engine off the sensor must read about zero (GM: above 40 kPa after 10 s is a fault, Ford diesel above 70 kPa); with it running the value is compared with a model of speed and oil temperature (GM single-stage pump ±50 kPa). GM checks two-stage pumps against limits per stage and calibrates P0521 with the pump valve – so a real pressure fault can also set it. GM type B, two trips.

causes_en: Signal line shorted to ground or open
5 V reference failed or shorted
Sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or oily
P0522.en: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Low
P0522.desc: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0522 means the signal voltage is below its limit: GM 2018 below 5 % of the 5 V reference, Ford petrol below 0.25 V, Ford diesel below 0.018 V, about 5 s. As the sensor gives about 0.5 V at zero pressure, this is an electrical fault – real low pressure is P0524. GM's 2006 V8s used the warning lamp only with cylinder deactivation; GM's 4.6 L Northstar then allows cam phasing only above 1500 rpm.

causes_en: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Oil or moisture in the connector
P0523.en: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A High
P0523.desc: The oil pressure sensor matters for emissions control because modern engines use it as an input – for two-stage or regulated oil pumps, hydraulic cam phasers and GM's cylinder deactivation, whose lifters switch by oil pressure. P0523 means the signal voltage is above its limit: GM 2018 above 95 % of the 5 V reference, GM 2006 above 4.89 V, Ford petrol above 4.75 V, Ford diesel above 4.992 V, about 5 s. Typical are an open sensor ground or a signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage. Real excess pressure is not reported here – Ford uses P055F for that. GM's 2006 V8s used the warning lamp only with cylinder deactivation.

causes_en: Oil level too low, oil loss or consumption
Too thin oil, fuel dilution or clogged pick-up screen
Oil pump or pressure control valve faulty or stuck
Worn crankshaft or camshaft bearings
False setting by software in the cold (Ram EcoDiesel)
P0524.desc: P0524 is not a sensor fault but a condition: the measured oil pressure is below a minimum depending on speed, load and temperature (Ford diesel 30–90 kPa) for about 5 s, with the sensor itself plausible. Its purpose is engine protection; Ford petrol engines with mid-lock cam phasers drive them into the locked position. GM's tables do not use it; FCA updated the Ram EcoDiesel software against false setting in the cold. Stop the engine, check the oil level and confirm with a mechanical gauge.

causes_en: Servo worn or sticking, cable misadjusted
Vacuum leak at hose or diaphragm (vacuum servo)
Wiring, connector or fuse to the servo
Brake or clutch switch interrupting the servo release
P0525.en: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0525.desc: P0525 concerns vehicles with a separate cruise control servo – a vacuum or electric actuator on the throttle cable driven by the engine module: the control circuit is electrically sound, but the response does not match the command. With electronic throttle the engine module controls the throttle itself, so the code hardly applies there. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0525. CARB names cruise control as the example of an emission-neutral diagnosis: switching it off as the default reaction suffices, so usually no warning lamp.

causes_en: Hall sensor at the fan clutch faulty
Wiring or connector (chafing at the shroud, corrosion)
Clutch not turning despite command
Engine module or supply
P0526.desc: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0526 means no usable signal although the clutch is driven: GM Duramax below 500 rpm with fan duty at least 36 % for 2 s; the 6.6 L LML distinguishes a level stuck low or high; GM petrol V8s set it when no pulses arrive with the engine running. Type B, two trips. GM also reports a missing signal under P0526. A GM bulletin for 2011–2013 Duramax vans and pick-ups names loud fan noise and weak air conditioning at low speed.

causes_en: Sensor or trigger element damaged, wrong air gap
Interference or ground fault on the sensor line
Viscous clutch slipping or sticking (real speed off)
P0527.desc: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0527 means a signal is present but implausible – spikes, jumps or a speed that does not fit the clutch command and engine speed. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0527; GM covers implausibility through P0483 (target versus actual) and P0493. CARB requires input components used by other diagnoses to be checked for plausibility.

causes_en: Sensor faulty
Wire open or connector off
Fan or clutch really not turning
P0528.en: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0528.desc: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0528 means no pulses arrive from the sensor although the fan should be turning. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0528 – GM detects exactly this state (fan below 4 rpm with the engine running) but reports it as P0526. CARB requires input components to be checked for open and short circuits.

causes_en: Loose contact at connector or wiring at the fan (vibration, chafing)
Sensor in the fan clutch intermittently faulty
Clutch itself faulty
P0529.desc: Engine-driven fans with an electronically controlled viscous clutch (GM petrol SUVs and pick-ups 2004–2006, GM Duramax, Ford 6.7 L Power Stroke) have a Hall sensor reporting fan speed; the fan checks P0483, P0494 and P0495 need it. P0529 means the speed signal drops out or jumps at times. It is documented only for Ford's 6.7 L Power Stroke in the 2016–2019 Super Duty and F-650/750: a Ford service message lists it with P0480, P0494, P0495 and P0691–P0694 for fans running permanently or not at all, and warns against replacing the clutch too early – check wiring, connector and sensor first. Ford's summaries give no thresholds.

causes_en: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain
P052A.en: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P052A.desc: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052A means bank 1 was too far advanced. Outside cold start, P0011 applies.

causes_en: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (stuck in base position)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain
P052B.en: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P052B.desc: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052B means bank 1 was too far retarded – typical for a phaser stuck in its locked base position.

causes_en: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (bank 2)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain
P052C.en: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P052C.desc: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052C means bank 2 of a V engine was too far advanced. Outside cold start, P0021 applies.

causes_en: Cam phaser sticking or lock pin not releasing (bank 2)
Low oil level, wrong viscosity or sludged oil
Oil control valve sticking or screen clogged
Stretched timing chain
P052D.en: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P052D.desc: Some engines shift the intake (A) camshaft right after a cold start so that more exhaust heat reaches the catalyst; CARB requires each commanded element of this cold-start strategy to be monitored under its own codes. Documented only by Ford (from 2008): during the first 60 s it checks the cam position for 5 s and sets a code above 11° deviation, plus a stuck-pin test (10° commanded, under 2° movement) and an averaged deviation index. Warning lamp after two trips; afterwards the normal cam codes take over. P052D means bank 2 of a V engine was too far retarded. Outside cold start, P0022 applies.

causes_en: Diaphragm of the regulating valve torn or fatigued
Part-load ventilation valve blocked (oil carbon, sludge)
Elbow or hose at the valve cracked, clamp leaking
Engine module software
P052E.desc: P052E is a function fault of the crankcase ventilation pressure regulating valve. Audi's 3.0 TFSI has a diaphragm valve whose torn diaphragm or elbow causes false air and whistling; Mercedes' M270/M274 have a switched part-load ventilation valve that blocks with oil carbon and lets oil into the intake – blue smoke, rough running, lack of power; Mercedes extended the emission warranty on the intake module. GM Europe's 2.0 diesel in the Saab 9-5 uses P052E differently, for PCV heater performance – which J2012 lists as P053D.

causes_en: Main feed to the module open or high-resistance (fuse, connector, corroded ring terminal)
Poor ground of the glow plug module
System voltage too low or too high (weak battery, regulator fault)
Glow plug module faulty internally
P052F.en: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage
P052F.desc: Diesel glow plugs are switched by a separate glow plug control module fed from the battery, with its own ground, a command from the engine module and a diagnostic line back. P052F means its supply voltage is out of range. Ford's 6.7 L and 3.0 L Power Stroke set it below 6.5 V, above 16.5 V or with an open supply, after about 1 s, continuously. An FCA bulletin shows P052F together with all six glow plug open codes P0671–P0676, because without supply no current flows – check main feed, connector and grounds first. GM does not use it.

causes_en: Connector or contacts corroded or loose
Pressure sensor faulty
Wire open or chafed
5 V reference shorted by another sensor
P0530.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P0530.desc: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0530 is the general circuit fault; GM and the Saab 9-4X use the more precise P0532/P0533 instead. Saab's 2006 9-5 diesel (Bosch EDC16) assigns P0530 differently, to a short to ground below 0.1 V for 0.6 s, switching off the A/C relay. Warning lamp depends on the maker.

Refrigerant charge wrong (too little or too much)

P0531.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0531.desc: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0531 means the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the expected pressure. GM compares the pressure rise after compressor engagement with a model of ambient and coolant temperature, road speed and fan speed, 100 samples of 100 ms, type X without warning lamp. Saab's 2006 9-5 diesel assigns P0531 differently, to a short to positive above 4.9 V with 101 kPa substitute value.

P0532.desc: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0532 means the signal voltage is too low – GM below 3 % of the 5 V reference in 80 of 100 samples (about 2 s), from a signal shorted to ground, an open signal line or a lost 5 V reference; an empty system at ambient pressure usually still reads in range. P0533.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P0533.desc: The engine module reads the high-side refrigerant pressure sensor (5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) to switch or regulate the compressor, raise the radiator fans at high pressure and pre-control the compressor load at idle. CARB therefore requires A/C components to be monitored where they alter fuel or ignition control or feed other diagnoses (from 2006–2008). P0534.desc: P0534 reports too little refrigerant (a leak), not a sensor circuit: the module compares pressure or temperature in the circuit with a model, and the compressor is locked out for protection. FCA's 2020 Ram EcoDiesel sets it with the warning lamp; a software update fixed false setting. In GM's Volt, Spark EV and Lyriq the circuit also cools the traction battery – GM prescribes recovering and weighing the charge (Volt at least 800 of 950 g) and comparing the battery's refrigerant temperature sensors with ambient.

P0535.desc: The evaporator temperature sensor, an NTC thermistor behind the evaporator, prevents icing: near 0–3 °C the compressor is switched off or reduced. Usually the climate module reads it and reports body codes; P0535–P0539 only arise where the engine module controls the compressor and reads the sensor. P0535 is the general circuit fault; the compressor is usually locked out or run with a substitute value. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the description follows CARB's input component rules.

P053A.desc: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053A means its control circuit is open. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM. The heater then has no effect, which only matters in hard frost.

P053B.en: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low
P053B.desc: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053B means the low-side control line is shorted to ground, so the heater stays on regardless of command – it works in frost, but heats permanently. GM's diesels of 2016 check it with 20 of 40 samples below 90 °C coolant without warning lamp, GM Europe's 2.0 CDTI in the Saab 9-5 with the lamp on the first trip – a difference even within GM.

The module switches it to ground. P053C means the control line is shorted to positive: the driver cannot switch, the heater stays off, or the driver overloads and switches off. P053D.desc: The PCV heater is an electric element of a few ohms (Saab: 6–10 Ω) at the junction of the ventilation hose and the intake; it stops water in the blow-by gas from freezing and blocking the ventilation in frost. The module switches it to ground. P053D means the heater is electrically connected but its effect or current is implausible – current outside the target window, an overheated driver, or the expected warming does not occur. No manufacturer document available to us uses P053D; GM Europe checks this function under P052E. Frost protection is then uncertain.

causes_en: Ventilation or oil separator blocked or frozen
Pressure regulating or PCV valve faulty
Increased blow-by (piston rings, turbo oil side)
Leaking vacuum reservoir or pump in the valve cover
P053E.desc: P053E is the system code for crankcase pressure above an operating-point limit while the sensor itself is plausible. Normally the crankcase runs at a slight vacuum (GM: −1 to −5 inH2O). No manufacturer document available to us uses P053E – Ford reports the same under P051B (above 5 inHg at idle air flow). Excess pressure pushes oil past seals and the dipstick, carries oil mist into the intake and raises oil consumption. CARB requires the PCV system to be monitored.

P053F.en: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1
P053F.desc: Petrol direct-injection engines often inject twice after a cold start, once late in the compression stroke, to heat the catalyst; this needs rail pressure within a window. P053F reports that the window was not reached often enough. Documented only by Ford's EcoBoost: over the whole cold-start phase it compares the time in the window with the phase duration against 0.70, once per cold start, with fuel level at least 15 % and the fuel sensors sound. The module then drops this mode, the catalyst lights off later; warning lamp after two trips. GM does not use P053F.

P0540.desc: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. Cummins checks it by the manifold temperature rise, Iveco by the battery voltage dip when the relay switches. P0540 is the general circuit fault of heater A without low/high assignment. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

P0541 means the voltage in the monitored circuit stays too low – typically a control line or relay coil shorted to ground or open, so the relay does not switch and there is no preheating. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

P0542.en: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High
P0542.desc: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0542 means the voltage stays high although the heater is commanded on – a control line shorted to positive or a relay that does not switch. A shorted or welded relay can also power the heater permanently; Ram recalled 6.7 L Cummins trucks because a shorted heater relay could start a fire. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

P0543.en: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Open
P0543.desc: Some diesels – typically Cummins engines in Ram pick-ups and commercial vehicles, and Iveco – heat the intake air with a grid heater in the intake manifold instead of or alongside glow plugs. It draws very high current through a relay (on recent Ram a solid-state relay) and is switched by the engine module before and after starting; CARB requires cold-start aids to be monitored. P0543 means an open circuit at heater A – in the control line or relay coil, or depending on the maker in the power circuit or heating element itself. It is detected by driver diagnosis with the output off, by a missing voltage dip on switching on or by a missing temperature rise. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM's Duramax LML has an intake heater but reports it under its own codes P154A–P154D.

P0544.en: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0544.desc: The exhaust gas temperature sensor is a thermistor in a voltage divider with the module's pull-up resistor; the first one (sensor 1) sits before the turbocharger, the oxidation catalyst or after it depending on the maker. Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0544 is the general fault of bank 1 sensor 1. Ford's 6.7 L diesel uses it not as a circuit fault but for plausibility against an exhaust temperature model: after at least 6 h off it compares sensor and model over 200–400 s, a fault exceeding ±80 °C for 20 s, once per trip. GM's Duramax does not use P0544. The module then runs on a model value and may restrict filter regeneration.

Diesels use it for particulate filter regeneration and component protection; CARB names it explicitly as a monitored input. P0545 means the signal is below range: GM L5P below 142 Ω in 10 of 20 samples, GM LML below 0.65 V, Ford 6.7 L below 0.10 V for about 2 s, Saab 9-5 2.0 TiD below 0.1 V for 1 s. Usually a signal shorted to ground. GM USA uses two trips, GM Europe in the Saab one. The module uses a substitute value and blocks filter regeneration.

P054A.en: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P054A.desc: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. Ford watches the deviation with an averaged variance index for each direction; GM (Saab 9-4X V6) uses only the retard codes, above 6° for 1 s or 4 s cumulative, type B. The commonest cause is oil pressure building too slowly when cold. P054A means bank 1 was too far advanced. Mercedes (M276) traces it to slow oil pressure – 1 bar should be reached after about 3 s; Audi (Q5 3.2) and VW (Atlas 3.6 and 2.0 T) fixed it by software.

P054B.desc: Camshaft B is the exhaust camshaft. During catalyst heating after a cold start some engines set it to a specific position; CARB requires such commanded elements to be monitored with their own codes, separate from the normal cam codes. GM's test procedure checks oil level and pressure, a phaser sweep from 0 to 40° and the control valve at 7–12 Ω.

Oil entering combustion (turbo seal, crankcase ventilation)
Rail pressure actually higher than measured
Wrong injector correction codes after replacement
P054E.en: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Lower Than Expected
P054E.desc: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054E means the engine holds idle with much less fuel than expected – more energy arrives than commanded, for example from injectors delivering too much, oil entering combustion or wrong injector correction codes.

causes_en: Injectors delivering too little (coked, high return flow)
Rail pressure actually lower, fuel supply (filter, air)
Mechanical losses: compression, seizing accessories
EGR valve stuck open or intake blocked
P054F.en: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Higher Than Expected
P054F.desc: Diesel only. At controlled idle the module compares the fuel quantity the idle governor needs for target speed with a model value; CARB sets the limit from 2013 at ±50 % of what a sound engine needs. Ford's diesel sets the codes beyond ±50 % for 5 s at standstill with warm engine and no filter regeneration; GM compares with 0.5 times a minimum map or 1.5 times a maximum map, 200 of 255 samples, type B. P054F means the governor needs much more fuel than expected – the commanded quantity does not arrive or the engine has extra losses: clogged injectors, low compression, an EGR valve stuck open or additional load from accessories.

causes_en: Connector or wire open or corroded (splash zone at the pump)
Sensor or switch faulty, often also leaking
5 V reference or ground disturbed
Engine module
P0550.desc: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0550 is the general circuit fault. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Without the signal the engine can drop or stall at full lock, or the module raises idle permanently as a substitute.

Signal line shorted to ground (ground means active)
Permanently high pressure (steering valve sticking, kinked line)
Vehicle speed signal faulty (Saab depends on P0501)
P0551.en: Power Steering Pressure Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P0551.desc: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. That makes it an input to idle control under CARB. Switches (Saab, Mitsubishi) ground a pull-up; analogue 5 V sensors (Toyota) give about 0.45 V at zero pressure. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0551 means the switch reports high pressure where that is implausible – at speed there is hardly any steering. Mitsubishi sets it when the switch stays on through 10 drive-and-stop cycles; Saab's Trionic T8 after 600 s above 50 km/h, keeping raised idle as substitute and without warning lamp.

P0554.desc: Hydraulic power steering has a pressure switch or sensor on the high-pressure line; when the wheel is turned at standstill, pump pressure and engine load rise sharply, so the engine module raises idle air in advance to stop the engine stalling. GM's and Ford's tables do not use P0550–P0554. P0554 means the signal flutters. Mitsubishi sets it when the switch changes state at 10 Hz or more for 20 s above 50 km/h – no sound switch switches that fast. Causes are electrical (loose contact) as well as hydraulic: pressure pulsation from air or low fluid, or an unsteady pump.

P058A.desc: The battery monitor module (intelligent battery sensor) sits on the negative terminal of the 12 V battery: a shunt measures current, electronics also measure voltage and temperature and calculate state of charge, health and cranking ability, reporting over LIN. Energy management uses the data for alternator control, idle boost and stop-start release, which is why the engine module diagnoses it. GM sets P058A–P058F in its engine modules from 2016 as type B, warning lamp after two trips. P058A means the module reports an internal fault of its own over LIN. Battery data are then unreliable – stop-start is blocked and the alternator usually runs a fixed substitute voltage. Loss of communication is a separate U code.

P0597.desc: A map-controlled thermostat is a wax thermostat with a built-in heating resistor (Valeo: about 10 Ω). Unheated it opens late, for hot running at part load; the engine module heats it by map under full load or towing so it opens earlier. CARB requires the thermostat to be monitored and the heater circuit counts as an output component. GM switches it to ground with a low-side driver and checks it every second, fault after 15 of 30 samples, type B; Hyundai/Kia/Genesis and VW/Audi use the codes as well. P0597 means the heater circuit is open – GM above 200 kΩ with the driver off. The thermostat then only works through its wax and opens late, so coolant runs hotter under load; Audi's 4.2 FSI also limits engine speed. Genesis (G80/G90 3.3 T, 3.8) replaced thermostats from an early production lot.

A separately evaluated position sensor, as these titles assume, is described in Ford patents (Hall sensor on the motor or sensor on the linkage). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code: today the sensor sits inside the LIN actuator, whose faults appear as P059F/P05AE, P05A1/P05B0 or U0284/U0285. Without position feedback the shutter is usually driven open. P059B (shutter A) means the signal is electrically valid but does not match the commanded position or learned travel – GM covers such deviations under P059F/P05AE instead.

Connector corroded or with water ingress

P059F.en: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance/Stuck Off
P059F.desc: The active grille shutter (A = upper or only shutter, B = second) closes louvres to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and requires its components to be monitored. P059F compares commanded and reached position. GM checks it in two stages – detection, then five clearing attempts – type B, two trips; Ford's 3.0 L diesel at over 6° deviation in operation or 20° when learning fully open. 'Stuck off' means stuck closed at Toyota (failure type 73) and Nissan; GM and Ford use P059F for any deviation. Typical are ice, snow, debris or a bent bracket – a closed shutter can make the engine run hot in traffic.

Several fixes were software updates (Mazda, Audi Q7, VW Jetta); Audi's 2022–24 A3 limits top speed to 100 mph with a shutter fault.

P05A1.en: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance

P05A2.en: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit/Open
P05A2.desc: An active grille shutter closes louvres in the grille to cut drag and speed warm-up and opens them for cooling; CARB names it as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators (Ford 3.0 L diesel, Toyota) check their own coil and supply and report over LIN; simpler ones (VW 1.8 T) have their own supply and a control line from the engine module. GM uses none of P05A2–P05A8. A fault usually only costs fuel and warm-up time. P05A2 concerns the control or motor coil circuit. Ford's 3.0 L diesel reports an open and a shorted coil under it, checked by the actuator at the start and 500 ms after each movement, fault after 10 s. Toyota uses P05A2 as a collective code with a failure-type byte for short to ground, short to positive, open or stuck.

P05B8.desc: After a crash the restraint control module tells the engine module that airbags or belt tensioners have fired; the engine module then cuts the fuel pump (Ford: until the ignition is cycled) and possibly the engine. Depending on the maker the message travels over CAN and/or a dedicated wire with a defined level or voltage drop. P05B8 means the wired signal line is open – no valid rest level arrives. After a real crash the fuel cut-off may then not be triggered via this line. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; it is a safety function, not an emission-relevant monitor, so usually without warning lamp.

P05B9 means the signal line stays below its valid rest level – usually a short to ground. P05BA means the signal line stays above its valid range – a short to battery or ignition voltage, or with a pull-up in the engine module an open circuit. The fuel cut-off may then not work via this line. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; it is a safety function, not an emission-relevant monitor, so usually without warning lamp.

P05BB.desc: After a crash the restraint control module tells the engine module that airbags or belt tensioners have fired; the engine module then cuts the fuel pump (Ford: until the ignition is cycled) and possibly the engine. Depending on the maker the message travels over CAN and/or a dedicated wire with a defined level or voltage drop. P05BB is an event code: the engine module received a valid deployment message. The fuel pump is cut, the engine may stop, doors are unlocked by other modules, and Ford's engine module freezes recorded data. After a crash the restraint module must be replaced; a used module with a stored crash can also cause it. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; it is a safety function, not an emission-relevant monitor, so usually without warning lamp.

P05C0.en: Active Grille Air Shutter Module A Over Temperature
P05C0.desc: Shutters cut drag and speed warm-up when closed and open for cooling; CARB names them as an off-cycle CO2 technology and treats the actuator as an output component. Smart actuators report over LIN (loss of communication: U0285); a fault usually costs fuel and warm-up time, a closed shutter can make the engine run hot under load. P05C0 means the smart actuator of shutter A (the upper one) measures its control chip above 140 °C for 10 s and switches its driver off for protection. Documented only for Ford's 3.0 L diesel. Usual causes are continuous motor load from a stiff or blocked shutter or a shorted coil, or an internal fault; it may work again after cooling.

P05C2.desc: An engine coolant pressure sensor (5 V reference, ratiometric signal) measures pressure in the cooling circuit; in a sealed circuit pressure rises with temperature, so deviations reveal leaks or a loose cap – described in Navistar and GE patents for commercial and rail engines. P05CC.en: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1
P05CC.desc: During catalyst heating after a cold start the engine module commands a specific cam phaser position for more residual gas and exhaust heat; CARB requires this to be monitored under codes separate from the normal cam codes. These 'performance' codes are GM's current form (since about 2015/16; older GM engines and Ford use the direction codes P052A ff and P054A ff): fault when commanded and actual position differ by more than 4° or 6° once the target is stable. P05CC watches intake camshaft A on bank 1 – the cold-start counterpart of P0011. GM's 3.0 L twin turbo sets it above 4°, 60 of 100 samples, type B; the 2.0 L turbo in the Envision above 6° as type A after one trip. A GM bulletin for the 2024–25 Traverse, Enclave and Acadia (2.5 L turbo, electric phaser) names a damaged phaser motor with rattle, together with P0011/P0016.

P05D0.en: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit

No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM covers the same switch with the more specific P05D1–P05D3.

P05DB.en: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P05DB.desc: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DB is the general circuit or open-circuit fault of channel B. Toyota's electronically controlled brake (RAV4 Hybrid 2024–25) reports channel B faults under it; while it is stored, the A/B correlation does not run.

P05DE.desc: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DE means channel B is above its valid range – an open signal, ground or reference line or a short to positive. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV sets it with the regeneration warning light and the check engine light.

causes_en: Loose contact or fretting corrosion at the sensor connector
Broken or chafed wire in the moving pedal area
Sensor track or Hall element worn
Interference on the shared 5 V reference
P05DF.en: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05DF.desc: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems use a dual-channel pedal travel sensor; channel B runs opposite to A at Toyota (3.6–4.4 V at rest, falling when pressed), so a common fault of both channels shows up. It feeds brake assist and regenerative blending; CARB requires inputs used by other diagnoses to be monitored. A channel fault blocks the A/B correlation P05E0 and usually limits brake assist or regeneration. P05DF means channel B jumps or is noisy within its valid range – loose contacts or brief interruptions. Toyota lists it as a channel B code that blocks the correlation check; no admissible manufacturer document available to us gives thresholds.

causes_en: Pedal travel sensor faulty internally (channels drift apart)
Contact resistance or corrosion in the connector or harness of one channel
Sensor not calibrated after replacement or pedal work
Foot resting lightly on the brake while accelerating (GM)
Brake or hybrid control module faulty
P05E0.en: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P05E0.desc: Brake-by-wire and hybrid systems measure brake pedal travel with a two-channel sensor; the channels often run in opposite directions (Toyota RAV4 hybrid 2024–25: one rises from about 1 V, the other falls from about 4 V). P05E0 means both channels are electrically fine but no longer match each other. Toyota sets it when the relationship is invalid for 0.2 s and lights the lamp at once; Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV adds the regenerative brake warning. Braking falls back to plain hydraulics, so the pedal may feel hard and regeneration is off. GM notes for the CT6, Bolt, Malibu and Volt 2016–18 that the code can also appear without a defect if the driver rests a foot lightly on the brake (1.8–5.6 mm travel) for 60 s while accelerating. Single-channel faults are P057A–P057E and P05DB–P05DF.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector (front end, splash water)
Chafed or broken wire (5 V, signal, ground)
Sensor faulty internally (signal jumps)
Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor
P05E1.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05E1.desc: The refrigerant pressure sensor (three wires, 5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) tells the engine module the A/C pressure; it uses it to switch the radiator fan, to block the compressor at too high or too low pressure and to pre-control idle load. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, but they need not light the lamp if they do not affect emissions. 'Intermittent/Erratic' means the signal jumps implausibly fast or briefly leaves its valid range without staying low or high long enough for those codes. Sensor A is usually the high-pressure sensor; GM and Saab report it only as P0532/P0533 (circuit low/high, at GM below 3 % or above 98 % of 5 V) and P0531, so no manufacturer document available to us uses P05E1 itself. Typically the compressor is blocked and the fan runs. GM rates sensor A faults without the lamp, the Saab 9-4X with it.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor B connector
Chafed or broken harness
Sensor B faulty
5 V reference or control module
P05E2.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P05E2.desc: The refrigerant pressure sensor (three wires, 5 V reference, signal rising with pressure) tells the engine module the A/C pressure; it uses it to switch the radiator fan, to block the compressor at too high or too low pressure and to pre-control idle load. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility, but they need not light the lamp if they do not affect emissions. 'Intermittent/Erratic' means the signal jumps implausibly fast or briefly leaves its valid range without staying low or high long enough for those codes. Sensor B is a second pressure sensor; which one depends on the maker – typically the low-pressure side or a second circuit in heat pump systems. Its other codes are P2515–P2518. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E2, so this follows the sensor A family. Expect the A/C or heat pump to switch off intermittently.

causes_en: Broken wire or corroded connector at the park brake switch or sensor
Switch or pressure sensor faulty
Faulty diode in the switch circuit (Volvo)
Vehicle or brake module delivers a wrong status
P05E3.desc: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E3 is the general circuit fault – usually an open circuit or undefined state. Low and high signals are P05E4 and P05E5.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafed)
Sensor 5 V supply missing or shorted to ground
Sensor faulty internally
Module input faulty
P05E4.desc: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E4 means the signal is below the lower limit: on a three-wire sensor a signal shorted to ground or a missing 5 V supply; on a simple ground switch it looks like a permanently applied brake.

causes_en: Open signal or ground wire
Connector at the switch or sensor loose or corroded
Sensor faulty
Signal wire shorted to voltage

causes_en: New pressure sensor and old switch report differently (switch point, delayed change)
Faulty diode in the switch circuit
Low air pressure or leak in the spring brake circuit
Switch or sensor sticking or faulty
P05E6.desc: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E6 is the one code of the family with a manufacturer description: at Volvo both signals must change together and agree; if they contradict each other or one changes late, the code sets. Volvo advises starting the diagnosis with the brake released.

causes_en: Loose contact or corrosion at connector or splice
Chafed wire with intermittent short
Switch bouncing or worn
Module connector
P05E7.desc: The engine module reads the park brake status, directly or via another module, because strategies depend on it: a parked diesel filter regeneration only runs with the park brake applied (Navistar), idle shutdown and PTO logic use it, and Ford delays an automatic restart while the electric park brake moves. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored. The only documented user of this code family is Volvo Trucks: since OBD 2021 a second park brake sensor (about 0.5 V applied, 3.5 V released) must agree with the old switch; the engine module reports the fault. No passenger car maker uses it verifiably. P05E7 means the signal jumps briefly without being permanently low or high – changes without operation, while driving or too quickly in a row. The status is then discarded and regeneration or stop-start is blocked.

causes_en: Connector at the valve loose, corroded or spread
Valve solenoid coil open
Broken wire in the harness
Output driver in the module faulty
P05E8.en: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit/Open
P05E8.desc: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05E8 means the control circuit is open: the driver sees missing voltage or high resistance.

causes_en: Control wire chafing against ground (block, bracket)
Shorted turns in the valve
Moisture or oil in the connector
Output driver in the module
P05E9.en: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit Low
P05E9.desc: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05E9 means the control circuit voltage is too low – control wire shorted to ground or shorted coil turns.

causes_en: Control wire touching battery or ignition voltage
Valve coil shorted (overcurrent at the driver)
Connector or wiring damage
Control module
P05EA.en: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit High
P05EA.desc: The engine oil bypass valve is an electrically switched solenoid that, according to patents (Hyundai/Kia), routes oil around the oil cooler when cold so the engine warms up faster with less friction, and through the cooler once the oil is hot. It is not the purely mechanical oil filter bypass. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. No manufacturer document available to us uses P05E8–P05EA, and no vehicle with these codes was found. If the circuit fails, the valve stays in its unpowered position – depending on design oil may run too hot under load or warm up slowly. P05EA means the control circuit voltage is too high – a short to battery or overcurrent at the driver, so the valve cannot be operated.

causes_en: Engine module software or calibration (false trigger)
Exhaust temperature sensor before the SCR reads low or slow
Heating measure not effective: throttle, EGR cooler bypass or turbo vanes sticking
Post or retarded injection not effective (injectors)
Exhaust leak before the sensor or extremely cold conditions
P05EB.en: Cold Start SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P05EB.desc: After a cold start a diesel heats its exhaust actively – retarded and post injection, intake or exhaust throttling, higher idle, EGR cooler bypass – so the SCR catalyst quickly reaches the temperature at which urea dosing can start (around 180–200 °C). P05EB sets when the measured temperature at the SCR inlet stays below the expected or modelled value within a set time after the start: the heating strategy is not working. CARB requires this 'catalyst warm-up' monitor for light-duty diesels from model year 2026 (20 %) to 2028 (100 %); GM 2025 and Ford 2023 tables do not contain the code yet. Volvo Trucks used it on 2016–17 heavy-duty engines and advised a software check instead of replacing parts. The lamp comes on; no power limitation from this code alone is known.

causes_en: Engine module software or internal fault (request and execution differ)
Cold start mode blocked by other faults (coolant or fuel temperature, rail pressure)
Injector driver or injector circuit
Weak battery during cold start
P05EC.desc: To heat the exhaust after a cold start, a diesel shifts its start of injection, usually later, plus post injections. CARB requires faults of such elements during the cold start strategy to be reported under codes separate from normal operation – hence P05EC. GM's 2025 diesels compare the start of injection requested by the application software with the timing actually scheduled for the injector drivers, during cold start only; a deviation beyond ±4 or ±5 in 88 of 176 or 8 of 16 samples sets the code and the lamp in the first trip. Ford's 2023 diesel instead checks whether the cold start operating mode is really activated when requested (10 s). Mechanical injector timing faults in normal operation are P01CB ff and P020A ff; the petrol counterpart for ignition timing is P050B.

causes_en: Main fuse or feed wire to the heater module faulty, connector corroded (splash zone)
Poor module ground
Weak battery or charging fault (system voltage too low or too high)
Heater control module faulty internally
P05ED.en: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
P05ED.desc: Some diesels use a separate control module or power stage for the DEF heaters in tank, pump and lines; without heating, frozen fluid cannot thaw in winter and dosing stays blocked. P05ED reports that this module's supply voltage is outside its allowed window – a blown main fuse, an open feed or ground, or system voltage too low or too high. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Thresholds are not published; GM's L5P monitors the comparable heater supply under its own codes and flags a drop of more than 3 V below battery voltage while heating is requested. Start with fuse, feed, ground and battery or charging system.

causes_en: Connector at the pump or tank module corroded or loose
Open wire in the harness to the tank
Fuse or relay of the pump supply faulty
Pump or tank module open internally
P05EE.desc: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05EE means the supply circuit is open: when the supply is switched on, no voltage or current reaches the pump branch. Ford's comparable check flags a pump controller voltage below 6 V. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes_en: Supply line shorted to ground (chafed against the frame)
High contact resistance or corrosion in the connector
Pump shorted internally or stiff (high current)
Weak battery or charging system
P05EF.en: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05EF.desc: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05EF means the supply voltage is too low or the supply line is shorted to ground. GM's 6.6 L diesel monitors the same high-side driver under P1043 (short to ground with driver on, about 0.5 Ω, 3 s, first trip); Ford flags its pump controller voltage below 8.5 V. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes_en: Pump supply shorted to battery positive in the harness
Overvoltage from the charging system or a jump start
Moisture or corrosion causing leakage current in the connector
Relay or driver does not switch off
P05F0.en: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05F0.desc: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F0 means the supply voltage is too high, or voltage is present although the supply is switched off (short to battery). GM's 6.6 L diesel monitors this as P1044 (two trips); Ford flags pump voltage above 16 V or controller voltage above 19 V. No manufacturer document available to us uses this exact code; GM and Ford monitor the same function under their own codes. Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes_en: Pump supply relay stuck (welded contacts)
Semiconductor driver shorted
External voltage or short to positive in the harness
Software or calibration fault
P05F1.en: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck On
P05F1.desc: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function. P05F1 means the pump supply stays on although the module switches it off – typically detected after the switch-off command, e.g. during after-run, when the feedback still shows voltage. A welded relay or a shorted semiconductor switch is the usual reason. Chrysler (FCA) lists this code among those that trigger the DEF inducement: a 'Service DEF System' warning, a countdown after 50 miles and no restart after 150 miles (P241D). Without supply the pump cannot build pressure, dosing stops and NOx rises; pressure or SCR efficiency codes may follow.

causes_en: Relay does not pull in or fuse blown
Open in the relay control or load circuit
Output driver in the engine module faulty
Electronics of the tank module faulty (no feedback)
P05F2.en: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck Off
P05F2.desc: The electric supply pump in the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF, AdBlue) tank module builds the dosing pressure for the SCR catalyst. Its supply voltage is monitored separately from the pump control circuit (P208A ff); CARB requires SCR components and their outputs to be checked for circuit faults and function.
