P0737.desc: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0737 is the general circuit fault of this output; low and high are P0738/P0739. Not to be confused with the engine speed input at the transmission module (P0725 ff). A tachometer or dependent display then reads wrong or nothing, while driving is usually unaffected.

P0738.en: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit Low
P0738.desc: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0738 means this output is too low, typically shorted to ground, so it can no longer switch high. The opposite is P0739, the general fault P0737. A tachometer or dependent display then reads zero or jumps, while driving is usually unaffected.

Shift-by-wire: range actuator or park module, range sensor or its calibration

CAN communication or control module
P073D.desc: P073D means neutral is commanded but not reached or not held. GM uses it on vehicles with electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire, e.g. Cadillac XT4): the selector or engine module compares commanded and actual range from the range sensor and flags it after 1.8–2 s in the selector module or 10 s in the engine module, after two trips. For Ford's 6F35 the supplier Sonnax describes a mechanical cause: a forward or direct clutch dragging in neutral, visible as turbine speed staying only 200–400 rpm below engine speed. The car may creep in N; range changes may be locked. The opposite, stuck in neutral, is P072A.

causes_en: Range actuator or park module centred wrongly or faulty (shift-by-wire)
Module software (e.g. after an over-the-air update)
Range sensor reports the wrong actual range
Reverse clutch or brake, valve or shift fork (DCT)
Fluid level or system pressure
P073E.desc: P073E means reverse is commanded but not reached. Two uses are documented. With electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire) GM compares the commanded range with the actual range reported by the transmission and flags it if reverse is not reached within 1.8–3 s in the selector or diesel engine module, or 10 s in petrol engine modules, after two trips; GM bulletins name a range actuator centred wrongly (LaCrosse, XT5) and software after an over-the-air update (2025 Equinox/Terrain). On dual-clutch transmissions (2020–23 Corvette, Maserati MC20) it means the reverse gear cannot be engaged. Stuck in reverse is P072B, slip in reverse P0736.

causes_en: Shift fork valve or solenoid in the mechatronic unit sticking (dirt, wear)

Learned shift fork or clutch values lost or wrong

P073F.desc: Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P073F means the first gear, on the odd sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072C, slip in an engaged gear P0731. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.

causes_en: Open or corroded harness or transmission pass-through connector
Converter clutch solenoid coil open
Internal transmission harness or mechatronic unit
Driver stage in the module faulty
FCA: actual converter slip (clutch wear, fluid) or software
P0740.desc: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0740 concerns the control circuit of the converter clutch solenoid. Ford flags an open circuit when the driver feedback line disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with MIL; a 2006 GM table checks 0/12 V with more than 43 of 50 failed counts after two trips – newer GM units use P2761/P2763/P2764. FCA's Ram 6.7 reads P0740 as converter slip out of range and moved it to two trips by software in 2013. The clutch is then switched off: higher engine speed when cruising, more fuel, hotter fluid.

causes_en: Fluid level too low, old or burnt fluid
Converter clutch control valve worn or sticking, bore worn

Solenoid mechanically sluggish (electrically fine)
Leaking turbine shaft seals or pump
P0741.en: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P0741.desc: P0741 means the converter clutch does not lock although commanded – slip stays too high while the circuit is electrically fine. Thresholds: GM's T43 at least 130 rpm for 5 s twice, the 6T70 50 rpm for 5 s three times, Saab's Aisin AF40 over 100 rpm for 2 s, all after two trips; Ford over 100–200 rpm or a speed ratio below 0.93 over five lock-up events; Subaru engine speed more than 9/8 of target for 10.2 s. The module then locks out the clutch, sometimes the top gear, and uses a hot-mode shift pattern. Low or burnt fluid, a worn control valve in the valve body and a glazed converter clutch are the usual causes; Hyundai's 8-speed bulletin calls for a new converter.

P0742.en: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On
P0742.desc: P0742 means the converter clutch stays applied although commanded off – there is almost no slip. GM's T43 flags −50 to +13 rpm for 1.5 s six times and the 6T70 −20 to +30 rpm for 2.5 s, both after one trip; Allison and Saab's Aisin AF40 after two trips, the AF40 also when the engine stalls without slip. Typical is the engine stalling when stopping or when selecting D or R, plus jerking at low speed. Note the different uses: Ford's P0742 is a short to ground in the clutch solenoid circuit (stuck on is P2758 there), and Saab's 9-3 of 2003 uses it for a mechanical lock-up fault.

P0743.desc: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0743 is the collective electrical code for the converter clutch solenoid circuit – open, short to ground or to positive – detected by terminal voltage, driver feedback or current. Subaru flags it after 0.14 s and lights the MIL after two trips, Saab's 9-3 of 2003 above 1356 mA for 500 ms, Allison after 1.5 s; older Ford transmissions also use it. The clutch is switched off; Saab's Aisin boxes go into limp mode, Subaru does not.

P0744.desc: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. In J2012 P0744 is an intermittent fault in the converter clutch circuit, but no manufacturer document available to us uses it that way: Ford flags a short to power via the driver feedback line after 0.5–5 s with MIL, and Nissan's CVT bulletins treat it as a functional converter fault checked at the valve body and belt. GM does not use it. Short interruptions make the clutch drop out and reapply, and lock-up may be disabled for the trip.

P0745.desc: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0745 is the general code for this valve; the sub-codes P0746–P0749 follow. It is documented on Mitsubishi CVTs as a current plausibility check: at most 400 mA while 750 mA or more is commanded for 5 s, or 1.34 A or more for 1 s. A failure usually leaves the valve unpowered, so pressure goes to maximum: harsh shifts and, depending on the transmission, limp mode in a fixed gear.

P0746.en: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0746.desc: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0746 means the valve is electrically fine but the commanded pressure does not build. GM's clutch-to-clutch units detect it as slip: 400 rpm or more for 1.5 s (T87), or clutch 1 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s three times (9-speed), after one trip; Allison when the oncoming clutch does not apply. Mitsubishi's dual-clutch flags 500 mA current deviation. Slipping or flaring on shifts, a missed gear and limp mode follow; GM's 9-speed bulletin checks clutch plates and replaces the valve body.

P0747.en: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On
P0747.desc: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0747 means the valve is electrically fine but pressure stays applied. On GM's clutch-to-clutch units the off-going clutch 1 does not release – slip stays below 50 rpm (9-speed, 0.8 s on loaded downshifts), and Allison flags 25 rpm or less for 0.3–1 s, both after one trip. On line pressure valves it means permanently high pressure. Harsh, abrupt shifts, a tied-up transmission and a default gear follow. GM noted false settings on 2017 8-speeds: clear and retest first.

P074A.desc: Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P074A means the second gear, on the even sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072D, slip in an engaged gear P0732. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.

P0750.desc: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, newer GM units have separate low/high codes, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's 9-5: A = valve S2). P0750 is the general code for solenoid A and is used in practice for an open circuit: Ford's step automatics (2012–2023) set it when the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with shorts to ground and power as P0973/P0974; Ram's 6.7 L with Aisin transmission calls it 'control circuit open', and a 2023 bulletin traces it to a leaking capacitor in the engine module. GM does not use P0750. With the solenoid unpowered the transmission falls back to a hydraulic default gear with maximum pressure.

P0751.desc: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; together the solenoid states select the gear, and the module checks the result by gear ratio, slip or a pressure switch – the pattern of wrong gears shows which solenoid hangs off or on. P0751 means solenoid A is commanded on but valve, clutch or gear do not follow. GM's 6T70 flags a ratio of 1.34–1.48 with slip of 400 rpm for 0.3 s eight times and locks out first gear; GM 4-speeds recognise the pattern 2-2-3-3; both after two trips. Allison checks its pressure switch for 5 s after one trip. Ford's 'functionally failed off' covers the whole clutch circuit, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins show purely mechanical causes such as a leaking clutch cylinder.

P0752.desc: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; together the solenoid states select the gear, and the module checks the result by gear ratio, slip or a pressure switch – the pattern of wrong gears shows which solenoid hangs off or on. P0752 means solenoid A is commanded off but its clutch stays applied. GM's 6T70 flags slip of 400 rpm for 2 s five times after one trip and then runs only reverse, first and third with maximum pressure; GM's T43 a ratio of 3.83–4.23 (first instead of fourth); GM 4-speeds the pattern 1-1-4-4 after two trips; Allison its pressure switch after 2 s. Ford calls it 'functionally failed on'. A clutch that does not release can tie up the transmission.

Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, newer GM units have separate low/high codes, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's 9-5: A = valve S2). P0753 is the collective electrical code for solenoid A. GM's older engine-controlled 4-speeds check 0/12 V feedback and flag an open or short to ground at more than 43 of 50 failed counts; Subaru compares the driver transistor voltage with the command for 30 ms, lights the MIL after two trips and holds third gear; Saab's Aisin boxes measure current; Hyundai's 8-speed uses it for the underdrive clutch valve. Ford and newer GM do not use P0753.

Brief dropouts make the module switch the solenoid off and enter limp mode until the next start.

P075A.desc: Shift solenoid G only exists on transmissions with seven or more solenoids. Ford's 10R80 and 8F35 use solenoids A–F, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch pressure valve codes, the Allison 1000 uses three; the only documented user of the G block is Hyundai/Genesis' 8-speed, which assigns P075A and P075D to its on/off solenoids. Hyundai's bulletins for the Genesis, Equus and G80/G90 (2012–2018) use P075A for the on/off solenoid 'SS-A' – on the G80/G90 in connection with the park lock – and treat it as a circuit fault: replace valve and electronic module, then load the valve data. That 'SS-A' is Hyundai's own numbering, not solenoid A in the J2012 scheme.

causes_en: Overfilled at fluid change or repair (wrong check temperature or procedure)
Level sensor drifting (reads too high)

P075F.desc: P075F is not a circuit fault but a condition: a working fluid level sensor reports a level above the target band – the counterpart of P070F. In the Allison patent the transmission module reports 'too high, drain a quart or more', measuring only with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid and low input speed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. Overfilling makes rotating parts churn the fluid, which foams, pressure control becomes unsteady, fluid escapes at the vent and temperature rises; an FCA bulletin traces poor shifting after repairs to overfilling. Automatic transmission fluid level depends strongly on temperature – topping up cold often overfills.

P0760.desc: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's Aisin 9-5: C = valve S4, D = valve S5). P0760 is the general code for solenoid C and, at Ford, means an open circuit: the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, continuously; shorts to ground and power are P0979/P0980. On Ford's 6R80, 6F35/6F55 and 6R140, solenoid C is the proportional valve of the CB26 brake for second and sixth gear. If the solenoid supply is switched off, Ford transmissions keep park, reverse, neutral and fifth gear with maximum pressure.

P0761.desc: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; the module checks whether its clutch follows the command by gear ratio, shift time or a pressure switch. P0761 means solenoid C is commanded on but its clutch does not follow. GM's Honda-built five-speed (Saturn Vue) combines a ratio check – first gear running in the window of second for 1.2 s – with a 3–4 shift faster than 0.8 s, after two trips. The 2007 Allison 1000 checks pressure switch 3 for 5 s, after one trip. Ford's 'functionally failed off' covers the CB26 brake circuit; Dodge's Aisin AS6 uses the code for solenoid 3, while Mitsubishi uses it for pressure switches.

P0762.desc: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; the module checks whether its clutch follows the command by gear ratio, shift time or a pressure switch. P0762 means solenoid C is commanded off but its clutch stays applied. GM's Honda-built five-speed flags a 2–3 shift slower than 0.8 s together with a 4–5 shift faster than 0.8 s, after two trips; the Allison 1000 a pressure switch 3 still applied after 2 s (up to 4 s when cold), after one trip. Ford's 10R80 bulletins list it with a leaking clutch cylinder.

P076F.desc: P076F means the ratio in seventh gear is wrong: input speed divided by output speed does not match the commanded gear, so a clutch slips or another gear is engaged. It only exists on transmissions with seven or more gears. Ford's 10-speed 10R80 and 10R140 list it in bulletins together with the other ratio codes and the check engine light – causes include a migrating sleeve on a clutch cylinder causing hydraulic leaks and sticking valve body valves. Ford's ratio check elsewhere flags more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times. On GM's Corvette with seven-speed manual gearbox, P076F is a plausibility check of the gear position sensor instead (ratio window 0.41–0.50), after one trip.

P0770.desc: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0770 is the general code for solenoid E; Ford uses it for an open circuit, detected when the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, and on the 6R80/6F it covers all circuit faults of the solenoid. On Ram's 6.7 L with Aisin AS69RC a 2023 bulletin traces P0770 to a leaking capacitor in the engine module, together with other circuit codes. Limp mode follows; on the 6R80/6F engine braking in first or the 4th–6th gears may be missing.

P0771.desc: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0771 is Ford's functional check by gear ratio over 10 events (2012) or 3 (2020–23, 2023 diesel). On the 6R80/6F it means the multiplex valve stays in its rest position, so solenoid D acts on the wrong clutch; valve and spool cannot be told apart. On the 6R140 the 4-5-6 clutch does not apply. Ford counts the whole clutch system in, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins list P0771 with mechanical repairs. Slipping or missing gears and limp mode follow.

P0775.desc: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0776.en: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance/Stuck Off
P0776.desc: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0776 means the valve is electrically fine but pressure stays too low. GM's 8-speed flags gear slip of 400 rpm for 1.5 s three times, the 9-speed clutch 2 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s, the CVT primary pressure below 200 kPa for 3 s – all after one trip. Mitsubishi's Jatco CVT flags secondary pressure 1.2 MPa off target; Nissan's bulletin calls for a mechanical CVT repair, a GM 6T70 bulletin a broken wave spring. Slipping, missing gears or lack of drive and limp mode follow.

P077A.en: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Loss of Direction Signal
P077A.desc: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077A means the sensor still delivers speed pulses but no usable direction information – the pulse width stays outside the direction windows or one Hall element has failed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM checks direction coherence under P0721. Hill hold, auto hold or stop-start may then be disabled and the forward/reverse change runs in a substitute mode.

causes_en: Output speed sensor faulty (direction evaluation disturbed)
Wrong or incorrectly fitted sensor (orientation to the wheel)
Reluctor wheel damaged, metal debris on the sensor
Faulty reference (input or intermediate shaft sensor)
P077B.en: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Direction Error
P077B.desc: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077B means the sensor reports a direction that does not fit – for example reverse while a forward gear is engaged and the input and intermediate shaft sensors confirm forward motion. GM's transmission modules list P077B as a blocking condition for other checks, but run the actual check under their own codes: direction contradicts the gear for 2.5 s above 500 rpm, after one trip. Speed and direction are then unreliable: hill hold and the park and reverse logic fall back to substitute modes.

P077C.en: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Low
P077C.desc: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077C means this voltage is below 0.25 V – a short to ground of under about 0.5 Ω between signal and module ground – for more than 0.05 s with the system above 10 V; GM rates it after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks so that P0722 is not set instead of the actual short. Without output speed the transmission enters limp mode and road speed may be missing. On GM's 10-speed input and output sensors share a supply.

P077D.en: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit High
P077D.desc: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077D is the mirror of P077C: the voltage is above 4.75 V – a short to the module supply of under about 0.5 Ω – for more than 0.05 s, after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks; a GM hybrid also blocks its idle diagnosis. Without usable output speed the transmission enters limp mode, and speedometer or cruise control may fail.

P077E.en: Transmission Fluid Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation
P077E.desc: P077E is a plausibility check between several fluid temperature readings – for example sensors A and B, sump and valve body, or the module's internal temperature. If they differ by more than allowed after a settling time, such as a long stop, the code sets, without being able to blame a single sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM checks each sensor alone (P0711, with the module temperature on the 6T70), and Ford has no multi-sensor check. A substitute value then limits converter clutch and shift adaption.

P077F.desc: P077F checks the ratio in a second reverse gear: input speed divided by output speed lies outside the tolerance band around the target ratio – a slipping clutch, a wrong gear or a sensor fault. Only transmissions with two reverse ratios need it, such as Mercedes' 7G-Tronic (−3.42 and −2.23, with the second reverse kept in limp mode) and its 5G-Tronic predecessor; GM's 9- and 10-speeds, Ford's 10R and ZF's 8HP have one. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the check works like the other ratio codes such as P0736.

P0780.desc: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0780 is the collective code when the faulty shift is not assigned to a gear. GM's 2006 Aisin-type five-speed counts five shifts that are too long, too short or tied up with fluid above 60 °C and lights the MIL at once; GM's Honda-built unit flags a 3–4 shift that stays in the lower ratio after two trips; Saab's 2010 Aisin six-speed counts ten faulty shifts without MIL, limits torque and keeps second and reverse. Nissan fixed P0780 on the 2021 Rogue CVT with new software.

P0785.desc: Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0791.en: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0791.desc: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. Ford uses P0791 as its only intermediate shaft code, for 'no or too little signal': while the vehicle drives under power (turbine at least 1500 rpm, output at least 650 rpm or 15 mph), the sensor reports below 250 rpm for 5 s – in the 2012 and 2020–23 summaries, with MIL. A Toyota bulletin for the U760 (Highlander, Venza, Camry 2009–10) replaces the countershaft sensor for P0791/P0793. GM's 10-speed has two such sensors but uses its own codes. Limp mode and harsh shifts follow.

P079A.desc: The 'friction element slip' codes monitor a clutch that is commanded locked in a power-split hybrid transmission: the module calculates its slip from electric motor, engine and output speeds (target 0 rpm) and flags slip above a threshold for a minimum time, with sufficient line pressure and clutch torque; from 2016 GM also flags a calculated friction energy threshold at once. P07A2.en: Transmission Friction Element A Performance/Stuck Off
P07A2.desc: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. P07A2 concerns clutch A. Ford's DPS6 PowerShift dry dual-clutch (Fiesta, Focus) uses it for clutch A – input shaft 1 with gears 1, 3 and 5 – as 'functionally stuck off', next to the electrical codes of its electric clutch actuator; Ford publishes no thresholds. A GM bulletin for the 2017 LaCrosse and 2017–19 XT5 lists P07A2 as 'transmission clutch 1 performance' together with ratio codes, caused by a misaligned range actuator. GM's hybrids do not use it.

P07B2.en: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit/Open
P07B2.desc: With electronic gear selection the park position sensor/switch reports the park request or position. P07BF.en: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P07BF.desc: These low/high codes are a purely electrical check of the sensor's signal voltage at the module and run even with the vehicle at rest – unlike the circuit, range, no-signal and intermittent codes, which evaluate speed while driving. P07CB.desc: Many automatics have a thermostat in the fluid cooler circuit or a coolant-to-oil heat exchanger: a BMW patent describes a wax thermostat that bypasses the cooler until about 76 °C, a Ford patent a heat exchanger that warms transmission fluid from the coolant after a cold start. P07CB means this thermostat does not work as expected: fluid warms up too slowly (stuck open) or overheats (stuck closed). No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM checks fluid warm-up under the temperature sensor code P0711 (below 15 °C after the warm-up time, two trips). The check works like CARB's engine thermostat monitor (P0128). Slow warm-up raises consumption and delays converter lock-up; overheating ages fluid quickly.

P07CC.en: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit Low

P07D7.desc: P07D7 means gear 8 cannot be disengaged: the module commands a shift out of 8th, but the transmission stays in it. It is the counterpart to P07D8, where gear 8 cannot be engaged. The only documented user is Maserati's eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox in the MC20 (from model year 2023), whose bulletin lists it next to the other 'Stuck in Gear' codes: hydraulic actuators move the shift forks, and a fork that does not reach neutral is reported. The repair path there first runs a service fast-learn with valve flushing and new adaptation, then records system pressure – it should hold 20–30 bar; drops below 5 bar point to the mechatronic unit, a stable pressure to the gearbox itself. No thresholds or trip counts are published.

P07D8.desc: Unable to Engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – here 8th. Documented users are eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes with hydraulically moved, position-monitored shift forks. A GM bulletin for the 2020–23 Corvette lists it with the MIL on, caused by a solenoid or internal switch sticking from debris: valve cleaning is only advised when system pressure codes are present as well, otherwise a service fast-learn; if that fails, the mechanics are damaged. Maserati's MC20 lists it with a pressure check of 20–30 bar. On a dual-clutch box the half carrying the even gears may be locked out. No published thresholds or trip counts.

P07D9.desc: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07D9 covers 8th gear. Ford's 10R80 (F-150, Mustang, Ranger, Expedition and others) and 10R140 (2020 Super Duty) list it in bulletins on harsh or delayed shifts, caused by adaptive learning, sticking valve-body valves or a migrating sleeve in a clutch cylinder. Nissan's nine-speed Frontier and Titan set it with the MIL on; a Stellantis bulletin pairs it with P0731 on low-mileage vehicles with wrong factory adaptives. Hyundai's eight-speeds and GM's 10-speed do not use it.

P07DA.desc: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. They continue the series P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift'. No manufacturer document available to us uses P07DA or P07DB: Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion (speed must drop by more than 30 rpm on an upshift, flare above 300 rpm) without a gear-specific code, Ford's 10R80 feeds the solenoid function codes and GM the clutch valve codes. P07DA names the change between 6th and 7th gear, in either direction, as faulty; it exists only on transmissions with seven or more gears. Flags and thresholds follow the manufacturer's own logic.

P07DC.desc: The series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA and P07FD for 9 and 10) covers a shift that leaves the starting gear but lands in a gear other than the commanded target – a skipped or overshot gear. A module can see this after the shift because the measured ratio matches the wrong gear. No manufacturer document available to us uses the series: Ford assigns such patterns to the shift solenoid that caused them (P0751 ff), newer GM automatics report clutch pressure valve codes. P07DC starts from gear 1. It differs from P0731 (wrong ratio while in gear 1, a slipping clutch), P072C (gear 1 cannot be left) and P0781 (the shift itself takes too long or flares). Detection, MIL and trip count therefore follow only by analogy from CARB's functional check and Ford's ratio and shift completion checks.

causes_en: Manual park release cable misrouted or actuated
Range actuator misaligned or its coupling offset
Control module software
Park lock actuator or its ground faulty
Range or park position signal wrong
P07E4.desc: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E4 means park is not reached or not held within the allowed time. GM gives thresholds: 2 s in 2018 tables and the ICCM of its electronic range selector (2000 ms), 6–10 s in later tables, type B with the MIL after two trips; a 2018 bulletin for LaCrosse and XT5 blames a misaligned coupling of the range control module. Ford sets it with the wrench lamp instead of the MIL – on the 2020 Escape and Corsair a misrouted park release cable, on the Mach-E software – and applies the electric parking brake. Ram 1500 (2019) sets the MIL; Stellantis names a used manual park release as the most common cause.

causes_en: Range control actuator misaligned or faulty
Software or after-effect of an over-the-air update
Range sensor signal wrong
Forward clutch or line pressure missing
P07E5.desc: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E5 means drive is requested but not reached in time. Only GM documents it: its electronic range selector (LaCrosse, XT5, XT4, 2025 Equinox and Terrain) allows 10 s in most tables, 3 s in the 2018 Diesel table and 2000 ms in the selector module, type B with the MIL after two trips. A 2018 bulletin blames a misaligned range control module coupling, its 2019 revision adds ratio codes; on the 2025 Equinox and Terrain it can appear after an over-the-air update and clears after a ten-minute rest. The car does not move forward or falls back to neutral.

causes_en: Park lock actuator failed internally

Low system voltage
P07E6.desc: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E6 means park cannot be left: the pawl stays engaged or its position feedback keeps reporting P. Ford documents it on the HF45 hybrid transmission (2023–24 Escape, 2022–24 Maverick), where the inverter control module monitors the park actuator – the P on the rotary selector flashes, the wrench lamp comes on and an internally failed actuator is replaced (about 13–14 h) – and on the 2024–25 Mach-E, where a high resistance in the park motor ground is fixed with new software and a ground harness. Maserati lists it for the MC20 dual-clutch gearbox. Ford keeps it off the MIL; GM tables do not list it.

causes_en: Range actuator or selector shaft sticking
Range sensor wrongly reporting D
Selector sensor or software
P07E7.desc: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E7 means drive cannot be left: after a request for P, N or R the transmission stays in D. It is the counterpart to P07E5, where drive cannot be engaged, and to P07E6 for park. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM's range selector module checks requested against reached range in the same way for P07E4 and P07E5 (2000 ms, two trips). With shift-by-wire the fault matters for safety, because the car cannot be put into park or neutral. Typical causes would be a sticking range actuator or selector shaft, a range sensor wrongly reporting D, or the selector or its software.

causes_en: Wire or connector between selector and shift module open

P07E8.desc: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07E8 is the open-circuit check of these sensor lines: if one sensor input is pulled above 4.5 V for 2.4 s with the ignition on, the code sets. Mitsubishi lists it with the MIL but without a fail-safe reaction, because the remaining sensors still identify the position. Low and high are P07EA/P07EB. GM and Ford use their own codes for their selectors.

P07E9.en: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Performance
P07E9.desc: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07E9 is the plausibility check of the sensor voltage: valid levels lie only in defined on and off windows, and a sensor sitting for 2.4 s in a forbidden band in between (0.6–1.07, 2.12–2.67 or 3.28–4.5 V) sets it – typically contact resistance, moisture or a sensor beginning to fail. Mitsubishi defines no fail-safe reaction. Note the title: 'Circuit Performance', not 'Range/Performance'.

P07EA.en: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Low
P07EA.desc: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07EA is the electrical low check: one sensor reads below 0.6 V for 2.4 s – a signal wire shorted to ground or a missing sensor supply. Mitsubishi defines no fail-safe reaction. If all bits drop out at once, P07EF follows and the transmission goes to neutral.

P07EC.desc: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EC sets when a single bit does not change as the lever moves through its positions – it is stuck on or off. The other bits still identify the position, but the decision takes at least a second. Mitsubishi shows only the yellow electric-shift warning, without the MIL. Two or more stuck bits are P07ED.

causes_en: Selector sensor board faulty
Selector connector corroded or loose (several pins)

P07ED.en: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Stuck
P07ED.desc: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07ED is the step after P07EC: at least two bits are stuck, so the position can no longer be decoded reliably. Mitsubishi then puts the drive in neutral and blocks changes between P, R, N and D, lights the MIL and the red or yellow shift warning; the car cannot be driven and has to be towed.

Outdated module software
Selector or harness
P07EE.en: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Range/Performance
P07EE.desc: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EE is the range and plausibility fault of the position code; Mitsubishi assigns it solely to the electric shift module itself – the pattern fits no position or contradicts itself. A generic scan tool shows the fault as P0914 'Gear Shift Position Circuit A'. Shifting is blocked, the drive goes to neutral and the MIL comes on; the usual repair is a software update or the module.

causes_en: Selector plug disconnected or its supply or ground open
Selector sensor board faulty
Electric shift module
P07EF.en: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Low
P07EF.desc: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EF is the low state of the whole pattern: all eight bits report off, which is no valid code – typically a disconnected selector plug or a missing common supply or ground. Mitsubishi detects it already at standstill after about 10 s with the ignition on, puts the drive in neutral and lights the MIL.

causes_en: Selector signal wires shorted to the supply
Selector faulty
Shift module
P07F0.en: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit High
P07F0.desc: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07F0 would be the high counterpart of P07EF: the position code reports a high state that matches no valid position, for example signal levels pulled up by a short to the supply. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – on Mitsubishi's selector 'all on' is the valid home position, so a high state cannot be told apart there. By analogy to P07EF a module would block range changes or select neutral.

causes_en: Sensor wire or connector open
Speed sensor faulty
Control module or software
P07F1.en: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P07F1.desc: P07F1 is the general circuit code of a third input or turbine shaft speed sensor, after sensor A (P0715) and B (P2765); low and high for sensor C are P07C3 and P07C4. No production use could be found in GM tables from 2015 to 2025, Ford's summaries of 2012 and 2020–23, Mitsubishi's code index or manufacturer bulletins; such a sensor would make sense on transmissions with three input shafts or a hybrid input. The check would follow P0715: no plausible signal while driving or an open circuit. The module then uses a substitute value, keeps the converter clutch open and shifts more harshly; with emissions impact CARB requires the MIL.

causes_en: Shift-by-wire module faulty or its software
Communication wire or connector
Weak battery during start-up
P07F2.en: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit
P07F2.desc: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F2 reports a fault in its communication. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift sets it when the module's start-up CAN check fails and blames the module itself; it switches to neutral only if the CVT or the whole system is affected too, and one of its two entries carries no MIL. GM (U18AA, U2409) and Ford (U101F, without MIL) report the same function under their own U codes.

causes_en: Communication wire shorted to ground
Module output stage faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
P07F3.en: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit Low
P07F3.desc: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F3 is the electrical low check of its communication line: the line is shorted to ground and stays at a low level. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the code fits a dedicated signal or redundancy line between selector, range control module and transmission or engine module rather than a CAN bus. GM handles a bus short under its own U2409 (bus off for 1 s, two trips). The module may block range changes or select neutral.

causes_en: Communication wire shorted to the supply
Module faulty
Connector fault
P07F4.en: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit High
P07F4.desc: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F4 is the electrical high check of its communication line: the line is shorted to the supply and stays at a high level. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; as with P07F3 it fits a dedicated signal or redundancy line rather than a CAN bus, whose faults GM reports under its own U codes. The module may block range changes or select neutral.

causes_en: Weak battery or charging system
Fuse, supply or ground wire of the module with high resistance
High actuator motor current on a weak supply
P07F5.en: Transmission Range Control Module System Voltage Low
P07F5.desc: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F5 means its supply voltage is too low. No manufacturer document available to us uses the generic code, but GM checks exactly this under its own P17B0: battery voltage at the range control module at or below 9 V for 5 s within a 6 s window, type C without MIL. With too little voltage the actuator may not set the range or park pawl reliably; GM also suspends further checks of the module. A weak battery or a resistance in the module's fuse, supply or ground is the usual cause.

causes_en: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong
P07F6.desc: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07F6 covers 9th gear. Ford's 10R80 bulletins from 2023 to 2025 (F-150, Mustang, Ranger, Explorer, Transit, Expedition) list it with the other ratio codes; the causes are adaptive learning, the valve body and a migrating clutch cylinder sleeve. The 10R140 bulletin of 2021 does not mention it. Nissan's nine-speed Frontier and Titan set it with the MIL on; the repair check drives each gear 1–9 for at least 10 s in manual mode.

causes_en: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong
P07F7.desc: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07F7 covers 10th gear, so in practice only ten-speed automatics. Ford's 10R80 lists it in all its ratio bulletins. On the 2020 Super Duty with the 10R140 a 2025 bulletin shows P07F7 alone, with the powertrain wrench lamp instead of the MIL and 10th gear locked out, caused by a migrating sleeve in a clutch cylinder that leaks; an earlier bulletin blames sticking main valve-body valves. GM's 10-speed reports through clutch valve codes instead.

causes_en: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
Fluid or filter contaminated
P07F8.desc: P07F8 means gear 9 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 9th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. The family is documented only for 8th gear on eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes (Maserati MC20: P07D7 and P07D8; Corvette 2020–23: P07D8), where hydraulic actuators move shift forks under position monitoring. Nine- and ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford, GM and Nissan report faults in 9th gear as a ratio code (P07F6) or through solenoid and clutch valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes_en: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
Shift fork or synchronizer damaged
P07F9.desc: P07F9 means the transmission does not reach the commanded 9th gear – the counterpart to P07F8, where 9th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. 'Unable to Engage' is documented only for eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes, for example the 2020–23 Corvette (P07D8, MIL on, sticking solenoid from debris). Nine- and ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford, GM and Nissan report faults in 9th gear as a ratio code (P07F6) or through valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes_en: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition
P07FA.desc: P07FA belongs to the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9, P07FD for 10): when leaving 9th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 9th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Ten-speed users such as Ford's 10R family and GM's 10L report such faults through ratio or valve codes; Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code. Possible causes are a sticking shift or clutch valve, a worn or leaking clutch, or wrong adaptives.

causes_en: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
Fluid or filter contaminated
P07FB.desc: P07FB means gear 10 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 10th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. The family is documented only for 8th gear on eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes (Maserati MC20, Corvette 2020–23); no dual-clutch gearbox with ten gears and these codes is known. Ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford and GM report faults in 10th gear as a ratio code (P07F7, on Ford's 10R140 with 10th gear locked out) or through valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes_en: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
Shift fork or synchronizer damaged
P07FC.desc: P07FC means the transmission does not reach the commanded 10th gear – the counterpart to P07FB, where 10th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. 'Unable to Engage' is documented only for eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes, for example the 2020–23 Corvette (P07D8). Ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford and GM report a missing 10th gear as a ratio code (P07F7) or through valve codes; Ford's 10R140 then locks out 10th. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes_en: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition
P07FD.desc: P07FD closes the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9): when leaving 10th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 10th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Ten-speed users such as Ford's 10R family and GM's 10L report such faults through ratio or valve codes; Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code. Possible causes are a sticking shift or clutch valve, a worn or leaking clutch, or wrong adaptives.

causes_en: Shift actuator or shift valve sticking
System pressure low or unstable
Mechanical damage in the gear train
Position or speed sensor signal wrong
P07FE.desc: P07FE is the catch-all of the 'Stuck in Gear' family: the transmission stays in a gear it was commanded to leave, but the module cannot or does not name the gear. The gear-specific codes are P072B–P073C for reverse and gears 1–7, P07D7 for 8th, P07F8 for 9th and P07FB for 10th. No manufacturer document available to us uses P07FE; the gear-specific codes are documented on dual-clutch gearboxes such as Ford's DPS6 and Maserati's MC20, whose actuators move shift drums or forks. Typical causes are a sticking shift actuator or valve, low or unstable system pressure, mechanical damage, or a faulty position or speed signal.

causes_en: Transmission control module software misjudging the cold phase
Shift valve or hydraulics too slow with cold fluid
Wrong or aged fluid, low level
Fluid temperature sensor reading wrong
P07FF.desc: P07FF means the transmission does not work as expected during the cold-start phase, shortly after starting with cold, thick fluid – for example a gear preselection or a clutch or valve response outside the expected window. The only documented user is Mercedes-Benz: its 2024 bulletin for the eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox 8G-DCT in the compact models (A-Class, CLA, GLA, GLB) names P07FF together with P0921, with reverse not available, a possible limp-home mode and the MIL; after switching off and on everything works again, and the fix was new control unit software. No thresholds or trip counts are published. It is not CARB's cold-start emission strategy, which concerns engine and catalyst heating (P050A ff), but a functional check of the transmission.

causes_en: Fault in the transfer case system stored in its module (shift motor, sensor, clutch)
Wiring or connector at the transfer case (terminal tension, corrosion)
Transfer case module software
Transfer case module faulty
P0800.desc: P0800 works like P0700 for the transmission: the transfer case control module has detected a fault of its own that it rates as emissions-relevant and asks the engine control module to turn on the MIL. The engine module only stores P0800; the actual fault – often C, U or manufacturer codes – sits in the transfer case module and needs a scan tool that addresses it. CARB requires monitoring of an electronic transfer case only where it feeds other diagnostics, for example the 4WD-low signal that GM uses as an enable condition; this is why most transfer case modules never request the MIL and P0800 hardly appears in manufacturer documents. A GM bulletin for 2020–23 trucks with 'Service 4WD' and the MIL points to wiring and terminal contact at the transfer case.

causes_en: Connector at the reverse inhibit solenoid loose or corroded
Solenoid coil open
Harness between engine module and gearbox damaged
Engine module driver faulty
P0801.desc: On GM manual gearboxes (Tremec T56/TR6060 in Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V and ATS-V) the engine module drives a solenoid that blocks reverse while the car moves forward. P0801 means its control circuit is open. GM's tables describe the check: the low-side driver's internal diagnosis flags an open line with at least 9 V and the engine above 250 rpm, 20 failures in 25 samples of 250 ms – about 6 s; in 2006 a 5 s comparison of commanded and actual driver state. GM rates it type C, emissions-neutral and without MIL, from 2019 with a 'service vehicle soon' note. Depending on how it fails, reverse cannot be engaged or is no longer blocked. The title was updated to the current J2012 wording with '/Open'.

causes_en: MIL request wire or connector between the modules open or corroded
Transmission module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Module output or input faulty
Wrong or retrofitted transmission module without this line
P0802.en: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
P0802.desc: On older vehicles with a separate transmission module and no MIL message on the CAN bus, the transmission module signals 'MIL on' over its own wire to the engine module. P0802 checks this wire for an open circuit. GM's Duramax tables of 2004 and 2005 (Allison 1000) describe it: at key-on the transmission module briefly pulls the line active like a bulb check; if the engine module sees no off-to-on transition between 0.125 and 7 s after ignition, the line is treated as open – type B, MIL after two trips. Only then is P0700 evaluated. The wire itself must be monitored because an open line would stop transmission emission faults from lighting the MIL. Newer vehicles send the request over CAN, where faults appear as U codes.

causes_en: Solenoid unplugged or replaced by a skip-shift eliminator with the wrong resistance
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
Solenoid coil open
Harness damaged
Engine module driver faulty
P0803.desc: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid in the shifter housing that, at light load and low speed blocks the way from 1st into 2nd and 3rd so the driver shifts 1 to 4 – a measure for fuel economy ratings; the 1-4 lamp (P0804) shows it. P0803 means the solenoid control circuit is open. GM's tables check the low-side driver while it is off: too low a voltage or over 200 kΩ to ground, with at least 9 V and over 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms (2019 LT5: 20 of 25), type B with the MIL after two trips; shorts are P080C and P080D. An open circuit leaves the solenoid unpowered, so 1 to 2 always works. 'Skip-shift eliminators' with the wrong resistance are a frequent cause.

causes_en: Bulb or LED in the cluster faulty
Wire or connector between engine module and cluster open or shorted
Instrument cluster board faulty
Engine module output faulty
P0804.desc: With GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes, a '1-4' lamp in the cluster tells the driver that the lockout is active and to shift from 1st directly into 4th. P0804 means the control circuit of this lamp is faulty – open, shorted, or the lamp does not follow its command. No GM table from 2004 to 2025 available to us contains it, because newer cars switch the indicator by a CAN message from the instrument cluster without a separate engine-module line check; the code therefore mainly concerns older vehicles with a lamp driven directly by the engine module. The lockout itself (P0803) keeps working, only the hint is missing; there is no limp mode, and the MIL behavior is not documented.

causes_en: Clutch position sensor faulty (pedal or actuator)
Connector or harness open, corroded or shorted
Transmission module software (Nissan)
Control unit internal fault (Ford DPS6: clutch motor driver)
P0805.desc: The J2012 family 'Clutch Position Sensor A' (P0805 circuit, P0806 range/performance, P0807 low, P0808 high, P0809 intermittent, P080A not learned) covers the position of a clutch – the pedal of a manual gearbox, the clutch actuator of an automated or dual-clutch gearbox, or a clutch inside an automatic. P0805 is the general circuit fault. Uses differ: Nissan's 2022 Pathfinder with its nine-speed automatic stores it in the transmission module, lights the MIL and disables idle stop ('Idle Stop System Fault'), fixed with new software. Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the module-internal chip that drives the clutch A motor, so a control unit fault rather than an outside sensor. GM reads its clutch pedal sensor under P0806–P0808 only.

causes_en: Pedal sensor or Hall sensors of the clutch motor faulty
Pedal sensor misadjusted or not relearned after clutch work
Harness or connector with contact resistance
Clutch actuator motor faulty (DPS6)
Master cylinder leaking, pedal does not fully return
P0806.en: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0806.desc: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0806 is the plausibility check. On GM's LT4 manual cars the pedal sensor is compared with gear detection: if it reports the clutch pressed while engine and output speed show a valid gear, a filtered position error above 4 % sets the code (above 5.6 mph, not in 4WD low), type A with the MIL after one trip. On Ford's DPS6 it reports a fault of the Hall sensors on the clutch A motor; Saab sets it for a frozen pedal signal and switches off cruise control.

causes_en: Signal wire open or shorted to ground
5 V reference of the sensor missing
Pedal sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or pins loose
P0807.en: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0807.desc: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0807 means the signal is too low. GM's three-wire pedal sensor on a 5 V reference has dead bands at both ends: below 4 % of the reference counts as low or open, 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms (about 3 s), engine not cranking, over 9 V, type A with the MIL after one trip. Saab names an open circuit or short to ground. With the clutch position unknown, cruise control, start-stop and starter release by the sensor are blocked.

causes_en: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Pedal sensor faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
P0808.en: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0808.desc: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0808 means the signal is too high. GM sets it above 96 % of the 5 V reference with the same 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms, type A with the MIL after one trip; Saab's 2012 9-3 above 4.8 V for longer than 0.6 s, with cruise control switched off. Typical causes are an open sensor ground or a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage.

causes_en: Clutch A actuator motor or its Hall sensors faulty
Loose contact at the actuator connector
Transmission module Hall evaluation faulty
Supply voltage dips
P0809.en: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0809.desc: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0809 is documented only for Ford's DPS6 (Fiesta from 2011, Focus from 2012): the motor that operates clutch A carries three Hall sensors, one per phase, and while the motor turns they must produce a fixed sequence; a wrong sequence sets the code. The clutch B counterpart is P087E. The module then loses confidence in the clutch position, so clutch A with the odd gears 1, 3 and 5 is restricted. GM and Saab do not use P0809; Ford publishes no thresholds.

causes_en: Relearn not done after sensor, clutch or module replacement
Clutch badly worn or misadjusted
Pedal sensor misadjusted or wrongly fitted
Engine module reprogrammed or replaced
P080A.desc: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P080A means the learned clutch position is missing or implausible. On GM manual cars the factory learns the pedal position 'clutch fully pressed', and the engine module then tracks it as the clutch wears; a learned value outside 9.0–36.0 % of travel sets the code (250 ms, type A, one trip), a factory counter keeps the MIL off during assembly. Saab clears it by relearning with the scan tool. A relearn is needed after replacing the pedal sensor, master cylinder, clutch or engine module.

causes_en: Solenoid coil with shorted turns or resistance out of range
Retrofitted skip-shift eliminator with the wrong value
Corroded connector at the gearbox (contact resistance)
Control module or software
P080B.en: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
P080B.desc: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080B would be the range or performance fault of this circuit: electrically plausible, but outside the expected range for the command – for example a coil resistance outside its window, a partial short or contact resistance. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM's tables from 2006 to 2019 check the solenoid only electrically (P0803 open, P080C short to ground, P080D short to positive). CARB requires a functional check of outputs where feasible. The lockout may then work unreliably.

causes_en: Control wire chafed through to ground at gearbox or frame
Solenoid coil shorted to its housing
Connector corroded or water ingress
Older GM modules: circuit open or solenoid unplugged
Engine module driver faulty
P080C.en: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P080C.desc: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080C means the control line is shorted to ground: with the driver off it should sit at battery voltage through the coil but reads low (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to ground). GM checks it from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips; the 2019 LT5 uses 20 of 25 samples and type A, one trip. In the 2015/16 tables P080C also covers an open circuit. A low-side short keeps the solenoid energized, so the lockout may stay active.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage (damaged harness)
Solenoid coil with shorted turns (resistance near zero)
Substitute resistor ('eliminator') with too low a value
Engine module driver faulty
P080D.en: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High
P080D.desc: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080D means the control line is shorted to positive: with the low-side driver on, the line should be pulled to ground but reads high (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to the supply). The solenoid cannot be energized and the driver is protected or switched off. GM checks it only with the driver on, from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips in all tables from 2015 to 2019. Without power the solenoid does not lock, so 1 to 2 stays free.

causes_en: Control unit software with too tight parameters
Clutch actuator or hydraulics (pressure, valve) faulty
Clutch position sensor inaccurate
Wrong or aged fluid, worn clutch
P0810.desc: P0810 reports a control error of an electronically or hydraulically operated clutch: commanded and actual position differ too much or for too long. It is documented on Stellantis plug-in hybrids – Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH transmission – where it concerns the K0 disconnect clutch between engine and electric motor. According to the 2024 and 2025 bulletins the clutch adaptation ran at standstill or in electric mode, drive was lost until the next key cycle and the MIL came on; the cause was too tight setting parameters, fixed with new transmission software, partly together with P2885. On automated or dual-clutch gearboxes the same idea applies when the clutch actuator misses its target position.

causes_en: Transmission module calculating wrong slip (speed capture)
Clutch worn or overheated
Fluid burnt or wrong (wet clutch)
Clutch pressure or actuator too low
Input speed sensor faulty
P0811.desc: P0811 means clutch A slips too much while it should be closed – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 1 with the odd gears. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch; thresholds are not published. Audi's seven-speed S tronic DL382 (A4 to A7 and Q5, 2020–24) sets it intermittently together with P081E and input speed sensor codes, partly also clutch temperature too high; the cause was the transmission module calculating wrong slip, and the fix was a new module. Genuine slip from wear or overheating shows as flaring take-off and burnt fluid. The module limits torque, may lock out the affected half and go to limp mode.

causes_en: Reverse or back-up lamp switch faulty or misadjusted
Connector loose or wire broken (e.g. after clutch work)
Back-up lamp circuit fuse blown
Gear position sensor reporting the wrong position
P0812.desc: P0812 concerns the input 'reverse engaged' at the engine or transmission module – the reverse or back-up lamp switch on a manual gearbox, or the R contact of a selector. Modules check it for open or stuck states and against a second source such as a gear position sensor or the direction from speed sensors. A Honda patent describes this double detection: reverse counts only when switch and gear position sensor agree; if only one reports R, it is a fault and engine speed is limited. No manufacturer document with thresholds is available to us. Back-up lamps, reversing camera or parking aids may fail; on automated manual gearboxes reverse may be blocked. CARB lets such safety and comfort inputs run without the MIL.

causes_en: Wire from module to relay or body module open or shorted
Back-up lamp relay or connected load faulty
Connector corroded
Module output stage faulty
P0813.desc: P0813 concerns a signal 'reverse active' that a module puts out – usually the transmission module, on manual cars the engine or body module – for example to the back-up lamp relay, the reversing camera or the body module. Like other driver outputs it is checked by comparing commanded and actual state, which reveals an open circuit or a short. Saab's 2012 transmission module reports a short to positive on its park/neutral output in the same way. No manufacturer document with thresholds for the reverse output is available to us. Back-up lamps, camera or mirror tilt may stop working; driving itself is not affected, and CARB allows such outputs without the MIL.

causes_en: Shift module software (Jeep Compass)
Connector or wire to the selector display or cluster
Display LED or selector module faulty
Range sensor or transmission module delivering an invalid range
P0814.desc: P0814 concerns the drive or data circuit of the range display – the PRNDL or PRNDM display or lighting on the selector, sometimes in the instrument cluster. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: the electronic shift module stores P0814 with the MIL on, the selector lighting flickers or goes dark, and in a 2020 bulletin the lever could be moved out of park during cranking so that the engine stalled. The cause was software in the shift module, fixed by reflashing; a 2022 bulletin adds P081C. A wrong or missing range display matters for safety because the driver cannot reliably see P, R or N. No thresholds are published.

causes_en: Tap switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Signal wire shorted to positive
Selector assembly (Hall sensor, resistor network) faulty
Clockspring or steering wheel wiring (paddles)
P0815.desc: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0815 is the upshift switch. GM's 2019 and 2025 tables set it when 'tap up' stays on for more than 1 s in P or N, or permanently in a drive range; the 2018 hybrid table uses 2 s in P/N and 655 s in drive; type C without MIL. Ford's 6R80 and 6F35 SelectShift report a switch closed in P, R or N without MIL. On Saab's 9-4X with the 6T70 a Hall switch feeds a resistor network on one wire: a short to positive sets P0815 or P0816, a short to ground or an open sets P0826. Manual shifting is then disabled.

causes_en: Downshift switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Signal wire shorted to positive
Selector assembly faulty
Body or transmission module
P0816.desc: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0816 is the mirror of P0815 for the downshift switch. GM's 2025 table sets it when 'tap down' stays on for more than 1 s (100 ms raster, over 9 V), the 2018 hybrid table after 2 s in P/N or 655 s in drive, type C without MIL; Saab's 9-4X after 1 s in P/N or 10 minutes in a drive range; Ford's SelectShift when the switch is closed in P, R or N, without MIL. On selectors with a resistor network a short to positive in the downshift branch sets P0816. Manual shifting is disabled, automatic operation stays normal.

causes_en: Starter disable wire to the body module open or shorted
Connector corroded or pins pushed back
Transmission module with built-in range switch faulty
Body module faulty
P0817.desc: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P0817 is the general or open-circuit fault of this line. Saab sets it when the output reports 'start allowed' but the feedback shows 'off' for more than 100 ms, twice in a row, with 6–16 V and no limp mode; it rates the fault type D, without any lamp. The engine then cannot be started. Low and high are P081A and P081B; vehicles that send the start release over a bus often report similar faults as U codes or P0850.

causes_en: Neutral or disconnect switch at the transfer case or axle faulty
Underbody wiring or connector corroded or damaged
Transfer case actuator does not reach its end position
Control module or software
P0818.desc: P0818 concerns a switch input that reports whether the driveline is disconnected – on four-wheel-drive vehicles typically the neutral position of the transfer case or an axle disconnect, on hybrids a disconnect clutch between engine and transmission, as a Ford patent uses the term. It matters for OBD because in transfer case neutral the engine runs without load and wheel speed does not match the ratio, so misfire, ratio and vehicle speed monitors must know about it; CARB requires monitoring only then. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0818, and which of the two meanings applies cannot be proven. All-wheel drive or neutral may then be unavailable.

causes_en: Tap switch sticking or faulty
