Selector cable misadjusted
Selector wiring or connectors
P0819.en: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
P0819.desc: P0819 is the plausibility check between the tap-up and tap-down switches and the range sensor: a shift request may only appear in the manual gate or in drive. If a tap switch reports in P, R or N, or taps arrive without the manual gate being detected, the correlation is broken. GM's 2019 tables and Ford's 2012 SelectShift run exactly this check but assign the fault to the switch concerned as P0815 or P0816; no manufacturer with its own P0819 is documented. Manual shifting would be disabled while automatic operation stays normal, without the MIL. Causes are a sticking tap switch, a misadjusted range sensor or selector cable, or the selector wiring.

causes_en: P/N line to the engine module shorted to ground
Line or connector open
Connector oxidized or pins pushed back

P081A.desc: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081A means the start release line is too low – the output is shorted to ground or open. Saab's 2012 9-3 transmission module checks it in D, where the output must have a defined state, with 9–18 V, not in limp mode and continuously; no time threshold is published. Because the engine module then sees no 'P/N', the engine may not start.

causes_en: P/N line shorted to positive (chafed against a supply wire)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Transmission module output stage faulty
P081B.desc: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081B means the start release line stays at positive, so the 'P/N' level is present in a drive range. Saab's 2012 9-3 checks it only outside P and N, with 9–18 V and not in limp mode. A short to positive could in principle allow a start in gear; the diagnosis catches it, and Saab names as the effect that the engine may not start because the release is refused.

P081C.desc: P081C concerns the input 'park position' – the P contact of the selector or shift module, or the park pawl feedback – which controls switching off the ignition, key release, starter release and the 'not in park' warning. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: a 2022 bulletin lists P081C with the MIL on, with 'Vehicle not in Park' shown although P is engaged; the car cannot be switched off, modules stay awake and the battery drains. The cause was shift module software, fixed by reflashing. The check is a circuit or plausibility test of the P signal against the range sensor; no thresholds are published.

causes_en: Neutral contact, range switch or neutral sensor faulty or misadjusted

Wire or connector

P081D.desc: P081D concerns the input 'neutral' – the N contact of the selector or range switch, on manual cars a neutral switch or sensor for start-stop. Neutral serves for starter release, idle control without load, start-stop release and enabling other diagnostics. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the range sensor or speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P081D; its sister P081C is documented on the Jeep Compass, and Saab's range switch shows that P and N are the two start positions. The engine may then not start in N, start-stop is disabled and idle diagnostics may be suspended.

causes_en: Transmission module speed capture faulty

P081E.desc: P081E is the counterpart to P0811 for clutch B – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 2 with the even gears and reverse, which Audi calls 'clutch 2'. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch and flags slip above its limit. Audi's DL382 S tronic (2020–24) sets it intermittently with P0811 and input speed codes; the bulletins report a transmission malfunction and 'reverse gear unavailable', and the fix was a new transmission module with improved parts from late 2023. A failed clutch 2 typically means no reverse and no even gears.

P081F.en: Brake Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) Signal Correlation
P081F.desc: The brake transmission shift interlock (BTSI) is a solenoid or actuator that locks the selector in park until the brake pedal is pressed, as US rule FMVSS 114 requires. 'Signal correlation' is the plausibility check between the interlock command or feedback and its input signals – brake switch and selector position: for example the lock released without a brake signal, or still active although the brake is pressed. The selector then cannot leave park, or it moves without the brake and the safety function is missing. Electrical faults of the lock solenoid have their own codes P0928–P0931. No manufacturer document with P081F is available to us; a GM service update for the 2016 Malibu and 2016–17 Volt explains the part and the 'won't shift out of park' complaint. CARB may exempt such safety parts from monitoring.

Position sensor in the selector assembly faulty

P0820.en: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
P0820.desc: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0820 is the umbrella code: the module does not tell X from Y, or sees an invalid combination of both axes that matches no gate position. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV, which names it 'shift lever position (main) circuit malfunction' and sets it for an impossible lever position, without published thresholds. GM reads its X/Y sensors under P082A–P082F instead. Range selection may be blocked and the vehicle stays in P or N.

P0821.en: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0821.desc: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0821 is the general circuit fault of X sensor 1 – an open or invalid signal – for modules that do not report low and high separately. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports the same axis in finer steps as P082A, P082B and P082C. A GM patent describes checking each sensor's x value separately: an invalid value makes that sensor unusable, and with a redundant sensor 2 the car can usually go on.

P0822.en: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0822.desc: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0822 is the same for the Y axis – the second direction of movement, on an H-gate the select gate. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports the Y axis as P082D, P082E and P082F. A failed Y sensor can hide a gate change, for example into the manual gate or the reverse gate.

P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0823 watches X sensor 1 for short dropouts and jumps – a signal that changes faster than the lever can move, or briefly disappears. Such checks typically count jumps within a time window; no manufacturer publishes thresholds. GM folds a disturbed X signal (a frequency error of the PWM signal) into P082A, and its patent rejects a value at once if it was faulty before and differs from its partner.

P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0824 is the same for the Y axis: short dropouts or jumps of Y sensor 1. GM folds Y-axis disturbances into P082D; thresholds for P0824 are not published anywhere. The symptoms are an occasional warning, a gate change that is sometimes not recognized, and occasional limp mode.

Wire or connector to the selector assembly

P0825.desc: P0825 concerns a switch on the selector that reports pushing or pulling the lever – sequential + and – shifting – or the start of a shift movement, hence 'shift anticipate'. Its purpose: the control unit of an automated manual gearbox can prepare clutch and engine torque before the actual gear change is detected; a LuK patent describes such shift-intent detection, which reports intent when the lever signal exceeds a filtered, load-dependent reference and cancels on a reversal. A fault is typically a switch reporting 'pressed' without lever movement or never, implausible against the X/Y sensors. No manufacturer document with P0825 is available to us. Shift-intent detection is then off, gear changes are slower or sequential shifting is disabled.

P0826.en: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
P0826.desc: Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0826 is the general fault of the shared circuit. GM (6L80 in 2011, 2019, 2025, hybrids) sets it when the circuit shows an invalid voltage for at least 60 s with 8.6–32 V and 400–7500 rpm, without MIL. On Saab's 9-4X with the 6T70 a short to ground or an open sets P0826. Saab's 2003–04 9-3 Sentronic reports below 0.2 V or above 6.7 V for over 30 s under P0826 with a fault-type byte, lights 'Check gearbox' and locks the lever in P/N. Ram's 2025 heavy-duty trucks set it with P0827 and P085F and the MIL, fixed with transmission software. Manual shifting is then disabled.

Transmission software (Ram 2025)
Control module faulty
P0827.en: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low
P0827.desc: Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0827 means the shared circuit voltage is too low – a short to ground, depending on the design an open on a pulled-up input, or a switch held closed. The only documented user is Ram's 2025 heavy-duty truck with the 6.7 Cummins and eight-speed TorqueFlite HD: a 2026 bulletin lists P0827 with P0826 and P085F and the MIL; the display shows N although P is engaged, the engine cannot be switched off and limp mode is possible. The fix was new transmission software. Saab reports the same state under P0826 (below 0.2 V for 30 s), GM under P0826.

P0828.en: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit High
P0828.desc: Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0828 means the shared circuit voltage is too high – a short to positive, or on ground-switching switches with a pull-up also an open. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: Saab's 9-3 Sentronic reports this state as P0826 (above 6.7 V for more than 30 s), Saab's 9-4X as P0815 or P0816, and GM as P0826. Manual shifting would be disabled while automatic operation stays normal.

P0829.desc: Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. P0829 covers the change between 5th and 6th gear in either direction; J2012 placed it here because P0785 ff were already taken, between P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift' and P07DA/P07DB for 6-7 and 7-8. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code (speed must drop by more than 30 rpm on an upshift, flare above 300 rpm), Ford's automatics feed the solenoid function codes and GM the clutch valve codes. It exists only on transmissions with at least six gears; MIL and trip count follow the manufacturer.

P082A.en: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
P082A.desc: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. GM uses P082A–P082F on its electronic range selector (2019 tables, Cadillac XT4, 2025): a Hall sensor delivers a PWM signal, measured as duty cycle. P082A sets when the measured X position lies outside the lever's path (5.5 % duty cycle equals about 100 N of side force), the PWM signal has a frequency error, or X sensors 1 and 2 differ by more than 12 %; 3 of 4 samples in 2019, 10 of 12 in 2025 with an added angle check. Type B, MIL after two trips; the other sensor takes over.

P082B.en: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Low
P082B.desc: Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. Sensor 2 then takes over; if both fail, park is selected, as GM's patent describes.

P0830.desc: Clutch pedal switches A and B are digital inputs of manual gearboxes: they release the starter only with the pedal pressed, switch off cruise control and tell start-stop whether the clutch is open. Which switch is A or B is up to each manufacturer – FCA calls the pedal-up switch A. Ford's 2020–23 summary checks a dual switch over more than 40 pedal applications and reports a stuck switch without MIL (P0830 stuck high, P0833 stuck low, comparison P0704). P0830 is the general fault of switch A. On Ford it means the switch is stuck high. On a 2012–13 Jeep Wrangler with the six-speed manual, Chrysler reprogrammed the engine module for unwanted cruise control cut-outs with P0830; an FCA tip notes that a driver resting a foot on the pedal keeps the pedal-up switch on and sets the code. The MIL depends on the manufacturer.

P0831.en: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit Low
P0831.desc: Clutch pedal switches A and B are digital inputs of manual gearboxes: they release the starter only with the pedal pressed, switch off cruise control and tell start-stop whether the clutch is open. P0831 means switch A stays at ground or 0 V where a high level is expected – a short to ground, or an open supply on a positive-switching circuit. GM's 2006 Corvette and CTS-V with the LS2 and LS7 check it on manual gearboxes only, type C without MIL (400 of 500 samples of 100 ms; the table layout makes the sample count uncertain).

P0850.desc: The park/neutral input tells the engine control module whether the automatic is in P or N, or a manual gearbox in neutral. On GM's 6T70, as in the Saab 9-4X, the module sees P/N while the range switch reports a gear for 0.2 s above 10 km/h and 75 Nm, type C without MIL; it then uses the range switch for start release.

P0856.desc: The traction control input carries the request of the ABS/stability module to the engine module to cut torque when wheels spin. Older cars used a wire with a voltage or duty-cycle signal, hence the low and high variants; today it is a CAN message, where pure loss of communication sets U0121 or U0415 instead. P0863.desc: The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL. P0867.desc: P0867 to P0869 cover the system or line pressure of the gearbox as a whole: a pressure sensor measures it and the control module compares it with the pressure it commands. Faults of the sensor circuit itself have their own codes (Chrysler 68RFE P0932 ff), the single switches A to H have theirs (P0840 ff). Thresholds are not published; the codes are documented in bulletins for the Ram 68RFE and for the Tremec dual clutch of Corvette C8 and Maserati MC20. P0867 is the general pressure fault. GM's Corvette bulletin reads it as 'no system pressure': the pump delivers nothing or the fluid is almost gone, so valve cleaning is pointless and the gearbox needs a mechanical check. The car may lose drive completely.

P0870.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit
P0870.desc: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0870 is the general fault. Allison's 2006 table uses it for the switch on valve S3: if it reports pressure for more than 20 ms with the valve at rest, the valve is retried twice and the case classed as electrical, mechanical or sporadic, type A. Mitsubishi's Jatco CVT sets it when the high clutch switch stays on for 1.5 s while the clutch should be exhausted. On Ram's 68RFE it came with P0871 from mechanical damage.

causes_en: Pressure switch stuck closed or shorted internally
Signal wire shorted to ground inside the gearbox
Clutch circuit does not exhaust: dirt, sticking valve
Range sensor wrong (Allison comparison)
P0877.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
P0877.desc: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0877 means switch D reports pressure while its clutch is exhausted. GM checks the 1-2-3-4 clutch below 50 kPa commanded and sets it after 5 counts, without MIL. Allison 2007 uses it for the reverse switch reporting R in a forward or park range for over 1 s, type A with MIL; it then suspends the gear ratio checks.

causes_en: Signal wire or connector open (gearbox pass-through, harness)
Pressure switch does not close (diaphragm, seal)
Clutch pressure does not build: low fluid, leak, regulator valve
Gearbox module input
P0878.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit High
P0878.desc: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0878 means switch D reports no pressure although pressure is commanded. GM checks the 1-2-3-4 clutch above 700 kPa and sets it after 6 counts on the 6L80 or 8 on the 6T70, without MIL. Allison 2007 sets it when the reverse switch stays open in R or fails its check after engine stop, type A.

Dirt or sticking valve (dual clutch)

P0879.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch D Circuit Intermittent
P0879.desc: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. Like P0874 it is documented only for the Corvette C8 dual clutch in GM bulletin 21-NA-033, with MIL: clean the valves, relearn, then trace the circuit if the code returns. No thresholds are published.

causes_en: Gearbox module faulty internally (motor driver)
Water or corrosion at the gearbox module connector
Clutch B motor or its wiring faulty
Weak supply to the gearbox module
P087A.desc: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. Ford sets P087A for a fault in that internal driver; wiring faults of the motor have their own codes (P090A, P090C, P090D). Ford's warranty extension 19N07 covers replacing the gearbox module when it is the cause, which is common here. Clutch B can then no longer be controlled safely.

causes_en: Hall sensor in the clutch B motor faulty
Wiring or connector between motor and gearbox module
Input of the gearbox module faulty
Water ingress or corrosion
P087B.en: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P087B.desc: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. Ford sets P087B for a Hall sensor fault on the clutch B motor: one Hall signal is missing or implausible, so the module no longer knows the motor and clutch position reliably. The counterpart for clutch A is P0806. Judder, missed shifts and limp mode follow, with MIL.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
5 V supply to the sensor open
Sensor faulty
Module reference disturbed

P087C.desc: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. For P087C no maker is documented; Ford folds Hall faults into P087B. The code means the sensor signal is below its limit: signal wire shorted to ground, supply missing or a sensor without output. Signal wire shorted to voltage

P087D.en: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit High
P087D.desc: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. causes_en: Hall sensor in the clutch B motor dropping out
Loose contact at motor or module connector
Motor sluggish or slipping mechanically

P087E.en: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P087E.desc: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. Ford sets P087E for a sequence fault: when the clutch B motor turns, its three Hall sensors produce a fixed pattern; if a step is skipped or the order is wrong, motor and clutch position become unreliable. Typical are sporadic Hall dropouts and loose contacts. The counterpart for clutch A is P0809.

causes_en: Harness or connector between module and valve body damaged or corroded
TCU fuse or transmission relay faulty
Weak battery, charging fault, poor ground
Gearbox module faulty
P0880.desc: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0880 is the general fault. Hyundai's 2017–19 six-speed automatics set it when the solenoid supply drops below 7 V or rises above 22 V: MIL on, limp mode in 4th gear. Hyundai's bulletin points to the valve body harness and the TCU fuses and expressly not to the gearbox.

causes_en: Contact resistance in supply or ground, voltage drop under load
Alternator or battery problem
Relay with worn contacts
Internal measurement of the module faulty
P0881.desc: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0881 means the supply is electrically within range but implausible, for example differing from the engine module's system voltage or dipping when the solenoids switch on. No maker publishes a strategy for it.

causes_en: Weak battery or alternator not charging
Transmission relay, fuse or fuse box module faulty (Chrysler)
Corroded ground or supply wire, connector at the module
Module faulty
P0882.desc: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0882 means the supply is too low: Ford sets it below 9 V, continuously and with MIL. Chrysler's RFE, RLE and TE automatics test it when the key goes to run: if the module reads less than 3 V at the transmission control relay outputs while commanding the relay on, the code sets and the solenoids stay dead.

causes_en: Alternator voltage regulator faulty (overcharging)
Jump start with 24 V or charger in boost mode
Poor battery ground, regulator measures wrongly
Module measurement faulty
P0883.desc: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0883 means the supply is too high: Ford sets it above 16 V, continuously and with MIL; GM's counterpart P0563 sets at 18 V. Typical triggers are a failed alternator regulator or a jump start with 24 V. Overvoltage endangers the output stages, so the module may switch the solenoids off.

causes_en: Loose or unlatched connector at fuse box or module
Ignition switch or relay with contact dropouts
Battery terminal or ground loose
Internal module reset
P0884.desc: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0884 reports a brief loss of supply. Chrysler calls it 'power up at speed': the module notices on start-up that the vehicle is already moving, so it must have rebooted while driving. In field reports from NHTSA investigation PE07-027 on 2007 Jeeps it was stored after engine stalls, among others from an unlatched fuse box connector.

causes_en: Relay faulty (coil open) or missing
Wire between relay and module open, connector or fuse box contact
Fuse of the relay coil blown
Module software (FCA 948TE reflash)
P0885.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0885 means the coil circuit is open; the module checks its relay driver output at key-on. Ford lists it in its powertrain code list with or without MIL depending on vehicle; on FCA's 948TE nine-speed in the 2015 Cherokee and Chrysler 200 it was cured with a gearbox module reflash.

causes_en: Control wire chafed to ground
Relay coil shorted
Module driver faulty
P0886.en: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P0886.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0886 means the coil control line is shorted to ground or the driver reports a short, so the relay pulls in unintentionally or the driver shuts down. No maker documents the code; its neighbours P0885 and P0887 are documented by Ford and FCA.

P0887.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. Fuse in the load circuit

P0888.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0888 is the general fault of the sense line, without telling low, high or range apart. Moisture or corrosion in relay or socket
Ground or supply problem
P0889.en: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P0889.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0889 means the read-back voltage does not fit the switching state or the system voltage: clearly below battery voltage, a voltage drop across the contact or a delayed drop-out. No maker publishes a strategy.

causes_en: Filter change interval reached
Heavy contamination from clutch wear
Filter changed without resetting the monitor
Faulty main valve body (Allison serial range)
P088A.desc: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. Its filter life monitor judges the pressure drop across the filter circuit; in Allison's patent a differential pressure valve operates a switch with temperature-dependent time limits. P088A, called 'filter maintenance alert' by Allison, is the early warning: the wrench symbol flashes. A faulty main valve body in some 3000/4000 units triggered it early (field action 2019FA07). After a filter change the monitor is reset by a selector sequence.

causes_en: Filter change overdue
Monitor not reset after the change
Increased internal wear debris
Faulty main valve body (Allison)
P088B.desc: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. P088B is the second stage of the filter life monitor: the filter counts as heavily clogged or its change as overdue, and the CHECK TRANS lamp comes on. Isuzu names it the most common reason for that lamp on its Allison trucks, a maintenance item rather than a gearbox defect. Allison's patent allows limiting gearbox functions at this stage; the bulletins describe only the warning. Change the filter and reset the monitor.

causes_en: Wire between engine module and gearbox chafed to ground (tunnel, near exhaust)
Solenoid coil shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in the gearbox connector
Engine module driver faulty
P088C.desc: The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code. GM rates it type C without MIL; from 2019 a service message appears. P0801 is the open circuit. P088C means the control line is shorted to ground, so the solenoid is energised unintentionally or can no longer be switched off.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a supply wire in the harness
Solenoid coil low-resistance or shorted (driver overcurrent)
Moisture or corrosion between supply and control pin
Engine module driver faulty
P088D.desc: The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code. GM rates it type C without MIL; from 2019 a service message appears. P0801 is the open circuit. P088D means the control line is shorted to voltage: when the driver switches on it sees too high a level or overcurrent, and the solenoid can no longer be operated, so reverse may stay locked.

causes_en: Planet gears or pins seized or broken (lubrication, overheating)
Tooth damage on sun or ring gear
Speed sensor (engine, motor-generator, output) reading wrong
Low or worn fluid
P088E.desc: P088E means the module has found that a planetary gear set no longer keeps the fixed speed relation between its sun, carrier and ring gear, for example through broken planet gears, seized planet pins or stripped teeth. No maker's table or bulletin documents the code. It suits power-split hybrid transmissions, which measure speeds at several members: a Toyota patent compares the road speed calculated from engine, generator speed and planetary ratio with the measured one, flags a deviation of about 10 km/h for about 1 s and then drives electrically only. In stepped automatics such damage usually shows as ratio or slip codes.

causes_en: Relay contacts frozen or corroded (Subaru ignition relay)
Outdated engine module software (Subaru)
Fuse or wire between relay and gearbox module
Weak battery
P0890.en: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
P0890.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0890 means the relay delivers no voltage despite the command. Subaru documents it in four bulletins from 2022 to 2025 (Ascent, WRX, Impreza, Crosstrek, Forester): after a short trip below 0 °C condensation freezes the ignition relay contacts, the starter does not crank and P0700 often comes along. Engine module software cycles the contacts; the 2025 Forester also gets a vented relay.

Sense or output line shorted to voltage
Wrong relay fitted
P0891.en: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
P0891.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0891 means voltage is present at the relay output although the relay is off: a stuck or welded contact or a back-feed. The module then cannot switch the solenoids off for a safe emergency gear, and it may stay powered after key-off and drain the battery. No maker documents the code.

Relay with worn contacts
Wire broken by vibration
P0892.en: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
P0892.desc: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0885 to P0887 cover the coil control of that relay, P0888 to P0892 its sense line, which reads back the switched output and compares it with the command. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0892 reports a sense signal that drops out now and then, from a loose contact in relay, socket or wiring. Brief supply interruptions can reboot the module (compare P0884) and cause shift shocks. No maker publishes a strategy.

causes_en: Gearbox module software or calibration
Shift or pressure valve sticking (dirt), control valve body faulty
Clutch plates stuck or welded
Speed sensor false signal
P0893.desc: P0893 means more shift elements are applied than the commanded gear allows, so the gearbox binds up. It is detected through speeds, when the ratio matches no valid gear and input speed collapses, or through commanded clutch capacities: a GM patent flags capacities above their limits for longer than roughly 200 to 500 ms and reacts by downshifting or falling back to the hydraulic limp mode. Nissan's 2020–22 Frontier and Titan nine-speed set it with all ratio codes and MIL; Land Rover cured P0893 on the ZF 9HP48 Evoque with gearbox software.

causes_en: Low, wrong or worn fluid
Converter clutch PWM solenoid cracked or regulator bore worn (GM 4L60-E)
Worn clutch plates or converter clutch lining
Pump not priming, cracked suction filter (Allison)
Control module software
P0894.desc: P0894 reports slip of a gearbox component, found by comparing speeds. GM's 4L60-E applies it to the torque converter clutch: with lock-up commanded, slip between 100 and 550 rpm for 12.75 s on the third attempt in 4th gear sets it, type B with MIL after two trips; the module first freezes adaptation and raises line pressure. Lexus (Aisin AB60F) and Allison 1000 use it for a slipping shift element or low pressure and name the fluid level first. On the 4L60-E a cracked converter clutch PWM solenoid is a known cause.

causes_en: Pressure control valve stuck towards high pressure or line pressure too high
Shift adaptation faulty or reset, wrong software
Valve body: sticking spool, faulty damper or accumulator
Wrong fluid or level
P0895.desc: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. Gearbox modules adapt fill time and pressure to keep it in a calibrated window; the code sets when adaptation is at its limit and the time is still outside. No maker could be found using these generic codes; Saab's 1994 900 automatic monitored the same with its own code P1832, a window of 0.3 to 1.3 s and a limp program. P0895 means the shift completes faster than the window: clutch pressure too high or applied too early, giving a harsh shift.

causes_en: Low or worn fluid, low pressure (pump, filter)
Worn clutch plates or band
Pressure or shift valve sticking, leaking piston seals
Lost or reset adaptation, software
P0896.desc: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. Gearbox modules adapt fill time and pressure to keep it in a calibrated window; the code sets when adaptation is at its limit and the time is still outside. No maker could be found using these generic codes; Saab's 1994 900 automatic monitored the same with its own code P1832, a window of 0.3 to 1.3 s and a limp program. P0896 means the transition takes longer than the window: the engine flares between gears from low pressure or worn plates. Long shifts heat the clutches, so a fixed gear is a common reaction.

causes_en: Fluid change interval exceeded
Fluid changed without resetting the oil life monitor
Heavy duty (heat, stop-and-go, retarder) shortens calculated life
Prognostics disabled afterwards (Allison special case)
P0897.desc: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. Its oil life monitor counts down the remaining fluid life from operating hours, distance, shifts and load factors such as fluid temperature, open converter and retarder use. With little life remaining, TRANS SERVICE shows for two minutes after every start; if the change and reset do not follow within a set period, CHECK TRANS lights and P0897 becomes active. Correct calculation assumes approved fluid (TES 295/668).

Engine or gearbox module connector corroded
Gearbox module output faulty
P0898.en: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Low
P0898.desc: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866. P0898 means the request wire stays at ground: a short to ground or, with active-high logic, a gearbox module without power. The engine module can then not tell a real request from a wiring fault. No maker documents the code; Subaru's P0865 is the closest documented equivalent.

causes_en: Wire open (pull-up in the engine module)
Short to voltage
Gearbox module without power or ground
Gearbox module faulty
P0899.en: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit High
P0899.desc: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866. P0899 means the request wire stays high: an open line held up by the engine module's pull-up, a short to voltage or, with active-low logic, a gearbox module without power. No maker documents the code; Subaru's equivalent is P0866, set after more than 3 s high with MIL after two trips.

Spilled liquid in the centre console
P089A.en: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089A.desc: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089A, the general circuit fault of X sensor 2, is used by no maker found; GM reports circuit faults through duty-cycle low or high and frequency errors under P089B.

P089B.desc: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089E, for jumping or briefly dropping X sensor 2 signals, is used by no maker found; GM catches signal disturbances through the frequency error under P089B. The counterpart for sensor 1, P0823, is unused as well.

causes_en: Wire or connector at the selector module open
Sensor 2 faulty
Corrosion from liquid in the console
P089F.en: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089F.desc: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089F, the general circuit fault of Y sensor 2, is used by no maker found; GM reports that sensor under P08A0 to P08A2. In GM's patent a sensor counts as invalid as a whole once its X or Y value fails.

causes_en: Sensor 2 in the selector assembly drifting or faulty
Selector mechanism worn, bent or binding, lever leaves its nominal path
Loose contact or interference on the PWM signal line
Spilled liquid in the centre console
P08A0.en: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P08A0.desc: Sensor 2 is the redundant second Hall sensor that reports the Y-axis travel of an electronic selector lever as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses it in its electronic range selection (ECM and ICCM tables 2019–2025, Cadillac XT4 among them). P08A0 is set when sensor 2 reports a lever path outside the shifter gate (tolerance 5.5 %, ICCM 6–11 % of duty cycle), its frequency check fails, or it disagrees with Y sensor 1 by more than 12 %. Debounce is 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms (2025: 10 of 12). Type B, MIL after two trips. Low/High of the same sensor are P08A1/P08A2. GM's patent lets the other sensor carry on; only when both are invalid may the module ask for park.

causes_en: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor supply open or connector backed out
Sensor 2 in the selector assembly without output
Connector corrosion from liquid in the console
P08A1.en: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P08A1.desc: The selector lever's Y-axis sensor 2 is one of two redundant Hall sensors that send the lever travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM documents P08A1 for its electronic range selection: the code sets when the measured duty cycle of Y sensor 2 drops below 17 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or below 5 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025), checked 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms or 10 of 12 in later years. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a dead sensor output. Type B, MIL after two trips. Unlike P08A0 this is a pure signal limit, not a plausibility check; high is P08A2. Sensor 1 keeps the selector working.

causes_en: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Sensor ground open or high resistance
Internal fault of sensor 2 in the selector assembly
P08A2.en: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit High
P08A2.desc: Y sensor 2 is the backup Hall sensor of an electronic selector lever and reports the lever's Y-axis travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses P08A2 in its electronic range selection and sets it when the duty cycle of Y sensor 2 rises above 88 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or above 95 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025); 3 failures in 4 samples at 25 ms, in later calibrations 10 of 12. A signal line shorted to voltage, an open ground or an internal sensor fault are the usual reasons. Type B, MIL after two trips. Range/performance and low are P08A0 and P08A1; sensor 1 of the same axis reports via P082D to P082F. With one sensor still valid, the lever stays usable.

causes_en: Loose or fretting contact at the selector connector
Harness chafed by console or lever movement
Sensor 2 with intermittent internal fault
P08A3.en: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08A3.desc: This code covers short dropouts or jumps in the signal of the second, redundant Y-axis sensor of an electronic selector lever. No manufacturer documents P08A3 publicly. GM, the only proven user of this sensor family, uses only range/performance, low and high (P08A0 to P08A2) in all OBD tables from 2016 to 2025 and catches an unsteady PWM signal through the frequency check inside P08A0. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires input components to be monitored for circuit faults and plausibility. GM's patent on two redundant lever sensors explains why a second sensor exists: if one becomes invalid, the other keeps range selection alive. Expect loose contacts in the console harness; the MIL status depends on the maker.

causes_en: One of the two X sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path
P08A4.en: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A4.desc: An electronic selector lever with redundant sensing measures the X axis with two sensors. P08A4 means the two X readings no longer agree although each may be within its own limits. No manufacturer documents P08A4 publicly. GM, which runs dual PWM lever sensors, folds this comparison into the range/performance codes: P089B sets when X sensor 2 differs from sensor 1 by more than 12 % duty cycle. GM patents describe the principle: each sensor is checked against the gate and against its partner, and on disagreement the module trusts the more robust signal or commands neutral or park. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) demands such plausibility monitoring. Y-axis counterpart is P08A5, the whole system P08A6.

causes_en: One of the two Y sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path
P08A5.en: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A5.desc: P08A5 is the Y-axis twin of P08A4: the two redundant sensors that measure the selector lever's Y travel disagree beyond a calibrated limit. No manufacturer documents P08A5 publicly. In GM's electronic range selection the same check exists but is reported as range/performance: P08A0 sets when Y sensor 2 and Y sensor 1 differ by more than 12 % duty cycle, Type B. GM's patents show why redundancy matters: a disagreeing pair is resolved by trusting the more fault-tolerant signal, and if that is not possible the module selects neutral or park. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires such rationality checks for inputs. For the driver this means a refused or held range; repairs usually replace the selector assembly.

causes_en: Tyre size changed without relearning the top-gear ratio (FCA manual)
Control module software needing an update
Modified transfer case gearing, fault only in 4Low
Internal fault or connector problem of the electronic shift module
P08A6.en: Gear Lever Position Sensor System - Multiple Sensor Correlation
P08A6.desc: Here the module compares the combined gear lever position information with other evidence and finds no consistent picture. Two makers document it. FCA/Stellantis sets P08A6 in the PCM of 6-speed manual Jeeps such as the Wrangler JL as the all-gear-sensor check: the sensed gear is compared with a learned top-gear engine-to-road-speed ratio, so larger tyres trigger it until that ratio is relearned in sixth at 40–80 mph; a 4Low issue and software updates are also known, with MIL. Maserati's electronic shift module stores P08A6-64 for signal plausibility, leaving no gear selectable. Unlike P08A4/P08A5 it concerns the whole sensor system, not one sensor pair.

causes_en: Loose connector or broken wire at the pedal sensor (pedal box wiring flexes with every clutch stroke)
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor A
Missing 5 V reference or sensor ground
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module
P08A7.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P08A7.desc: Sensor A is the analog or PWM sensor that reports how far the clutch pedal of a manual car is pressed; the engine controller needs it for start-stop, cruise control, gear detection and starter release. P08A7 is the general circuit or open-wire fault of that sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: GM folds an open circuit into its low-signal code P08A9, and Ford lists only P08A9/P08AA for sensor A. Saab's 2012 9-3 used the older P0806 as a comparable circuit fault (Check Engine, cruise control off). Range/performance, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes P08A8–P08AB. Expect a warning lamp and disabled start-stop or cruise control until the wiring or sensor is repaired.

causes_en: Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket, so its reading no longer matches pedal travel
Worn or drifting sensor track giving an offset signal
Driver resting a foot on the clutch pedal, or a floor mat holding it down
Corroded connector adding resistance to signal or ground
P08A8.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P08A8.desc: P08A8 flags a clutch pedal sensor whose signal is electrically valid but contradicts how the car is actually driving. GM uses it on manual cars since model year 2018 (before: P0806), e.g. the LV7 1.4 L engine and the 2019 Corvette ZR1 (LT5): when engine speed to output shaft speed shows that a gear is engaged and transmitting torque, but the pedal reads as pressed, the filtered position error must stay below 4 %. Enabled above 4.3 mph (LT5: 5.6 mph), not in 4WD low, torque above a table, no circuit, crank or speed sensor faults; Type A, MIL after one trip. Circuit faults are P08A9/P08AA. Typical result: start-stop and cruise control off, and the engine computer may misjudge clutch state.

causes_en: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground in the pedal area
Open signal wire or missing 5 V reference (connector off, broken wire)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Shared 5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same circuit
P08A9.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P08A9.desc: The sensor is designed with dead bands at both ends, so a signal near 0 V can only come from a fault. GM sets P08A9 when the signal stays below 4 % of the 5 V reference (low voltage or open circuit) for 400 of 500 samples taken every 12.5 ms, with the engine not cranking and system voltage above 9 V (10 V in some 2018 tables); Type A, MIL after one trip. GM used P0807 for this before 2018 and lists P08A9 for the LV7, the 2019 Corvette ZR1 and its 2018 OBDG04 engines. Ford's 2020–23 gasoline summary uses P08A9 for cars with dual PWM pedal sensors or a single analog sensor plus switches, detected in under a second. The high-side counterpart is P08AA; sensor B low is P08B6.

causes_en: Open sensor ground wire or corroded ground pin
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module
P08AA.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P08AA.desc: P08AA is the mirror image of P08A9: the pedal sensor signal climbs into the upper dead band that a healthy sensor never reaches. GM's threshold is above 96 % of the 5 V reference for 400 of 500 samples at 12.5 ms, engine not cranking, system voltage above 9 V; Type A, MIL after one trip. It replaced GM's pre-2018 P0808 and appears in the LV7, 2019 Corvette ZR1 and 2018 OBDG04 tables. Ford's 2020–23 gasoline summary lists P08AA for both its dual PWM and single analog clutch pedal sensor layouts, flagged in under a second. A lost sensor ground or a signal shorted to the reference are the usual triggers. Sensor B high is P08B7; the driver mostly loses start-stop and cruise control.

causes_en: Loose or worn terminals in the pedal sensor connector
Wire breaking inside its insulation where the harness flexes with the pedal
Worn sensor track causing signal dropouts at certain pedal positions
Moisture or corrosion in the footwell connector
P08AB.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08AB.desc: P08AB is meant for a clutch pedal sensor A signal that jumps, drops out briefly or changes faster than a foot could move the pedal, without staying out of range long enough for the low or high codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's published tables for the same sensor use only P08A8, P08A9, P08AA and P08AC, and its low/high checks need 400 of 500 bad samples, so short dropouts would go unnoticed there; Ford names only low, high and A/B correlation. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility. In practice the cause is usually a loose connector or a wire that breaks inside its insulation as the pedal moves. Start-stop and cruise control may cut out intermittently.

causes_en: Relearn not performed after replacing the sensor, clutch parts or engine control module
Learned position drifted out of the allowed window (worn clutch, wrong pedal stop, air in hydraulics)
Learn procedure aborted, for example by low battery voltage
Faulty or misaligned clutch pedal sensor preventing a valid learn
P08AC.desc: The engine controller has to know at which pedal position the clutch is fully released or disengaged. GM teaches the fully applied position at the factory and then adapts it over time to clutch wear. P08AC is set when this learned value falls outside a window (LV7 1.4 L: 7–33 %, 2019 Corvette ZR1: 9–36 % of travel) or when the manufacturer's enable counter shows the learn was never completed; 250 ms loop, Type A, MIL after one trip. Before 2018 GM used P080A. After replacing the sensor, pedal parts, clutch or ECM, a relearn with a scan tool is needed; FCA, for example, issued a Renegade bulletin calling for a clutch pedal sensor learn. Circuit faults (P08A9/P08AA) must be cleared first.

causes_en: Wire to the sensor broken or stretched by shift shaft movement
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
Sensor B open internally
P08AD.desc: A neutral position sensor tells the engine module whether a manual gearbox is in neutral, which start-stop, remote start and rev matching rely on. Sensor B is a second sensor or channel next to sensor A (P086A ff). P08AD flags an open or otherwise faulty sensor B circuit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi (sender G701) and GM (Corvette LT5) are only known to use the A codes. A GM patent shows why a B channel exists: two Hall sensors on the shift shaft give a PWM signal, and in neutral both must read the same. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring of such inputs. Expected effect: start-stop stays off; MIL status depends on the maker.

causes_en: Sensor B or its magnet misaligned after gearbox work
Sensor B drifting or faulty
Worn shift shaft or detent giving an unclear neutral position
P08AE.en: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08AE.desc: Sensor B is the second neutral sensor or channel on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox, complementing sensor A (P086A ff). P08AE means its signal is electrically present but implausible: it stays outside the expected window, does not change when gears are engaged, or reports neutral while the gear ratio says otherwise. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi's G701 and GM's LT5 Corvette are only known to use the A codes. Per a GM patent the neutral sensor is a Hall sensor pair with a PWM output that changes with every gear, so such a plausibility check is possible. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires rationality monitoring of inputs. Start-stop is usually disabled; repair often means adjusting or replacing the sensor.

causes_en: Signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Sensor supply open
Sensor B without output
Water or corrosion in the connector at the gearbox
P08AF.en: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08AF.desc: The signal of neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel of a manual gearbox, has fallen below its lower electrical limit. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a sensor without output. No manufacturer documents P08AF publicly; the A-sensor codes are documented by Audi (sender G701, three-wire Hall sensor) and by GM on the LT5 Corvette. A GM patent describes the sensor as two Hall elements on the shift shaft feeding a PWM signal to the engine module. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires low/high circuit monitoring of such inputs. High is P08B0, the A-sensor equivalent P086C. Start-stop is usually blocked; the MIL status is left to the manufacturer.

causes_en: Signal or ground wire pulled apart, harness too short
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Sensor B open internally
P08B0.en: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B0.desc: P08B0 reports that the signal of neutral position sensor B on a manual gearbox is above its upper electrical limit. With a three-wire Hall sensor this usually points to an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage. No manufacturer documents P08B0 publicly. For the A sensor Audi does: the 2019–20 Q3 and 2022–23 A3 store P086D/P086E because the wires to sender G701 were too short and were pulled apart by shifting, fixed by lengthening them 20 mm; the same harness logic applies to a B sensor. A GM patent explains the dual-Hall neutral sensor with PWM output. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring. Low is P08AF; start-stop is typically off.

causes_en: Wire strained or partly broken by gearbox movement
Loose or fretting connector contact
Sensor B with intermittent internal fault
P08B1.en: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B1.desc: Neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel on a manual gearbox's shift shaft, delivers a signal that drops out or jumps for short moments. No manufacturer documents P08B1 publicly. The closest documented case is on the A sensor: Audi's bulletin for the 2019–20 Q3 and 2022–23 A3 traces P086D/P086E to wires to sender G701 that were too short, so every gear change strained them; lengthening by 20 mm cures it. A Dura patent notes that a neutral signal must persist for a minimum time before start-stop may stop the engine, so a flickering sensor blocks the function. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring. Steady faults appear as P08AD, P08AF or P08B0.

causes_en: One of the two neutral sensors drifting or faulty
Magnet on the shift shaft shifted or sensor misaligned after repair
Neutral position not relearned after component replacement
P08B2.desc: On a manual gearbox with two neutral sensors or two channels, the engine module compares A and B. P08B2 means they disagree: one reports neutral, the other a gear, or their values differ beyond a calibrated limit, while each may look fine electrically. No manufacturer documents P08B2 publicly. A GM patent describes exactly this layout: two Hall sensors with their own magnets on the shift shaft, whose PWM outputs must be identical in neutral as an integrity check. Audi's G701 and GM's LT5 Corvette use only the A codes. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires rationality monitoring of inputs. Because neutral cannot be confirmed, start-stop and remote start stay off; usual fix is aligning or replacing the sensor.

causes_en: Learn procedure not done after sensor, gearbox or module replacement
Learn run aborted, lever unsteady or linkage misadjusted
Learned values erased by software update or module reset
Sensor mounted outside the learnable range or faulty
P08B3.en: Neutral Position Sensor B Not Learned
P08B3.desc: Analog neutral sensors report a position value, and the control module must learn which value means neutral to cover part and fitting tolerances. P08B3 says no valid learned value exists for sensor B, typically after replacing the sensor, gearbox or module, after a software update, or after an aborted learn. No manufacturer documents P08B3 publicly; the A counterpart P086F is used by GM on the LT5 Corvette. A Schaeffler patent describes the learn: the driver engages neutral and the gears, and a run is rejected if the reading wanders too much in its roughly one-second window. FCA notes a neutral sensor learn procedure after service that restores cruise control. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) applies. Fix is usually a relearn by scan tool.

causes_en: Loose connector or broken wire on the sensor B channel
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor B (often a shared housing with sensor A)
Missing supply or ground for sensor B
Faulty sensor B input in the engine control module
P08B4.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P08B4.desc: Some manual cars read the clutch pedal with two independent sensors so a single failure can be detected; Ford's 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary describes such a dual PWM layout. Sensor B is the second channel. P08B4 is the general circuit or open-wire fault of that second sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: Ford uses only P08B6/P08B7 for sensor B plus P08B9 for the A/B comparison, and GM's tables cover sensor A alone. The code therefore rests on CARB's requirement to monitor such inputs for circuit faults. Sensor A's counterpart is P08A7. As long as sensor A is healthy the controller can usually still judge the pedal, but start-stop is often locked out until the fault is fixed.

causes_en: Sensor B drifting or worn so its value no longer follows pedal travel
Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket
Corrosion adding resistance in the sensor B circuit
P08B5.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08B5.desc: P08B5 covers a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal lies within its electrical limits but is implausible on its own, for example stuck at one value while the pedal moves or not matching the driving state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's dual PWM pedal sensor layout files any disagreement between the two channels under P08B9 rather than a B-only plausibility code, and GM applies the comparable in-gear plausibility check only to sensor A (P08A8: error above 4 % while a gear is engaged). CARB requires plausibility monitoring for inputs used by other diagnostics. If a manufacturer uses it, expect start-stop to be disabled; the clutch itself keeps working because it is hydraulically operated.

causes_en: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Lost supply voltage to sensor B (open wire, connector off)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B
P08B6.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08B6.desc: P08B6 means the signal of the second clutch pedal sensor has dropped below its valid range. Ford lists it in the 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary under dual PWM clutch sensors, together with P08A9/P08AA for sensor A, P08B7 for sensor B high and P08B9 for the A/B comparison; monitoring runs continuously and needs less than one second to flag a fault. Ford does not mark the code as non-MIL, unlike its clutch switch codes. For a PWM sensor, low usually means the output is stuck at ground (no pulses or 0 % duty cycle), caused by a short to ground, a lost supply or a dead sensor. GM's published tables have no sensor B. The driver mainly notices a warning lamp and missing start-stop.

causes_en: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B, leaving the input at its pull-up level
Sensor B signal shorted to a voltage source
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B
P08B7.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B7.desc: P08B7 is set when the second clutch pedal sensor reports a value above its valid range. Ford uses it on vehicles with two PWM clutch pedal sensors, as listed in its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary next to P08B6 (sensor B low), P08A9/P08AA (sensor A) and P08B9 (A/B correlation); the check is continuous and decides within one second. The clutch switch codes on the same page are marked non-MIL, the sensor codes are not. With a PWM output, high typically means the line is held at its pull-up level (100 % duty cycle), which points to an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage. GM's published tables cover sensor A only. Effect for the driver: warning lamp, start-stop locked out.

causes_en: Loose or worn terminals in the sensor B connector
Wire fatiguing where the harness flexes with pedal movement
Sensor B producing glitches internally
P08B8.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B8.desc: P08B8 is intended for a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal drops out briefly or jumps without staying out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford, the only maker found to publish sensor B codes, lists just low (P08B6), high (P08B7) and the A/B comparison (P08B9) for its dual PWM pedal sensors, so short glitches there would most likely surface as a correlation fault; GM covers sensor A only. CARB requires circuit and plausibility monitoring of such inputs. Likely culprits are worn connector terminals or a wire fatiguing where the harness moves with the pedal. Sensor A's counterpart is P08AB. Drivers may see start-stop drop out now and then.

causes_en: One of the two sensors drifting or worn so the channels no longer agree
Sticking or misadjusted clutch switch on systems with one sensor plus switches
Corroded connector or wiring adding resistance to one channel
Sensor assembly or pedal stop misaligned after repairs
P08B9.en: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P08B9.desc: P08B9 is stored when two independent measurements of the clutch pedal disagree. Ford uses it in two ways per its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary: with dual PWM sensors it compares sensor A with sensor B and decides within a second; with a single analog sensor plus two clutch switches it covers an in-range rationality fault or any switch-related mismatch, the switch part being judged over about 40 clutch cycles at different speeds. FCA patented a similar cross-check of the pedal sensor against the clutch interlock switch, which disables electronic stop-start on a mismatch and cannot always tell which part failed. Circuit faults of each sensor have their own codes (P08A9/P08AA, P08B6/P08B7).

causes_en: Solenoid or its control valve sticking inside the valve body
Internal transmission fault from production, debris spreading through the hydraulics
Contaminated or wrong transmission fluid
Connector or harness fault at the solenoid
P08BA.desc: Base code for the twelfth pressure control solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve carries the letter L is up to the manufacturer. Toyota is the one documented user: bulletin T-SB-0094-24 for the 2024 Tacoma and Tacoma Hybrid lists it as P08BA71, actuator stuck, next to the stuck faults of solenoids A, C, D, G and H and a torque converter clutch stuck off. Because Toyota reports the fault type through the suffix, the stuck valve sits under this base code rather than under P08BB/P08BC. The MIL comes on. For trucks built before the production change Toyota's fix is a new transmission with torque converter, on the hybrid also the hybrid module. GM's Corvette dual clutch tables contain no L code.

causes_en: Valve spool held closed by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Leaking seal or circuit downstream of the valve
P08BB.en: Pressure Control Solenoid L Performance/Stuck Off
P08BB.desc: Set when pressure control solenoid L is commanded but the pressure or shift element it serves does not respond, i.e. the valve acts as if it were stuck in its off state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Toyota, the only known user of letter L, reports a stuck valve as P08BA with suffix 71 instead. The closest documented analogue is GM's P08C4 for solenoid M on the Corvette dual clutch, where an intrusive routine moves the shift rods slightly and flags the valve when the expected rod travel stays below 100 µm. CARB requires such functional checks for transmission solenoids. P08BC is the opposite fault, P08BF to P08C2 cover the circuit. The driver notices missing or harsh shifts.

causes_en: Valve spool held open by debris
Worn bore in the valve body letting pressure through
Output stage or wiring keeping the solenoid energised
P08BC.en: Pressure Control Solenoid L Stuck On
P08BC.desc: Set when pressure control solenoid L keeps applying pressure although the control module has commanded it off, so the element it feeds stays loaded. No manufacturer publishes this code. Toyota, the only documented user of letter L, files a stuck valve under P08BA71 instead. GM's P08C5 for solenoid M of the Corvette dual clutch shows how such a check can work: after a selector valve change the module watches the shift rods, and unexpected movement of one rod or relaxation of another within 200 ms points to a valve that keeps pressure on. CARB lists transmission solenoids as monitored output components. P08BB is the stuck off counterpart. For the driver this means shift shock, binding or a fallback gear.

causes_en: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Corroded connector or damaged internal harness
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module
P08BD.desc: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid L that the module does not break down further into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly; Toyota, the one known user of letter L, has only published the stuck fault P08BA71. Manufacturers that diagnose their solenoids in detail use the specific circuit codes instead, as GM does for solenoid M with P08C8, P08CA and P08CB, each fed by the diagnostic status of the output driver chip. CARB requires a circuit continuity check for every monitored transmission solenoid. The usual culprits are coil, connector or the internal harness; the driver sees the warning light and, depending on the valve, a restricted gear range.

causes_en: Loose or spread terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector
Chafed wire touching ground intermittently
Debris making the valve hang only now and then
P08BE.desc: Reports a fault of pressure control solenoid L that comes and goes, typically a circuit that drops out briefly or a valve response that is only occasionally implausible. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and in earlier packages the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids also proved unused. Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, publishes only P08BA71. GM's circuit tests for the comparable solenoid M confirm a fault only after it persists for 150 ms, which is why brief dropouts tend to surface as a stored circuit code instead. CARB requires transmission solenoids to be monitored. Loose pins and chafed wires are the likely causes; symptoms are occasional shift flare or a short-lived fallback mode.

causes_en: Connector loose, unplugged or corroded
Broken wire in the internal or external harness
Solenoid coil burnt open
P08BF.en: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit/Open
P08BF.desc: Points to an open control circuit of pressure control solenoid L: the module sees no load where the coil should be. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only known user of letter L, has published just P08BA71. GM's open-load test for the analogous solenoid M (P08C8) shows the method: with the low-side driver switched off, the coil should pull the sense pin up to battery voltage; if the driver chip can hold it between roughly 1.7 and 3 V with a tiny current, the circuit is open. Confirmation takes 150 ms. P08C1 and P08C2 are the short to ground and short to power. Typical results are a fallback gear and the warning light.

causes_en: Coil resistance out of specification
High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module
P08C0.en: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08C0.desc: Set when the control circuit of pressure control solenoid L is electrically intact but its behaviour is implausible, for example the current through the coil does not match the commanded value. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only documented user of letter L, publishes only P08BA71. As an orientation, GM's tables for the comparable solenoid M list a current check next to the circuit tests: a deviation of more than 70 % for 60 ms or more than 400 mA for 300 ms between target and estimated current, without naming P08C9 for it. Causes are a coil with changed resistance, contact resistance or supply problems. P08BF, P08C1 and P08C2 cover clear open or short faults.

causes_en: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
Fluid or moisture in the connector
P08C1.en: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit Low
P08C1.desc: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too low, usually a short to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71. GM's equivalent for solenoid M (P08CA) illustrates the check: while the low-side driver is switched on, the sense pin is examined and a value below about 1.7 V is read as a short to ground, confirmed after 150 ms with battery voltage between 8.75 and 18 V. Depending on the wiring, a ground short can energise the valve permanently or make it uncontrollable. P08C2 is the high counterpart, P08BF the open circuit. Expect a fallback gear and the warning light.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short between adjacent solenoid wires in the internal harness
Defective output stage in the transmission control module
P08C2.en: Pressure Control Solenoid L Control Circuit High
P08C2.desc: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too high, typically a short to battery voltage or to a neighbouring output. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71. GM's equivalent for solenoid M (P08CB) uses two tests: with the low-side driver on, a sense voltage above 0.7 to 1.1 V, depending on supply voltage, means a short to power; at shutdown each output is also switched on in turn to detect a short to a neighbouring output, which is then stored and reported at the next start. A shorted valve usually cannot be switched off. P08C1 is the low counterpart, P08BF the open circuit.

causes_en: Valve sticking from debris in the valve body
Fault in the solenoid wiring or connector
Worn or failed solenoid
P08C3.desc: Base code for the thirteenth pressure control solenoid; the letter is assigned by the manufacturer. GM uses letter M in the Tremec eight-speed dual clutch of the Corvette (RPO M1L/M1M): its 2023–2025 TCM tables name the part synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft, while valves 2 to 5 report under P27B9 onwards.
