GM does not set this base code but the specific ones: P08C4 and P08C5 for hydraulic sticking, P08C8, P08CA and P08CB for the circuit. No other manufacturer documents P08C3 publicly. If it appears, the module has seen a non-specific fault of this valve; the driver typically notices the warning light and rough or missing gear changes on that shaft.

causes_en: Valve stuck closed by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Low system pressure or fluid level
P08C4.en: Pressure Control Solenoid M Performance/Stuck Off
P08C4.desc: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft, is hydraulically stuck off. The test runs inside a synchronizer recovery or integrity routine, started after a shift-related fault or when the stored gear does not match the sensed gears at start-up: the shift rods are moved slightly, and if a rod travels 100 µm or less where the valve should move it, a current profile check of the valve has to fail three times before the fault is confirmed. Type A, MIL at once. Bulletin 21-NA-033 blames debris; the fix is GDS valve cleaning three times, service clean and fast learn, and a new control valve body only if it returns.

causes_en: Valve held open by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Worn valve bore in the control valve body
P08C5.en: Pressure Control Solenoid M Stuck On
P08C5.desc: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, serving the odd-gear shaft, keeps pressure on although it is commanded off. The check runs whenever the selector pilot valve changes position: a valve stuck on keeps pushing a shift rod, so after the switch the pressure is routed elsewhere. If within 200 ms one rod moves unintentionally by 1000 µm or more while another relaxes by 125 µm or more, and both position sensors are electrically fine, the fault is set. Type A, monitored continuously. Bulletins 21-NA-033 and 23-NA-197 list it with the other valve codes; debris in the control valve body is the main cause. P08C4 is the stuck off counterpart.

causes_en: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Damaged connector or internal harness
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P08C6.desc: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid M without a finer split into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly. GM, the documented user of letter M on the Corvette dual clutch (synchronizer actuation valve 1), reports electrical faults only through the specific codes P08C8, P08CA and P08CB, which are derived from the diagnostic status of the low-side driver chip and confirmed after 150 ms. CARB requires a circuit check for every monitored transmission solenoid. A manufacturer setting P08C6 would point to coil, connector or harness of this valve; for the driver this means the warning light and restricted shifting on the affected shaft.

causes_en: Loose terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector
Chafed wire with intermittent contact
Debris causing occasional valve hang-ups
P08C7.desc: Reports an on-and-off fault of pressure control solenoid M, such as brief circuit dropouts or occasional implausible responses. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses letter M for synchronizer actuation valve 1 of the Corvette dual clutch, lists no intermittent code for it, and earlier packages found the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids unused as well. GM's circuit tests need a fault to last 150 ms, so short dropouts mostly end up as P08C8, P08CA or P08CB once they persist. CARB requires transmission solenoids to be monitored. Loose terminals and chafed wires are the likely causes; symptoms are sporadic shift faults and a warning light that comes and goes.

causes_en: Connector at the control valve body loose or corroded
Broken wire in the internal harness
Solenoid coil open
P08C8.en: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit/Open
P08C8.desc: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for an open circuit at synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft. The open-load test runs with the low-side driver switched off: an intact coil pulls the sense pin to battery voltage, so if the driver chip can hold it between about 1.7 and 3 V (each ±0.5 V) with a very small current, the circuit is considered open. The fault must persist for 150 ms with battery voltage between 8.75 and 18 V and the engine not cranking; it is suspended while P0882 or P0883 indicates a supply problem. Type A, MIL at once. Without this valve the odd shaft cannot be shifted reliably, so a fallback mode is likely.

causes_en: Coil resistance out of specification
High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module
P08C9.en: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08C9.desc: Meant for a control circuit of pressure control solenoid M that is not open or shorted but behaves implausibly, for instance a coil current that does not follow the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, which uses letter M for synchronizer actuation valve 1 of the Corvette dual clutch, publishes only open, low, high and the two hydraulic codes for it; its tables do describe a current check that compares target and estimated current (more than 70 % for 60 ms or more than 400 mA for 300 ms), but without naming P08C9. CARB requires monitoring of transmission solenoids. Possible causes are a coil with drifting resistance, contact resistance or supply voltage problems; shift quality may suffer.

causes_en: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
Fluid in the transmission connector
P08CA.en: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit Low
P08CA.desc: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for a short to ground in the circuit of synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft. The test runs while the low-side driver is switched on: the sense pin should then sit at a defined level, and if the driver chip reports it below about 1.7 V (±0.5 V), a ground short is assumed. Confirmation takes 150 ms at 8.75 to 18 V battery voltage with the engine not cranking, and the check is suspended when P0882 or P0883 is present. Type A, MIL at once, monitored continuously. Valves 2 to 5 have their own low codes (P27BF onwards). The driver should expect a fallback mode until the wiring fault is repaired.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short to an adjacent solenoid wire in the internal harness
Defective driver stage in the transmission control module
P08CB.en: Pressure Control Solenoid M Control Circuit High
P08CB.desc: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for synchronizer actuation valve 1 (odd-gear shaft) in two situations. First, a short to battery voltage: with the low-side driver on, a sense voltage above 0.7, 0.9 or 1.1 V (±0.1 V), depending on supply voltage, counts as a shorted load, confirmed after 150 ms. Second, a short to a neighbouring output: at shutdown every output is switched on in turn, a cross-reaction is stored in memory and the code is set at the next start. Type A, MIL at once. The check pauses while P0882 or P0883 is present. A valve shorted to power cannot be switched off, so the transmission will usually go into a fallback mode.

causes_en: Shift solenoid J faulty (coil or valve)
Contaminated or degraded transmission fluid restricting the valve
Connector or harness fault between TCM and solenoid
Transmission control module output fault
P08CC.desc: Base code for the tenth on/off shift solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve gets the letter J is decided by the manufacturer. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's gasoline OBD summary ends its shift solenoid list at SS E, the Genesis 8-speed bulletin stops at solenoid F, and GM and Toyota label their later valves as pressure control or clutch solenoids, so J stays unused in the known sources. CARB requires automatic transmission solenoids to be checked for functional response and circuit faults. A manufacturer reporting the fault type through a DTC suffix, as Toyota does for pressure control solenoid L, would store such faults under this base code instead of P08CD to P08D4. Expect harsh, missing or substitute-gear shifts.

causes_en: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the off position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Worn clutch pack or leaking seal in the circuit served by the valve
Solenoid coil too weak to move the valve
P08CD.desc: Set when shift solenoid J is switched on but the gear or clutch it controls does not respond, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest documented analogue is GM's P0751 on the 6-speed transmissions: the TCM commands first gear and flags shift solenoid A stuck off when slip reaches 400 rpm with the gear ratio out of window, a two-trip fault. Ford sets P0751 to P0771 when the obtained gear or shift pattern shows a solenoid functionally failed off after three solenoid events. CARB requires this kind of functional check. P08CE is the opposite fault, P08CF and P08D1 to P08D4 cover the circuit. The driver notices slipping, flare or a missing gear.

causes_en: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the applied position by debris or varnish
Contaminated transmission fluid after internal wear
Control circuit shorted so the solenoid stays energised
TCM output driver does not switch off
P08CE.desc: Set when shift solenoid J is switched off but its clutch or shift valve stays applied, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its on position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's P0752 on the 6-speed transmissions is the nearest documented counterpart: with third gear commanded, the TCM flags shift solenoid A stuck on when the gearbox slip reaches 400 rpm while first or second gear is actually obtained, and the MIL comes on after one trip. Ford sets its stuck-on codes P0752 to P0772 from the gear or shift pattern actually reached. CARB requires such functional monitoring. P08CD is the opposite fault. Because an applied clutch can tie up the gearbox, drivers may feel a wrong gear, a harsh engagement or limp mode.

causes_en: Solenoid coil open or shorted internally
Damaged harness, corroded or loose connector at the transmission
Fault in the internal transmission harness or solenoid body
TCM output driver fault
P08CF.desc: General electrical fault of shift solenoid J, used when a manufacturer does not split the circuit fault into open, low, high or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The analogue for solenoid A, P0753, is used by Hyundai for Genesis G80 and G90 8-speed transmissions as Shift Control Solenoid Valve A Electrical; bulletin 21-AT-016HG lists electrical codes for valves A to F and has the solenoid replaced after checking the harness, without any J valve. Ford's electrical check flags a solenoid when driver feedback disagrees with the commanded state for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires circuit monitoring when a functional check is not feasible. P08D1 to P08D4 are the detailed circuit codes. Shift quality usually drops at once.

causes_en: Loose or corroded connector losing contact under vibration or heat
Chafed harness with intermittent short or break
Valve sticking now and then due to contaminated fluid
Solenoid coil failing only when hot
P08D0.desc: Reserved for a shift solenoid J fault that comes and goes instead of being present continuously, typically brief circuit dropouts or erratic valve response. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the intermittent codes of the earlier shift solenoids, such as P0754 for solenoid A, are not used in the GM and Ford sources checked either; those makers report dropouts through their open, short or functional codes. Ford runs its solenoid electrical checks continuously with 0.5 to 5 second filters, so short interruptions are caught there. CARB requires circuit monitoring of transmission output components in general. P08CF and P08D1 to P08D4 are the permanent electrical faults. Drivers notice occasional harsh shifts or a passing warning light.

causes_en: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High resistance at connector pins or internal harness
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM or solenoid feed
Faulty current sensing in the TCM output stage
P08D1.en: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08D1.desc: Set when the control circuit of shift solenoid J is electrically intact but its measured values, usually solenoid current or driver feedback, lie outside the expected window for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The analogue for solenoid A, P0972, is likewise not used in the GM and Ford sources checked; Ford reports such current faults by its own electrical current check, which flags feedback current out of range for 0.5 seconds. CARB requires output circuits to be checked for faults beyond plain opens and shorts. P08D2 and P08D3 cover low and high circuit voltage, P08D4 an open circuit, P08CF a general electrical fault. Shift quality may suffer because the valve no longer moves as intended.

causes_en: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Solenoid coil with internal short
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Faulty output stage in the TCM
P08D2.en: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit Low
P08D2.desc: Set when the TCM sees too little voltage on the control line of shift solenoid J, typically because the line or the coil is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J would be a tenth on/off valve, which none of the known transmission sources assigns. GM's analogue for solenoid A, P0973 on the 6-speed units, fails when the output driver reports a ground short for 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and lights the MIL after one trip; Ford names the same fault on its solenoids a short to ground. CARB requires such circuit checks. P08D3 is the high-side fault, P08D4 the open circuit. The TCM usually switches the valve off and runs a substitute gear.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying conductor
Open solenoid coil (on systems that report opens as high)
Moisture in the transmission connector bridging pins
P08D3.en: Shift Solenoid J Control Circuit High
P08D3.desc: Logged when the control line of shift solenoid J reads higher than the commanded state allows, pointing to a short to battery voltage or, on some designs, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In GM's tables the high code for solenoid A, P0974, covers both an open circuit and a short to power, fails after 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and needs two trips for the MIL, while Ford keeps opens apart and uses its high code for shorts to power only. Which reading applies to J therefore depends on the maker. CARB requires the circuit check. P08D2 is the low-side counterpart, P08D4 the dedicated open-circuit code. A valve that cannot be driven correctly leads to wrong or missing gears.

causes_en: Broken control wire or loose terminal
Burnt-out solenoid coil
Transmission connector not fully seated after service
P08D4.desc: Dedicated code for an open control circuit of shift solenoid J: the TCM drives the valve but no current flows through wire, connector or coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The known analogues show why: Ford files an open circuit under the base code of each solenoid (P0750 for solenoid A) and GM includes it in the high-voltage code P0974, so neither needs a separate open code. Ford detects such electrical faults when driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires open and short checks on transmission outputs. P08D2 and P08D3 are the short-circuit codes. An unpowered valve rests in its default state, so a gear may be missing or locked.

causes_en: Shift solenoid K faulty (coil or valve)
Harness or connector fault between TCM and solenoid
Degraded or contaminated transmission fluid
TCM output fault
P08D5.desc: Base code for shift solenoid K, the eleventh on/off shift valve in SAE's lettering. Which valve carries the letter is up to the manufacturer, and none documents K publicly: Ford's gasoline OBD summary lists shift solenoids only up to SS E, Hyundai's bulletin 21-AT-016HG for the Genesis 8-speed ends at shift control solenoid F, and GM's 2016 to 2025 tables contain no code of the K group. Ford shows how a base code can be used: its P0750 stands for an open circuit of solenoid A. CARB requires functional and circuit monitoring of shift solenoids. P08D6 to P08DD split the fault into functional and circuit types. Expect harsh or missing shifts and possibly a fixed substitute gear.

causes_en: Valve or shift spool held in rest position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak line pressure
Leaking seal or worn clutch pack in the circuit fed by the valve
P08D6.desc: Indicates that shift solenoid K was commanded on but the gear or clutch behind it never engaged, as if the valve stayed in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A documented model is GM's P0751 for solenoid A on the 6-speed units: with first gear commanded, the TCM counts a fault when slip reaches 400 rpm and the measured ratio sits in a fixed window that points to the wrong gear, and it needs two trips to light the MIL. Ford infers a solenoid failed off from the obtained gear or shift pattern over three solenoid events. CARB requires this functional check. The reverse fault is P08D7. Typical signs are engine flare during shifts and a skipped gear.

causes_en: Valve or shift spool jammed in applied position
Metal debris in the fluid after internal wear
TCM output or shorted wire keeps the solenoid energised
P08D7.desc: Stored when shift solenoid K is switched off but the circuit it feeds stays pressurised, so a clutch remains applied. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's P0752 for solenoid A is the documented analogue: with third gear commanded, the TCM fails the valve when gearbox slip reaches 400 rpm while the transmission actually sits in first or second, and the MIL lights after a single trip. Ford flags stuck-on solenoids from the gear actually reached during its mechanical check. CARB demands this functional monitoring. P08D6 is the opposite fault, P08D8 and P08DA to P08DD the circuit faults. Drivers may notice a wrong starting gear, binding, harsh engagement or emergency mode.

causes_en: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Damaged harness or corroded connector
TCM output driver fault
P08D8.desc: Collective electrical fault for shift solenoid K, used by makers that do not split circuit faults into low, high, open or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The pattern exists for earlier letters: Hyundai stores P0753 (shift control solenoid valve A electrical) on the Genesis G80 and G90 8-speed and, per bulletin 21-AT-016HG, replaces the solenoid once the harness checks out, with valves listed only up to F. Ford's electrical check fails a solenoid when the driver feedback contradicts the command for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires circuit monitoring of transmission outputs. P08DA to P08DD are the detailed codes. The TCM usually reacts at once with altered shifting.

causes_en: Loose or fretted terminal in the transmission connector
Chafed wire that touches only under vibration
Solenoid coil dropping out at high fluid temperature
P08D9.desc: Meant for a shift solenoid K fault that appears and vanishes, such as a connector losing contact over bumps or a coil dropping out when hot. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the sources checked even uses the intermittent code of solenoid A, P0754; GM and Ford catch brief interruptions with their open, short and functional codes instead. Ford runs its electrical checks continuously with 0.5 to 5 second filters. CARB asks for circuit monitoring of output components without prescribing an intermittent code. Unlike the permanent fault P08D8, the symptoms here come and go: an occasional hard shift or a warning light that is gone after a restart.

causes_en: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Corroded or loose pins adding resistance
TCM output stage no longer delivers correct current
P08DA.en: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08DA.desc: Points to a control circuit of shift solenoid K that is neither open nor shorted, yet whose measured values, usually coil current, do not fit the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the analogue for solenoid A, P0972, is not used in the GM or Ford sources either. Ford covers the same failure with an electrical current check that trips when the feedback current stays out of range for 0.5 seconds. Causes are typically a coil with changed resistance, a high-resistance contact or a weak TCM driver. CARB requires output circuits to be checked beyond plain opens and shorts. P08DB, P08DC and P08DD cover low, high and open. The valve may switch late or incompletely.

causes_en: Control wire rubbed through to ground
Internally shorted solenoid coil
TCM output stage fault
P08DB.en: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit Low
P08DB.desc: The TCM's output stage reports a voltage on the shift solenoid K control circuit below what the commanded state requires, the classic sign of a control wire rubbing through to ground or a coil with an internal short. No manufacturer documents this K code publicly. For solenoid A, GM's 6-speed tables set P0973 when a ground short is flagged for 1.2 out of 1.5 seconds, with at least 9 V supply and the engine running, and light the MIL after one trip; Ford lists P0973 as short to ground. CARB mandates the check. P08DC is the opposite fault and P08DD the open circuit. Many TCMs then disable the valve, so expect a limp-home gear.

causes_en: Control wire touching a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high
TCM low-side driver no longer pulls the line down
P08DC.en: Shift Solenoid K Control Circuit High
P08DC.desc: The monitored control line of shift solenoid K sits closer to supply voltage than it should, for instance because it touches a powered wire or, depending on the driver design, because the coil is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM treats the solenoid A version, P0974, as open or power short and fails it after 1.2 of 1.5 seconds, but lights the MIL only after two trips. Ford's P0974 means a short to power only, because Ford reports opens separately. CARB requires this circuit check. P08DB is the low counterpart, P08DD the open-circuit code. A valve shorted to power may stay energised, giving a wrong gear or harsh engagements.

causes_en: Broken wire or pushed-out terminal
Failed internal transmission harness
Burnt-out solenoid coil
P08DD.desc: Signals that the control circuit of shift solenoid K is open, so commanding the valve produces no current: a broken wire, a pushed-out terminal, a burnt coil or a failed internal transmission harness. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford handles opens through the base code of each solenoid, P0750 for solenoid A, while GM's tables fold them into the circuit-high code P0974, so a separate open code like this one stays unused in both systems. CARB requires transmission outputs to be checked for opens. P08DB and P08DC are the short-circuit codes, P08D8 the general electrical fault. Without power the valve stays in its rest position, so one gear range drops out.

causes_en: Shift solenoid L faulty
Wiring or connector fault on the solenoid circuit
Debris in the valve body affecting the valve
P08DE.desc: Base code for shift solenoid L, which in SAE's lettering would be the twelfth on/off shift valve of an automatic transmission. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. It must not be confused with pressure control solenoid L, which Toyota uses on the 2024 Tacoma under its own code family. Ford's gasoline summary stops at shift solenoid E, Hyundai's Genesis 8-speed bulletin at F, and GM's 2016 to 2025 OBD tables show no L shift solenoid. For a maker using base codes, Ford's practice is the model: P0750 there means an open circuit. CARB requires shift solenoids to be monitored. The detailed fault types are P08DF to P08E6. Shift quality and gear availability may suffer.

causes_en: Shift spool jammed by debris
Low line pressure or low fluid level
Leak in the clutch circuit fed by the valve
P08DF.desc: Functional fault of shift solenoid L: the TCM switches the valve on, but speed sensor data show that the intended clutch did not take up, so the valve acts as if stuck off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The detection logic is known from the analogue for solenoid A: Ford compares the obtained gear or shift pattern over three solenoid events, and GM's P0751 counts repeated slip of at least 400 rpm in a ratio window that does not match first gear, with the MIL after two trips. Typical causes are a valve jammed by debris, low line pressure or a leaking clutch circuit rather than wiring. CARB requires the check. P08E0 is the stuck-on fault. Expect flare or a missing gear.

causes_en: Shift spool seized in applied position
Contaminated fluid after clutch or bearing wear
TCM output stage does not switch off
P08E0.desc: Functional fault of shift solenoid L in the opposite direction: although switched off, the valve keeps its circuit applied, leaving engaged a clutch that should be released. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. As a model, GM's P0752 for solenoid A sets after one trip when gearbox slip reaches 400 rpm with third gear commanded but first or second actually engaged, and Ford's mechanical check reads a stuck-on solenoid from the gear the transmission really obtains. CARB requires such functional checks. Electrical causes are rare here; a seized spool or an output stage that never switches off is more likely. P08DF is the stuck-off fault. Possible effects are tie-up, harsh shifts and limp mode.

causes_en: Solenoid L coil failed electrically
Harness or connector damage on the solenoid circuit
TCM output fault
P08E1.desc: General electrical malfunction of shift solenoid L, intended for transmissions whose TCM does not distinguish or separately report low, high and open circuit faults. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The equivalent electrical code is in real use for lower letters, for example P2709 for shift control solenoid valve F on the 2017 and 2018 Genesis G80 and G90 8-speed, where Hyundai's bulletin 21-AT-016HG calls for harness checks and solenoid replacement. Ford fails a solenoid electrically when the driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB requires the circuit check. P08E3 to P08E6 are the detailed codes, P08E2 the intermittent one.

causes_en: Loose terminal or poor pin tension in the connector
Insulation chafed at a bracket or edge
Coil that fails intermittently when hot
P08E2.desc: Reserved for an unstable fault of shift solenoid L that is detected, disappears and may return, typically from a loose terminal, a chafed wire that only touches under vibration or a heat-sensitive coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The intermittent codes of the lower letters, beginning with P0754 for solenoid A, are absent from the GM and Ford documents checked as well; those systems record short dropouts as ordinary circuit or functional faults, Ford with continuous checks filtered over 0.5 to 5 seconds. CARB asks for circuit monitoring in general. For diagnosis, freeze frame data and a wiggle test help more than a static resistance check. Symptoms appear only now and then.

causes_en: Coil resistance drifting with temperature
Corroded pins adding resistance
TCM output stage losing drive strength
P08E3.en: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit Range/Performance
P08E3.desc: Plausibility fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L: the circuit is not open or shorted, but voltage or current during actuation is implausible for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the matching code for solenoid A, P0972, is likewise absent from the GM and Ford documents checked. Ford's electrical current check, which flags feedback current out of range for 0.5 seconds, shows how such a test works. Practical causes are coil resistance drifting with temperature, corroded pins adding resistance or a TCM output stage losing drive strength. CARB requires output circuits to be checked beyond opens and shorts. P08E4 to P08E6 are the clear-cut circuit codes. Shifts may feel soft or delayed.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Coil with shorted windings
Fluid or moisture in the connector creating a path to ground
P08E4.en: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit Low
P08E4.desc: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L. Usually it means a short to ground on the control wire, less often a coil with shorted windings that pulls the voltage down. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's analogue for solenoid A, P0973 on the 6-speed units, needs a ground-short flag from the output hardware for 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and lights the MIL after one trip; Ford names P0973 a short to ground and runs the check continuously. CARB requires circuit monitoring. P08E5 is the high-voltage counterpart, P08E6 the open circuit. A shorted output usually forces the TCM into a safe substitute gear, and acceleration feels weaker.

causes_en: Control wire chafed against a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high
TCM output stage fault
P08E5.en: Shift Solenoid L Control Circuit High
P08E5.desc: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L, set when the line shows battery voltage or a floating high level while the TCM expects otherwise. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The analogue for solenoid A illustrates the two possible readings: in GM's 6-speed tables P0974 covers an open circuit as well as a short to power, fails after 1.2 of 1.5 seconds and needs two trips for the MIL, whereas Ford's P0974 only means a short to power. A wire chafed against a powered conductor inside the transmission harness is a typical cause. CARB requires the check. P08E4 is the low counterpart, P08E6 the open circuit. The valve may stay on, giving wrong gears.

causes_en: Break in the harness or internal transmission wiring
Open solenoid coil
Connector unlatched or terminal backed out
P08E6.desc: Open circuit in the control path of shift solenoid L: harness, connector, internal transmission wiring or the coil itself no longer carry current, so the valve cannot be energised. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Among the documented analogues, Ford reports an open circuit through each solenoid's base code, P0750 for solenoid A, and GM counts it as part of the high-voltage code P0974; a stand-alone open code therefore has no known user. Ford's electrical checks need 0.5 to 5 seconds of mismatch between command and feedback. CARB requires the check. Measuring coil resistance at the transmission connector separates a coil fault from a harness break. P08E4 and P08E5 cover the shorts.

causes_en: Enable wire open or connector at the clutch actuator not seated
Internal electronics fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Corroded or water-damaged connector near the drive unit
Faulty enable driver in the drive motor control module
P08E7.en: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit
P08E7.desc: Covers the enable line with which a drive motor control module activates the actuator of a clutch that couples or uncouples electric drive motor A from the wheels. The code sets when the module sees an electrical fault on that line, typically an open circuit or an implausible state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest known hardware is the front electric drive unit of the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, which has a disconnect clutch actuator, a clutch pawl and a position switch; GM lists separate faults there, such as P08ED and a lost-communication code for the actuator. CARB requires circuit checks on such output components. P08E8 and P08E9 are the low and high variants. The driver usually loses electric assist on that axle.

causes_en: Enable wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internal short at the actuator enable input
Water ingress in the actuator connector
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module
P08E8.en: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit Low
P08E8.desc: Set when the voltage on the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator stays below the expected range, usually because the wire or the actuator input is shorted to ground. The control module can then no longer switch the actuator on, so the clutch cannot be engaged or released on command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the comparable hardware is the front drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray with its disconnect clutch actuator, pawl and switch, for which GM publishes only P08ED and an actuator communication fault. CARB requires such circuit monitoring. P08E7 is the general circuit fault, P08E9 the high-side counterpart. Electric drive on that axle is typically disabled.

causes_en: Enable wire shorted to a supply circuit
Open ground or reference circuit of the actuator
Internal fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module
P08E9.en: Drive Motor A Clutch Enable Circuit High
P08E9.desc: Set when the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator reads higher than it should, for example because it is shorted to a supply voltage or the line floats due to an open ground. The module then cannot reliably switch the actuator off or confirm its state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the nearest known application is the front electric drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray, whose disconnect clutch actuator and switch GM services as separate parts but describes only under P08ED and a communication code. CARB covers the fault through its output component monitoring. P08E8 is the low-side counterpart, P08E7 the general circuit fault. The system normally keeps the motor uncoupled.

causes_en: Faulty disconnect clutch position switch or sensor
Open signal or reference wire to the position switch
Corroded or loose connector at the drive unit
Faulty input stage in the drive motor control module
P08EA.en: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit
P08EA.desc: Concerns the sensor or switch that reports where the pawl of the drive motor A disconnect clutch sits, i.e. whether the form-locking clutch is engaged or released. The code sets when the control module finds an electrical fault in that signal circuit, such as an open line or a signal outside its valid states. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM fits a drive motor disconnect clutch switch to the front drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray and blames it for P08ED; pawl clutches with dedicated position sensors are described in supplier patents such as one from Means Industries. CARB requires input circuit checks. P08EB and P08EC are the low and high variants, P08ED the plausibility fault. Electric drive on that axle is usually inhibited.

causes_en: Position signal wire shorted to ground
Missing supply voltage to the position switch
Position switch or sensor failed low
P08EB.en: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit Low
P08EB.desc: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays below its valid range, which points to a short to ground in the signal wire, a missing sensor supply or a sensor that has failed low. The module then cannot tell whether the pawl has engaged. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the matching hardware is the disconnect clutch switch on the front drive unit of the Corvette E-Ray, which GM links only to P08ED, and supplier patents describe such position sensing on pawl or strut clutches. CARB requires out-of-range checks on these inputs. P08EC is the high-side fault, P08EA the general circuit fault. The system typically keeps the motor uncoupled and lights a warning.

causes_en: Open signal or ground wire of the position switch
Signal wire shorted to a supply circuit
Position switch or sensor failed high
P08EC.en: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Circuit High
P08EC.desc: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays above its valid range. Typical reasons are an open signal or ground wire, which lets the input float high, or a short to a supply voltage. The module then has no trustworthy feedback on whether the clutch is engaged. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the closest documented hardware is the disconnect clutch switch on the Corvette E-Ray front drive unit, tied by GM only to P08ED, and patents on pawl or strut clutches with position sensors show the principle. CARB requires out-of-range monitoring. P08EB is the low-side fault, P08EA the general circuit fault, P08ED the plausibility check. Electric drive on that axle is usually locked out.

causes_en: Faulty drive motor disconnect clutch switch (GM E-Ray bulletin)
Disconnect clutch actuator not moving the pawl fully
Worn or binding pawl or clutch teeth inside the drive unit
P08ED.en: Drive Motor A Clutch Pawl Position Performance
P08ED.desc: A plausibility fault: the pawl position reported for the drive motor A disconnect clutch does not match what the control module commanded, or the clutch did not reach the expected position, even though the circuit itself is electrically intact. GM documents the code for the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, whose front electric drive unit uses a clutch pawl and a disconnect clutch actuator; bulletin 24-NA-165 says it is stored in the drive motor control module, lights the MIL and is usually caused by the disconnect clutch switch, which is replaced as an external part. Electrical faults of the same signal are P08EA to P08EC; actuator enable faults are P08E7 to P08E9. The driver mostly sees the warning lamp and loss of electric front drive.

causes_en: Failed clutch A actuator motor (open winding or internal fault)
Loose connector or broken wire between TCM and actuator
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM
P0900.desc: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator that opens and closes clutch A in an automated or dual-clutch transmission. The code sets when the module detects an open circuit, so it cannot energise the actuator. Ford documents it for the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox in the Fiesta and Focus, where each dry clutch is moved by a three-phase electric motor with hall sensors; P0900 is the open-circuit check of the clutch A motor, alongside P0902 (short to ground) and P0903 (short to power). Ford program 20B23 for some 2016-2017 Focus cars lists P0900 with a lit check engine light and erratic shifts caused by failed clutch actuator motors. P090A is the same fault on clutch B.

causes_en: Weak or worn clutch A actuator motor (dual-clutch units)
High resistance in the transmission harness or sub-harness
TCM fault or outdated TCM software
P0901.en: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0901.desc: Set when the clutch A actuator circuit is electrically present but does not behave as expected, for instance when the measured current or response deviates too far from the target. Usage differs by maker. Ford lists P0901 among the DPS6 PowerShift codes, and trade guidance recommends swapping the two identical clutch motors: if the fault moves to clutch B, the motor is bad. Honda added P0901 on the 2015 TLX V6 nine-speed automatic for abnormal resistance in the clutch pressure control solenoid circuits, with failsafe gear hold and MIL. FCA recall 16V529 on 9-speed models also uses it to decide on a harness replacement. P0900, P0902 and P0903 are the pure circuit faults; P090B is the clutch B counterpart.

mfr.Audi: Clutch master cylinder failure, Clutch solenoid failure, Transmission Control Module (TCM) failure

causes_en: Clutch A actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Chafed motor wire touching ground
P0902.en: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit Low
P0902.desc: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a low state, in practice a short to ground on a motor or control line. Ford defines it exactly this way for the DPS6 PowerShift transmission: the TCM tests the three-phase clutch A motor for open circuit (P0900), short to ground (P0902) and short to power (P0903), next to hall sensor and sequence checks. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P0902 among the codes for which a failed TCM can be the cause, so the module itself is a real suspect besides the motor and harness. P090C is the same fault on clutch B. With the clutch no longer controllable, the gearbox goes into a fallback mode.

causes_en: Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Internal fault in the clutch A actuator motor
Faulty motor driver in the TCM
P0903.en: Clutch A Actuator Control Circuit High
P0903.desc: Set when the control circuit of the clutch A actuator shows a high state, meaning a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford names P0903 as the short-to-power test of the clutch A motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox of the Fiesta and Focus, part of a set with P0900 for an open circuit and P0902 for a short to ground. Ford's OBD summary gives no thresholds for these motor checks. Because both DPS6 clutch motors are identical, swapping them shows whether the motor or the harness and TCM side is at fault. CARB requires such circuit checks on transmission output components. P090D is the same fault on clutch B. The clutch is released and the vehicle may not drive normally.

causes_en: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at the gate select sensor or actuator unit
Chafed or broken sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gate select position sensor (often integrated in the shift and select actuator)
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module
P0904.desc: Circuit A of the gate select position sensor tells the control module of an automated manual gearbox where the shift mechanism stands in the select direction, i.e. which gate (for example 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 or reverse) is lined up. This generic circuit code sets when the module sees an electrical fault on that signal that is not covered by the more specific low, high or intermittent variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Aisin AI and Isuzu patents describe such select stroke or select position sensors working next to an electric or hydraulic select actuator, and CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs of this kind. P0905 to P0908 are the siblings, P09A2 and P09A6 the same signal on circuits B and C. Without a valid gate signal the gearbox usually stops shifting or holds one gear.

causes_en: Worn or drifting gate select sensor, main and redundant tracks disagree
High resistance at connector pins distorting the sensor voltage
Gate positions not relearned after actuator, clutch or TCM replacement
Loose or displaced magnet or sensor mounting on the select shaft
P0905.en: Gate Select Position Circuit A Range/Performance
P0905.desc: Plausibility fault of the gate select position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The signal is electrically within limits, but it does not fit what the control module expects: typical checks compare the measured select travel with the learned gate positions and the commanded target gate. No manufacturer documents this code in freely citable material. Patents by Aisin AI on select control with target and actual gate, and on fallback strategies after a stroke sensor failure, show how the module depends on this signal; CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0904, P0906 and P0907 cover the electrical faults, P0909 a select movement that misses its target. The driver typically sees a fallback mode with no or limited shifting.

causes_en: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
P0906.en: Gate Select Position Circuit A Low
P0906.desc: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Common causes are a short to ground on the signal line, a missing sensor supply, or an internal sensor defect; with many sensor designs a broken signal wire also reads low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Aisin AI and Isuzu describe select stroke and select position sensors with a defined voltage curve across the gates in their patents, so a value below that curve is clearly out of range; CARB calls for out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0907 is the matching high fault, P09A4 and P09A8 are the low faults of circuits B and C. Without a gate signal the gearbox usually locks gear changes or holds a safe gear.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the gate select sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
P0907.en: Gate Select Position Circuit A High
P0907.desc: Set when the gate select position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Typical causes are a short of the signal line to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, a broken sensor ground, or an internal sensor fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The patents of Aisin AI and Isuzu on select control show that the module derives the active gate directly from this sensor voltage, so a reading above the valid band leaves it blind in the select direction; CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0906 is the opposite low fault, P09A5 and P09A9 are the high faults of circuits B and C. For the driver this usually means a warning lamp and a gearbox that no longer changes gear or stays in a fallback gear.

causes_en: Loose or spread terminals at the sensor or actuator connector
Harness damage that only opens or shorts under engine movement
Moisture or corrosion in the connector near the gearbox
P0908.en: Gate Select Position Circuit A Intermittent
P0908.desc: Points to a gate select position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox, too briefly or too irregularly for a steady low or high fault. Loose terminals, a damaged harness that moves with the engine, or moisture in the connector at the shift and select actuator are the usual reasons. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. An Aisin AI patent explains why even short sensor dropouts matter: if a stroke sensor fails while driving, the controller can no longer confirm the engaged gear and must switch to a fallback strategy. CARB requires circuit and rationality checks on such inputs. P0904 to P0907 are the steady faults of the same circuit. Drivers often notice occasional neutral drops or refused shifts that vanish again.

causes_en: Stiff or jammed select shaft, shift head or internal selector mechanism
Worn select motor (brushes, gears) with too little force
Select sensor offset or gate positions not relearned
Weak battery or voltage drop on the actuator supply
P0909.desc: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox commands the select actuator to a new gate, but the measured select position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits may be electrically fine; the fault lies in the closed loop as a whole. Typical reasons are a jammed or stiff select shaft or shift head, a worn or weak select motor, or a sensor offset. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. An Aisin AI patent describes select control with target and actual gates, and a Hyundai/Kia patent detects jammed or stuck shift actuators from motor current. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0910 to P0913 are the actuator circuit faults, P0919 the same error in the shift direction. The gearbox may refuse gears or stay in neutral.

causes_en: Failed clutch B actuator motor
Loose connector or broken wire to the clutch B motor
Faulty motor driver inside the TCM
P090A.desc: Watches the drive circuit of the actuator for clutch B, the second clutch of a dual-clutch transmission, and sets when the module finds an open circuit. Ford uses it on the DPS6 PowerShift of the Fiesta and Focus: the clutch B electric motor is tested for driver faults (P087A), hall sensor faults (P087B), sequence errors (P087E), an open circuit (P090A), a short to ground (P090C) and a short to power (P090D). Trade guidance for the DPS6 is to swap the two identical clutch motors; if the code moves to the clutch A equivalent P0900, the motor is defective, otherwise the harness or TCM is. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. Shifting becomes erratic and the gearbox may refuse to drive.

causes_en: Worn or sluggish clutch B actuator motor
TCM fault (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Damaged harness between TCM and clutch B motor
P090B.en: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Performance
P090B.desc: Set when the clutch B actuator circuit is electrically connected but the actuator does not respond as commanded, for example too slowly or with an unexpected current draw. Ford uses P090B on the DPS6 PowerShift transmission. Trade guidance for this gearbox starts with a visual check of the harness from the TCM to the clutch B motor, then swaps the two identical clutch motors: if the code becomes P0901, the motor with its built-in position sensor is faulty; if P090B stays, the circuit or TCM needs pinpoint testing. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P090B as a code where the TCM itself can be the cause. P090A, P090C and P090D are the pure circuit faults of clutch B.

causes_en: Clutch B actuator motor with internal short to ground
Failed TCM output stage (Ford program 14M02 lists this code)
Chafed motor wire touching ground
P090C.en: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit Low
P090C.desc: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a low state, which on the documented application means a short to ground. Ford defines P090C as the short-to-ground check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift gearbox, paired with P090A for an open circuit and P090D for a short to power. Ford's TCM program 14M02 for 2011-2015 Fiesta and Focus also lists P090C among the codes that a defective TCM can cause, so the module belongs on the suspect list along with the motor and its wiring. Swapping the identical clutch motors helps: if the fault moves to P0902, the motor is bad. CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. Expect missing gears, erratic shifts or no drive.

causes_en: Failed clutch B actuator motor (Ford program 20B23)
Motor or control wire shorted to a supply line
Faulty motor driver in the TCM
P090D.en: Clutch B Actuator Control Circuit High
P090D.desc: Set when the control circuit of the clutch B actuator shows a high state, i.e. a motor or control line is shorted to battery voltage. Ford documents P090D as the short-to-power check of the clutch B motor in the DPS6 PowerShift transmission of the Fiesta and Focus. Ford customer satisfaction program 20B23, covering some 2016-2017 Focus cars, names P090D together with P0900 and several hall and driver codes as signs of failed clutch actuator motors, with erratic shifting, vibration and a lit check engine light; dealers replaced both motors. P090A and P090C are the open and ground faults of the same circuit, P0903 the clutch A equivalent. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission outputs.

causes_en: Open winding or worn brushes in the select motor
Broken actuator wire or terminal pushed out of the connector
Corroded actuator connector near the gearbox
Faulty actuator driver stage in the transmission control module
P0910.desc: Concerns the drive circuit of the gate select actuator, the motor or valve that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox sideways from gate to gate. The code sets when the control module finds this output open or electrically faulty, for example when no current flows although the driver stage is switched on. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia patents describe select and shift actuators as electric motors fed by the transmission controller; older and heavy-duty systems use hydraulic or pneumatic select cylinders with solenoid valves. CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. P0911 to P0913 are the range, low and high variants, P0909 a select movement that misses its target. Without the select actuator the gearbox cannot change gates and stays in its current gear or neutral.

causes_en: Worn select motor drawing abnormal current
Stiff select mechanism overloading the actuator
High resistance in actuator wiring or connector
P0911.desc: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but the current, voltage or response measured on it does not fit the command, for example a current that is too high or too low for the requested movement. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent explains why controllers watch actuator current closely: jamming and sticking raise the motor load, and the motor can be damaged if this is not caught early. An Isuzu patent describes electric select actuators controlled by the transmission module. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0910, P0912 and P0913 are the clear electrical faults, P0909 the failure to reach a gate. Gear changes become slow or are blocked.

causes_en: Actuator wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the select motor, e.g. from brush debris
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P0912.desc: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state, which usually means a short to ground on a motor or control line, or an internal short in the actuator. Many controllers then switch the affected output off to protect the driver stage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia describe in their patents select and shift actuators built as electric motors and driven by the transmission controller, which is the hardware this circuit check covers; CARB requires circuit monitoring of such outputs. P0913 is the matching high fault, P0910 an open circuit and P0911 a plausibility fault. With the select actuator disabled, the gearbox can no longer change gates.

causes_en: Actuator wire shorted to battery voltage
Open motor winding read as high voltage by the driver stage
Driver stage in the transmission control module stuck on
P0913.desc: Set when the drive circuit of the gate select actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Usual causes are a short of a motor or control line to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on the circuit design an open load can also read high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents by Isuzu and Hyundai/Kia describe electric select and shift actuators that the transmission controller powers directly, and CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. P0912 is the opposite low fault, P0910 the open circuit, P0911 the plausibility fault and P0909 a select movement that misses its gate. The driver sees a warning lamp and a gearbox that can no longer change gates.

causes_en: Loose or corroded connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox
Faulty gear shift position sensor
Faulty sensor input or reference supply in the transmission control module
P0914.desc: Circuit A of the gear shift position sensor reports how far the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox has moved in the shift direction, i.e. whether a gear is engaged, in neutral or in between. This generic circuit code sets on an electrical fault on that signal that does not match the more specific variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. An Aisin AI patent pairs such a shift stroke sensor with a select stroke sensor, and a Nissan/Aichi patent places the shift position sensor as a magnet and field detector on the piston of a hydraulic shift actuator. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0915 to P0919 are the siblings, P091A and P095A the same signal on circuits B and C. Without it the module cannot confirm the engaged gear and usually blocks shifting.

causes_en: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, redundant tracks disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rod
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or TCM replacement
High resistance at connector pins distorting the signal
P0915.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Range/Performance
P0915.desc: Plausibility fault of the gear shift position signal on circuit A in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, but the reading does not fit: the signal does not change while the shift actuator moves, or the engaged position does not match the learned gear positions. No manufacturer documents this code in freely citable material. A Nissan/Aichi patent points out that sensor brackets on shift forks can deform under vibration and spoil the reading, and an Aisin AI patent describes the fallback when a stroke sensor can no longer be trusted. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0914, P0916 and P0917 are the electrical faults, P0919 a shift movement that misses its target. Shifting becomes limited or stops.

causes_en: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor reference supply interrupted or shorted
Internal defect of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
P0916.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Low
P0916.desc: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. A short to ground on the signal line, a lost sensor supply or an internal sensor defect are the usual causes; depending on the sensor design a broken signal wire reads low as well. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In the patents of Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi the shift stroke or shift position sensor is the only feedback telling the controller whether a gear is engaged, so a missing signal stops automatic shifting. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0917 is the matching high fault, P091C and P095C are the low faults of circuits B and C. The gearbox typically locks gear changes or drops to neutral.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Internal fault of the shift position sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
P0917.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit A High
P0917.desc: Set when the gear shift position signal on circuit A of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to the sensor supply or to battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor itself may be faulty. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi patents show the shift stroke or shift position sensor as the feedback that confirms an engaged gear; with a reading above the valid band the controller can no longer tell neutral from an engaged gear. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P0916 is the opposite low fault, P091D and P095D are the high faults of circuits B and C, P0919 a shift movement that misses its target. Shifting is usually locked.

causes_en: Connector at the shift sensor or actuator unit losing contact under vibration
Chafed or partially broken sensor wire near the gearbox
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Shift position sensor with an internal contact or track fault
P0918.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit A Intermittent
P0918.desc: Flags a gear shift position signal on circuit A that drops out or jumps for short moments in an automated manual gearbox. The module sees implausible steps or brief losses that are too short or too irregular for a lasting low or high fault. Typical triggers are terminals that lose contact under vibration, a chafed harness moving with the powertrain, or moisture at the actuator connector. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi show the shift stroke sensor as the feedback that confirms an engaged gear. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0914, P0916 and P0917 are the steady electrical faults of circuit A, P0915 the plausibility fault. Shifts may abort or the gearbox may briefly fall back to neutral.

causes_en: Stiff or jammed shift rail, shift fork or synchroniser
Worn shift motor or leaking shift cylinder that no longer delivers full force
Low pressure in the hydraulic supply on hydraulically actuated units
Shift positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
P0919.desc: Set when the control module of an automated manual gearbox drives the shift actuator towards a gear, but the measured shift position does not reach the target within the allowed time and tolerance. Sensor and actuator circuits can be electrically intact; the fault concerns the closed loop as a whole. Usual reasons are a stiff or jammed shift rail or synchroniser, a weak actuator, low hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units, or a sensor offset. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent detects jammed shift actuators from motor current, and an Isuzu patent controls the shift motor by stroke ranges using a shift stroke sensor. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0909 is the same error in the select direction, P0920 to P0927 the actuator circuits. Gears may not engage.

causes_en: Loose or corroded connector at the shift position sensor
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit B
Faulty shift position sensor B
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module
P091A.desc: Circuit B is a second channel reporting the shift position of an automated manual gearbox, for instance a redundant sensor track or a separate sensor on another shift rail. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault on that signal that matches none of the more specific B variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and which physical sensor carries the letter B depends on the design. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi describe shift stroke sensors as the feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent also covers the fallback when a stroke sensor fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P091B to P091D are the B siblings, P0914 and P095A the same signal on circuits A and C. Shifting may be restricted.

causes_en: Worn or drifting shift position sensor, channels A and B disagree
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit
P091B.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit B Range/Performance
P091B.desc: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit B in an automated manual gearbox. The voltage stays within its electrical limits, yet the value does not fit: it disagrees with circuit A, does not change while the shift actuator moves, or does not match the learned gear positions. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent notes that sensor mountings on shift parts can deform under vibration and falsify the reading, and an Aisin AI patent describes how the control continues when a stroke sensor is no longer trusted. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P091A, P091C and P091D are the electrical faults of circuit B, P0915 the same check on circuit A. Gear changes may be limited.

causes_en: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to ground
Open or shorted sensor supply line
Faulty shift position sensor B
P091C.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit B Low
P091C.desc: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays below its lowest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. Usually the signal line is shorted to ground, the sensor supply is missing, or the sensor has failed internally. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi present the shift stroke or shift position sensor as the feedback that confirms an engaged gear; with a reading below the valid band that confirmation is lost on this channel. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P091D is the opposite high fault, P0916 and P095C are the low faults of circuits A and C, P091B the plausibility fault of circuit B. The gearbox may run in fallback mode.

causes_en: Signal wire of circuit B shorted to supply or battery voltage
Open sensor ground
Faulty shift position sensor B
P091D.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit B High
P091D.desc: Set when the shift position signal on circuit B of an automated manual gearbox stays above its highest valid value for longer than a calibrated time. The signal line may be shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage, the sensor ground may be open, or the sensor may be faulty. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Patents from Aisin AI and Nissan/Aichi present the shift stroke or shift position sensor as the feedback for gear engagement, so a reading above the valid band leaves the module unable to judge this channel. CARB requires out-of-range checks on such inputs. P091C is the opposite low fault, P0917 and P095D are the high faults of circuits A and C, P091B the plausibility fault of circuit B. Shifting is usually restricted.

causes_en: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P0920.desc: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the forward shift direction. Depending on design this is one of two solenoid valves on a double-acting shift cylinder or one rotation direction of an electric shift motor. The code sets when the module finds this output open or electrically faulty, e.g. no current while the driver is on. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. A ZF patent feeds each chamber of a double-acting cylinder through its own 3/2 solenoid valve, an Isuzu patent turns the shift motor forward or reverse by shift direction. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0921 to P0923 are the siblings, P0924 the reverse direction. Gears in this direction can no longer be engaged.

causes_en: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units
P0921.en: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0921.desc: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting movement do not fit the command, for example a current that is too high for the requested stroke or a shift position that hardly changes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent explains that jamming raises the motor load of a shift actuator and must be caught early, and a ZF patent shows double-acting shift cylinders with one solenoid valve per chamber. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0920, P0922 and P0923 are the clear electrical faults, P0925 the reverse direction, P0919 the missed target. Forward shifts become slow or fail.

causes_en: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector
P0922.en: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit Low
P0922.desc: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually points to a short to ground on a valve or motor line, or to an internal short in the actuator. Many controllers then switch the output off to protect the driver stage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent drives each chamber of a double-acting shift cylinder through its own solenoid valve, and an Isuzu patent runs an electric shift motor in both directions, so a fault can affect one shift direction only. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0923 is the opposite high fault, P0920 the open circuit, P0926 the reverse direction. Gears in this direction are blocked.

causes_en: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs
P0923.en: Gear Shift Forward Actuator Circuit High
P0923.desc: Set when the drive circuit of the forward shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Typical reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage, or a driver stage in the module that no longer switches off; depending on circuit design an open load can also read high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent describes double-acting shift cylinders whose chambers each have a 3/2 solenoid valve, and an Isuzu patent drives a shift motor forward or reverse by shift direction. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0922 is the opposite low fault, P0920 the open circuit, P0927 the reverse direction. An actuator that stays energised can hold or force a gear, so shifting is usually locked.

causes_en: Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the shift actuator or valve
Broken drive wire between module and actuator
Open solenoid coil or motor winding in the actuator
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P0924.desc: Concerns the drive circuit that moves the shift mechanism of an automated manual gearbox in the reverse shift direction, i.e. opposite to the forward actuator. It does not mean the reverse gear itself. Depending on design this is the second solenoid valve of a double-acting shift cylinder or the second rotation direction of an electric shift motor. The code sets when the module finds this output open or electrically faulty. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. A ZF patent assigns one 3/2 solenoid valve to each cylinder chamber, an Isuzu patent reverses the shift motor depending on shift direction. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0925 to P0927 are the siblings, P0920 the forward direction. Gears in this direction cannot be engaged.

causes_en: Sticking shift valve, worn shift motor or stiff shift linkage
Solenoid or motor resistance out of specification
Increased contact resistance in connector or wiring
Insufficient hydraulic pressure on hydraulic units
P0925.en: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit Range/Performance
P0925.desc: Plausibility fault in the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the actuator that moves the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction. The circuit is neither open nor shorted, but current, voltage or the resulting shift movement do not match the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Hyundai/Kia patent detects jammed shift actuators from rising motor current, and a ZF patent shows double-acting shift cylinders with one solenoid valve per chamber, so each direction can be judged on its own. CARB requires functional checks on such outputs. P0924, P0926 and P0927 are the clear electrical faults, P0921 the forward direction, P0919 the missed target. Shifts in this direction become slow or fail.

causes_en: Drive wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil or shift motor
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the connector
P0926.en: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit Low
P0926.desc: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox, the one moving the shift mechanism opposite to the forward direction, shows a voltage that is too low for the current switching state. This usually means a valve or motor line shorted to ground or an internal short in the actuator; the module often switches the output off to protect itself. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent drives each chamber of a double-acting shift cylinder through its own solenoid valve, an Isuzu patent runs the shift motor in both directions. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0927 is the opposite high fault, P0924 the open circuit, P0922 the forward direction. Gears in this direction are blocked.

causes_en: Drive wire shorted to battery voltage
Driver stage in the control module stuck on
Open coil or winding read as high on some circuit designs
P0927.en: Gear Shift Reverse Actuator Circuit High
P0927.desc: Set when the drive circuit of the reverse shift actuator of an automated manual gearbox shows a voltage that is too high for the current switching state. Common reasons are a valve or motor line shorted to battery voltage or a driver stage that no longer switches off; on some circuit designs an open load also reads high. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A ZF patent describes double-acting shift cylinders with a 3/2 solenoid valve on each chamber, and an Isuzu patent reverses an electric shift motor according to shift direction, so the reverse direction has its own output. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0926 is the opposite low fault, P0924 the open circuit, P0923 the forward direction. A permanently energised actuator can force a gear, so shifting is usually locked.

causes_en: Internal fault in the electronic shifter module, often logged together with P0607 (documented by FCA)
Shift lock solenoid coil open
Broken wire, poorly crimped or pushed-out terminal on the shift lock circuit
P0928.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A/Open
P0928.desc: The module that drives the shift lock (brake transmission shift interlock, BTSI) sees no continuity on control circuit A, so it cannot reliably release the selector from Park. FCA/Chrysler uses the code as P0928-00 BTSI Control: bulletin 08-072-14 (2013-14 Ram 1500, 2014 Durango with 8-speed) and 21-034-15 (2015 Chrysler 300 rotary shifter) name it when the selector will not leave Park or the knob turns without the brake applied; the cure there is a new electronic shifter. P0929 is the plausibility fault, P0930 and P0931 the low and high faults of circuit A, P092A the same open fault on circuit B. The driver usually cannot shift out of Park until the fault clears or the manual release is used.

causes_en: Gear shift module software that misjudges the actuator position (Ford reprogramming bulletins)
Worn or binding lock actuator inside the shifter assembly
Poor pin fit or damaged pin at the shifter connector
P0929.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0929.desc: Set when the shift lock actuator on circuit A is electrically present but does not respond as commanded, for example it fails to reach the locked or released position. Ford stores it in the gear shift module (GSM): SSM 51057 and 53039 list P0929:77 (commanded position not reachable) on Mach-E, Escape, Bronco Sport, Maverick and Transit, fixed by GSM software or replacement; TSB 25-2045 adds P0929:00, :07 and :9A on 2021-24 F-150 together with a selector that will not leave or enter Park, and checks pin 3 of connector C211. Ford shows the wrench lamp, not the MIL. P0928, P0930 and P0931 are the pure electrical faults of circuit A, P092B the same fault on circuit B.

causes_en: Broken wire or loose terminal on circuit B at the shifter
Open coil in the second lock solenoid
Shifter connector not fully seated after console work
P092A.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B/Open
P092A.desc: Reports an open on control circuit B of the shift lock. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none says which lock is B. One possible use is a second lock actuator: GHSP patents describe shifters where a further solenoid holds the lever in Neutral below a set speed unless the brake is pressed, beside the usual Park lock. CARB requires output circuits to be checked for continuity but may exempt safety-only systems. The FCA recall on the BTSI solenoid shows how such a lock fails in practice. P0928 is the same open fault on circuit A, P092B the plausibility fault, P092C and P092D the low and high faults of circuit B. Expect a lever that is locked in a position or no longer locked.

causes_en: Lock pin or actuator binding inside the shifter assembly
Shifter module software misjudging the actuator response
Weak battery or poor supply leaving the solenoid too little force
P092B.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P092B.desc: Set when the actuator on shift lock circuit B is wired correctly but does not reach or report the commanded lock or release state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest documented case is Ford P0929 on circuit A, where the gear shift module logs that the commanded position was not reached and the cure is new GSM software or a new module. CARB asks for a functional check of output components where feasible. GHSP patents show that a shifter can carry a second lock solenoid, for instance a Neutral lock. P092A, P092C and P092D are the open, low and high faults of circuit B, P0929 the matching fault on circuit A. The lever may stay locked, or the lock may engage late.

causes_en: Circuit B wire chafed to ground near the shifter
Shorted turns in the second lock solenoid
Liquid spilled into the shifter causing leakage to ground
P092C.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B Low
P092C.desc: The voltage on shift lock control circuit B is lower than expected, usually because the wire or the solenoid has a path to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly or names the lock behind circuit B. GHSP patents describe shifters with a second solenoid next to the Park lock, for example one that holds the lever in Neutral unless speed is low and the brake is applied. CARB requires output circuits to be checked for shorts but allows safety-only systems to be left out. P092D is the high fault, P092A the open and P092B the plausibility fault of circuit B; P0930 is the low fault on circuit A. A shorted lock circuit can leave the lever locked or let it move without the brake.

causes_en: Circuit B wire shorted to a supply voltage
Poor crimp or loose terminal at the second lock solenoid
Open coil in the second lock solenoid
P092D.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit B High
P092D.desc: The module sees a higher voltage on shift lock circuit B than the commanded state allows, such as a short to supply or, with a low-side driver, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The documented counterpart on circuit A is FCA P0931 in recall 16V-249, where a badly crimped BTSI solenoid terminal on 2016 Grand Cherokees set the high fault and kept the lever in Park.
