GHSP patents show that a shifter may carry a second lock solenoid, so circuit B can be a separate lock. CARB requires circuit fault checks on outputs, with an exemption path for safety-only systems. P092C is the low, P092A the open fault of circuit B; P0931 is the same fault on circuit A.

causes_en: Shift lock control wire chafed through to ground in the console or under the carpet
Shorted turns in the shift lock solenoid coil
Spilled liquid in the shifter area causing leakage to ground
P0930.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A Low
P0930.desc: The voltage on control circuit A of the shift lock solenoid stays below the expected level, typically a short to ground or a driver output pulled low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. FCA uses the sibling codes on the same brake transmission shift interlock (P0928 BTSI Control, P0931 on the 2016 Grand Cherokee). CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit continuity and shorts, while a safety-only system may be exempt, which is why these faults often do not light the MIL. P0928 is the open, P0931 the high fault, P0929 the plausibility fault of circuit A; P092C is the low fault on circuit B. Depending on the design the selector stays locked in Park or is no longer locked at all.

causes_en: Poorly crimped or loose terminal on the shift lock solenoid harness (FCA recall 16V-249)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open shift lock solenoid coil seen as high voltage by a low-side driver
P0931.en: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator Control Circuit A High
P0931.desc: The control module reads a voltage on shift lock circuit A that is higher than the commanded state allows. FCA documents the code directly: in recall 16V-249 the Jefferson North plant found 2016 Jeep Grand Cherokee (WK) vehicles with active or stored P0931-00 whose selector would not release from Park. The cause was a badly crimped terminal on the BTSI solenoid harness from shifter supplier GHSP; FCA replaced the gear selector and warned that losing the solenoid could leave the lever locked in Park or Neutral. So a poor connection, not only a short to battery, can show up as High. P0930 is the low, P0928 the open fault of circuit A; P092D is the high fault on circuit B.

causes_en: Fault in the solenoid pack or valve body module that carries the pressure sensor (open solenoid, internal lead frame)
Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector terminals
5 V reference or sensor ground interrupted
Transmission or powertrain control module fault
P0932.desc: General electrical fault in the circuit of the sensor that reports hydraulic pressure in the gearbox, usually line pressure in an automatic or system pressure in an automated manual or dual-clutch unit. The module sees a signal it cannot use at all, without a clear low or high pattern. Chrysler names it Line Pressure Sensor Circuit Fault; an ALLDATA case on a 2003 Grand Cherokee 4.7 automatic shows it together with P0935, caused by an open line pressure solenoid in the solenoid pack. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission inputs. P0934 and P0935 are the low and high faults, P0933 the plausibility fault, P0936 the intermittent one. Expect harsh shifts, often with line pressure forced to maximum.

causes_en: Open circuit or fault in the line pressure control solenoid causing real excess pressure
Pressure sensor drifting or reading offset
Worn or sticking valves in the valve body
Wrong fluid level or degraded fluid
P0933.desc: The pressure reading is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state. Chrysler RFE, RLE and TES transmissions set it when measured line pressure is more than 25 psi (172 kPa) above the commanded value while staying below the highest pressure ever used in that gear; Sonnax notes that a maximum-pressure condition from an open pressure control solenoid circuit can trigger it and mislead toward the sensor. Ferrari lists P0933 on its DCT as an invalid hydraulic pressure sensor signal, read in the NCR gearbox ECU. Neighbours: P0932, P0934 and P0935 are circuit faults, P0936 intermittent, P0869 a true high line pressure. The driver notices firm or harsh shifts.

causes_en: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
5 V reference open or shorted
Pressure sensor or the solenoid pack carrying it failed
Control module fault
P0934.desc: The pressure sensor signal sits below its valid window. Chrysler RFE transmissions feed the line pressure sensor with a 5 V reference and expect 0.35 to 4.75 V; P0934 sets when the signal stays at or below 0.35 V for 0.18 s, monitored continuously with the engine running. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost 5 V reference or a failed sensor. Ferrari also uses P0934 on its DCT, described as hydraulic pressure sensor signal too low. P0935 is the opposite high fault, P0932 the general circuit fault, P0933 plausibility and P0936 intermittent. Without a usable pressure signal the control usually raises pressure to a safe maximum, so shifts turn harsh.

causes_en: Sensor ground open or poor terminal contact
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Pressure sensor or solenoid pack failed internally
Control module fault
P0935.desc: The pressure sensor signal sits above its valid window. On Chrysler RFE transmissions the line pressure sensor normally reads between 0.35 and 4.75 V; P0935 sets when the signal stays at or above 4.75 V for 0.18 s with the engine running. That pattern points to a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage, an open sensor ground or a sensor failed internally. An ALLDATA case on a 2003 Grand Cherokee logged it with P0932. Ferrari lists P0935 on its DCT as hydraulic pressure sensor signal too high. P0934 is the low counterpart, P0932 the general circuit fault, P0933 plausibility, P0936 intermittent. Expect harsh shifts and possibly a limp mode.

mfr.Audi: Hydraulic power unit assembly failure, Transmission Control Module (TCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Poor crimp or solder joint at the sensor connector
Chafed harness making intermittent contact
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Sensor with an internal intermittent fault
P0936.desc: The hydraulic pressure signal drops out or jumps for short periods, too briefly or irregularly for a lasting low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The underlying sensor is the same one Chrysler uses for line pressure on RFE units and Ferrari for system pressure on its DCT, where the steady faults appear as P0934 and P0935. Gears Magazine names poor solder joints and crimps at the sensor terminals as a frequent source of intermittent pressure sensor codes. CARB requires circuit checks on such transmission inputs. P0932 to P0935 cover the general, plausibility, low and high faults. The driver may see a warning that comes and goes and occasional harsh shifts.

causes_en: Connector at the temperature sensor loose, corroded or oil-soaked
Damaged sensor wiring near the gearbox or cooler lines
Temperature sensor failed
P0937.desc: General electrical fault in the circuit of the temperature sensor for the hydraulic fluid of an automated gearbox, without a clear low or high pattern. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Ferrari shows where such a sensor sits: its DCT carries a radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor reported under P0938 to P0940 in the NCR gearbox ECU. The control needs this value to correct pressure and clutch fill for viscosity. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission sensors. P0938 is the plausibility fault, P0939 and P0940 low and high, P0941 intermittent; P0711 to P0713 cover the main transmission fluid temperature sensor. Shift quality may suffer and a warning appears.

causes_en: Temperature sensor drifting or reacting sluggishly
Signal lost through connector or wiring fault (as in Ferrari's no-signal case)
Real temperature anomaly from a cooler or thermostat fault
P0938.desc: By J2012 wording the hydraulic oil temperature reading is electrically valid but implausible, for example frozen, rising too slowly after a cold start or disagreeing with other temperature values. Ferrari uses P0938 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, but describes it in its bulletin as no signal, an electrical fault rather than a plausibility check; the code is read in the NCR gearbox ECU. CARB asks for rationality checks on temperature inputs. P0937 is the general circuit fault, P0939 and P0940 the low and high faults, P0941 intermittent. A wrong temperature value leads to poorly matched clutch and shift pressures and may limit the cooling strategy.

causes_en: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Temperature sensor shorted internally
Control module input fault
P0939.en: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0939.desc: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits below its valid window. With the usual NTC thermistor, a low voltage corresponds to an implausibly hot reading and typically comes from a signal wire shorted to ground or a sensor shorted internally. Ferrari uses P0939 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, described as signal too low and read in the NCR gearbox ECU. CARB requires out-of-range checks on transmission sensors. P0940 is the high counterpart, P0937 the general circuit fault, P0938 plausibility and P0941 intermittent. Because the module believes the oil is very hot, it may reduce torque, change shift strategy or show an overheat warning.

causes_en: Accumulator solenoid coil open
Connector unplugged or wire broken between module and solenoid
Fault in the internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed
P093A.desc: The control circuit of the solenoid that opens or locks a hydraulic accumulator in the gearbox is open. Such accumulators store pressurised fluid, for example to keep clutches applied during engine stop-start, as GM's patents on a stop-start accumulator and an accumulator with solenoid valve describe. No manufacturer documents P093A publicly. GM uses its own P171A for the same fault on the surge accumulator solenoid: failed if circuit impedance exceeds 200 kOhm in 32 of 40 samples, Type B with MIL after two trips. P093B and P093C are the low and high faults, P093D the performance fault. Stop-start is usually disabled, and the first restart may engage with a jolt.

causes_en: Solenoid control wire shorted to ground
Solenoid coil shorted internally
Output driver in the control module failed
P093B.desc: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads low, usually a control wire shorted to ground or a coil with very low resistance. No manufacturer documents P093B publicly. GM covers the same fault on its surge accumulator solenoid with P171B: failed short to ground when circuit impedance drops below 0.5 Ohm in 32 of 40 samples, Type B with MIL after two trips. The accumulator holds pressurised fluid so clutches stay applied during an engine auto-stop, as GM's stop-start accumulator patent explains. P093A is the open-circuit fault, P093C the high fault and P093D the performance fault. A grounded control line can leave the valve permanently energised, and stop-start is typically switched off.

causes_en: Solenoid control wire shorted to battery voltage
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Output driver in the control module failed
P093C.desc: The control circuit of the hydraulic accumulator solenoid reads high, typically a control wire shorted to battery voltage so the driver cannot switch the valve as commanded. No manufacturer documents P093C publicly. GM covers the same fault on its surge accumulator solenoid with P171C: failed short to voltage when the circuit impedance criterion of 0.5 Ohm is met in 6 of 8 samples, Type B with MIL after two trips. GM's patent on an accumulator with solenoid valve shows how the valve holds or releases the stored fluid. P093A is the open circuit, P093B the low fault and P093D the performance fault. Stop-start is usually disabled; a valve that never closes cannot keep the accumulator charged during an auto-stop.

causes_en: Accumulator solenoid stuck open (drains) or closed (no fill)
Accumulator piston or bore leaking
Leakage at clutch seals or a worn valve body
Missing or misplaced check ball after a rebuild
P093D.desc: The accumulator solenoid circuit is electrically sound, but the accumulator system does not deliver the expected hydraulic result. No manufacturer documents P093D publicly. GM's comparable P171D on the 9-speed transmission watches turbine speed during an engine auto-start: if it exceeds a predicted value because holding clutches slip from too little stored pressure, it counts a failure, enabled between 0 and 110 °C transmission fluid temperature, Type B. Gears Magazine names a solenoid stuck open or closed, a leaking accumulator piston, clutch or valve body leakage and misplaced check balls as causes. P093A to P093C are the electrical faults. Stop-start is disabled and the restart may feel like a bang.

causes_en: Open signal or ground wire, or connector unplugged
Temperature sensor open internally
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
P0940.en: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0940.desc: The hydraulic oil temperature sensor signal sits above its valid window. With an NTC thermistor this matches an extremely cold reading, typically from an open circuit, an unplugged connector, a broken ground or a short to a voltage source. Ferrari uses P0940 on its DCT for the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet oil temperature sensor, described as an electrical fault with signal too high, read in the NCR gearbox ECU. CARB requires out-of-range checks on transmission sensors. P0939 is the low counterpart, P0937 the general circuit fault, P0938 plausibility and P0941 intermittent. With a substitute value the gearbox works on, but clutch and shift pressures are no longer matched to the real oil temperature.

causes_en: Loose contact at the sensor connector under vibration or heat
Chafed wiring near hot gearbox or cooler parts
Sensor with an intermittent internal fault
P0941.en: Hydraulic Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0941.desc: The hydraulic oil temperature signal jumps or drops out briefly, too short or irregular for a lasting low or high fault. Since fluid temperature changes slowly, a sudden step is a clear sign of an electrical problem rather than a real temperature change. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ferrari's DCT bulletin shows the related sensor at the radiator outlet and gearbox inlet, with its steady faults under P0938 to P0940. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission sensors. P0937 is the general circuit fault, P0938 plausibility, P0939 and P0940 low and high. For the driver this means a warning that may come and go and shift quality that changes from one moment to the next.

causes_en: Fluid loss at the reservoir cap or hydraulic power unit seals
Worn pump motor or faulty pump relay
Damaged wiring, connectors or power supply of the pump
Transmission control module fault
P0942.desc: General fault of the unit that generates and stores hydraulic pressure for an automated gearbox or its auxiliary oil supply: motor-driven pump, accumulator and pressure control. Toyota sets P0942 on the 2001 to 2005 MR2 Spyder sequential gearbox together with the SMT warning light and a buzzing pump, or with gears that can no longer be changed; fluid seeping from the reservoir cap or the seal of the hydraulic power unit is a known cause, fixed with new seal rings. Ferrari reads P0942 on its DCT differently, as system pressure command signal too low. CARB requires functional checks of transmission outputs. P0943 and P0944 are the cycling and pressure-loss faults, P0945 to P0948 the pump control circuit.

mfr.Audi: Hydraulic power unit assembly failure, Transmission Control Module (TCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Accumulator has lost its gas precharge
Internal leakage at valves, seals or actuator cylinders
Faulty pressure switch or pressure sensor giving wrong cut-in point
Low or aerated hydraulic fluid
P0943.en: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Cycling Period Too Short
P0943.desc: In a hydraulic pressure unit the pump charges an accumulator up to a cut-out pressure and switches off until pressure falls to the cut-in point. By J2012 wording this code means the pump switches on again too soon, so the interval between charging cycles is shorter than expected. Typical reasons are internal leakage across valves or seals, or an accumulator that has lost its gas precharge and stores too little oil. Audi patents describe such accumulator and leakage checks based on charging switch-over times and pressure decay. No manufacturer documents this exact meaning publicly; Ferrari uses P0943 on its DCT for a system pressure command signal that is too high. CARB requires functional checks of transmission outputs. P0942 is the general fault, P0944 the loss of pressure.

causes_en: Pump loses prime (air drawn in through filter, seal or strainer pipe)
Blocked oil strainer or suction tube
Worn or failed pump (mechanical or electric)
Leaking check valve or internal leak in the valve body
P0944.en: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Loss of Pressure
P0944.desc: The pump runs but the expected hydraulic pressure does not build or collapses. Stellantis names it Loss of Hydraulic Pump Prime: a 2023 STAR case lists it with P0868 and a slow engagement after the vehicle has stood, both set as the only transmission codes with the MIL on, and the fix was a new transmission; an FCA defect file from 2015 also shows it beside line pressure low. Mercedes uses P0944 on the 722.9 automatic with electric auxiliary oil pump for stop-start, as internal fault of that pump; stop-start stops working, and a leaking check valve between converter housing and pump is one cause. Ferrari reads it on its DCT as no system pressure signal with pressure loss. P0943 covers short cycles, P0868 low fluid pressure.

mfr.Audi: Clogged transmission filter, Transmission fluid level is low, Transmission oil pump failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Pump relay coil open or relay not seated
Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay
Failed output stage in the control module
P0945.desc: The control module drives the motor of the hydraulic pump through a relay or a direct output. This code reports a general circuit fault or an open in that control path, so the pump cannot be switched reliably. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The layout is shown by a ZF patent for an automated gearbox, in which a motor-driven pump draws oil from a reservoir and charges a pressure accumulator behind a one-way valve, with shut-off valves feeding the shift cylinders. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0946 is the plausibility fault, P0947 and P0948 low and high; P094E covers the pump supply instead of the control side. Without the pump the gearbox soon runs out of pressure.

causes_en: Relay contacts welded or sticking
Pump supply or control wire shorted to battery voltage
Faulty pump state feedback or control module
P0946.desc: The pump control circuit is electrically intact, but its behaviour does not match the command, for example a pump that keeps running after being switched off, or one that switches but is not followed by the expected feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In the hydraulic unit of an automated gearbox, as shown in a ZF patent, the pump only has to run until the accumulator is charged; a relay that sticks or switches late upsets that cycle. CARB requires functional checks on transmission outputs. P0945 is the general circuit or open fault, P0947 and P0948 the low and high faults, P094B a pump stuck on regardless of the relay. A pump that never stops drains the battery and wears quickly.

causes_en: Relay control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Shorted relay coil
Damaged output stage in the control module
P0947.desc: The voltage on the control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver is lower than the module expects for the commanded state. Usually the line is shorted to ground or the relay coil is shorted, so the output may be overloaded and the pump runs when it should not, or the driver shuts down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The hydraulic unit it belongs to, a motor-driven pump that charges an accumulator for the shift and clutch cylinders of an automated gearbox, is described in a ZF patent. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0948 is the high counterpart, P0945 the open fault, P0946 plausibility. Pressure supply for shifting may fail.

causes_en: Relay control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open relay coil seen as high level by the driver
Control module fault
P0948.desc: The control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver shows a higher voltage than expected, typically because it is shorted to battery voltage or the relay coil is open on a low-side driver. The pump then cannot be switched on, or the module sees it as active when it is not. J2012 places this code with the pump control circuit; Ferrari however reads P0948 on its DCT as no signal from the system pressure output, an unrelated use. The pump and accumulator unit of an automated gearbox is described in a ZF patent. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0947 is the low counterpart, P0945 the open fault and P0946 the plausibility fault. Expect a warning and possible loss of pump pressure.

causes_en: Relearn not run after clutch, actuator or control unit replacement
Adaptation values erased by software update or battery disconnection
Learning aborted by low voltage or worn clutch outside the learn window
P0949.en: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning Not Complete
P0949.desc: Status code for an automatically shifted manual gearbox: the control unit has not yet finished learning its adaptation values, above all the clutch touch point and the end positions of the shift actuators. Such learning runs after a new control unit, clutch or actuator, after a software update and sometimes after the battery was disconnected; Hyundai and Kia patents show how the touch point is found and corrected from shaft speed changes. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The code is a reminder rather than a hardware fault; launch and shifts may be jerky until learning is done. P0950 to P0954 cover the manual control circuit, P0806 to P0808 the clutch position sensor. MIL use depends on the maker.

causes_en: Internal fault of the pump controller or driver stage
Pump motor drawing excess current (worn bearings, fluid in motor)
High resistance in supply or ground of the driver
P094A.desc: Concerns the electronic driver that powers the motor of a hydraulic or electric oil pump, often a separate pump controller. The driver reports, or the module infers, that it cannot deliver the commanded speed or current although the circuit is not open or shorted. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Hyundai shows what such a driver monitors on its wet 8-speed DCT pumps: overcurrent, current and Hall sensor faults and internal faults, filed under its own P193D and P1C2E codes. Mercedes reports an internal fault of the 722.9 auxiliary oil pump under P0944 instead. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094B and P094C are stuck pump faults, P094D overheating, P094E supply; P0C29 is the equivalent for auxiliary fluid pumps of automatics.

causes_en: Pump relay contacts welded closed
Leakage or lost accumulator charge keeps pressure below cut-out
Shorted driver stage or supply wire shorted to battery voltage
P094B.desc: The hydraulic pump keeps running although the module has switched it off, or it never reaches its cut-out point. Causes are a welded relay or shorted driver, or a pump that cannot reach cut-out pressure because of leakage. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In the pump and accumulator unit of an automated gearbox, described in a ZF patent, the pump should rest once the accumulator is charged. Toyota links a constantly buzzing pump on the MR2 sequential gearbox to fluid loss at the hydraulic power unit, reported under P0942. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094C is the opposite fault, P0946 the relay plausibility fault, P0943 the too-short cycle. Battery drain and pump wear follow.

causes_en: Air in the pump after service or a suction leak
Seized or failed pump motor
Blocked strainer or leaking check valve
Supply or relay fault stopping the pump
P094C.desc: The pump is commanded on but does not deliver: it does not turn, turns too slowly or produces too little pressure. The module judges this from pressure or speed feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Mercedes reports a comparable condition of the electric auxiliary oil pump on the 722.9 automatic under P0944; its test plan checks connector and fuse, supply voltage, CAN lines and software, then a check valve in the converter housing, before the pump is replaced. Hyundai lists a stuck high-flow pump on its 8-speed DCT as P193E71. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094B is the opposite fault, P094A the driver, P0944 the pressure loss of the whole unit.

causes_en: Pump running too long because of leakage or a stuck relay
Defective pump controller board
Very hot transmission fluid or blocked cooling
P094D.desc: The hydraulic or electric oil pump, or its integrated controller, has become too hot. The temperature is usually measured on the controller board and the pump is derated or switched off to protect it. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Hyundai lists the same condition for the high-flow pump of its wet 8-speed DCT as P193D4B, over temperature, and P1C2E92 for the high-pressure pump motor control. Kia recalled stop-start oil pump controllers in 2023 because a damaged capacitor could short and overheat the board, harness and connector. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094A is the driver fault, P094B a pump that never stops, a common reason for heat build-up.

causes_en: Blown pump fuse
Open or corroded supply wire or connector
Weak battery or poor main ground lowering pump supply voltage
P094E.desc: Fault in the power feed of the hydraulic or electric oil pump: fuse, supply wire, connector or relay output. The module sees missing or implausible supply at the pump or its controller. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Mercedes shows the checks that belong to it on the electric auxiliary oil pump of the 722.9 automatic, although it reports that pump under P0944: connector and fuse first, then supply voltage and CAN lines. Hyundai lists an open circuit of its DCT high-flow pump as P193D13. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0945 to P0948 concern the control side, P094A the driver, P0562 general low system voltage. Without supply the pump stops and stop-start is usually blocked.

causes_en: Failed up/down switch or sensor in the selector lever or paddles
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the shifter (e.g. after spilled liquid)
Clockspring or steering column wiring fault on paddle-shift vehicles
P0950.desc: General electrical fault in the circuit that carries the driver's manual up and down requests to the transmission control, as used by tip-shift gates on automatics and by automated manual gearboxes. A Chrysler patent shows the classic design: a transverse gate beside the drive positions with a proximity switch that signals upshift on one side and downshift on the other. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The module typically checks the switch signals for states that cannot occur. P0951 to P0954 are the range, low, high and intermittent faults, P0955 onward the mode select circuit. Usually manual shifting is disabled while normal automatic driving remains available; MIL use varies.

causes_en: Sticking or worn up/down tip switch, request signal stays active
Displaced magnet or damaged Hall sensor board in the selector lever
Spilled liquid or dirt in the shifter causing cross-talk between contacts
Faulty input stage in the transmission or shifter control module
P0951.en: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0951.desc: Plausibility fault in the circuit that reports the driver's manual upshift and downshift requests, typically the tip gate of an automatic selector lever or steering wheel paddles. The signal is electrically valid but makes no sense, for example both requests active together or a request held far longer than any tap. A Volkswagen patent explains that the Hall elements in such tip gates are hard to diagnose and proposes checking all sensors and lines while the lever sits in P or R. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0950 is the general circuit fault, P0952 to P0954 the low, high and intermittent faults. Usually only manual shifting is disabled.

causes_en: Signal wire of the up/down circuit chafed through and shorted to ground
Tip switch stuck in the closed position
Moisture or spilled drink in the shifter creating a leakage path to ground
Low supply voltage to a Hall-type tip sensor
P0952.en: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Low
P0952.desc: The control unit sees the voltage on the manual up/down request circuit below its expected window, typically a signal wire shorted to ground or a switch stuck in the grounded state. In many tip gates the moving contact switches to ground, as a Nissan patent shows, so a short to ground can mimic a permanently held request; a Volkswagen patent describes checking the Hall tip sensors for shorts and breaks while the lever is in P or R. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0953 is the high counterpart, P0950 the general and P0951 the plausibility fault. In practice manual shifting is locked out while D keeps shifting automatically.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to a voltage-carrying wire in the shifter harness
Broken wire or unplugged connector on a pulled-up input
Missing ground of the tip switch or Hall sensor
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
P0953.en: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit High
P0953.desc: Voltage on the manual up/down request circuit lies above its expected window. Common reasons are a signal wire shorted to battery voltage or, where the input is pulled up internally, a broken wire or a switch that never closes. A Volkswagen patent names a short to plus and a line break as faults its tip-gate diagnosis detects with the lever in P or R; a Chrysler patent shows the classic AutoStick-style gate with one switch for up and one for down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0952 covers the low side, P0954 dropouts, P0950 the general fault. Manual shifting is usually disabled, automatic mode remains.

causes_en: Loose or spread pins in the selector lever connector
Harness broken internally where it moves with the lever or steering column
Worn or oxidised tip switch contacts
P0954.en: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Intermittent
P0954.desc: The manual up/down request signal drops out or flickers for short moments, so a single tap may arrive twice, late or not at all. Unlike P0952 and P0953 the voltage is not stuck outside its window; it jumps between states without a matching lever movement. Typical triggers are loose pins in the shifter connector, worn contacts or a harness that flexes with the lever. A Chrysler patent shows how simple contact switches in the gate signal each request, a Volkswagen patent how Hall tip sensors and their lines are checked. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks. P0950 is the general fault. The driver notices missed or doubled manual shifts.

causes_en: Failed manual mode switch or microswitch in the selector lever
Corroded or loose connector at the selector lever assembly
Damaged wiring between selector lever and transmission control module
P0955.desc: Fault in the circuit that tells the transmission control whether the driver has moved the selector lever from D into the manual gate. A Nissan patent shows a dedicated manual mode switch with two contacts on separate inputs, so a break or a short to ground can be told apart; a Hyundai patent uses a microswitch on the lever. Genesis bulletins for 2017-18 G80 and G90 automatics list Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit for the cable-shift version, with a check engine light and a part from the shift lever group as repair, though the table prints the code as P0995 and P095500. So at least Hyundai uses ASM for the manual mode of a torque converter automatic. P0956 to P0959 are the detailed variants, P0950 the up/down request circuit.

causes_en: Mode switch or its actuating foot misaligned on the lever
Worn switch contacts giving contradictory states on both inputs
Transmission range sensor out of adjustment, disagrees with the mode signal
Worn selector lever bushings allowing side play
P0956.en: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Range/Performance
P0956.desc: The manual mode signal is electrically valid but contradicts other information, for example manual mode reported while the range sensor reads P, R or N, or the mode switch never changing although the up/down requests arrive. A Hyundai patent uses a microswitch with two opposing contacts and treats identical or missing signals on both inputs as a defect; a Nissan patent likewise compares two contacts of the manual mode switch. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly, and Hyundai's mode circuit fault is only documented as the general code P0955. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0957 to P0959 cover low, high and intermittent faults. Manual mode is usually blocked.

causes_en: Mode signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Mode switch stuck in the grounded position
Liquid or dirt in the selector lever housing
P0957.en: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Low
P0957.desc: Voltage in the manual mode circuit, the signal that reports the selector lever in the manual gate, is below the expected range. Mostly the signal line has a short to ground or the switch contact hangs in its grounded position. A Nissan patent describes a manual mode switch whose moving contact is grounded and explains how the control unit spots a contact shorted to earth from its two inputs. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Hyundai's mode circuit fault appears in Genesis bulletins only as the general code. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0958 is the high counterpart, P0955 the general and P0956 the plausibility fault. Expect manual mode to be unavailable or stuck on.

causes_en: Broken mode signal wire or disconnected shifter plug
Missing ground at the mode switch
Mode signal shorted to a voltage-carrying wire
P0958.en: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit High
P0958.desc: The manual mode signal from the selector lever reads above its expected range. Possible causes are a short to supply voltage or, with an internally pulled-up input, an open circuit or missing switch ground that keeps the line high. A Nissan patent explains how two separately wired contacts let the control unit recognise a break in the manual mode switch, and a Hyundai patent shows the lever microswitch that reports the change from D to M. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Hyundai's mode fault is only documented as P0955. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0957 is the low side, P0959 the intermittent variant. Usually the gearbox stays in automatic mode.

causes_en: Loose pins in the selector lever connector
Worn or bouncing mode microswitch
Harness damaged where it moves with the lever
P0959.en: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Intermittent
P0959.desc: The signal reporting the selector lever in the manual gate drops out or toggles briefly while the lever is not moved, so the transmission control switches between manual and automatic mode on its own. The voltage is not stuck out of range as with P0957 or P0958 but jumps. Loose connector pins at the lever, a harness that flexes with the shifter or a worn microswitch are typical. A Hyundai patent shows such a microswitch actuated by the lever's sideways movement, a Nissan patent the two-contact mode switch. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks. P0955 is the general fault, P0954 the intermittent fault of the up/down circuit.

causes_en: Loose or corroded connector at shift position sensor C
Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit C
Faulty shift position sensor C
Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module
P095A.desc: Circuit C is a third channel reporting the shift position inside an automated manual gearbox, for example a further sensor track or a sensor on another shift rail or selector shaft. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault of that signal that fits none of the more specific C variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and which sensor carries the letter C depends on the design. A Nissan/Aichi patent describes shift stroke sensors as the feedback for engaging gears, an Aisin AI patent the fallback when a stroke sensor fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095B to P095D are the C siblings, P0914 and P091A the same signal on circuits A and B. Shifting may be restricted.

causes_en: Worn or drifting shift position sensor C disagreeing with the other channels
Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail
Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement
Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit
P095B.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Range/Performance
P095B.desc: Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit C of an automated manual gearbox. The voltage is electrically acceptable, but the value does not fit: it contradicts the other position channels, stays put while the shift actuator moves, or misses the learned gear positions. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent points out that sensor mountings on shift parts can give way under vibration and distort the reading; an Aisin AI patent explains how control carries on when a stroke sensor can no longer be trusted. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P095A, P095C and P095D are the electrical faults of circuit C, P0915 and P091B the same check on A and B.

causes_en: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground
Open or shorted 5 V supply of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C
P095C.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Low
P095C.desc: The signal of shift position sensor C in an automated manual gearbox lies below its permitted voltage window. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a sensor with an internal fault pulling its output down. Because the value is physically impossible, the control unit can flag it quickly without comparing it to other channels. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent shows shift stroke sensors as the position feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent the fallback strategy when such a sensor drops out. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095D is the high counterpart, P095A the general and P095B the plausibility fault; P0916 and P091C are the low faults of A and B.

causes_en: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to the 5 V supply or battery voltage
Open ground circuit of the sensor
Internally failed shift position sensor C
P095D.en: Gear Shift Position Circuit C High
P095D.desc: Shift position sensor C of an automated manual gearbox delivers a voltage above its permitted window. This usually points to a signal wire shorted to the supply, a broken sensor ground or, with a pulled-up input, an interrupted signal line. Since no real shift position produces such a value, the module can set the code without cross-checking other channels. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent describes shift stroke sensors as feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent how control continues when one of them fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095C is the low counterpart, P095A the general and P095B the plausibility fault; P0917 and P091D are the high faults of A and B.

causes_en: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body or solenoid assembly
Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin at the transmission connector or pass-through
Broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module
P0960.en: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
P0960.desc: Open-circuit fault in the driver circuit of pressure control solenoid A: the module measures an impedance far above the coil value, as if a wire, pin or winding were broken. Which solenoid carries the letter A depends on the gearbox. Ford uses it for the line pressure (EPC) solenoid; GM's 8-speed for clutch 1 (CB1278R), the 9- and 10-speeds for clutch CB123456(R), Allison 1000 for main modulation (line) pressure and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the odd-clutch valve. GM flags more than 200 kOhm for 0.3 s (Type A), Allison 173 kOhm or more after an intrusive test. GM six-speeds report an open under P0963 instead. Low and high are P0962/P0963, performance P0961. Expect maximum line pressure, harsh shifts or a fixed limp gear.

causes_en: Solenoid with internal electrical or mechanical fault, current no longer follows the command
Debris or varnish in the fluid sticking the solenoid or regulator valve
High resistance at connector or pass-through distorting the current
Low fluid level causing pressure errors (CVT pulley monitor)
P0961.en: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0961.desc: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid A: the circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid does not behave as commanded. On GM's six-speeds, where A is the line pressure solenoid, the Saab 9-4X 6T70 sets it when measured and commanded current differ for 5 s, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s; both Type B, two trips. Allison 1000 flags a current error of 0.5 A or more in 40 of 80 samples (Type A). Ford's 2023 diesel summary lists it as a PC A current range fault. In GM's CVT, A feeds the secondary pulley: a pressure error above 500 kPa steady or 1,500 kPa transient, confirmed by a ratio error, sets it after 5 s. Electrical faults are P0960, P0962 and P0963. The module usually commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations.

mfr.Audi: Transmission shift solenoid failure

causes_en: Control wire chafed through and touching ground
Internally shorted solenoid coil
Transmission fluid or water in the connector bridging pins
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0962.en: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0962.desc: Pressure control solenoid A circuit low: the driver sees a short to ground. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid this way; a short there opens a high-side switch that cuts power to the shift solenoids and leaves park, reverse, neutral and one fixed forward gear at maximum line pressure. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, A is the line pressure solenoid; the fault matures in 1.5 to 2 s and is Type A, with reverse and 5th gear only, no converter lock-up and maximum line pressure. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use A for a clutch solenoid and treat less than 0.5 ohm as a short, Allison 1000 for main modulation pressure (125 ms). Siblings: P0960 open, P0963 high, P0961 performance.

causes_en: Open coil or high-resistance connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or contaminated connector at the transmission
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0963.en: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit High
P0963.desc: Pressure control solenoid A circuit high: the driver detects a short to voltage, and on GM's six-speeds also an open circuit, since those units have no separate open code. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (line pressure solenoid) sets it after 5 s as Type B, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s over two trips; the module then commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid for short to power and, in some applications, keeps P0963 like P0960 without MIL because maximum line pressure does not raise emissions. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds and Allison 1000 (power short within 75 ms) use A for a clutch or main modulation solenoid. Expect firm, harsh shifts rather than slipping. Siblings: P0960, P0961, P0962.

causes_en: Open solenoid coil
Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Broken control wire
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0964.en: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open
P0964.desc: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid B. What B controls differs by gearbox: GM's 8-speed uses it for clutch 2 (CB12345R), the 9-speed for CB29 and the 10-speed for CB128910R, Allison 1000 for pressure control solenoid 2, and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the even-clutch pressure valve. GM sets it at more than 200 kOhm for 0.3 s (Type A, one trip), Allison at 173 kOhm or more after an intrusive test, the dual-clutch unit after 150 ms. GM six-speeds do not use P0964; an open in their 3-5-reverse solenoid shows up as P0967. Ford's OBD summaries list no B or C codes. Depending on the clutch involved, gears are lost or the unit drops into a fixed limp gear. Siblings: P0965, P0966, P0967.

causes_en: Worn or internally faulty solenoid, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or its regulator valve
Internal leak in the CVT primary pulley circuit
High resistance in connector or pass-through
P0965.en: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0965.desc: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid B: wiring is intact, but current or resulting pressure does not match the command. In the Saab 9-4X 6T70, solenoid 2 feeds the 3-5-reverse clutch; a current mismatch for 5 s sets a Type C code without MIL and freezes that clutch's adaptations, and GM's 2016 six-speed table also lists it without MIL. Allison 1000 checks for a current error of 0.5 A or more within 250 ms windows (Type A). In GM's CVT, B controls the primary pulley: a pressure error above 500 kPa steady or 1,500 kPa transient, confirmed by a ratio error for 5 s, sets a Type A code. Electrical faults of B are P0964, P0966 and P0967. Symptoms range from none to rough 3rd, 5th or reverse, or CVT ratio problems.

causes_en: Chafed control wire touching ground
Internally shorted solenoid in the valve body assembly
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0966.en: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
P0966.desc: Pressure control solenoid B circuit low, meaning a short to ground in the driver circuit. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch; a short lasting 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) or 1 s (Saab) sets a Type A code with a fixed limp mode: reverse and 5th gear, maximum line pressure, converter clutch off. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use B for a clutch solenoid and treat less than 0.5 ohm as a short; Allison 1000 uses it for pressure control solenoid 2 with ground-short detection in 125 ms. Ford does not use the B codes. Siblings are P0964 open, P0967 high and P0965 performance; solenoids A and C follow the same scheme.

causes_en: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or contaminated transmission connector
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0967.en: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit High
P0967.desc: Pressure control solenoid B circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, since they have no P0964. For the Saab 9-4X 6T70, where B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch, the module needs 1 s, stores a Type A code and limits the transmission to reverse and 3rd gear at maximum line pressure; GM's 2018 six-speed table uses 0.3 s and one trip. GM's 8-speed (clutch 2), the 9- and 10-speeds, Allison 1000 (power short within 75 ms) and GM's dual-clutch gearbox (even-clutch valve) report the same fault on their solenoid B. Ford does not use it. Siblings: P0964 open, P0966 low, P0965 performance. Repairs usually involve the solenoid body or valve body module.

causes_en: Open solenoid coil
Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness
Broken control wire
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0968.en: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
P0968.desc: Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid C. GM's 8-speed assigns C to clutch 3 (C13567), the 9-speed to CB38 and the 10-speed to C23457910; an impedance above 200 kOhm for 0.3 s counts as open and sets a Type A code after one trip. In GM's dual-clutch gearbox, C is the redundant shutdown valve of the odd clutch, checked for open load while its output is switched off and confirmed after 150 ms. GM six-speeds report an open C solenoid as P0971, and neither Ford's summaries nor the Allison 1000 tables list C codes. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission output components. Low and high are P0970/P0971, performance P0969; the usual result is a lost gear range or limp mode.

causes_en: Solenoid 3 with internal fault, current no longer matches the command
Debris sticking the solenoid or the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve
High resistance in the internal connection to the module
P0969.en: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0969.desc: Performance fault of pressure control solenoid C. Publicly documented only for GM's front-drive six-speeds: on the Saab 9-4X 6T70, clutch pressure solenoid 3 feeds the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches through the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve. If measured current differs from the commanded current for 5 s, the module stores a Type C code and freezes the adaptations of both clutches. GM's 2016 table (C456/CBR1 solenoid) sets it after an invalid feedback for 4.4 of 5 s, also without MIL. Other GM users such as the 8- to 10-speeds list only open, low and high for C, and Ford does not use C. Drivers rarely notice more than gradually rougher 4-5-6 or reverse engagements. Electrical faults: P0968, P0970, P0971.

causes_en: Internally shorted solenoid in the control solenoid valve assembly
Chafed control wire touching ground
Fluid or moisture in the connector
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0970.en: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0970.desc: Pressure control solenoid C circuit low, a short to ground in the driver. On GM's six-speeds C is the C456/CBR1 solenoid; on the Saab 9-4X 6T70 it is clutch pressure solenoid 3 for the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches. A short for 1 s (Saab) or 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) sets a Type A code: only reverse and 5th gear, no converter lock-up, maximum line pressure. GM's 8-speed uses C for clutch 3 (C13567), the 9- and 10-speeds for CB38 or C23457910 with less than 0.5 ohm counting as a short; GM's dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the odd-clutch shutdown valve. Siblings: P0968 open, P0971 high, P0969 performance. Since the solenoid sits in the valve body, repairs often mean the control solenoid valve assembly.

causes_en: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Damaged or loose transmission connector
Faulty output stage in the control module
P0971.en: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0971.desc: Pressure control solenoid C circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, as there is no separate open code there. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (clutch pressure solenoid 3, low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches) and GM's 2018 six-speed table set it after 1 s or 0.3 s as Type A, with limp mode in reverse and 5th gear at maximum line pressure. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use the code for their clutch solenoid C; GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the redundant odd-clutch shutdown valve, where too high a voltage at the sense pin with the output switched on counts as a short. Ford does not use C codes. Siblings: P0968 open, P0970 low, P0969 performance. A loose connector can make the fault come and go.

causes_en: Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid A (Allison-type usage)
Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector or internal harness
Chafed or broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P0972.en: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0972.desc: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A: the circuit is not plainly shorted, yet its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. Today's large makers rarely use the code. GM's 2007 table for the Allison 1000 six-speed used it for an open SS1 circuit: after three hardware fault samples the module opens the low-side driver as an intrusive test and reports P0972 if four more samples show no short to ground (400 ms, Type A, MIL at once). Newer GM Allison tables move that open to P097A. Ferrari's DCT bulletin reuses P0972 for a missing signal from the actuator 1 engage position sensor, not a solenoid. Ford and GM six-speeds report opens elsewhere. Shorts are P0973/P0974.

causes_en: Control wire to solenoid A chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid A or the control solenoid assembly
Fluid or metal debris bridging pins at the transmission connector
Faulty low-side driver in the transmission or powertrain module
P0973.en: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
P0973.desc: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A, usually a short to ground. Ford lists it as SSA short to ground beside P0750 (open) for the 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140, checked by a driver feedback line within 0.5 to 5 s. GM six-speeds (6L/6T) call SS A the mode 2 solenoid and set P0973 after 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 needs 2 s, Type A, then only reverse and 5th remain. GM's 2016 Allison 1000 table folds ground short (0.42 ohm or less) and open (200 kOhm or more) into this code over 10 counts. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) maps it to shift solenoid valve 2. High side is P0974.

causes_en: Open coil or broken wire where the maker reports opens under the high code (GM six-speed)
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Spread or corroded pins at the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P0974.en: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit High
P0974.desc: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A. What it covers depends on the maker. Ford reserves it for a short to power on SSA, because an open SSA circuit sets P0750. GM six-speeds put both an open and a power short of the mode 2 solenoid here: 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL only after two trips. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 waits 2 s, Type B, and then blocks 1st gear. GM's Allison 1000 tables of 2016 and 2023 treat it as a pure power short (0.39 ohm or less, 3 samples, 75 or 60 ms) and report opens separately. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) sets it when solenoid valve 2 reads off while commanded on, 100 ms five times, Type A. Ground-side faults are P0973.

causes_en: Poorly crimped terminals causing intermittent high resistance (FCA 9-speed recall)
Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid B
Outdated transmission software that misreads harness resistance
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P0975.en: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0975.desc: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Three documented uses differ widely. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS2 circuit, confirmed by an intrusive low-side test (400 ms, Type A). FCA's 2016 recall for the 9-speed front-drive transaxle (Cherokee, 200, Renegade, 500X, ProMaster City) names P0975 with P0978, P0981 and P0984 as the codes set by intermittent high resistance from poorly crimped terminals in the range sensor harness under old TCM software; updated software reports that case as P0901 instead. Ferrari's DCT uses P0975 for a missing actuator 2 position signal. Low/high are P0976/P0977.

causes_en: Solenoid B control wire shorted to ground or housing
Internal short in solenoid B or its valve body assembly
Moisture or debris bridging pins at the connector
Faulty driver in the transmission control module
P0976.en: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
P0976.desc: Low-voltage fault, normally a ground short, in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. On GM six-speeds SS B is the mode 3 multiplex valve; the 2016 table sets P0976 after 1.2 of 1.5 s without lighting the MIL, while the Saab 9-4X 6T70 version needs 2 s, is Type B and raises line pressure. Ford uses it for SSB short to ground, with P0755 for an open; on the 2023 Super Duty diesel SSB is fed by solenoid supply TSPC2, so a P2669 supply fault disables this check. GM's Allison 1000 merges ground short and open into it in 2016, but from 2022 reports opens as P097B and keeps P0976 for ground faults found by an intrusive test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). High side is P0977.

causes_en: Open solenoid B coil or wire on GM six-speeds, where opens report as high
Control wire shorted to battery or a switched supply
Damaged pins or seals at the transmission pass-through connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P0977.en: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit High
P0977.desc: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. GM six-speeds put an open or a power short of the mode 3 multiplex valve here, 1.2 of 1.5 s; the 2016 table sets it without MIL, the 2019 table with MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 treats it more severely than P0976: 2 s, Type A, high-side driver off, only reverse and 5th gear left, no converter lockup. Ford uses it strictly for SSB short to power, as in its 2012 and later summaries. GM's Allison 1000 checks for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three samples (75 ms in 2016, 60 ms in 2023). FCA 9-speed and Aisin uses are not documented for this code. Ground-side faults are P0976.

causes_en: Intermittent high resistance at crimped harness terminals (FCA 9-speed)
Open coil of shift solenoid C (Allison-type usage)
Transmission software that predates the manufacturer's fix
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P0978.en: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0978.desc: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS3 circuit, but only while the commanded gear is not reverse trim, 5th or 6th; the table even prints the label Circuit Low beside an open-circuit test, an apparent typo. FCA lists P0978 among the four codes that the 2014–2016 9-speed transaxle set under old software when the range sensor harness had poor crimps. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses it for a missing signal from the actuator 4 engage position sensor. Ford and GM six-speeds do not use it. Low/high are P0979/P0980, the current open code P097C.

causes_en: Solenoid C control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid C inside the valve body
Open coil on GM 2016 Allison calibrations, which report opens under this code
Faulty low-side driver in the control module
P0979.en: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
P0979.desc: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid C. GM uses it mainly on the Allison 1000 six-speed of its heavy pickups and chassis cabs: in 2016 a ground short of 0.22 ohm or less, stricter than the 0.42 ohm for SS1 and SS2, or an open of 200 kOhm or more counts after 10 samples (250 ms, Type A). From 2022 the open moves to P097C and P0979 needs an intrusive low-side test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The Allison PS3 pressure switch test (P0872) also points to P0979 when its fault is electrical. Ford uses it for SSC short to ground beside P0760 open; on 6R80 and 6F, SSC drives the CB26 clutch. High side is P0980.

causes_en: Open coil of shift solenoid 1/A
Unplugged, corroded or pushed-out pin at the transmission connector
Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness
Faulty low-side driver in the control module
P097A.desc: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A, a code that later J2012 editions added; older lists still show P097A as reserved. GM is the only maker found that documents it: the 2022 to 2025 tables for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its heavy-duty trucks call it Shift Solenoid 1 Control Circuit Open. After one hardware fault the module flags pending, and after three samples it opens the low-side driver as a test; three more open readings at 9 to 18 V set the code (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The same gearbox once used P0972 for this and P0973 in 2016. Ford reports an open SSA as P0750, GM six-speeds as P0974, and Genesis folds all electrical faults of A into P0753.

causes_en: Open coil of shift solenoid 2/B
Loose or corroded terminal on the solenoid B circuit
Wire broken by vibration or heat near the transmission
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P097B.desc: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Public use is again limited to GM's Allison 1000 six-speed in heavy-duty trucks, where the 2022 to 2025 tables label it Shift Solenoid 2 Control Circuit Open. SS2 shares high-side driver 2 with SS1 and SS3, so the open test only runs while that supply is on and free of P2669, P2670 or P2671. It confirms an open by switching the low-side driver off and needs three samples, 120 ms, MIL after one trip. Allison's 2007 table filed the same check as P0975, the 2016 table under P0976. Ford reports an open SSB as P0755, GM six-speeds as P0977. Low/high are P0976/P0977.

causes_en: Open coil of shift solenoid 3/C
Loose, wet or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid C
Faulty low-side driver in the control module
P097C.desc: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its 2022 to 2025 heavy-duty tables as Shift Solenoid 3 Control Circuit Open, with the same intrusive low-side test as SS1 and SS2: three samples, 120 ms, battery 9 to 18 V, MIL after one trip. It is the youngest of three codes for this one fault on that gearbox: 2007 used P0978, only outside reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear, 2016 merged it into P0979 with a 200 kOhm limit. Ford reports an open SSC under P0760, and no other maker was found using P097C. A related pressure switch code may set too, because SS3 strokes the S3 valve that switch PS3 watches.

causes_en: Open coil of shift solenoid D
Disconnected or corroded terminal in the solenoid D circuit
Broken wire in the transmission harness
Faulty driver in the control module
P097D.desc: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. No maker documents this code publicly. GM's Allison tables that use P097A to P097C stop at shift solenoid 3, and Ford, which has a solenoid D in its 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140 gearboxes, reports an open SSD under the base code P0765, with P0982/P0983 for ground and power shorts. Any use would follow the CARB rule that every transmission output must be checked for lack of circuit continuity, plus the pattern of the A to C codes: a high-impedance reading confirmed by switching the driver. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F, SSD feeds either CBLR or C456 through a multiplex valve, so an open there would disturb first and upper gears alike.

causes_en: Open coil of shift solenoid E
Poor contact at the solenoid E terminal or lead frame
Broken signal wire to solenoid E
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P097E.desc: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. No manufacturer was found that documents this code. Ford, the main user of an SSE, still reports an open SSE under P0770; its 2023 diesel summary pairs that with P0985 for ground and P0986 for power shorts, and powers SSE from supply TSPC1 together with SSA and SSC. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSE is an on/off solenoid that switches the multiplexing of SSD, while the 6R140 uses a variable force SSE for clutch C456. Without a public owner the code rests on the CARB demand for circuit continuity checks on transmission outputs and on GM's A to C pattern. Opens in shared supply wiring usually set P0657 first.

causes_en: Open coil of shift solenoid F
Loose or corroded terminal at the valve body connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid F
Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module
P097F.desc: Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid F. It is the only code in its family for letter F, since J2012 has no range/performance, low or high codes for F in this block. No maker was found to document it. Hyundai's Genesis bulletin for the eight-speed (2017–2018 G80 and G90) shows how F is handled in practice: an electrical fault of shift control solenoid F (labelled 8LR) is reported under P2709 and fixed by replacing the solenoid. Other makers with six or more clutches use their own codes. A P097F would follow the CARB requirement to test every transmission output for circuit continuity, by analogy with GM's open tests for solenoids 1 to 3.

causes_en: Solenoid C control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Shorted turns in solenoid C lowering its resistance
Adjacent pins bridged by fluid or debris in the connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P0980.en: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High
P0980.desc: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid C, meaning a short to supply. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed: the 2007 table wants four consecutive power-short samples (100 ms, Type A) and skips the check in reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear; later tables (2016, 2018) look for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three counts within 75 ms, and from 2022 within 60 ms, MIL after one trip. Ford uses it for SSC short to power in all its listed gearboxes, with P0760 for an open. Neither GM's 6L/6T six-speeds nor Saab's documented gearboxes use P0980. The ground counterpart is P0979, the open code for the Allison is P097C.

causes_en: Weak terminal crimps causing intermittent resistance (FCA recall S55)
Transmission software not yet updated by the recall
Solenoid D coil resistance out of range
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P0981.en: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0981.desc: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. GM's Allison tables end at solenoid C, and Ford checks SSD only with P0765, P0982 and P0983, so the large North American users skip it. Two codegenau sources exist. FCA's recall S55 (NHTSA 16V-529) covers about 323,400 vehicles with the 9-speed front-drive transaxle; with old TCM software, intermittent high resistance from weak crimps in the range sensor harness could set P0981 or its siblings, and the remedy is new software plus, if a code is present, a new harness. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses P0981 for a missing signal from the actuator 3 position sensor. Low/high for D are P0982/P0983.

causes_en: Solenoid D control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid D or the main control assembly
Damaged internal lead frame or connector inside the transmission
Faulty driver in the powertrain or transmission module
P0982.en: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
P0982.desc: Low-voltage fault, in practice a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford is the documented user: its summaries list SSD with P0765 open, P0982 short to ground and P0983 short to power, checked continuously through the driver feedback within 0.5 to 5 s. Which clutch this hits depends on the gearbox. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSD is a variable force solenoid feeding CBLR or C456 via the SSE multiplex valve; in the 6R140 it drives CBLR alone. In the 2023 diesel summary SSD is fed from supply TSPC2 with SSB, the converter clutch and line pressure solenoid. GM's six-speed and Allison tables do not use P0982. Ferrari reuses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too low.

causes_en: Solenoid D control wire shorted to a supply
Solenoid D with shorted windings
Conductive contamination between neighbouring pins
Faulty smart driver or output stage in the module
P0983.en: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit High
P0983.desc: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford defines it narrowly as SSD short to power; the open circuit stays with P0765. On the 6R140 the solenoid outputs are run by a smart driver chip (ADLER) that does the open and short checks itself, while older units use a feedback line from the output stage; both need 0.5 to 5 s. Since SSD on Ford six-speeds controls the low/reverse clutch, either alone or through the multiplex valve, a constant power short can apply that clutch at the wrong time. The 2020–2023 gasoline summary keeps the same assignment. GM documents no P0983 for its geared automatics, and Ferrari uses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too high. Ground faults are P0982.

causes_en: Range sensor harness with weak crimps (FCA 9-speed recall)
TCM software below the recall level
Internal transmission fault when the code returns after the update
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P0984.en: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0984.desc: Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford checks SSE with P0770, P0985 and P0986 only, GM's documented tables never reach letter E, and even Ferrari's DCT list, which reuses most of its neighbours, skips P0984. The one codegenau source is FCA: in recall S55 for the 9-speed front-drive transaxle it names P0984 together with P0975, P0978 and P0981. Under old TCM software, a range sensor harness with poor crimps and intermittent high resistance could set them; with new software the same fault shows as P0901, and these four codes then point to a separate transmission problem. Otherwise the code rests only on the CARB rule for transmission output checks. Low/high are P0985/P0986.

causes_en: Solenoid E control wire shorted to ground
Internal short of solenoid E
Water or fluid in the transmission connector
Faulty driver stage in the transmission module
P0985.en: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
P0985.desc: Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford lists it for SSE on the 5R110W and 6R140 and in its 2020–2023 gasoline and 2023 diesel summaries, beside P0770 for an open; for the 6R80 and 6F, whose SSE is the on/off multiplex solenoid, the 2012 text names only P0770. Saab's 2010 9-5 with the Aisin six-speed uses P0985 differently, for shift solenoid valve 1: the module sees the circuit reading on while it is commanded off, 100 ms five times in a row, Type A; it then turns all solenoids off and freezes adaptation. Voltage must be 10.2 to 15.5 V and the engine above 400 rpm. High side is P0986.

causes_en: Solenoid E control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Open coil or wire where the maker reads it as high (Saab/Aisin)
Bent or corroded terminals at the solenoid E connector
Faulty driver stage in the control module
P0986.en: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit High
P0986.desc: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford means a short to power on SSE; an open sets P0770 and a ground short P0985. On the 6R140 SSE is a variable force solenoid for the C456 clutch, so a short to power can hold that clutch on. Saab's 2010 9-5 with the Aisin six-speed instead assigns P0986 to shift solenoid valve 1 and sets it when the circuit reads off although it is commanded on, which also catches an open coil: 100 ms, five times, Type A, all solenoids then switched off. GM's published transmission tables do not use the code. Because makers split opens differently, check the maker's table before replacing parts.

causes_en: Failed pressure sensor or switch E
Open or shorted signal wire or poor connector contact
Faulty input stage in the transmission control module
P0987.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit
P0987.desc: General circuit fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only public user of switch E found, GM's 6T70/6T75 family (Saab 9-4X: switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutch regulator valve), reports only P0989 and P0990 for it, both as plausibility counts. P0987 is the slot for a module that sees a generic circuit fault on a fifth pressure sensor or switch, for example an open or out-of-range signal, without separating low from high. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance is P0988, low and high are P0989/P0990; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878. Typical effects are frozen shift adaptations and harsher shifts.

causes_en: Damaged or delaminated switch film, switch reacts late or not at all
Debris in the fluid holding the switch or its regulator valve
Low fluid level or real pressure deviation in the clutch circuit
P0988.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance
P0988.desc: Range/performance fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the commanded clutch state or the pressure expected from other inputs. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's 6T70/6T75 family, the one public user of switch E (switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 regulator valve), folds such plausibility checks into P0989 and P0990; its switch logic table shows which gears should pressurise the switch. Sonnax describes how these normally closed film switches in the valve body module fail through debris or delaminated films. CARB requires rationality checks of transmission inputs. Siblings: P0987 circuit, P0989 low, P0990 high.

causes_en: Damaged or delaminated film in switch 5 of the valve body module
Debris keeping pressure away from the switch
R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve sticking
Low fluid level
P0989.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P0989.desc: Pressure switch E reads low, meaning no pressure, when it should show pressure. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; the normally closed switch sees pressure while both the low/reverse and the 4-5-6 clutch are released. The module counts clutch releases after which the signal stays low, checked with commanded clutch pressure at 50 kPa or less: 18 counts in GM's 2011 tables and on the Saab 9-4X, 17 in the 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code without MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. Sonnax lists P0989 among typical switch failures in this valve body module. P0990 is the stuck-high counterpart; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878.

causes_en: Switch 5 stuck open by a damaged film or debris
R1/4-5-6 regulator valve not moving, switch stays pressurised
Signal circuit shorted to voltage or open inside the module
P0990.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
P0990.desc: Pressure switch E reads high, meaning pressure, when it should be vented. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; applying the low/reverse or 4-5-6 clutch moves that valve and should exhaust the switch. If the signal stays high after such an apply, with commanded clutch pressure at 700 kPa or more, the module counts it: 15 counts on the Saab 9-4X, 30 in GM's 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code, so no MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. According to Saab, normal debris in the fluid can set it intermittently without noticeable symptoms. A short to voltage on the signal wire has the same effect. P0989 is the stuck-low case.

causes_en: Loose or corroded contact at the valve body module connector
Debris or damaged diaphragm film making the switch contact flicker
Chafed internal harness that shorts or opens under vibration
Fault in the transmission control module input stage
P0991.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
P0991.desc: The module has seen the signal of the fifth transmission pressure sensor or switch drop out or jump briefly, without a steady low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only switch E found in public sources is GM's TFP switch 5 in the 6T70/6T75 valve body module (Saab 9-4X 2011), a normally closed switch that GM monitors only through P0989 and P0990: signal stuck low at commanded pressure of 50 kPa or less, or stuck high, counted over clutch releases and logged as Special No Trip without MIL. An intermittent check would follow the CARB rule that transmission inputs be monitored for circuit faults. Steady faults are P0987 to P0990. Expect frozen shift adaptation and the odd harsh shift.

causes_en: Open or damaged signal wire or connector to the switch
Pressure switch or sensor failed inside the valve body module
Transmission control module input fault
P0992.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit
P0992.desc: General circuit fault of a sixth transmission pressure sensor or switch, labelled F. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no gearbox with a switch F was found. GM's six-speeds stop at TFP switch 5 (letter E, P0989/P0990), and Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed monitors its 2-6 brake, high clutch and low-reverse brake switches under P0846, P0876 and P0988, which are letters B, D and E. Pressure switches like these sit in the valve body module and tell the module which clutch is applied; Sonnax describes them as normally closed film-and-piston switches. P0992 would be the code for an open or implausible circuit without a low/high split, as CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance, low, high and intermittent are P0993 to P0996.

causes_en: Sticking clutch regulator valve feeding the switch
Worn or delaminated switch film, debris in the switch
Low or contaminated transmission fluid
P0993.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Range/Performance
P0993.desc: Pressure sensor or switch F is electrically intact, but its reading does not match what the module expects from the commanded clutch state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest documented logic is GM's for switch E (TFP switch 5, 6T70/6T75): the module checks after each clutch release whether the switch returns to its exhausted state and counts failures, at 50 kPa or less commanded pressure for the low case. A sixth switch would be checked the same way, plausibility against commanded pressure and gear, which CARB requires for transmission inputs. Typical causes are sticking regulator valves, debris and worn switch films rather than wiring. P0992 is the plain circuit fault, P0994/P0995 are low and high.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Switch stuck closed by debris or damaged film
Clutch circuit not reaching pressure (valve or seal leak)
P0994.en: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit Low
P0994.desc: The signal of pressure sensor or switch F stays low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. With a normally closed switch as described by Sonnax for GM's valve body modules, low means the contacts stay closed, so the module sees no pressure where pressure should be, or the signal wire is shorted to ground. GM's equivalent for switch E, P0989, flags a low signal when commanded pressure is 50 kPa or less and handles it as Special No Trip without MIL; Saab's 9-4X text gives 0 V as the low state and 12 V as high.
