CARB requires these inverter cooling outputs to be checked for circuit faults. Open and high faults are P0B38 and P0B3A; running faults use P0C74 and P2D05 ff.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Pump control input open so the line floats high
Controller software misjudging the circuit, fixed by update
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty
P0B3A.en: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P0B3A.desc: P0B3A sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B stays higher than expected, typically a short to battery voltage on the command line or, with some driver designs, an open pump input that floats high. The module then cannot switch the pump as requested. No manufacturer documents P0B3A publicly. As reference points, FCA has a pump B on its 4xe models with the performance code P0C74, and Ford lists the pump A high code P0A07 among PCM codes fixed by a battery controller update on the 2020 Explorer and Aviator hybrids. CARB requires inverter thermal management outputs to be monitored. Open and low faults are P0B38 and P0B39. Overheating protection may reduce power.

causes_en: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent fault in the flexible printed circuit to the battery controller (Ford Mach-E)
Sensor software misreading inverter noise, fixed by update (Honda)
Internal failure of the traction battery requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
P0B3B.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit
P0B3B.desc: Voltage sense A to Z and beyond are the cell or cell-group sense channels of the battery monitoring electronics, unlike the pack voltage sense codes P0ABA and P0B14 ff, which measure the whole pack. P0B3B is the circuit code for channel A. GM uses it in the battery energy control module as an open sense line check: neighbouring cell readings differ by 1.3 V or more, or a cell reads under 36 mV with balancing on, or a splice reads over 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V), for 0.6 s; Type A, one trip. Ford stores P0B3B with other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV and 2023 Mach-E; Honda's 2014-2015 Accord Hybrid used it for a cell voltage sensor fault caused by inverter noise.

causes_en: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack
P0B3C.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Range/Performance
P0B3C.desc: P0B3C flags a cell voltage channel A that reads plausible values but does not follow the other cells. GM runs this check in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 as a stuck-in-range test: while the average cell voltage moves by at least 0.005 V in one direction between samples, channel A must move as well; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip. FCA names the code Voltage Sense 1 Circuit Performance on the Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid and fixes it, together with P0B41 and further channels, by reprogramming the battery pack control module. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes. The system limits battery power or shuts down hybrid operation.

causes_en: Battery pack control module software, fixed by update (Ram eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
P0B3D.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low
P0B3D.desc: P0B3D sets when cell voltage channel A reads below the lowest value a real cell can have, which points to the measurement rather than the cell. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, provided no open sense line, communication or balancing fault is active. FCA lists P0B3D as Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low on the 2019 Ram 1500 with eTorque mild hybrid, next to the pack-level code P0ABA, and cures it with a battery pack control module update. A genuinely low cell is reported with separate cell voltage codes. Expect reduced or blocked hybrid assist.

causes_en: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA)
Open sense line letting the input float high
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
P0B3E.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit High
P0B3E.desc: P0B3E sets when cell voltage channel A reads above any value a healthy lithium-ion cell reaches, so the reading is treated as a sensing fault. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip. FCA uses the code on the 2021 Jeep Wrangler 4xe as Voltage Sense 1 Circuit High and on the 2019 Ram 1500 eTorque as Voltage Sense A Circuit High; in both cases a battery pack control module update removes a false MIL. A truly overcharged cell sets separate cell voltage high codes such as P0DE7 instead. Low, range and open faults are P0B3D, P0B3C and P0B3B. The car limits battery use.

causes_en: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines
P0B3F.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B3F.desc: P0B3F is reserved for a cell voltage channel A that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents P0B3F publicly. GM's 2019 tables show how the siblings on the same channel work: an open line test (P0B3B), a stuck-in-range test against the other cells (P0B3C) and fixed limits of 0.2 V and 4.8 V (P0B3D, P0B3E); an erratic test would watch for implausible jumps between samples. CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored as input components, with fault codes pinpointing the smallest replaceable unit. Loose connections at the cell taps or the monitoring board are the usual suspects. Hybrid power may be limited.

causes_en: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, e-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
P0B40.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit
P0B40.desc: P0B40 is the circuit code of cell voltage sense channel B, the second cell or cell group the battery monitoring electronics measures; pack-level voltage uses P0ABA and P0B14 ff instead. GM applies the same open sense line test as on channel A: a 1.3 V jump between neighbouring cells, under 36 mV with balancing on, or splice voltage above 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V) for 0.6 s, Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B40 among the open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV, where the fix is a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and e-Transit, where an intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller is to blame. Expect no start or no charging.

causes_en: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack
P0B41.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B41.desc: P0B41 reports that cell voltage channel B gives values inside the normal range that fail a plausibility check against the other cells. In GM's 2019 tables Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 compares sample-to-sample changes: if the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V while channel B stays unchanged, a failure is counted, and 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip, with system voltage above 10.2 V. FCA calls it Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Performance on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and lists it with P0B3C and further channels in battery pack control module update bulletins. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults of channel B are P0B40, P0B42, P0B43 and P0B44.

causes_en: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
P0B42.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
P0B42.desc: P0B42 sets when cell voltage channel B reads implausibly low, below what any usable cell would show. GM's battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only when no open sense line, slave communication or balancing fault is present. FCA uses P0B42 as Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Low on the 2022 Grand Wagoneer and Wagoneer with the 5.7 L eTorque mild hybrid; its bulletin calls the MIL false, mentions inoperative start-stop and a car that seems to run on fuel only, and prescribes a battery pack control module update. Cells that are actually weak set separate cell voltage codes. High and range faults are P0B43 and P0B41.

causes_en: Open sense line letting the input float high
Battery controller software misreading the channel
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed
P0B43.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit High
P0B43.desc: P0B43 sets when cell voltage channel B reads higher than a lithium-ion cell can physically reach in service, so the controller blames the measurement path. GM documents the criteria for its battery energy control module: cell voltage B at 4.8 V or above for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, with open sense line, communication and balancing faults ruled out first. Beyond GM, no manufacturer documents P0B43 publicly; FCA's sister code P0B3E for channel A shows that software in the battery controller can cause such readings. CARB treats battery voltage sensors as monitored input components. Overcharged cells use separate cell voltage codes. Low, range and open faults of channel B are P0B42, P0B41 and P0B40.

causes_en: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines
P0B44.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B44.desc: P0B44 is the J2012 slot for a cell voltage channel B whose reading jumps or drops out for short moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents P0B44 publicly. For orientation, GM's 2019 tables check channel B for open sense lines (P0B40), frozen values compared with the other cells (P0B41) and fixed limits of 0.2 V and 4.8 V (P0B42, P0B43); an erratic monitor would add a test for implausible steps between samples. CARB requires the storage system's voltage sensors to be monitored as inputs and faults to be pinpointed to the smallest replaceable unit. Typical causes are vibration-loosened cell taps and connectors on the monitoring board. Warnings may come and go with driving conditions.

causes_en: Open cell sense tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel C
Intermittent flexible printed circuit between cells and battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
P0B45.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit
P0B45.desc: Voltage sense C is the third cell or cell-group measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics, not a pack voltage input like P0ABA. P0B45 reports an electrical break in that channel. GM's battery energy control module sets it when its open sense line test fails for 0.6 s: adjacent cell readings at least 1.3 V apart, a cell below 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (bus bar splice 0.5 V); Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B45 with the other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid, fixed by a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit, where an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit is blamed. Expect no start or no charging.

causes_en: Battery controller software misjudging the channel, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Measuring chip input for channel C stuck at a constant value
High-resistance cell tap damping the channel C signal
P0B46.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
P0B46.desc: With P0B46 the channel C wiring is intact; the value on it looks plausible but no longer behaves like a real cell. GM's 2019 tables run the test in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2: whenever the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V in one direction, channel C has to follow; if it stays frozen in 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms, the code sets, Type A. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt uses a window of 7 out of 8 seconds instead. Chrysler calls the code Voltage Sense 3 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica plug-in hybrid and cures it by reflashing the battery pack control module. So before opening the battery, check the controller software level.

causes_en: Sense lines of channel C shorted to each other or to a neighbouring tap
Failed measuring input in the battery monitoring module
Loose or corroded block connector shared by blocks 3 and 4 (GM two-mode)
P0B47.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
P0B47.desc: P0B47 is stored when channel C delivers a voltage too low to come from a working cell or block, so the controller blames the measurement rather than the battery. GM documents two implementations. On lithium-ion packs the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, one trip, unless an open sense line, communication or balancing fault is already active. On the 2012 Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra two-mode hybrids channel C is nickel-metal hydride block 3; there block 3 and block 4 must both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Shorted sense lines or a failed measuring input are the usual suspects.

causes_en: Channel C sense line touching a tap of higher potential
Failed measuring input or reference in the monitoring electronics
Monitoring software fault, check for controller updates
P0B48.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit High
P0B48.desc: No healthy lithium-ion cell reaches 4.8 V, which is why GM's battery energy control module treats a channel C reading of 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window as a sensing fault and stores P0B48, Type A, one trip. On the 2012 two-mode full-size hybrids the threshold is scaled to a nickel-metal hydride block: block 3 above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Because the controller cannot trust the reading, it usually narrows the allowed charge and discharge power to protect the cells. For the driver this means less electric assist and possibly no plug-in charging. A cell that is really overcharged triggers separate cell voltage codes, not this one.

causes_en: Loose crimp or connector on the channel C sense line
Cracked solder joint on the cell monitoring board
Electrical noise from the inverter coupling into the sense line
P0B49.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B49.desc: P0B49 is reserved for a channel C signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing for good. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses the other four channel C codes, has no erratic test for it in its published tables. A technician would start from the freeze frame and log cell voltage C next to its neighbours while flexing the module harness, because a loose crimp or a cracked solder joint on the monitoring board shows up as spikes that a permanent test misses. CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored like any input and faults to be tied to the smallest replaceable unit. Warnings may come and go.

causes_en: Open channel D sense tap or connector (code set alone)
Faulty BECM flexible printed circuit affecting several channels (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV)
P0B4A.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit
P0B4A.desc: P0B4A is the open-circuit code of cell sense channel D, the fourth measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics. GM checks it in the battery energy control module with the same open sense line logic as the other channels: a gap of 1.3 V or more between adjacent cells, under 36 mV on a cell being balanced, or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V at a bus bar, for 0.6 s, Type A. For diagnosis, the pattern matters: if P0B4A stands alone, inspect the channel D tap and its connector; if Ford's whole open-line group from P0B3B upwards is set, as on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV or the 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit, a common cause such as the BECM flex cable or the battery itself is more likely.

causes_en: Outdated battery controller software (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Block or cell voltage measurement drifting away from the pack voltage
Measuring input of channel D frozen at a constant value
P0B4B.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance
P0B4B.desc: How the plausibility of channel D is judged depends on the pack. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids the battery pack control module multiplies block 4 by 20 and compares it with the pack voltage; a gap above 70 V in 160 of 170 samples sets P0B4B, Type B, two trips. Later lithium-ion packs compare movement instead: in the 2016 Cadillac ELR channel D must move with the average cell voltage, checked every 200 ms with 20 failures in 40 samples, Type A, and the 2019 tables use 35 of 40 samples. Chrysler lists the code as Voltage Sense 4 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica plug-in hybrid and fixes it with BPCM software. Separate codes cover open, low and high faults.

causes_en: Short between channel D sense line and a neighbouring line
Defective input on the cell monitoring module
Corroded tap shared by blocks 4 and 5 (GM two-mode)
P0B4C.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Low
P0B4C.desc: From the driver's seat P0B4C looks like a battery problem: the hybrid warning comes on and electric power is cut back. Technically it is a measuring fault on cell channel D, whose reading has fallen below what even a deeply discharged cell would show. GM's battery energy control module uses 0.2 V or less, held for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and skips the test while open sense line or communication faults are active. On the 2012 two-mode full-size hybrids, channel D is block 4, and the code needs blocks 4 and 5 both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. A genuinely weak cell produces separate cell voltage codes, so P0B4C points to wiring or the monitoring module.

causes_en: Channel D sense lead contacting a tap of higher potential
Damaged measuring input in the monitoring electronics
Moisture or contamination on the monitoring board creating leakage paths
P0B4D.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit High
P0B4D.desc: P0B4D sets when cell sense channel D reports more voltage than the cell or block behind it can deliver. GM's limits are 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s on lithium-ion packs (battery energy control module, Type A, one trip) and above 23 V for block 4 of the 2012 two-mode hybrids (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips). A practical first check is live data: if channel D sits far above its neighbours while the pack voltage and the other channels look normal, the fault is in the sense path, not in the cells. Typical findings are a sense lead that contacts a higher tap or a damaged measuring input. The controller limits power until the code is repaired.

causes_en: Connector or tap losing contact under vibration
Solder joint or crimp cracked by thermal cycling
P0B4E.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B4E.desc: P0B4E completes the five-code set of cell channel D. Where P0B4A means a lasting open circuit, P0B4B a frozen or implausible value and P0B4C or P0B4D a reading beyond fixed limits, this code is meant for short, irregular dropouts and spikes. No manufacturer documents P0B4E publicly, and GM's published hybrid tables, which cover the other four, contain no such test. CARB obliges manufacturers to monitor the storage system's voltage sensors as input components. In practice, intermittent sense faults trace back to vibration, thermal cycling and connectors that only lose contact on rough roads, which is why the fault often cannot be reproduced in the workshop.

causes_en: Internal failure of the high-voltage battery (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Broken channel E sense lead, splice or bus bar contact
P0B4F.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit
P0B4F.desc: Cell sense channel E is the fifth measuring path between the battery cells and the monitoring electronics; P0B4F means the controller sees it as electrically open. Ford's experience shows how serious this can be: on 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids P0B4F appears among up to fourteen open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C with a no-start condition, and the bulletin prescribes replacing the high-voltage battery. On the 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit the same family points to an intermittent flexible circuit at the BECM. GM's BECM logic needs 0.6 s of an open-line pattern, such as adjacent cells 1.3 V apart or a balanced cell under 36 mV, and stores the code as Type A.

causes_en: Battery pack control module software, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel E reading frozen in the measuring chip
Block voltage measurement drifting from pack voltage (GM two-mode)
P0B50.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Range/Performance
P0B50.desc: On the 2020 Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid P0B50 is called Voltage Sense 5 Circuit Performance and rarely comes alone: the FCA bulletin lists it with the other sense channels, contactor stuck codes, a long precharge time and wake-up circuit faults, all cured by updating the battery pack control module. Some owners also notice that scheduled charging fails because the pack does not wake up. GM defines the check precisely: channel E must change in step with the average cell voltage, and a stuck reading in 35 of 40 samples sets the code, Type A; the 2012 two-mode hybrids instead flag block 5 when 20 times its value differs from the pack voltage by over 70 V. Open, low and high faults are separate codes.

causes_en: Channel E sense line shorted to its neighbour
Faulty input on the cell monitoring slave board
Pin backed out of the monitoring harness connector
P0B51.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Low
P0B51.desc: P0B51 tells that cell sense channel E reads near zero. GM's battery energy control module only runs this check under clear conditions: the module is in run, crank or accessory mode, the second protection self-test is not running, and no slave communication, open sense line, balancing or internal performance fault is active. Then a reading of 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s in a 2 s window sets the code, Type A, one trip. The order matters for diagnosis: an open sense line or a lost slave board would be reported first by their own codes. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids channel E is block 5, set when blocks 5 and 6 both drop below 2 V, Type B. Electric operation is then restricted.

causes_en: Channel E sense line contacting a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the monitoring module
P0B52.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit High
P0B52.desc: The threshold behind P0B52 is chosen so that only a measurement error can reach it. A lithium-ion cell is fully charged at roughly 4.2 V, yet GM's battery energy control module waits for 4.8 V or more on channel E, for 1.4 s within 2 s, before storing the code as Type A, one trip. On the nickel-metal hydride packs of the 2012 two-mode trucks and SUVs the corresponding limit is 23 V for block 5, confirmed in 15 of 20 samples and stored as Type B. Since a false high reading could make the controller stop charging early or misjudge balancing, power and charging are restricted. Real overvoltage of a cell is reported by its own cell voltage codes.

causes_en: Intermittent contact at the channel E tap or connector
Chafed sense lead touching briefly under movement
Marginal component on the monitoring board
P0B53.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B53.desc: P0B53 belongs to cell sense channel E and describes a signal that is sometimes fine and sometimes not. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, for example, covers channel E with open, range, low and high tests but publishes no erratic test, so the meaning rests on the J2012 wording and on CARB's rule that every voltage sensor of the energy storage system must be monitored. For the workshop the useful evidence is the freeze frame plus a recorded drive: brief steps in cell voltage E that no other channel shares point to a contact problem on that one path. The driver sees warnings that clear and return, sometimes with a short loss of electric power.

causes_en: Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit built to Dec 2023)
Open channel F tap or splice
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)
P0B54.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit
P0B54.desc: Ford's 2024 special service message for the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit is the most instructive case for P0B54: vehicles built up to 9 December 2023 could store this and the other open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B5E, show the wrench light, refuse to start or charge, or display Stop Safely Now, and the cause was an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable rather than the cells. The 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV shows the same code with a battery replacement as remedy. P0B54 itself means sense channel F is electrically open; GM confirms this with neighbouring cells at least 1.3 V apart, a balanced cell under 36 mV or a splice above 0.1 V for 0.6 s, Type A.

causes_en: Battery controller software, fixed by update (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel F measuring input stuck or slow to respond
Increased resistance in the channel F tap or connector
P0B55.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Range/Performance
P0B55.desc: P0B55 is the plausibility code of cell channel F: the signal exists and lies inside its range, yet it does not move like the rest of the pack. On the 2016 Chevrolet Volt the vehicle integration control module checks whether channel F moves in the same direction as the average cell voltage, failing it after 7 seconds in an 8 second window, Type A; GM's 2019 tables use 35 failures in 40 samples of 100 ms. The 2012 two-mode hybrids compare block 6, times 20, with the pack voltage and allow 70 V. Chrysler labels it Voltage Sense 6 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica PHEV, the highest channel in that bulletin, and resolves it with BPCM software.

causes_en: Fault in the sense wire shared by blocks 6 and 7 (GM two-mode)
Channel F sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Failed input on the cell monitoring electronics
P0B56.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Low
P0B56.desc: The GM two-mode hybrids of 2012, Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra, show a detail of P0B56 that lithium-ion packs lack. Their nickel-metal hydride pack is read in blocks, channel F being block 6, and the battery pack control module sets the code only when block 6 and block 7 both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, two trips; a shared sense wire between the blocks is the obvious suspect then. In GM's lithium-ion systems the battery energy control module uses 0.2 V or less on cell voltage F for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. In both cases the controller assumes a failed measurement and reduces battery use until repair.

causes_en: Channel F sense lead touching a higher potential
Measuring input or reference fault in the module
P0B57.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit High
P0B57.desc: P0B57 stands for an implausibly high value on cell sense channel F, as opposed to P0B56 for an implausibly low one and P0B55 for a frozen value. GM uses fixed upper limits: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the battery energy control module of its lithium-ion systems (Type A, one trip), and above 23 V for block 6 in the 2012 two-mode trucks (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips). Both values lie clearly above what the cell or block can physically reach, so a real overcharge is not the explanation. Look for a sense lead in contact with a higher potential or for a measuring fault inside the module, and expect limited battery power and charging until then.

causes_en: Sense tap of channel F loosening under vibration
Damaged section of the flexible sense circuit
P0B58.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B58.desc: P0B58 is reserved for an erratic signal on cell sense channel F, and the honest state is short: no manufacturer documents this code publicly. The neighbouring codes are well covered; Ford and GM use the open circuit code P0B54, GM and Chrysler the range code P0B55, GM the fixed low and high limits. CARB demands monitoring of all battery voltage sensors of the storage system. An erratic test would catch sudden steps between successive samples that stay inside the low and high limits. Likely causes are a sense tap that loosens under vibration or a damaged section of the flexible circuit, and the symptoms typically come and go with road conditions and temperature.

causes_en: Open channel G tap, splice or bus bar contact
Intermittent BECM flexible circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)
P0B59.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit
P0B59.desc: Voltage sense G is the seventh cell measuring channel; how many cells or groups it covers depends on how the manufacturer splits the pack among monitoring chips. P0B59 is its open-circuit code. Two Ford bulletins name it: the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV, where the open-line group up to P0B7C leads to a battery replacement, and the 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit, where it is blamed on the BECM flexible printed circuit. GM's BECM sets it after 0.6 s of an open-line pattern such as adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a balanced cell under 36 mV or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V, Type A. If several channels report at once, suspect a shared connection first.

causes_en: Channel G measuring input frozen or drifting
Block 7 reading out of line with pack voltage (GM two-mode)
Monitoring software issue, check for updates
P0B5A.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Range/Performance
P0B5A.desc: P0B5A asks whether cell channel G behaves like a real cell. GM answers that question in three ways across its programmes. The 2019 hybrid tables expect channel G to trend with the average cell voltage and set the code after 35 frozen samples out of 40, Type A. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt uses a 7 of 8 second window, the Cadillac ELR 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms. The 2012 two-mode trucks compare block 7, multiplied by 20, with the pack voltage and fail it beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. The Chrysler Pacifica bulletin stops at channel 6, so no other maker is documented for this code. A frozen or drifting measurement input is the most common cause.

causes_en: Channel G sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Damaged or backed-out pin in the monitoring connector
Failed measuring input on the monitoring module
P0B5B.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Low
P0B5B.desc: When P0B5B appears, the battery controller has seen cell sense channel G at a level no usable cell would show, and it shuts down or restricts electric operation to stay on the safe side. GM documents the trigger for its lithium-ion systems as cell voltage G at or below 0.2 V for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, with the test held off while communication, open line or balancing faults are active. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids channel G is block 7, and the code needs blocks 7 and 8 together under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Sense wiring, connector pins and the monitoring input deserve attention before the cells, which have their own cell voltage codes.

causes_en: Channel G sense lead touching a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the module
Contamination or moisture on the monitoring board
P0B5C.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit High
P0B5C.desc: P0B5C marks an out-of-range high reading on cell sense channel G. For a technician the quickest plausibility check is arithmetic: the sum of all cell or block readings should match the pack voltage, so a single channel that reads far too high while the total stays normal is a sensing fault. GM formalises the limits as 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the battery energy control module of its lithium-ion systems, Type A, one trip, and as more than 23 V for block 7 of the 2012 two-mode trucks and SUVs, 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Overcharged cells are flagged by other codes. Until the fault is fixed, battery power and charging are limited.

causes_en: Marginal contact at the channel G tap or connector
Sense harness under strain, losing contact with pack movement
P0B5D.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B5D.desc: P0B5D is the J2012 code for an unsteady signal on cell sense channel G, a reading that flickers or drops out for moments without staying beyond a limit. No manufacturer documents P0B5D publicly. For orientation: GM monitors channel G with an open-line test (P0B59), a frozen-value comparison against the average cell voltage (P0B5A) and fixed low and high limits (P0B5B, P0B5C), but lists no erratic monitor. CARB requires the battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored and faults to be traced to the smallest replaceable unit. For the owner the result is a warning that may vanish after a restart and reappear later; the root cause is usually a marginal contact.

causes_en: Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable at the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit 2023)
Open cell tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel H
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
P0B5E.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit
P0B5E.desc: P0B5E flags a broken measuring path on voltage sense H, the eighth cell tap channel read by the battery monitoring electronics. In GM's 2019 tables the battery energy control module runs an open sense line test within a 0.6 s window: neighbouring cells diverging by 1.3 V or more, a cell under 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a bus bar splice) sets it as Type A. Ford names P0B5E in two bulletins: a no-start on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid, repaired with a new traction battery, and the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit, where H is the last code of the affected range and an intermittent flexible printed circuit at the BECM is blamed. Starting and charging may fail.

causes_en: Block or cell voltage input for channel H drifting away from the true value
Measuring chip input stuck at a constant value
Faulty pack voltage reference distorting the comparison
P0B5F.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Range/Performance
P0B5F.desc: With P0B5F the channel H wiring is intact, but the value it delivers does not fit the rest of the battery. GM runs two quite different plausibility tests. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra) channel H is nickel-metal hydride block 8 of 20; the battery pack control module multiplies blocks 8 and 9 by twenty and fails the test when both differ from the measured pack voltage by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B, two trips, with active pack voltage codes P0ABB to P0ABD blocking it. Lithium-ion systems in the 2019 tables look for a frozen reading instead: if H stays put while the average cell voltage trends, 35 of 40 samples set the code, Type A.

causes_en: Channel H sense lead shorted to ground or to the next lower tap
Failed measuring input on the cell monitoring board
Cell or block on channel H actually collapsed
P0B60.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Low
P0B60.desc: P0B60 means channel H reports less voltage than any healthy cell or block could hold, so the measurement itself is suspect. GM publishes three variants. Lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module (2016 and 2019 tables) trip at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, provided no open-line, communication or balancing fault is already stored. The BAS Plus mild hybrid in table 13OBDG05C uses a cell sense line threshold of 1.4 V and needs 7 failures out of 10, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks compare blocks 8 and 9, both under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Typical culprits are a sense lead shorted to ground or a failed input on the monitoring board.

causes_en: Channel H sense lead in contact with a higher cell tap
Lost reference connection letting the measuring input float
Internal fault of the cell monitoring chip
P0B61.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit High
P0B61.desc: A lithium-ion cell cannot sit much above about 4.2 V, so when channel H reads 4.8 V or more the GM battery energy control module concludes the sense circuit is wrong and stores P0B61 after 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets the same code at more than 4.65 V on the cell sense line in 7 of 10 samples, Type B, while the 2012 two-mode hybrids treat H as nickel-metal hydride block 8 and only object above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. A high reading usually comes from a sense lead touching a higher potential or from a monitoring input that floats when a reference connection is lost. Unlike P0B60 the controller here suspects overvoltage, so charging is typically blocked.

causes_en: Intermittent contact at the channel H connector or flexible circuit
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board
Inverter noise coupling into the sense line
P0B62.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B62.desc: P0B62 describes a channel H signal that jumps or cuts out for moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. It is worth noting that Ford's 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit bulletin attributes an intermittent flexible printed circuit fault to the open-circuit code P0B5E, not to P0B62, and GM's published tables contain no erratic monitor for channel H at all. The code is therefore defined by SAE J2012 but appears to remain unused in practice. CARB demands that battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system be checked like every other input. If it ever appears, logging channel H next to channels G and I while moving the harness is the sensible first step.

causes_en: Broken channel I sense wire, crimp or cell tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Corroded or loose connector at the cell monitoring board
P0B63.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit
P0B63.desc: Channel I is the ninth sense input of the battery monitoring chain, and P0B63 reports that its circuit is open. GM shows how differently this can be detected. The BAS Plus mild hybrid (table 13OBDG05C) watches the voltage of line N and its neighbour N-1: if both drop under 1.4 V and change by more than 0.5 V within 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples set the code, Type B. The newer battery energy control module of the 2019 tables relies on neighbouring cells drifting 1.3 V apart, a balancing test below 36 mV or a splice voltage, all within 0.6 s, Type A. Ford lists P0B63 among the open-line codes behind a no-start on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid and replaces the traction battery.

causes_en: Channel I measuring input frozen at a constant value
Battery controller software misjudging the channel
High-resistance cell tap damping the signal
P0B64.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Range/Performance
P0B64.desc: P0B64 is a rationality fault: channel I is connected and reads a believable number, yet it does not move with the other cells. GM's 2016 Chevrolet Volt compares the movement of each cell with the average; if channel I does not follow when the average moves by more than 0.022 V, 7 out of 8 seconds fail the check, Type A. The 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 tables keep the idea but count samples, 35 failures out of 40 at 100 ms. On the 2012 two-mode trucks the same code belongs to nickel-metal hydride block 9, whose scaled value must stay within 70 V of the pack voltage. Because the input is alive but stuck or drifting, a software update or the monitoring board is a likelier fix than wiring.

causes_en: Channel I sense lead shorted to ground or a lower tap
Connector fault affecting adjacent blocks 9 and 10 (two-mode)
Failed measuring input in the battery controller
P0B65.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Low
P0B65.desc: The 2012 GM two-mode hybrids show a detail worth knowing for P0B65: their battery pack control module only declares channel I, nickel-metal hydride block 9, too low when block 9 and its neighbour block 10 both read under 2 V, and only after 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms; the fault is Type B and needs two trips. A single weak block alone therefore does not set it. GM's lithium-ion controllers judge each cell on its own, setting P0B65 at 0.2 V or less held for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, as long as no open-line or communication fault has priority. The BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 1.4 V and 7 of 10 samples. In all cases the reading is too low to be a real cell.

causes_en: Channel I lead touching a higher-potential tap
Open reference or ground of the measuring chip
Genuinely overcharged cell after a charging control fault
P0B66.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit High
P0B66.desc: When channel I claims a voltage above what its cell or block can physically reach, the controller stores P0B66. The thresholds GM publishes depend on chemistry and architecture: lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module set it at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2012 two-mode trucks, which measure nickel-metal hydride block 9 rather than single cells, above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Every limit sits clearly above normal full charge, so a real overcharged cell is unlikely. Look first for a sense lead touching the next tap up or for a measuring input that has lost its reference.

causes_en: Sense contact on channel I opening under vibration or heat
Corroded terminal in the module connector
P0B67.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B67.desc: SAE J2012 reserves P0B67 for an unsteady signal on channel I, meaning readings that spike, drop and recover. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the GM tables that define the other four channel I codes includes an erratic test. The fault picture would sit between an open circuit (P0B63) and a frozen value (P0B64): the line works most of the time but loses contact under vibration, heat or current load. CARB requires battery voltage sensors to be monitored as inputs of the energy storage system, which explains why the code exists at all. For diagnosis, record cell voltage I with a scan tool during a drive and compare its noise with neighbouring channels H and J.

causes_en: Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Open sense wire or cell tap on channel J
Bad bus bar or splice connection near channel J
P0B68.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit
P0B68.desc: For owners of a 2019 or 2020 Ford Fusion plug-in hybrid, P0B68 is best known from bulletin 23-2039: the car will not start, the battery energy control module stores one or more open sense line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C, and the prescribed repair is a complete high-voltage traction battery. Technically the code says that the tenth measuring channel, J, has lost its connection to the cells. GM describes the test in detail for its lithium-ion packs: within 0.6 s it looks for adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a cell under 36 mV while being balanced, or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V, and sets P0B68 as Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid uses a 1.4 V and 0.5 V rate-of-change test, Type B.

causes_en: Channel J input reacting too little to real voltage changes
Corroded or high-resistance cell tap
Calibration error in the battery controller
P0B69.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Range/Performance
P0B69.desc: P0B69 is set when channel J is electrically present but its readings do not behave plausibly. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid explains the logic most clearly: once the average cell voltage moves by more than 0.045 V, the cell under test must move in the same direction and by at least half as much; 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, two trips. The 2019 lithium-ion tables use a tighter trigger of 0.022 V and 35 of 40 samples, Type A. On the 2012 two-mode trucks the code belongs to nickel-metal hydride block 10 and compares its scaled value with the pack voltage. Neither Ford nor Chrysler publishes this channel; Chrysler's Pacifica bulletin stops at sense 6.

causes_en: Channel J lead chafed through and shorted to ground
Damaged measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell on channel J internally shorted
P0B6A.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Low
P0B6A.desc: A reading of almost zero on channel J points to the measurement, not to the cell, and that is what P0B6A records. In GM's lithium-ion systems (2016 and 2019 tables) the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. The interesting part is what it ignores: while a module communication loss, an open sense line code, a balancing fault or an internal module fault is active, P0B6A stays silent so that the root cause is stored first. The 2012 two-mode hybrids look at nickel-metal hydride block 10 together with block 11, both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Expect reduced or no electric drive until the circuit is repaired.

causes_en: Channel J lead shorted to a higher block or cell tap
Faulty measuring input in the battery pack control module
P0B6B.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit High
P0B6B.desc: On GM's 2012 two-mode hybrid trucks the battery is divided into 20 nickel-metal hydride blocks, and channel J is block 10. The battery pack control module samples it every 100 ms while the 12 V supply is between 9 and 18 V; if block 10 reports more than 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, P0B6B is stored as Type B, so the MIL comes on after the second trip. Lithium-ion GM packs check single cells instead and set the code at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A; the BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 4.65 V. Since these limits lie well above any real charge level, a wiring short to a higher tap or a faulty sense input is the expected finding, not an overcharged battery.

causes_en: Marginal contact in the channel J harness or connector
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring electronics
P0B6C.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B6C.desc: No manufacturer documents P0B6C publicly. The code stands for a channel J signal that is unstable, with brief jumps or dropouts, as opposed to the steady faults covered by P0B68 to P0B6B. CARB section 1968.2 requires that the individual electronic inputs of a hybrid energy storage system, battery voltage sensors expressly included, be monitored for circuit and rationality faults; erratic behaviour is one way such a fault can show. GM, which publishes tests for the other four channel J codes, lists none for this one. For the driver it would mean a warning that comes and goes, possibly with short power cuts. A cable or connector with marginal contact is the most plausible cause.

causes_en: Loose or corroded bus bar connection at the channel K tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Broken sense wire between cells and monitoring board
P0B6D.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit
P0B6D.desc: P0B6D marks an open circuit on voltage sense K, the eleventh cell measuring channel. GM has used the code since its first published hybrid tables: in 2011 the open-line test already checked bus bar voltages, flagging more than 0.7 V. The 2019 battery energy control module refines it into seven cases, among them adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a cell under 36 mV with balancing active and splice voltages over 0.1 V, all judged in a 0.6 s window and set as Type A. Ford counts P0B6D among the open sense line codes that leave a 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid unable to start and fixes it by replacing the traction battery. Before any pack work, the high-voltage system has to be disabled by trained staff.

causes_en: Block or cell voltage measurement of channel K out of calibration
Pack voltage sensor reading off, distorting the comparison
Measuring input stuck at one value
P0B6E.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Range/Performance
P0B6E.desc: In a nickel-metal hydride pack with 20 equal blocks, twenty times one block voltage should roughly equal the whole pack voltage. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids use exactly this for P0B6E, assigned to block 11: the battery pack control module checks blocks 11 and 12, and if both scaled values deviate from the pack voltage sensor by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is set, Type B. The test only runs with the contactors closed for over 200 ms and no pack voltage fault active. GM's lithium-ion controllers judge channel K differently, as a frozen value that fails to follow the average cell voltage (35 of 40 samples, Type A, in the 2019 tables). No other manufacturer publishes it.

causes_en: Channel K sense line shorted to ground or a lower tap
Failed measuring input in the battery interface module
Blown protective element in the sense line
P0B6F.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Low
P0B6F.desc: GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid, the eAssist system in table 13OBDG05C, gives P0B6F a simple rule: if the cell sense line for channel K measures below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples at 200 ms while the 12 V supply is above 8.8 V, the code is stored as Type B, two trips. Since a lithium-ion cell in use never falls that low, the value must come from a short or a failed input. GM's later battery energy control modules work with 0.2 V and a 1.4 s window, Type A, and the 2012 two-mode trucks with nickel-metal hydride blocks 11 and 12, both under 2 V. The driver typically sees a hybrid warning and loses electric assist; the engine takes over more of the work.

causes_en: Channel K lead in contact with a higher tap
Floating measuring input after loss of its lower reference
Cell monitoring chip fault
P0B70.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit High
P0B70.desc: P0B70 says that cell voltage K reads too high to be genuine. GM's 2019 battery energy control module sets it at 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault with immediate MIL, and only when no communication loss, open sense line or internal module fault takes precedence. The same principle appears with other numbers elsewhere at GM: 4.65 V and 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, 23 V for nickel-metal hydride block 11 on the 2012 two-mode trucks. The difference to P0B6F is the direction, not the location: a high reading typically comes from a lead touching a higher potential, a low one from a short to a lower one. Charging is usually blocked while it is active.

causes_en: Fretting corrosion on channel K connector terminals
Sense harness under strain losing contact with movement
P0B71.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B71.desc: P0B71 belongs to the unsteady fault type: the channel K reading flickers or drops out momentarily without staying beyond a fixed limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Neither GM's hybrid tables from 2011 to 2019 nor the Ford and Chrysler bulletins on cell sense codes mention it, although they cover the open, plausibility, low and high codes of neighbouring channels. Its basis is the CARB requirement to monitor battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system as input components. In a workshop the approach would be a wiggle test on the module harness while watching cell voltage K live, plus a check of the connector terminals for fretting corrosion.

causes_en: Open sense lead, crimp or cell tap on channel L
Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
High-resistance splice or bus bar joint
P0B72.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit
P0B72.desc: P0B72 reports an open circuit on voltage sense L, the twelfth channel. One detail sets it apart from its neighbours: GM's 2011 hybrid tables list every open sense line code from P0B3B upward except P0B72 (and P0B90), so the early system did not use it, while L's range, low and high codes were present. Later GM tables include it. The BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it when lines N and N-1 fall below 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2019 battery energy control module uses its adjacent-cell, balancing and splice tests within 0.6 s, Type A. Ford's Fusion plug-in hybrid bulletin for 2019-2020 includes P0B72 and replaces the traction battery.

causes_en: Channel L input not following real cell voltage changes
Battery controller software or calibration issue
Corroded cell tap slowing the signal
P0B73.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Range/Performance
P0B73.desc: Channel L delivers a value, but P0B73 tells you that the value is not credible. GM checks this in three ways. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt and the 2019 lithium-ion systems test whether cell L moves in the same direction as the average once that average changes by more than 0.022 V, failing 7 of 8 seconds or 35 of 40 samples respectively, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid demands at least half of the average movement, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks treat L as nickel-metal hydride block 12 and compare blocks 12 and 13, scaled by twenty, with the pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. A battery controller reflash or measuring board repair is the usual remedy.

causes_en: Channel L sense lead shorted to a lower potential
Defective measuring input in the battery controller
Cell or block on channel L actually failed
P0B74.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Low
P0B74.desc: P0B74 is set when channel L reads implausibly low. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where L is nickel-metal hydride block 12 of 20, the battery pack control module needs both block 12 and block 13 under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples before it stores the code as Type B; no battery control module fault P0A1F may be active. For lithium-ion packs GM's 2016 and 2019 tables use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and the BAS Plus mild hybrid 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. A short of the sense lead to a lower potential, a defective monitoring input or, more rarely, a cell that has really collapsed are the candidates. The vehicle will normally restrict electric operation.

causes_en: Channel L lead touching a higher tap
Floating measuring input after an open reference line
Real overvoltage of the cell after a charging fault
P0B75.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit High
P0B75.desc: With P0B75 the battery controller rejects channel L because it reads above any value a real cell or block can reach. GM's lithium-ion systems in the 2016 Volt and the 2019 tables set it at 4.8 V or more over 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On the 2012 two-mode trucks, block 12 must exceed 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, sampled every 100 ms, before the code is stored as Type B. The pairing with P0B74 helps diagnosis: low points to a short downward, high to contact with a higher tap or a floating input. While it is active, charging and regeneration are normally limited to protect the pack.

causes_en: Intermittent contact at the channel L cell tap
Fatigued sense harness wire
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board
P0B76.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B76.desc: P0B76 closes the channel L group and covers an erratic signal: values that jump or vanish briefly while the circuit otherwise works. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, the only maker with public tables for L, defines open, plausibility, low and high tests for this channel but no erratic test, and the Ford bulletins name only the open-circuit code P0B72. CARB obliges manufacturers to monitor the battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system, which is the regulatory background of the code. Practically, an intermittent contact at the channel L tap, a fatigued harness or a cracked board joint would produce this picture. Warnings may disappear after a restart and return.

causes_en: Open or corroded tap of sense lead M at the cell connector
Fault inside the traction battery (Ford Fusion PHEV TSB 23-2039)
High resistance at a splice or busbar joint in the sense path
Defective cell monitoring board input
P0B77.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit
P0B77.desc: P0B77 flags an open or high-resistance tap on voltage sense M, the thirteenth cell channel. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases: adjacent cells differing by 1.3 V or more, a balancing gate reading below 36 mV, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice). M is the last channel there with the short 0.6 s window, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid instead needs lines N and N-1 both below 1.4 V plus a jump over 0.5 V within 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Ford's TSB 23-2039 names P0B77 for 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that no longer start and prescribes a new traction battery. Range, low and high faults on M carry their own codes.

causes_en: Measuring channel M stuck at a fixed value
Battery controller software needing an update
Block 13 voltage drifting from the pack on two-mode NiMH packs
P0B78.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Range/Performance
P0B78.desc: With P0B78 the controller doubts the reading of channel M rather than its wiring. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor watches for a frozen value: whenever the average of all cells moves by more than 0.022 V, cell M must follow by at least 0.005 V in the same direction, and 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set a Type A fault. The 2012 two-mode trucks map M to nickel-metal hydride block 13 and multiply blocks 13 and 14 by twenty; if that estimate misses the pack voltage by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is stored as Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid wants at least half the average movement, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. A plausible but wrong value is often a controller or measuring board issue.

causes_en: Sense lead M shorted to ground or a lower cell potential
Failed measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell or NiMH block on channel M actually collapsed
P0B79.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Low
P0B79.desc: P0B79 means that the voltage reported for sense M is too low to be real. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 set it at 0.2 V or less, held for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, and only while no open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead is reported by P0B77 first. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids M is block 13: the battery pack control module needs block 13 and block 14 both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 1.4 V, 7 of 10 samples, with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V. Typical sources are a sense lead shorted towards ground or a lower cell, a failed measuring input, or rarely a cell that has truly collapsed.

causes_en: Sense lead M in contact with a higher cell potential
Measuring input of channel M reading high
Real overvoltage of the cell after a balancing fault
P0B7A.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit High
P0B7A.desc: A reading on channel M above what any healthy cell can deliver produces P0B7A. For lithium-ion packs GM sets the line at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window and treats it as Type A, illuminating the MIL on the first trip. The BAS Plus mild hybrid already reacts above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Where M stands for NiMH block 13, as on the 2012 two-mode trucks, a block voltage above 23 V for 15 of 20 samples is the trigger, again Type B, with the 12 V system between 9 and 18 V. Because a cell itself rarely climbs that high, a sense lead touching a higher potential or a faulty measuring input is far more likely than overcharging. The vehicle will usually limit charging and electric drive.

causes_en: Loose crimp or connector at the channel M tap
Chafed wire in the cell sense harness
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board
P0B7B.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B7B.desc: P0B7B is reserved for a sense M signal that flickers: short dropouts or jumps while the circuit is otherwise intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's tables for channel M contain open, plausibility, low and high tests but no erratic test, and Ford's Fusion bulletin lists only the open-circuit code P0B77. The legal footing is CARB 1968.2, which requires the battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system to be monitored as electronic components and demands fault codes that point to the smallest replaceable unit. In practice a loose crimp at the M tap, a chafed lead in the sense harness or a cracked solder joint on the monitoring board would cause such a signal. Expect warnings that come and go.

causes_en: Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Sense lead N broken or with excessive resistance
Fault on the cell monitoring board
P0B7C.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit
P0B7C.desc: Voltage sense N, the fourteenth channel, reports a broken or high-resistance sense lead with P0B7C. It is the last code in Ford's TSB 23-2039: 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that fail to start with any open-circuit code from P0B3B up to P0B7C get a replacement traction battery; the bulletin names no channel beyond N. In GM's 2019 battery controller tables N is the first channel whose open test runs 0.8 s within a 1.6 s window instead of 0.6 s, while the criteria (1.3 V adjacent-cell difference, 36 mV balancing gate, splice limits) stay the same, Type A. A second GM program of 2016 closes the balancing gates in a test pattern, turns the voltage drop into a sense-line resistance and fails above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples, Type A.

causes_en: Channel N value not tracking the other cells
Outdated battery controller calibration
Block 14 or 15 voltage mismatch on two-mode NiMH packs
P0B7D.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Range/Performance
P0B7D.desc: P0B7D concerns a channel N value that stays inside its limits yet does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2016 tables show how the same check is tuned per vehicle: the Chevrolet Volt fails when cell N does not move with the average for 7 of 8 seconds, while the Cadillac ELR counts 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms once the average shifts by more than 0.006 V; both are Type A. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids N corresponds to NiMH block 14, and blocks 14 and 15 scaled by twenty must agree with the pack voltage within 70 V, otherwise 160 of 170 samples set a Type B code. The 2019 processor uses its 0.005 V trend test, 35 of 40 samples. Often a battery controller reflash or a board repair is the fix.

causes_en: Sense lead N shorted to a lower potential
Damaged input stage in the sense module
Deeply discharged or failed cell on channel N
P0B7E.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Low
P0B7E.desc: P0B7E sets when channel N reads below the lower plausibility limit. GM's 2016 program with a separate battery sense module uses less than 0.20 V and needs 14 failures in 18 samples, about 1.8 s at 100 ms each, before a Type A fault; the open-circuit test must not be failing at the same time. The other GM lithium-ion controllers use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s in 2 s, also Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid works with 1.4 V and 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On 2012 two-mode trucks N is NiMH block 14, and blocks 14 and 15 must both drop under 2 V. A low reading usually comes from the measuring path, not from the cell: a lead shorted to a lower potential or a damaged input stage.

causes_en: Sense lead N touching a higher potential
Drifted measuring input in the battery controller
Real overvoltage of the cell on channel N
P0B7F.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit High
P0B7F.desc: Channel N reporting more voltage than a cell can hold leads to P0B7F. GM uses three thresholds depending on the system: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s on most lithium-ion battery controllers, above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples on the 2016 program with a separate sense module, both Type A, and above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks treat N as NiMH block 14 and set the code above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. The low counterpart is P0B7E, an open lead is P0B7C. Before suspecting the cell, a technician checks whether the N lead touches a neighbouring higher potential or whether the measuring input has drifted.

causes_en: Contact at the N tap opening under vibration
Fretting corrosion in the sense harness connector
Solder joint cracking with temperature cycles
P0B80.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B80.desc: P0B80 describes an unsteady channel N signal: the voltage drops out or jumps for moments, then looks normal again. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's Fusion plug-in bulletin, which reaches exactly up to channel N, cites only the open-circuit code P0B7C, and GM's tables give channel N open, rationality, low and high diagnostics without a separate erratic test. Background is CARB 1968.2, under which battery voltage sensors in a hybrid energy storage system count as monitored components with their own fault codes. If a vehicle does store it, the trigger would be a contact that opens under vibration or temperature change, for example at the N tap, in the harness connector or at a board joint. Restarting may hide the fault for a while.

causes_en: Loose or high-resistance busbar joint at the O tap
Broken sense wire O in the battery harness
Faulty cell sense module
P0B81.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit
P0B81.desc: P0B81 stands for an open sense lead on channel O, the fifteenth cell tap. GM has used it from the start: the 2011 Volt battery tables already list P0B81 among the open sense line codes and detect, among other cases, a busbar connection voltage above 0.7 V. In the 2019 battery energy control module the test needs 0.8 s within a 1.6 s window, with adjacent cells 1.3 V or more apart or a balancing gate below 36 mV, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid compares lines N and N-1, both under 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Unlike channels M and N, P0B81 does not appear in Ford's Fusion plug-in bulletin. With the lead open, the controller loses sight of that cell and limits operation.

causes_en: Channel O reading frozen in the monitoring electronics
Battery controller software fault
Rising resistance in the O sense tap distorting the reading
P0B82.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Range/Performance
P0B82.desc: P0B82 is a plausibility verdict on channel O. GM's 2016 program with a battery sense module asks cell O to trend at least 0.002 V in the direction of the average whenever the average moves by more than 0.022 V; 35 failed evaluations out of 40 set a Type A code. The 2019 controllers use the same logic with 0.005 V. Where O is NiMH block 15, on the 2012 two-mode hybrids, the battery pack control module multiplies blocks 15 and 16 by twenty and compares the result with the pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid needs half the average movement, 20 of 40, Type B. Low, high and open faults on the same channel are reported separately as P0B83, P0B84 and P0B81.

causes_en: Short in the O sense path towards ground or a lower cell
Monitoring input reading low
Dead cell or NiMH block 15
P0B83.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Low
P0B83.desc: P0B83 reports that channel O reads implausibly low. It is not the same as an open lead: GM's lithium-ion controllers run this check only while no open sense line fault is present, so a broken wire shows as P0B81 instead. The low limit there is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On the 2012 two-mode trucks, where O is NiMH block 15, block 15 and block 16 must both be under 2 V for 15 of 20 samples, Type B, with the 12 V supply between 9 and 18 V. Short circuits in the sense path towards ground or a lower cell are the main suspects; a genuinely dead cell is the exception and usually brings neighbouring codes as well.

causes_en: Sense lead O shorted to a higher cell tap
Monitoring input of channel O reading too high
Cell overcharged because balancing failed
P0B84.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit High
P0B84.desc: P0B84 is stored when channel O sits above the upper limit of a credible cell voltage. For GM lithium-ion packs that limit is 4.8 V, held 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A; the 2016 program with a separate sense module tolerates up to 4.90 V and counts 14 failures in 18 samples, also Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid uses a lower ceiling of 4.65 V and a Type B rating. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids the reading belongs to NiMH block 15, which must exceed 23 V in 15 of 20 samples. For the driver the effect is a warning and a battery that is no longer charged fully or used for electric drive. Since true overvoltage is rare, the measuring lead and the input of the monitoring electronics are checked first.

causes_en: Loose busbar screw changing contact resistance at tap O
Moisture or corrosion in the sense harness connector
Cracked joint on the monitoring board
P0B85.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B85.desc: P0B85 would mark a channel O signal that is present but unsteady, with spikes or brief gaps. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; even GM, whose public tables cover channel O in detail from 2011 onward, defines only the open, rationality, low and high tests for it. The requirement behind the code family comes from CARB 1968.2: voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system must be monitored like other electronic components, with fault codes that identify the part to replace. A plausible cause for such a signal is a contact resistance that changes with movement, heat or moisture, typically at the cell tap, the busbar screw or the connector of the sense harness. A fault that vanishes and returns calls for wiggle testing with live data.

causes_en: Sense lead P open at the cell tap or connector
Excessive resistance in the sense line (corrosion, loose screw)
Defective input of the sense module
P0B86.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit
P0B86.desc: P0B86 belongs to channel P, the sixteenth sense lead, and indicates that this lead has lost its connection to the cell. Comparing GM's tables shows how the timing evolved: the 2016 Volt battery controller decides within 0.6 s, the 2019 version waits 0.8 s in a 1.6 s window; both use the 1.3 V adjacent-cell, 36 mV balancing gate and splice criteria and are Type A. GM's 2016 program with a separate sense module measures the sense line resistance instead, failing above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples. On the BAS Plus mild hybrid the code is Type B after 7 of 10 samples showing lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V with a step over 0.5 V. Ford's public bulletins do not list P0B86. The pack usually has to come out for repair.

causes_en: Measuring electronics for channel P out of tolerance
Software or calibration of the battery controller
NiMH block 16 or 17 out of balance with the pack
P0B87.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Range/Performance
P0B87.desc: P0B87 says channel P is delivering numbers that do not fit the rest of the battery. On GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid the cell under test must move at least 50 percent as far as the average cell voltage; if not, 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, i.e. MIL after two trips. GM's 2019 lithium-ion processor is stricter in its rating, Type A after 35 of 40 samples, and looks for a value that stays flat by less than 0.005 V while the average moves more than 0.022 V. The 2012 two-mode trucks check NiMH block 16, together with block 17, against the pack voltage with a 70 V window, 160 of 170 samples, Type B. Since wiring faults have their own codes (P0B86, P0B88, P0B89), this one points towards measuring electronics or software.

causes_en: Lead P shorted to a lower potential or chassis
Defective input in the battery interface module
Weak cell or NiMH block 16
P0B88.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Low
P0B88.desc: A too-low value on sense P, the sixteenth channel, is what P0B88 records. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it at a cell sense line below 1.4 V for 7 of 10 samples, sampled every 200 ms and only with the 12 V battery above 8.8 V; it rates the fault Type B. The full lithium-ion systems in GM's 2016 and 2019 tables react at 0.2 V or less after 1.4 s in a 2 s window and set it as Type A. In the 2012 two-mode NiMH pack, P is block 16; blocks 16 and 17 must both stay below 2 V for 15 of 20 samples. A collapsed reading usually traces back to a short between the P lead and a lower potential, sometimes to a defective input; it is rarely the cell itself. The open-circuit condition is reported separately with P0B86.

causes_en: Lead P in contact with a higher cell tap
Input fault in the cell monitoring electronics
Genuine overvoltage of the cell or block
P0B89.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit High
P0B89.desc: P0B89 covers the opposite case to P0B88: the voltage reported on channel P is above the plausible range. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids assign P to NiMH block 16 and set the code when the block exceeds 23 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, provided no battery controller fault P0A1F is active. In lithium-ion systems GM sets 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s as the limit, Type A, while the BAS Plus mild hybrid reacts above 4.65 V. GM's 2016 program with a separate sense module allows up to 4.90 V. Overcharging is unlikely to be the cause because the controller stops charging well below these values; a sense lead reaching a higher tap or an input fault is the usual explanation. Expect restricted charging.

causes_en: Fatigued wire at a bend of the sense harness
Connector losing contact as the pack warms up
Sporadic fault in the cell monitoring chip
P0B8A.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B8A.desc: P0B8A is the erratic-signal member of the channel P group. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it: GM describes open, rationality, low and high diagnostics for sense P in its 2016 and 2019 tables, but none for an intermittent signal, and the Ford bulletins stop at channel N. The code exists because CARB 1968.2 requires the voltage sensors of a hybrid battery to be monitored and malfunctions to be stored under distinct codes. If set, the picture would be a channel P value that briefly drops out or spikes, for instance through a fatigued wire near a bend in the sense harness or a connector that loses contact when the pack warms up. Readings in live data may look normal between the events.

causes_en: Sense lead Q open between cell tap and module
Loose or corroded connector at the second measuring group
Fault in the battery interface module
P0B8B.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit
P0B8B.desc: P0B8B marks an open circuit on voltage sense Q, the seventeenth channel. In GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid tables Q is the first channel whose open test is blocked by code P1B37 instead of P1B36, which suggests it sits in the next measuring group of the battery interface module; the criterion stays lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. GM's 2019 battery controller uses 0.8 s in a 1.6 s window, the 2016 version 0.6 s, both Type A with the 1.3 V and 36 mV criteria. The 2011 Volt list includes P0B8B as well. The two-mode NiMH trucks have no circuit code for block 17. Ford does not list it. Typically the vehicle restricts or blocks electric operation until repaired.

causes_en: Monitoring electronics misreading channel Q
Outdated battery controller software
Block 17 or 18 voltage deviating on two-mode NiMH packs
P0B8C.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Range/Performance
P0B8C.desc: P0B8C is set when channel Q reports a voltage that fails the plausibility test against the other cells or the pack. On GM's 2012 two-mode trucks Q is NiMH block 17; the battery pack control module takes block 17 and block 18, multiplies each by twenty and compares with the measured pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. GM's lithium-ion programs instead check that cell Q follows the average: the 2016 Volt within 7 of 8 seconds, the Cadillac ELR in 20 of 40 samples, the 2019 controllers in 35 of 40 samples with a 0.005 V trend, all Type A. Because the value itself is within limits, the driver may notice little beyond the MIL. A software update or replacement of the monitoring electronics resolves most cases.

causes_en: Short in the Q sense path to a lower potential
Sense module input reading low
Cell or block 17 deeply discharged
P0B8D.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Low
P0B8D.desc: P0B8D reports a voltage on sense Q below the lowest credible cell value. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers in the 2016 and 2019 tables use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and the 2016 program with a separate sense module 0.20 V with 14 of 18 samples. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid applies 1.4 V, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. In the 2012 two-mode NiMH pack Q is block 17 and the battery pack control module requires blocks 17 and 18 both under 2 V for 15 of 20 samples. The low test is suppressed while an open-line fault is active, so P0B8B takes precedence for a broken lead. Shorts in the sense path are the leading cause; a real deep discharge of the cell would normally trigger further battery codes too.

causes_en: Damaged harness letting lead Q touch the next tap
Measuring input of channel Q reading high
Real cell overvoltage after a balancing failure
P0B8E.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit High
P0B8E.desc: Channel Q reporting an implausibly high voltage sets P0B8E. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where Q is NiMH block 17, the limit is 23 V for 15 of 20 samples, Type B, checked only while the 12 V system lies between 9 and 18 V. GM's lithium-ion programs work at cell level: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s in the 2016 and 2019 battery controllers, more than 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples where a separate battery sense module measures, all Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid limit is 4.65 V. As with the other high codes of this family, wiring and measuring input are far more often to blame than the cell; a damaged harness that lets lead Q touch the next tap is a classic finding. Charging and regeneration are limited.

causes_en: Cracked crimp at the channel Q tap
Damaged flexible circuit between cells and monitoring board
Cold solder joint at the measuring chip
P0B8F.en: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B8F.desc: P0B8F closes the channel Q group and stands for a sense Q signal that is erratic rather than absent or out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
