causes_en: Sulphur poisoning from high-sulphur fuel — desulphation regeneration not running
Thermal aging of washcoat after high-temperature exposure
Downstream NOx sensor reading drifts
P2000.desc: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 1 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.

mfr.Audi: Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) failure, Intake air leak, Mass Airflow (MAF) sensor is dirty/loss of calibration

causes_en: Sulphur poisoning
Thermal aging of washcoat
P2001.desc: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 2 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.

causes_en: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
Filter substrate cracked or melted from runaway regeneration
Differential pressure sensor drift
Leak around DPF housing
P2002.en: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P2002.desc: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes_en: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
Filter substrate cracked or melted
P2003.en: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P2003.desc: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes_en: Carbon buildup blocks flap travel
IMRC actuator or vacuum motor failed
Linkage rod broken or disconnected
P2004.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2004.desc: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.

mfr.Audi: A failed IMRC actuator, A problem with the intake manifold or linkage, Wiring issues

causes_en: Carbon buildup blocks flap travel
IMRC actuator failed on bank 2
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2005.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2005.desc: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.

causes_en: Carbon deposits seize flap closed
Actuator stuck or vacuum line collapsed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2006.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2006.desc: The IMRC flap on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position and cannot open at higher rpm. Top-end power suffers because the runner is restricted, and the engine may breathe poorly above mid-range.

mfr.Audi: Intake manifold runner control actuator failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Restricted vacuum lines

causes_en: Carbon deposits seize flap closed on bank 2
Bank 2 actuator stuck
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2007.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2007.desc: Bank 2 counterpart to P2006. The IMRC flap on bank 2 cannot return to the open position and chokes intake flow at higher rpm.

causes_en: Solenoid coil open
Connector unplugged or corroded
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2008.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Open (Bank 1)
P2008.desc: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC solenoid for bank 1. No control current flows when the runner is commanded to switch, leaving the flap in its default position.

causes_en: Drive line shorted to ground
Solenoid internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2009.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2009.desc: The IMRC solenoid drive line for bank 1 reads below the lower threshold — short to ground or a failed driver stage. The runner cannot be switched on demand.

causes_en: Carbon buildup restricts flap travel
Actuator weak or vacuum supply low
Linkage worn — play between actuator and flap
P200A.desc: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 1 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.

causes_en: Carbon buildup
P200B.desc: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 2 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.

causes_en: Excessive soot load triggers runaway regeneration
Post-injection over-fueling during regeneration
DPF temperature sensor reading drifts high
P200C.desc: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 1 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.

causes_en: Runaway regeneration
P200D.desc: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 2 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.

causes_en: Persistent misfire dumps unburned fuel into the cat
Sustained rich mixture from leaking injector or fuel pressure regulator
Catalyst temperature sensor drifts high
P200E.desc: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 1 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.

causes_en: Misfire dumps fuel into cat
P200F.desc: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 2 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.

causes_en: Drive line shorted to supply
ECU driver stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2010.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2010.desc: Drive voltage at the IMRC solenoid on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply or an open ground side. The solenoid is energised constantly or the driver protection trips.

causes_en: Open wiring or chafed conductor in IMRC harness
Connector corroded — high resistance contact
Actuator solenoid winding open
P2011.desc: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is open or has lost continuity — control module no longer detects a closing path through the actuator winding.

causes_en: Short to ground in driver line
Actuator winding shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2012.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2012.desc: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads below the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to ground or a stuck-low driver inside the control module.

causes_en: Short to B+ in driver line
Open ground return on actuator
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2013.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2013.desc: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads above the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground side.

causes_en: Position sensor failed
Signal wire broken
P2014.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 1)
P2014.desc: The position feedback signal of the IMRC flap on bank 1 is missing or implausible. Without feedback, the ECU cannot verify that the commanded runner position has been reached.

causes_en: Connector clip worn — intermittent contact
Flap sticking due to carbon
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2015.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2015.desc: The IMRC position sensor on bank 1 reports a value, but it does not match the commanded flap state — for example, the flap is commanded closed yet the sensor still reads open. Common on engines where the connector pin clip wears out and the sensor reads erratic positions.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Position sensor failed low
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2016.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2016.desc: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 1 reads below the lower limit. Usually a short to ground on the signal wire or a failed sensor.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2017.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2017.desc: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 1 reads above the upper limit. Typically a short to supply, an open ground reference, or a sensor that failed high.

causes_en: Sensor element open
Signal wire open
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2018.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Open (Bank 2)
P2018.desc: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC position sensor on bank 2. Without position feedback the ECU cannot confirm runner switching and falls back to a default mode.

causes_en: Position sensor drift
Carbon buildup blocks flap travel
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2019.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2019.desc: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the commanded runner state — typically a sensor drift or sticking flap.

causes_en: DEF crystallisation clogs the dosing nozzle
DEF supply pressure below target
Valve coil ageing — slow response
P201A.en: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P201A.desc: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Unit 1): the signal is implausible or outside the valid range. This valve doses reductant (DEF/AdBlue) into the exhaust for SCR NOx reduction.

causes_en: Supply fuse blown
Open supply wire
Supply relay contacts pitted
P201B.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Supply Voltage Low (Bank 1)
P201B.desc: The supply voltage feeding the IMRC actuator on bank 1 is below the lower limit — typically a fuse, relay, or harness fault on the supply rail.

causes_en: Supply fuse blown
P201C.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Supply Voltage Low (Bank 2)
P201C.desc: The supply voltage feeding the IMRC actuator on bank 2 is below the lower limit — typically a fuse, relay, or harness fault on the supply rail.

causes_en: Actuator internal driver or sensor fault
Actuator overheated and derated
P201D.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Internal Performance (Bank 1)
P201D.desc: Internal self-diagnostics of the IMRC actuator on bank 1 report an off-spec condition — driver stage, position-feedback or thermal limit no longer matches the calibrated profile.

causes_en: Internal actuator fault
P201E.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Actuator Internal Performance (Bank 2)
P201E.desc: Internal self-diagnostics of the IMRC actuator on bank 2 report an off-spec condition — driver stage, position-feedback or thermal limit no longer matches the calibrated profile.

causes_en: Pump relay contacts welded
Pump driver line shorted to B+
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P201F.desc: Reductant Pump A Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.

causes_en: Signal shorted to ground
Sensor element shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2020.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2020.desc: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a voltage below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a sensor with very low resistance.

causes_en: Signal shorted to positive
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2021.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2021.desc: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a voltage above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or an open ground.

causes_en: Open signal line at IMRC position sensor
Signal shorted to B+
Sensor element failed
P2022.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2022.desc: The IMRC position sensor on bank 2 reports a signal above the upper plausibility limit — typically an open signal line, broken sensor, or short to B+.

causes_en: Loose terminal in connector
Water ingress into connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P2023.en: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2023.desc: The IMRC position sensor signal on bank 2 jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a loose pin, partially-broken conductor, or moisture in the connector.

causes_en: Vapor temperature sensor failed
Harness fault between sensor and PCM
P2024.en: EVAP Fuel Vapor Temperature Sensor Circuit

P20D2.desc: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes_en: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P20D3.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit Low
P20D3.desc: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes_en: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P20D4.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit High
P20D4.desc: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes_en: Injector stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P20D5.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Open
P20D5.desc: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Open: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes_en: Injector stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P20D6.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Closed
P20D6.desc: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Closed: the control module has detected this fault condition. This injector doses fuel into the exhaust to raise temperature for diesel particulate-filter regeneration; it does not fuel the engine.

causes_en: Winding or coil open
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P20D7.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit/Open
P20D7.desc: The control circuit for the dedicated aftertreatment fuel supply pump or solenoid is open — HC dosing into the exhaust will fail.

causes_en: Pump weak — flow or pressure below threshold
P20D8.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Performance
P20D8.desc: Aftertreatment fuel supply is electrically OK but does not deliver the commanded pressure or flow during regeneration — weak pump or partial blockage.

causes_en: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P20D9.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit Low
P20D9.desc: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P20DA.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit High
P20DA.desc: Aftertreatment fuel supply control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Solenoid stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P20DB.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Open
P20DB.desc: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck open mechanically — fuel pressure cannot be cut off, risk of over-fueling exhaust.

causes_en: Solenoid stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P20DC.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Closed
P20DC.desc: Aftertreatment fuel supply solenoid stuck closed — HC dosing into exhaust fails, regeneration cannot raise temperature.

causes_en: Sensor failed
Harness fault
P20DD.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit
P20DD.desc: A general electrical fault is reported on the aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor — used to verify the dedicated HC-dosing rail is primed.

causes_en: Sensor drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P20DE.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P20DE.desc: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor reads in range but plausibility fails — pressure does not rise during prime, drift across a regeneration.

causes_en: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P20DF.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P20DF.desc: Aftertreatment fuel-pressure sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Worn DEF pump
Leak in DEF line
Clogged DEF filter
P20E0.desc: The pressure in the SCR reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line is below the calibrated minimum. Without sufficient pressure the dosing module cannot atomise reagent properly, leading to NOx exceedence.

causes_en: Reductant pump worn or weak
Leak in pressure line
Inline filter clogged
P20E1.desc: The reductant (AdBlue/DEF) line pressure stays below the demanded value during dosing. The dosing system needs a stable supply pressure to inject metered amounts; without it the system cannot meet NOx targets.

causes_en: Return line blocked or frozen
Pressure sensor reads high
Dosing valve stuck closed
P20E2.desc: The reductant line pressure exceeds the upper limit. A blocked return path, a stuck pump or a faulty pressure sensor are common causes; over-pressure can damage the dosing valve and the pump head.

causes_en: One EGT sensor drifts
Exhaust leak between the two sensor positions
P20E3.desc: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes_en: One EGT sensor drifts
P20E4.desc: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. The ECU uses this temperature to protect the catalyst and diesel particulate filter.

causes_en: One EGT sensor drifts
P20E5.desc: EGT sensors 1 and 3 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance — one is reading off, or there is a real temperature gradient that exceeds the calibrated map (e.g. from a leaking exhaust joint between the two locations).

causes_en: Air pump weak
Leak in air line
P20E6.en: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too Low
P20E6.desc: The DEF system air-assist pressure is below the required threshold — pump weak, line leak, or pressure-control valve stuck open.

causes_en: Pressure control valve stuck closed
Air pump does not regulate
P20E7.en: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too High
P20E7.desc: The DEF system air-assist pressure exceeds the upper threshold — pressure-control valve stuck closed or air pump runaway.

causes_en: Reductant pump weak or failed
Reductant filter clogged with crystals
Leak in pressurised reductant line
P20E8.desc: Pressure in the AdBlue/DEF supply line is below the target. Usually a failing reductant pump, a clogged filter, frozen lines, or a leak in the pressurised circuit.

causes_en: Return line blocked or frozen
Pressure sensor reads high
P20E9.desc: Manufacturer-specific variant of the reductant over-pressure condition. The pressure exceeds the upper threshold during a defined operating window; on some platforms used in addition to P20E2 to flag a different test path.

causes_en: Pump motor open
Connector unplugged or corroded
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P20EA.desc: The control circuit to the reductant (DEF) dosing pump is open — no current flow detected. Without pump pressure no AdBlue reaches the SCR catalyst and NOx reduction stops.

causes_en: Heater element failed
Wiring open or connector loose
P20EB.desc: A general electrical fault on the reductant tank heater "A" control circuit. AdBlue freezes at -11 C, so the tank heater must work for cold-start dosing.

causes_en: Heater element open
Heater driver stuck off
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P20EC.desc: The reductant tank heater "A" does not heat when commanded on. Either a failed element or a stuck-off driver in the dosing module.

causes_en: Heater driver shorted on
Heater line shorted to positive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P20ED.desc: The reductant tank heater "A" stays energised even when not commanded — usually a shorted driver stage. Continuous heating wastes current and can overheat the heater element.

causes_en: SCR catalyst aged or poisoned
NOx sensor drift
Exhaust leak between upstream and downstream NOx sensors
P20EE.desc: The SCR catalyst on bank 1 is no longer reducing NOx to the level the ECU expects, even with proper reductant dosing and quality. Often the result of catalyst poisoning by sulphur or hydrocarbons, thermal aging, or a leak between the upstream and downstream NOx sensors.

causes_en: Urea crystals in dosing valve
Electrical fault in dosing valve
P20EF.desc: The SCR reductant injection valve does not deliver the commanded amount of reagent. Causes include clogging by urea crystals, electrical faults or incorrect spray pattern.

causes_en: Runaway DPF regeneration upstream
Temperature sensor drift high
P20F0.desc: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

causes_en: Runaway regeneration upstream
P20F1.desc: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2): the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

causes_en: SCR catalyst thermally aged
Catalyst poisoning from sulphur or oil ash
P20F2.en: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F2.desc: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes_en: Pre-catalyst thermally aged
P20F3.en: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F3.desc: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes_en: Dosing nozzle clogged with crystallised DEF
Pump weak — flow under target
P20F4.desc: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is below the model expectation — typically a clogged dosing nozzle, weak pump, or leak between pump and injector that recirculates DEF back to the tank.

causes_en: Injector seat leaks DEF into exhaust
Cracked line or fitting
P20F5.desc: The DEF consumption observed over the dosing window is above the model expectation — typically a leaking injector seat, leaking line fitting, or a pressure-control valve that vents constantly to the tank.

causes_en: Valve seat eroded or contaminated
Valve plunger seized open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P20F6.en: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P20F6.desc: The DEF injection valve at bank 1 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes_en: Valve seat eroded or contaminated
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P20F7.en: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P20F7.desc: The DEF injection valve at bank 2 unit 1 does not close when commanded — DEF flows continuously into the SCR. Risk of crystallisation in the catalyst and over-dosing.

causes_en: Solenoid winding ageing — resistance climbing
P20F8.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
P20F8.desc: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 1 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

causes_en: Solenoid winding ageing
P20F9.en: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 2)
P20F9.desc: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is electrically OK but its current draw or duty-cycle response is outside the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or a partially shorted driver.

causes_en: Pump motor winding open
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P20FA.desc: The control line driving DEF pump B is open. On large engines or dual-tank systems a second pump (B) supplements pump A; with B offline the system loses redundancy.

causes_en: Pump head crystallised — motor seized
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P20FB.en: Reductant Pump B Control Performance/Stuck Off
P20FB.desc: DEF pump B receives a run command but does not start, or shuts off prematurely.

causes_en: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P20FC.en: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P20FC.desc: DEF pump B control line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P20FD.en: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit High
P20FD.desc: DEF pump B control line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Metering unit aged or partially clogged
P20FE.desc: The first DEF metering unit (the integrated module that combines pump, filter, level sensor, and dosing valve) is electrically OK but does not deliver the expected pressure or flow during operation.

causes_en: Internal module fault
Calibration mismatch after software update
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P20FF.desc: The dedicated SCR/reductant control module reports an internal performance fault — failed self-tests, watchdog resets, or calibration mismatch. Frequently a forerunner of total module failure.

causes_en: Throttle motor failed
Connector loose or corroded
Wiring break to throttle body
P2100.en: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open
P2100.desc: The drive-by-wire throttle motor circuit is open — no current flow detected. The ECU loses authority over the throttle plate and forces a limp-home with reduced power.

causes_en: Throttle bore coked, plate sticks
Throttle motor worn
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2101.en: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.desc: The throttle motor responds, but its actual position does not track the commanded position within tolerance. Often a dirty throttle bore where the plate sticks, or a worn motor.

mfr.Audi: Accelerator Pedal Position (APP) assembly failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Throttle control motor failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Drive line shorted to ground
Throttle motor internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2102.en: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Low
P2102.desc: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is below the lower limit. Typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage in the ECU.

causes_en: Drive line shorted to supply
Throttle motor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2103.en: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit High
P2103.desc: Drive voltage to the throttle motor is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or an open ground.

causes_en: Severe upstream TAC fault
Throttle position signal invalid
P2104.en: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Idle
P2104.desc: The ECU has detected a fault severe enough that it forces the throttle actuator to the idle stop. The driver loses pedal authority — only idle is available until the underlying TAC fault clears.

causes_en: TPS1 and TPS2 disagree beyond limit
Throttle motor not controllable
P2105.en: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Engine Shutdown
P2105.desc: The TAC monitor commanded an engine shutdown because throttle authority can no longer be guaranteed safely. The most aggressive TAC limp mode — used when both throttle position sensors disagree or the motor is uncontrollable.

causes_en: Underlying TAC fault triggers limit
Pedal position sensor signal implausible
P2106.en: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited Power
P2106.desc: The TAC monitor restricts maximum throttle opening as a safety response to a TAC fault. The vehicle can still be driven, but accelerator pedal travel is capped.

causes_en: ECU internal processor fault
ECU software flash corrupted
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P2107.en: Throttle Actuator Control Module Internal Processor
P2107.desc: The internal processor or watchdog of the throttle actuator control module reports an internal fault. Communication between the TAC monitor core and the main ECU core has failed plausibility — typical for a defective ECU.

causes_en: ECU internal performance fault
ECU connector pins corroded
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P2108.desc: Self-tests within the TAC module fail their performance criteria — for example RAM/ROM checks or analog reference voltages drift. Indicates an aging ECU rather than a wiring fault.

causes_en: Carbon deposits on throttle plate
Throttle position sensor drift
Idle/throttle relearn not performed
P2109.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2109.desc: The ECU detects that the throttle position sensor A signal at the closed-throttle stop does not match the learned minimum value. The mechanical or electrical zero reference of the throttle has drifted out of the expected range, often after cleaning, replacement or wear.

causes_en: Motor winding open
Open wire to motor
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P210A.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit/Open
P210A.desc: The drive circuit of throttle actuator motor B is open. Throttle B is the secondary throttle on engines with two throttle bodies — typically used for tumble flap or charge-motion control.

causes_en: Motor brushes worn
Carbon buildup at throttle plate
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P210B.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P210B.desc: Throttle actuator B motor responds electrically but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically high-resistance brushes, partial winding fault, or a sticky throttle bore.

causes_en: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P210C.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit Low
P210C.desc: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P210D.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Circuit High
P210D.desc: Throttle actuator B motor drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: One potentiometer track worn — voltage drift
Water in pedal connector
P210E.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C/F Voltage Correlation
P210E.desc: The redundant throttle or accelerator pedal position channels C and F disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire systems compare two or three independent channels to detect a faulty potentiometer track.

causes_en: Protection mode triggered by paired throttle-B fault
P210F.en: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P210F.desc: Throttle B control has detected an unsafe condition and forced an RPM limit. Common protective response when motor current, throttle position feedback, or supply voltage on the B path is out of spec.

causes_en: Underlying TAC fault triggers rpm cap
Throttle response time out of spec
P2110.en: Throttle Actuator Control System — Forced Limited RPM
P2110.desc: The TAC monitor caps engine speed at a fixed limp-home rpm because it can no longer trust the throttle response. Driver may notice a hard rev limit well below redline.

causes_en: Throttle plate seized open
Return spring broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2111.en: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Open
P2111.desc: The throttle plate cannot be commanded back to the closed/idle position. Idle speed runs high or the engine cannot decelerate properly — safety-critical fault that usually triggers immediate limp mode.

causes_en: Throttle plate seized closed
Throttle motor seized or gear broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2112.en: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Closed
P2112.desc: The throttle plate cannot be commanded open. The engine stays at idle or stalls under load. Often caused by a seized motor, broken gear, or heavy carbon coking inside the throttle bore.

causes_en: Underlying throttle actuator fault
Pedal/throttle correlation fault
P2113.en: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Limited RPM
P2113.desc: The throttle actuator control has detected a fault and limits engine speed to a defined emergency value. The vehicle stays drivable but with severely reduced power until the underlying fault is cleared.

causes_en: Severe throttle actuator fault
TPS signal lost
P2114.en: Throttle Actuator Control System Forced Below Limit RPM
P2114.desc: The throttle actuator system has dropped engine speed below the normal limp limit because of a more serious fault. The engine may run only at idle or stall.

causes_en: Throttle plate sticking due to carbon
Internal sensor fault
P2115.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Minimum Stop Performance
P2115.desc: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor A is outside the expected range during the ECU self-check. The signal at fully closed throttle does not match the stored reference, indicating a mechanical or sensor issue.

causes_en: Carbon deposits affecting throttle motion
Internal sensor B fault
P2116.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Minimum Stop Performance
P2116.desc: The minimum stop calibration of throttle position sensor B does not match the learned reference during ECU self-test. Sensor B is the redundant channel used to cross-check sensor A.

causes_en: Internal pedal sensor fault
Corroded connector pins
P2117.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Minimum Stop Performance
P2117.desc: The minimum stop signal from throttle/pedal position sensor C is out of specification during initialization. Used on systems with three redundant sensor channels for safety-critical drive-by-wire control.

causes_en: Plate binding from carbon
Motor windings aged or open
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2118.en: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P2118.desc: The current draw of the throttle motor lies outside the expected range — either much higher (binding plate) or much lower (worn brushes, open winding) than calibrated.

causes_en: Throttle bore coked at closed-position stop
Plate or stop misadjusted after service
P2119.desc: When commanded to idle, the throttle plate does not reach the calibrated closed position. Often a coked throttle bore preventing the plate from seating fully.

causes_en: Carbon buildup holds plate open
Return spring broken
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P211A.en: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Open
P211A.desc: Throttle B is mechanically stuck open — typically carbon buildup or a broken return spring on the secondary throttle plate.

causes_en: Carbon buildup holds plate closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P211B.en: Throttle Actuator B Control System - Stuck Closed
P211B.desc: Throttle B is mechanically stuck closed — carbon buildup or a seized bearing on the secondary throttle.

causes_en: High friction in throttle bore
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P211C.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P211C.desc: Throttle B motor current draw does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction.

causes_en: Throttle body aged or contaminated
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P211D.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P211D.desc: The throttle B body itself does not respond as commanded — position feedback is plausible but does not track the setpoint within the calibrated time window.

causes_en: Internal processor fault
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
Supply voltage outside specification
P211E.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Processor
P211E.desc: The processor monitoring throttle B inside the throttle/PCM has reported a self-test failure — RAM check, ROM check, or watchdog timeout.

causes_en: Internal module fault
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
Supply voltage outside specification
P211F.en: Throttle Actuator B Control Module Performance
P211F.desc: The throttle control module on the B path reports general performance issues — internal fault, communication mismatch, or calibration drift.

causes_en: Pedal sensor track C failed
Signal wire open
P2120.desc: A general electrical fault on the "C" channel of the throttle or pedal position sensor. Drive-by-wire pedals carry two or three redundant tracks; "C" is the third channel.

causes_en: Sensor track C worn
Correlation with tracks A/B lost
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2121.desc: The "C" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an electrically valid signal that does not match the other channels or the operating point.

causes_en: Pedal sensor track worn
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2122.desc: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

mfr.Audi: Accelerator Pedal Position (APP) assembly failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Throttle control motor failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2123.desc: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "D" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes_en: Signal shorted to ground
Signal wire open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2124.desc: The "C" channel signal is below the lower threshold — usually a short to ground or an open signal wire.

causes_en: Signal shorted to positive
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2125.desc: The "C" channel signal is above the upper threshold — typically a short to positive or an open ground.

causes_en: Connector intermittent
Track C worn at common pedal angle
Harness routed against vibrating component
P2126.desc: The "C" channel produces an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a worn track inside the pedal sensor.

causes_en: Pedal sensor track worn
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2127.desc: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2128.desc: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "E" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.

causes_en: Connector intermittent
Track D worn
Harness routed against vibrating component
P2129.desc: The "D" channel of the throttle or pedal sensor produces an intermittent signal — typically marginal connector contacts.

causes_en: Sensor failed
Harness fault
P212A.desc: A general electrical fault is reported on throttle position sensor G — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. Sensor G is part of a multi-channel redundancy on dual-throttle systems.

causes_en: Sensor wiper sticks
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P212B.en: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
P212B.desc: TPS G reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, lags, or does not match the commanded throttle position.

causes_en: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P212C.en: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Low
P212C.desc: TPS G below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Open signal line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P212D.en: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit High
P212D.desc: TPS G above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Intermittent connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P212E.en: Throttle Position Sensor/Switch G Circuit Intermittent
P212E.desc: TPS G signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: One potentiometer track worn
P212F.en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch F/G Voltage Correlation
P212F.desc: Channels F and G of the throttle/pedal position sensor disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Drive-by-wire system has lost redundancy and may force limp mode.

causes_en: Sensor failed
P2130.desc: A general electrical fault is reported on throttle/pedal position sensor F — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

causes_en: Correlation with tracks D/F lost
Track E worn at common angle
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2131.desc: The "E" channel of the pedal/throttle sensor produces electrically valid values that do not match other channels or the operating window.

causes_en: Signal shorted to ground

P23FE.en: Bank 1 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FE.desc: The secondary fuel system B on bank 1 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 1 is biased by an offset on the B system.

causes_en: Secondary fuel system has drifted
P23FF.en: Bank 2 System B Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance
P23FF.desc: The secondary fuel system B on bank 2 (e.g. port-injection rail in a dual-injection engine, or LPG/CNG rail in a bi-fuel system) does not maintain calibrated mixture - lambda response on bank 2 is biased by an offset on the B system.

causes_en: Leak detection pump failed
Wiring open to pump
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2400.en: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Open
P2400.desc: The control circuit to the EVAP leak-detection pump is open. Without that pump the ECU cannot pressurise the fuel-vapour system to test for leaks.

causes_en: Drive line shorted to ground
Pump internal short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2401.en: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
P2401.desc: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is below the lower limit. Often a short to ground in the harness.

mfr.Audi: Evap leak detection pump failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Drive line shorted to supply
Pump ground open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2402.en: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
P2402.desc: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or open ground.

mfr.Audi: Evap leak detection pump failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Open in pump or sense wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P2403.en: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Open
P2403.desc: The leak detection pump (LDP) - which actively pressurises the EVAP system to find leaks - has an open sense circuit. The ECU cannot read the pump status during the diagnostic cycle.

causes_en: Pump diaphragm worn
Reed switch intermittent
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2404.en: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2404.desc: The sense (reed-switch or current-feedback) signal from the leak-detection pump is electrically valid but does not match expectations during a leak test. Often a worn pump diaphragm or a sticking reed contact.

causes_en: Sense line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2405.en: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Low
P2405.desc: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage below the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes_en: Sense line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2406.en: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit High
P2406.desc: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes_en: Pump diaphragm worn
Sense wiring high resistance
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2407.en: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2407.desc: The leak detection pump returns a sense signal that is electrically valid but does not match the expected response during the pump's self-test or pressure cycle.

causes_en: Cap switch worn
Cap seal aged, switch never seats
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2408.desc: On vehicles with a sensed fuel cap, the cap-status signal is electrically valid but does not change as expected when the cap is opened or closed.

causes_en: Contact drifted or dirty
P2409.en: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P2409.desc: The sensor or switch that detects whether the fuel cap is properly closed reports a value within plausible range yet not matching driver action.

causes_en: Open in heater or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P240A.en: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Open
P240A.desc: The leak detection pump heater - keeps the pump diaphragm warm in cold weather - has an open control circuit.

causes_en: Control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P240B.en: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Low
P240B.desc: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to ground. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes_en: Control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P240C.en: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit High
P240C.desc: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to supply. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

causes_en: Hose or fitting leak
P240D.en: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak
P240D.desc: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

causes_en: Hose, fitting or cylinder valve leak
P240E.en: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak
P240E.desc: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak: a leak has been detected in this brake-hydraulic circuit, which reduces braking pressure. Safety-critical.

causes_en: EGR valve or cooler sticky
P240F.desc: The EGR system reacts to commanded changes more slowly than calibrated - typically a partly clogged EGR cooler, sticky valve, or worn actuator.

causes_en: Cap switch stuck mechanically
Connector corroded
P2410.desc: The fuel cap status switch is stuck in one position — the ECU never sees the expected transition between open and closed.

causes_en: Signal wire open
Cap switch failed
P2411.desc: A general electrical fault on the fuel cap sensor/switch circuit — open or short.

causes_en: Intermittent contact at connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P2412.en: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P2412.desc: Same as P2409 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Carbon buildup in EGR passages
Sticking EGR valve
EGR differential pressure sensor fault
P2413.desc: The ECU monitors EGR flow indirectly through MAF, MAP or differential-pressure feedback and finds that actual EGR flow does not match the commanded value over a sustained period.

causes_en: Sensing element fouled
P2414.en: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2414.desc: Same as P237A but on the upstream sensor B1S1 (pre-catalyst). A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

causes_en: Valve coil open
Drive line open
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2415.desc: The ECU detects an open circuit on the EVAP switching valve drive line. The valve cannot be commanded between its purge and isolation positions.

causes_en: Valve seat stuck
Diaphragm torn
P2416.desc: The EVAP switching valve responds electrically but does not produce the expected pressure change. Often a stuck valve seat or a torn diaphragm.

causes_en: Valve seat stuck closed
Valve internals corroded
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2417.desc: The EVAP switching valve cannot reach the open position. Purge flow is blocked and the EVAP system cannot vent the canister.

causes_en: Switching valve failed
EVAP line blocked or kinked
P2418.en: EVAP Switching Valve Control Circuit Performance
P2418.desc: The evaporative switching valve — used on multi-path EVAP systems to route purge or pressure-test flow — does not respond as expected. Self-test fails because tank pressure does not change in the calibrated direction.

causes_en: Valve stuck open mechanically
Drive circuit always energised
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2419.desc: The EVAP switching valve cannot close. Tank pressure cannot be isolated for the leak detection test, and purge routing may bypass the canister.

causes_en: Harness swapped during repair
P241A.en: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241A.desc: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 1 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

causes_en: Harness swapped during repair
P241B.en: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 2 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241B.desc: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 2 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

causes_en: Ice in throttle bore
P241C.en: Throttle Actuator Control System Ice Blockage Bank 2
P241C.desc: The throttle actuator on bank 2 cannot move because of ice formation - typical for very cold ambient temperature with humid intake. Engine de-ices on warm-up.

causes_en: AdBlue tank empty or out of compliance
P241D.desc: The SCR inducement strategy (mandatory regulatory measure to enforce AdBlue refilling and emissions compliance) has reached the final stage and shut down the engine. Refill AdBlue and clear inducement fault to restart.

causes_en: Valve stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P241E.en: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Stuck Closed
P241E.desc: The valve that routes engine coolant to heat the AdBlue lines is stuck closed - AdBlue lines do not warm up and may freeze in cold weather, blocking dosing.

causes_en: Cooler fouled with soot or scaled
P241F.en: EGR Cooler B Efficiency Below Threshold
P241F.desc: The temperature drop across EGR cooler B is below the calibrated threshold - cooler is fouled with soot, has internal scaling, or coolant flow is restricted. Recirculated gas reaches the intake hotter than designed, increasing NOx and combustion temperatures.

causes_en: Valve stuck closed mechanically
Drive circuit open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2420.desc: The EVAP switching valve cannot open when commanded. Purge or test flow cannot reach the appropriate path and the leak monitor aborts.

causes_en: Vent valve mechanically stuck open
Dust/debris preventing valve seat
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2421.desc: The evaporative emission system vent valve does not close on command. The ECU detects that the evap system cannot hold pressure or vacuum because the canister is permanently vented to atmosphere.

causes_en: Vent valve seized closed
Drive circuit open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2422.en: EVAP Canister Vent Valve Stuck Closed
P2422.desc: The vent valve at the canister end of the EVAP system cannot open. Without ambient air entering the canister, fresh fuel cannot purge the stored vapors and refueling may trigger ORVR issues. Common with rusted or rodent-damaged vent valves.

mfr.Audi: EVAP vent valve failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Catalyst aging / thermal damage
Oxygen sensor drift
P2423.en: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P2423.desc: The ECU determines that the hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 1 no longer holds enough HC during cold start to meet emission targets. Often due to ageing or thermal damage.

causes_en: Catalyst adsorber aged
P2424.en: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
P2424.desc: The hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 2 - which traps HC during cold-start until the main catalyst lights off - is degraded; HC slip during cold start is above the calibrated threshold.

causes_en: Open in valve or wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P2425.en: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Open
P2425.desc: The valve that admits coolant flow to the EGR cooler has an open control circuit - cooling cannot be enabled and EGR temperatures stay too high.

causes_en: Control line shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2426.en: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Low
P2426.desc: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes_en: Control line shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2427.en: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit High
P2427.desc: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes_en: DPF blocked or active regeneration
P2428.en: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 1
P2428.desc: An EGT sensor on bank 1 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

causes_en: DPF blocked or active regeneration
P2429.en: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 2
P2429.desc: An EGT sensor on bank 2 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

causes_en: Open in sensor or wiring
P242A.en: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242A.desc: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 3 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

causes_en: Sensor element drifted
P242B.en: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242B.desc: Same as P242A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

causes_en: Signal shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

P242C.desc: Same as P242A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Signal shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P242D.en: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242D.desc: Same as P242A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P242E.desc: Same as P242A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: DPF full of ash
P242F.en: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 1
P242F.desc: The diesel particulate filter on bank 1 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.

causes_en: Open in sensor or wiring
P2430.en: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P2430.desc: A general circuit fault on the secondary air injection (AIR) system flow or pressure sensor on bank 1 - the sensor that verifies air pump flow during cold-start enrichment compensation.

causes_en: Defective SAI sensor
SAI sensor wiring fault
P2431.en: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2431.desc: The ECU detects a general fault in the secondary air injection system air flow or pressure sensor circuit. The diagnostic cannot verify proper SAI operation.

mfr.Audi: Air control solenoid failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Secondary Air System pressure sensor failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Clogged SAI passages
SAI sensor drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2432.desc: The signal of the SAI air flow or pressure sensor is implausible during operation. The reading does not change as expected when the air pump is commanded.

mfr.Audi: Air control solenoid failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Secondary Air System pressure sensor failure, Wiring issue

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2433.desc: Same as P2430 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P2434.desc: Same as P2430 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Open in sensor or wiring

P2435.desc: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

causes_en: Sensor element drifted
P2436.en: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2
P2436.desc: Same as P2430 on bank 2 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

causes_en: Signal shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2437.en: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P2437.desc: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes_en: Signal shorted to supply
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2438.en: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P2438.desc: Same as P2433 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Intermittent contact at connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P2439.en: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 2
P2439.desc: Same as P2434 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: DPF full of ash
P243A.en: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 2
P243A.desc: The diesel particulate filter on bank 2 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.

causes_en: DPF heavily clogged
P243B.en: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2
P243B.desc: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes_en: Short-trip operation
P243C.desc: The DPF on bank 2 needs regeneration more often than calibrated. Possible causes are an oil-burning engine, fuel-injector leak, short-trip operation, or a sensor offset.

causes_en: Regeneration too slow
P243D.desc: Regenerations on bank 2 take longer than calibrated to complete - typically a low EGT during the cycle (cold weather, short trips) or a partially aged catalyst before the DPF.

causes_en: Regeneration aborted before completion
P243E.desc: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes_en: Soot loading critical
P243F.en: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2
P243F.desc: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes_en: Switching valve stuck open by carbon or corrosion
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P2440.en: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2440.desc: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes_en: Switching valve stuck closed by carbon
Vacuum control line leak
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2441.en: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2441.desc: The switching valve on bank 1 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes_en: Switching valve stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P2442.en: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2442.desc: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes_en: Switching valve stuck closed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2443.desc: The switching valve on bank 2 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes_en: Pump seized by corrosion
Pump relay failed
Pump fuse blown
P2444.en: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P2444.desc: The secondary-air pump does not run when commanded during cold start. Often a seized pump (after exhaust back-feed corroded the impeller), a blown fuse, or a failed relay.

causes_en: Pump relay stuck closed
Drive line shorted to supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2445.en: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On (Bank 1)
P2445.desc: The secondary-air pump continues to run after the cold-start window, when the ECU has commanded it off. Usually a stuck-closed relay welding the pump permanently to battery voltage.

causes_en: Pump seized from condensate corrosion
Relay failed open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2446.en: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck Off (Bank 2)
P2446.desc: Bank 2 secondary air pump does not deliver air when commanded. The catalyst light-off process is delayed and cold-start emissions rise.

causes_en: Relay stuck closed
Driver stage shorted on
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2447.en: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck On (Bank 2)
P2447.desc: Bank 2 secondary air pump runs continuously. Either a stuck-on relay or a shorted control output keeps the pump powered when it should be off.

causes_en: AIR switching valve stuck open
P2448.en: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 1
P2448.desc: The secondary air injection system on bank 1 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

causes_en: AIR switching valve stuck open
P2449.en: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 2
P2449.desc: The secondary air injection system on bank 2 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

causes_en: Cracked or missing DPF substrate
Leak in pressure sensing line
P244A.en: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too Low
P244A.desc: The differential pressure across the DPF is below the calibrated minimum even at higher loads. Often a sign of a damaged or missing filter substrate, or a leak in the sensing line.

causes_en: Sensor zero-point drift
P244B.en: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Offset
P244B.desc: At engine off, the DPF differential pressure sensor does not return to zero within the allowed offset window. The static offset is too large to be ignored.

causes_en: Engine load too low for regeneration
P244C.en: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244C.desc: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 1 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes_en: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk
P244D.en: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244D.desc: Same as P244C with the EGT too high - regeneration paused to protect filter substrate from melt damage.

causes_en: Engine load too low for regeneration
P244E.en: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
P244E.desc: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 2 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes_en: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk
P244F.en: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2

causes_en: Mechanical failure of valve
Contamination preventing motion
P2450.desc: The EVAP switching valve does not respond to commands as expected. The valve is mechanically stuck or unable to switch between purge and vent paths, blocking proper leak diagnosis.

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

causes_en: Predominantly short-trip operation
Leaking injector raises soot output
High engine oil consumption (turbo seals, valve stems)

P24E1.desc: A general circuit fault on the NH3 (ammonia) sensor - measures ammonia slip downstream of the SCR catalyst to detect AdBlue overdose.

causes_en: Sensor element drifted
P24E2.en: NH3 Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P24E2.desc: Same as P24E1 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

causes_en: Signal shorted to ground

causes_en: Corroded or loose sensor connector
Chafed or vibrating harness near the exhaust
Aged ceramic sensor element drifting under heat cycles
P24E5.desc: The ammonia (NH3) slip sensor downstream of the SCR catalyst delivers an intermittent or erratic signal. The ECM expects a smooth voltage proportional to ammonia concentration in the tailpipe — sudden jumps, dropouts or noise mean the wiring, connector or sensing element is failing. Used to close-loop the AdBlue/DEF dosing strategy.

causes_en: Burnt-out heater winding inside the sensor
Broken wire or unplugged connector
Failed heater driver stage in the dosing module
P24E6.desc: The heater inside the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor warms the sensing cell to operating temperature so it can read tailpipe ammonia. The ECM detects an open in the heater control circuit — no current flows when the heater should be active, so the sensor never reaches its working point and SCR closed-loop control is suspended.

causes_en: Heater control wire shorted to ground
Internal short across the heater element
Low-side driver pulled down in the control module
P24E7.desc: The heater control circuit of the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor reads below the expected voltage range. Either the wiring is shorted to ground or the heater driver in the SCR/dosing module is stuck low. The sensor element never warms up, NH3 readings stay invalid and the SCR strategy falls back to open-loop dosing.

causes_en: Heater control wire shorted to battery voltage
High-side driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P24E8.desc: The heater control circuit of the NH3 slip sensor reads above the expected voltage range. Typically a short to battery voltage or a heater driver stuck high — duty-cycle control is lost, the heater either runs continuously or not at all, and the sensor element risks overheating before the ECM disables it.

causes_en: Aged heater with increased resistance
Poor thermal contact between heater and sensing cell
P24E9.desc: The heater of the NH3 slip sensor is electrically intact, but the warm-up profile or steady-state temperature feedback does not match the ECM model. The sensor takes too long to reach operating temperature or drifts away from setpoint, so SCR closed-loop control is delayed or held off.

causes_en: Open or shorted supply wire
Failing supply rail inside the dosing module
P24EA.desc: The supply rail that powers the NH3 slip sensor electronics (typically 5 V or 12 V from the dosing/SCR module) is out of tolerance. Without a stable supply the sensor cannot deliver a valid ammonia reading, and the ECM disables the closed-loop SCR strategy.

causes_en: Supply line shorted to ground
High-resistance ground at the SCR module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P24EB.en: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P24EB.desc: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage drops below the lower limit. Usually a partial short to ground in the supply line, an undersized ground path with high resistance, or an internal supply collapse in the SCR/dosing module. Sensor output is held invalid until the supply recovers.

causes_en: Supply line shorted to battery voltage
Failed voltage regulator in the dosing module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P24EC.en: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P24EC.desc: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage rises above the upper limit. Either the supply is shorted to battery voltage or an internal regulator in the dosing module has failed open. The sensor electronics may be damaged if the condition persists, so the ECM disables the input.

causes_en: New sensor installed but not coded/learned to the ECM
Corrupted calibration memory after voltage drop
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P24ED.desc: The NH3 slip sensor stores its individual calibration coefficients in non-volatile memory (EEPROM/flash). The ECM cannot read valid calibration values — either checksum fails, the memory is empty after replacement, or communication with the sensor electronics is broken. Without the trim values the raw ammonia reading is unreliable.

causes_en: Internal processor or firmware fault
Brown-out from supply voltage dips
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P24EE.desc: The microcontroller inside the smart NH3 slip sensor reports an internal performance fault — failed self-test, watchdog reset, or out-of-range plausibility checks. The sensor cannot guarantee its output value, the ECM marks the channel invalid and disables SCR closed-loop control on this branch.

causes_en: Broken wake-up wire or unplugged connector
Failed wake-up input stage in the module
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P24EF.desc: The wake-up line that brings a sleeping ECU back from low-power mode is open. Many networks use a dedicated hardware wake-up wire (door-latch trigger, terminal 15, CAN wake-up) so modules can stay asleep with the ignition off. Without it, the module either fails to wake up at start-up or stays awake and drains the battery.

causes_en: Wake-up wire shorted to ground
Door, hood or terminal switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P24F0.desc: The wake-up input on the control module reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted wake signal. The module either keeps waking up unnecessarily and drains the battery, or it cannot distinguish a real wake event from the stuck low level.

causes_en: Wake-up wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P24F1.desc: The wake-up input reads above the expected range — typically a short to battery voltage. The module sees a permanent wake-up request, never enters sleep mode and drains the battery while parked.

causes_en: One sensor drifting outside tolerance
Residual heat in the charge-air cooler after a hot soak
P24F2.en: EGR Temperature/Charge Air Cooler Temperature Correlation
P24F2.desc: After a long key-off soak both the EGR temperature sensor and the charge-air cooler outlet temperature sensor must read approximately the same ambient temperature. The ECM compares them and detects an implausible delta. One of the sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or is exposed to a heat source the model does not know about.

causes_en: One temperature sensor drifting outside tolerance
Recently active reductant tank heater warming the tank above ambient
P24F3.desc: After a long key-off soak the AdBlue/DEF tank temperature and the fuel tank temperature should read close to each other (both at ambient). The ECM detects an implausible spread, which usually means one of the two sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or has a heat source nearby that the plausibility model does not account for.

causes_en: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed
Soot clogging the protective tube
P24F4.en: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P24F4.desc: The pre-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level — for example after a fuel cut or transition into low-load. Aged ceramic cells, soot deposits or condensation inside the sensor protective tube slow the diffusion of NOx to the measuring element.

causes_en: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed
Soot clogging the protective tube
P24F5.en: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P24F5.desc: The post-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level. Same failure mechanism as the upstream sensor — aged element, soot or condensate — but post-catalyst the consequence is a degraded SCR conversion-efficiency monitor.

causes_en: Mechanically stuck open valve from soot or coking
Broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P24F6.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Open
P24F6.desc: On systems that inject HC dosing fuel or AIR-assisted reductant into the aftertreatment, a purge valve clears the line after each dosing event.
