The ECM detects the valve stuck open — pressure or flow does not build up against a closed valve, so the dosing line cannot be charged. Common on diesel HC-doser hardware (DPF regen support).

causes_en: Stuck closed by deposits or seized armature
Open coil — valve never opens
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P24F7.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Closed
P24F7.desc: The aftertreatment HC dosing or reductant purge valve is stuck closed. The ECM commands purge but the line is not cleared, leaving residual fluid that can foul nozzles or freeze in cold weather. Subsequent dosing events also fail because backpressure does not match the model.

causes_en: Open or shorted control wire
Failed driver stage in the dosing module
P24F8.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit
P24F8.desc: General electrical fault in the control circuit of the aftertreatment fuel/air purge valve. The ECM cannot drive the valve coil according to plausibility checks — open, short or unexpected feedback voltage. Until cleared, dosing line purge is suspended.

causes_en: Aged solenoid with weakened magnetic force
Coked armature with increased friction
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P24F9.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
P24F9.desc: The valve coil is electrically intact, but the response (current rise time, return-current decay, position feedback) does not match the ECM model. Typical for solenoids losing magnetic strength after long thermal cycling, or armatures with increased friction from coking.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Failed low-side driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P24FA.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Low
P24FA.desc: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a failed low-side driver. The valve is energised continuously when it should be off, or the diagnostic feedback voltage is pulled below threshold.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open ground or open coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P24FB.en: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit High
P24FB.desc: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground/return path. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve.

causes_en: Partial short across the heater element
Driver overheating due to poor cooling on the module
P24FC.en: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P24FC.desc: The PM (soot) sensor heater is driven by a current-limited stage so it can burn off accumulated soot before each measurement. The driver reports current or junction temperature above the safe limit and disables itself. Often a partial short across the heater or sensor element after coolant intrusion.

causes_en: Incorrect or non-OEM DPF installed
Coding mismatch after part replacement
P24FD.desc: The ECM identifies the installed particulate filter A as the wrong part — backpressure signature, regeneration efficiency or coded part-number do not match the application. Common after a non-OEM aftermarket DPF or a wrong-application replacement.

causes_en: Incorrect or non-OEM SCR catalyst installed
Coding mismatch after part replacement
P24FE.desc: The ECM identifies the installed SCR catalyst as the wrong part — NOx conversion efficiency, NH3 storage capacity or coded part-number do not match the expected application. Typical after fitting a non-OEM SCR brick or after a coding error following replacement.

causes_en: Tank heater stuck on
Heat soak from exhaust or engine bay
P24FF.desc: The temperature of the AdBlue/DEF in the dosing system exceeds the safe limit — risk of thermal decomposition (NH3/biuret formation) and clogged dosing nozzles. Often caused by a stuck-on tank heater, a stalled coolant return or proximity to a hot exhaust component.

causes_en: L-terminal shorted to ground
Alternator regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2500.desc: The L-terminal feedback line from the alternator (charging warning lamp circuit) reads below the lower limit. The lamp may stay on, and battery voltage may drift if regulation feedback is also affected.

mfr.Audi: Alternator failure, Battery failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: L-terminal shorted to supply
Alternator regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2501.desc: The L-terminal feedback from the alternator reads above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side. Charging diagnostics cannot run cleanly.

mfr.Audi: Alternator failure, Battery failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Alternator output fault
Voltage regulator fault
P2502.desc: The ECU detects an out-of-range charging system voltage without specifying high or low. Indicates a generic charging fault that requires further sub-code investigation.

causes_en: Weak alternator output
Faulty voltage regulator
Slipping drive belt
P2503.desc: The ECU detects that battery voltage during operation stays below the regulated target. The alternator output is insufficient to maintain charge under load, eventually leading to battery depletion.

mfr.Audi: Alternator failure, Battery failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Faulty voltage regulator
Poor alternator ground
P2504.desc: The ECU detects a battery voltage above the regulated upper limit. The voltage regulator is not limiting alternator output, risking damage to electronic modules and battery overcharge.

causes_en: Failed main relay
Blown fuse on the ECM power feed
Corroded connector pin at the ECM
P2505.desc: The ECM/PCM monitors the main switched battery feed (typically terminal 15 / ignition-switched supply via the main relay). A general fault is reported — either the input is missing entirely or it does not match the expected timing relative to ignition state. Engine may not start or stay running.

causes_en: Aged main relay contacts with rising contact resistance
Weak battery sagging during crank
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2506.desc: The switched-battery input to the ECM/PCM is present, but the level or transient behaviour is out of plausibility — sagging during cranking, slow ramp-up after main-relay close, or noisy. Often caused by aged main relay contacts or a weak battery feed under load.

causes_en: Main relay does not pull in
Open supply wire
Severely discharged battery
P2507.desc: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads below threshold while the ignition is on. Either the main relay does not close, the supply wire is broken or shorted to ground, or the battery is too low. Engine usually fails to start until the input recovers.

causes_en: Alternator regulator overvoltage
Improper external power source or jump-start
P2508.desc: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads above the upper threshold. Most often caused by a charging system overvoltage (failed alternator regulator) or wrong jump-start procedure. Sustained high voltage risks damaging ECU electronics.

causes_en: Poor battery cable connection
Intermittent main relay
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P2509.desc: The ECU detects sporadic interruptions of its supply voltage. The fault is set when supply drops below a threshold for short periods, often during cranking or due to a poor connection.

mfr.Audi: Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) power relay failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the oil pan
P250A.desc: General electrical fault on the engine oil level sensor circuit. The ECM cannot read a plausible level signal (analog level, ultrasonic or capacitive sender). Without a valid level reading the ECM disables oil-low warnings and dynamic service-interval calculation.

causes_en: Aged or contaminated sender
Foaming oil under high RPM masking the level
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P250B.en: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P250B.desc: The oil level sensor is electrically intact, but the level reading is implausible — for example a constant value across drives, jumps that cannot match real oil consumption, or readings outside the design range. Often a contaminated or aged float/ultrasonic sender.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sender shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P250C.en: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Low
P250C.desc: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit, typically a short to ground or an open at the reference end of the sender. The ECM treats the input as invalid and ignores oil-low warnings until the circuit is repaired.

mfr.Audi: Oil level sensor failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P250D.en: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit High
P250D.desc: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit, typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return. Pegged at maximum, the ECM cannot distinguish full from invalid and disables the level monitor.

causes_en: Loose or oil-soaked connector
Cracked sender housing
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P250E.en: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P250E.desc: The oil level signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually loose contacts, vibration cracks at the sender or oil sloshing on bumpy roads. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when the noise pattern exceeds the diagnostic limits.

causes_en: High oil consumption between services
External oil leak
Missed top-up since last service
P250F.desc: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks bearing damage and oil-pump cavitation, so the ECM sets a critical warning, may reduce torque and asks the driver to add oil immediately.

causes_en: Main relay contacts pitted
Sense wiring corroded
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2510.en: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2510.desc: The voltage reported on the main power relay sense line for the engine controller does not match expectation. The ECU may shut down too early or stay awake too long, draining the battery.

causes_en: Aged main relay contacts
Chafed sense wire shorting intermittently
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P2511.en: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
P2511.desc: The sense (feedback) line that lets the ECM verify the main power relay has actually closed shows intermittent dropouts. The ECM expects to see battery voltage on this line whenever the relay is energised — short losses suggest aged contacts, vibration or chafed wiring.

causes_en: Open request wire or unplugged module
Failed input stage in the EDR
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2512.desc: The Event Data Recorder (EDR / black box) request line — used by the ECM or restraint module to trigger the EDR to capture pre-crash data — is open. The ECM cannot trigger an event capture, so any subsequent crash event would not be recorded reliably.

causes_en: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2513.en: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit Low
P2513.desc: The EDR request line reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees a constant request (which it cannot service) or cannot pulse the line high to fire a real event capture.

causes_en: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2514.en: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit High
P2514.desc: The EDR request line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line back low to release the request, so the EDR may either ignore further requests or sit in a permanent triggered state.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element
P2515.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2515.desc: General electrical fault in the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit. Sensor B usually monitors the low-side or compressor-suction pressure (in addition to high-side sensor A). The ECM cannot read a plausible value and disables variable compressor control to avoid evaporator freeze-up or overpressure.

causes_en: Low refrigerant charge
Contaminated or aged sensor diaphragm
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2516.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2516.desc: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B is electrically intact, but its reading does not match the system model — for example pressures that do not fall when the compressor is off, do not change with ambient temperature, or contradict pressure sensor A. Often a refrigerant charge issue or a contaminated sensor.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2517.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2517.desc: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads below the lower limit. Either a short to ground in the signal wire, an open reference voltage at the sensor, or an internal short. The ECM ignores the reading and disables A/C closed-loop control until the circuit recovers.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2518.en: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2518.desc: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads above the upper limit. Typically a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or an overpressure event briefly pegging the sensor. ECM disables variable compressor control to protect the system.

causes_en: Open or shorted A/C request wire
HVAC module not transmitting the request
P2519.desc: General electrical fault on the A/C compressor request input A. This input tells the ECM that the HVAC controller wants the A/C compressor engaged. With the input invalid, the ECM cannot enable the compressor clutch — A/C does not cool, idle-up compensation is not applied.

causes_en: Open switch wire or unplugged switch
Failed PTO enable switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P251A.desc: The Power Take-Off (PTO) enable switch input to the ECM is open. PTO is used on trucks and work vehicles to drive auxiliary equipment from the engine — without a valid enable signal the ECM refuses to enter PTO operating mode, idle speed control changes do not apply.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to ground
Switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P251B.desc: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently closed switch. The ECM either sees PTO enabled when the operator has not requested it, or cannot release the PTO mode after work.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P251C.desc: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the input low, so the switch state is unreadable and PTO mode is locked out for safety.

causes_en: Broken shutdown wire or unplugged work attachment
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P251D.desc: The PTO engine-shutdown command line is open. This safety input lets a connected work attachment (or operator switch) request an immediate engine shutdown — for example when an interlock is opened on a stationary aerial work platform. With the line broken, the safety shutdown cannot be commanded.

causes_en: Shutdown wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P251E.desc: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted shutdown request. The ECM may treat this as an active shutdown command and refuse to start or keep the engine running while in PTO mode.

causes_en: Shutdown wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P251F.desc: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pulse the line low to acknowledge a shutdown request, so the operator-side safety chain is effectively disabled.

causes_en: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2520.desc: The A/C compressor request input A reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request. The ECM either sees A/C demanded all the time (cannot release idle-up, raises fuel use) or cannot distinguish a real request from the stuck low level.

causes_en: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2521.desc: The A/C request input A reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot pull the line low to read switch state, so the A/C compressor request is treated as invalid and the clutch stays disengaged.

causes_en: Open or shorted A/C request wire B
HVAC module not transmitting request B
P2522.desc: General electrical fault on the second A/C request input B. Many vehicles have two HVAC zones, a rear evaporator request, or a redundant request line — input B carries that signal. With the input invalid, the ECM cannot honour zone B compressor demand or rear-evap operation.

causes_en: Request wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2523.desc: The A/C request input B reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted request. Same effect as input A stuck low, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes_en: Request wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2524.desc: The A/C request input B reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the switch state, request B is treated as invalid.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element
P2525.desc: General electrical fault on the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor circuit. The reservoir stores manifold or pump-generated vacuum for systems like brake booster, EGR actuators or HVAC dampers. Without a valid reading the ECM disables vacuum-pump duty cycle control.

causes_en: Leaking reservoir or vacuum line
Aged sensor with offset drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2526.en: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2526.desc: The vacuum reservoir pressure sensor is electrically intact, but the reading does not match the model — vacuum that does not build up after pump activation, does not bleed off when consumers draw, or stays at one value. Often a partly clogged hose, a leaking reservoir or an aged sensor.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2527.en: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2527.desc: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — usually a short to ground or open reference. The ECM disables vacuum pump control until the input recovers.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2528.en: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2528.desc: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — usually a short to reference voltage or open signal return. ECM disables vacuum pump control to avoid overshooting.

causes_en: Loose connector
Chafed harness
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P2529.en: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2529.desc: The sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — loose connector, vibration, or chafed harness. The ECM filters short transients but flags the input when noise exceeds limits.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor electrode after long use
P252A.desc: General electrical fault on the engine oil quality sensor — typically a capacitive/dielectric sensor that estimates oil aging from permittivity, viscosity proxies and conductivity. With no valid reading the dynamic service-interval algorithm falls back to the fixed-interval default.

causes_en: Contaminated sensor electrode
Oil grade outside the sensor calibration range
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P252B.en: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P252B.desc: The oil quality sensor is electrically intact, but the readings do not match the model — for example permittivity that does not change after an oil change, or shifts inconsistent with km/h driven. Often a contaminated electrode or oil that does not fit the sensor calibration.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P252C.en: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Low
P252C.desc: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — typically a short to ground in the signal line or an internal short across the sensor electrode.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P252D.en: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit High
P252D.desc: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return.

causes_en: Loose oil-soaked connector
Cracked sensor housing
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P252E.en: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P252E.desc: The oil quality sensor signal jumps or drops out — usually a loose connector at the oil pan, an oil-soaked harness or vibration cracks at the sensor housing.

causes_en: Overfilled at last service
Fuel dilution from incomplete DPF regeneration
Coolant intrusion (head gasket / cooler)
P252F.desc: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level above the safe maximum after sensor checks pass. Overfilling raises foaming, blow-by and crankcase pressure — and on diesels with regen-by-injection, fuel dilution can drive the level up by itself. The ECM warns the driver and may flag for service.

causes_en: Faulty ignition switch contacts
Wiring or connector fault
P2530.desc: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the ignition switch run position input. The signal indicating that the ignition is in the run position is missing or implausible.

causes_en: Run input wire shorted to ground
Switch contact stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2531.en: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit Low
P2531.desc: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck low — short to ground or a permanently closed contact. The ECM cannot tell when the operator releases the switch from Run, so accessory and crank logic gets confused.

causes_en: Run input wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2532.en: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit High
P2532.desc: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect when the operator turns the switch back to off/accessory, so module sleep and accessory power timeouts do not work correctly.

causes_en: Open or shorted On/Start wire
P2533.desc: General electrical fault on the ignition switch On/Start (terminal 50 / crank) input. The ECM uses this signal to know when the starter is energised — without it the ECM cannot raise fuel and timing for cranking, the engine struggles to start or stalls right after.

causes_en: On/Start wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2534.en: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P2534.desc: The On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see crank request when the key is at rest, blocking accessory functions or causing unexpected starter cut-off logic.

causes_en: On/Start wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2535.en: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P2535.desc: The On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot read the crank state, modules dependent on this signal are unable to time their wake-up correctly.

causes_en: Open or shorted ACC wire
P2536.desc: General electrical fault on the ignition switch accessory (terminal 75 / ACC) input. ACC tells the ECM that radio, fans, accessory loads should be powered without the engine running. With the input invalid, the body controller may misjudge accessory power timing.

causes_en: ACC wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2537.en: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit Low
P2537.desc: The ACC input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact. The ECM may see ACC active continuously and refuse to enter sleep, draining the battery.

causes_en: ACC wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2538.en: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit High
P2538.desc: The ACC input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The ECM cannot detect when the operator releases the switch from ACC, accessory power timeouts do not work.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Failed sensor element
P2539.en: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
P2539.desc: General electrical fault on the low-pressure fuel system sensor — typically the lift-pump or pre-supply pressure sensor that monitors the rail feeding the high-pressure pump. With no valid reading, the ECM cannot verify that lift pressure is sufficient for HP-pump intake.

causes_en: Open sense wire
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P253A.desc: The PTO sense (engagement feedback) line is open. This input tells the ECM whether the PTO clutch or driveline is actually engaged after a request — it closes the loop on the PTO enable command. With it broken, the ECM cannot confirm engagement and refuses to ramp up to PTO speed setpoints.

causes_en: Sticky or worn PTO clutch
Mis-adjusted limit switch
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P253B.desc: The PTO sense circuit is electrically intact, but the engagement feedback does not match the command. The ECM requests engage and sees no engaged feedback (or vice versa) within the expected time window — drive-line slip, sticky clutch, or a mis-adjusted limit switch.

causes_en: Sense wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P253C.desc: The PTO sense input reads stuck low — short to ground or limit switch stuck closed. The ECM may see PTO continuously engaged.

causes_en: Sense wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P253D.desc: The PTO sense input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The ECM cannot detect engagement.

causes_en: Loose connector
Chattering limit switch
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P253E.desc: The PTO sense signal jumps or drops out — usually loose connectors, a chattering limit switch, or vibration on the work attachment.

causes_en: Service interval exceeded
High DPF regeneration load with fuel dilution
P253F.desc: The oil quality monitor concludes that the engine oil has reached the end of its useful life — based on permittivity, soot content, fuel dilution and total operating hours. The ECM requests an oil change before the next regen cycle to prevent accelerated bearing wear.

causes_en: Defective low-pressure sensor
Wiring or connector fault
P2540.en: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
P2540.desc: The ECU detects a general fault in the low-pressure fuel system pressure sensor circuit. Without a valid signal the ECU cannot verify lift-pump pressure or fuel rail pre-pressure.

causes_en: Sensor drift
Clogged fuel filter
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2541.en: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2541.desc: The signal of the low-pressure fuel sensor does not match the expected value during operation. Pressure does not rise as expected when the lift pump is commanded.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2542.en: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit High
P2542.desc: The low-pressure fuel system sensor signal voltage is above the upper limit. Either a short to reference voltage in the signal line, an open signal return, or a sensor reading pegged high after an internal failure. The HP-pump pressure-control strategy falls back to default.

causes_en: Open signal wire
Fault in requesting module
P2543.desc: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the power demand input signal used to coordinate accessory loads (e.g. AC compressor, alternator load). The signal is missing or implausible.

causes_en: CAN communication error
Fault in requesting module
P2544.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal A
P2544.desc: The ECU detects an invalid torque-management request signal A from another control unit (e.g. transmission, ESP, ABS) on the CAN bus. Cooperative torque control cannot be performed as expected.

causes_en: Requesting module sending invalid values
Communication bus corruption between modules
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2545.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Range/Performance
P2545.desc: The ECM receives torque-management requests from other modules (TCM during shifts, ABS/ESC during traction events, hybrid controller). Input A is electrically intact but its values do not match the system model — out-of-range steps, jumps, or persistent values that other modules cannot confirm.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
CAN message stuck at minimum value
P2546.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Low
P2546.desc: Torque management input A reads stuck low — analog short to ground or message stuck at minimum value. The ECM cannot trust the request and falls back to a safe default.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
CAN message stuck at maximum value
P2547.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal A High
P2547.desc: Torque management input A reads stuck high — analog short to reference voltage or message stuck at maximum value. The ECM rejects the request to avoid running unintended high-torque commands.

causes_en: Open or shorted wire / invalid CAN message
P2548.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal B
P2548.desc: General electrical fault on the second torque-management request input B. Used when more than one module needs to request torque adjustments — typically TCM on input A and ABS/ESC on input B, or chassis vs powertrain. With B invalid, only the A-side request is honoured.

causes_en: Requesting module sending invalid values
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P2549.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Range/Performance
P2549.desc: Input B is electrically intact but the values are implausible — same failure mode as the A-side performance fault, applied to the second torque-management channel.

causes_en: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P254A.desc: The PTO speed-selector switch 1 input is open. This switch lets the operator pick a preset PTO operating speed (idle, 800, 1200 rpm, etc.). With the input broken, the ECM cannot apply any operator-selected speed and falls back to a default speed.

causes_en: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P254B.desc: The selector input is electrically intact but the value is implausible — multiple positions asserted at once, or a value that cannot map to any of the configured speed presets. Often a sticky multi-position switch or a contaminated rotary contact.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P254C.en: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Low
P254C.desc: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P254D.en: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit High
P254D.desc: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes_en: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P254E.en: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P254E.desc: The PTO speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes_en: Open or shorted hood-switch wire
Aged switch with corroded contacts
P254F.desc: General electrical fault on the engine hood (bonnet) switch circuit. The hood switch tells the body controller and (on hybrids) the high-voltage system that the hood is open — used for security, alarm and HV-safety interlock. With the input invalid, alarm logic and HV interlock fall back to a safe state.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
P2550.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Low
P2550.desc: Torque management input B reads stuck low — short to ground or message at minimum. ECM rejects the request, only A-side is used.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
P2551.en: Torque Management Request Input Signal B High
P2551.desc: Torque management input B reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or message at maximum. ECM rejects the request to avoid unintended high-torque commands.

causes_en: Open or shorted inhibit wire
P2552.desc: General electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit input A. This input lets external safety functions (immobilizer, hybrid HV interlock, anti-theft) override the throttle or cut fuel delivery. With the input invalid the safety override is unreliable, so the ECM falls back to its safe default — typically inhibit asserted to err on the side of safety.

causes_en: Requesting module sending an inconsistent value
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P2553.desc: The throttle/fuel inhibit A signal is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the immobilizer reports OK, or de-asserted while a hybrid HV interlock is active. The ECM cannot trust the signal.

causes_en: Inhibit wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2554.desc: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted. ECM may treat it as continuous inhibit and refuse normal operation.

causes_en: Inhibit wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2555.desc: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. ECM cannot read the inhibit state and falls back to the safe default.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the sensor
Corroded connector at the expansion tank
P2556.desc: General electrical fault on the engine coolant level sensor/switch circuit. Many vehicles use a simple float-switch in the expansion tank, others use a continuous-level analog sensor. With the input invalid the ECM cannot warn for low coolant before overheating starts.

causes_en: Stuck float
Trapped air around the sensor
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2557.en: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2557.desc: The coolant level sensor is electrically intact, but the readings are implausible — for example a level that does not move at all over many drive cycles, or jumps that cannot match real coolant loss. Often a stuck float, contaminated electrode or air-locked sensor.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2558.en: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P2558.desc: Coolant level sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2559.en: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P2559.desc: Coolant level sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes_en: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P255A.desc: The second PTO speed-selector switch input is open. Switch 2 typically encodes a binary or multi-bit code together with switch 1 — together they select one of several preset PTO speeds. With switch 2 broken, only the half of the bit pattern is available, so several presets cannot be reached.

causes_en: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P255B.desc: PTO speed selector switch 2 is electrically intact but its value does not match a valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted, or values that do not map to any preset.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P255C.en: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Low
P255C.desc: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P255D.en: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit High
P255D.desc: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

causes_en: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P255E.en: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P255E.desc: PTO speed selector 2 signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

causes_en: HVAC module sending inconsistent request
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P255F.desc: The A/C request input A is electrically intact, but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the HVAC controller reports off, toggling rapidly, or sustained while compressor pressures cannot support it. The ECM disables A/C clutch engagement until the input becomes plausible.

causes_en: External coolant leak (hose, radiator, water pump)
Missed top-up since last service
Head gasket leaking coolant into combustion
P2560.desc: The coolant level monitor reports the engine coolant below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass. Continued operation risks overheating, head warping and head-gasket failure. The driver is warned and the ECM may reduce engine power until the level is restored.

causes_en: Internal fault in the HVAC module — read its DTCs
P2561.en: A/C Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2561.desc: The A/C / HVAC control module has requested the ECM to illuminate the malfunction indicator (MIL) because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. The original fault is stored in the HVAC module — this code only signals that the ECM has honoured the request.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the position sensor
Failed Hall element after thermal cycling
P2562.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit
P2562.desc: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor A — the feedback sensor on the wastegate or VGT actuator (often a contactless Hall sensor). Without valid position feedback the ECM cannot close the loop on boost control and falls back to open-loop duty cycle.

causes_en: Position sensor failed
Wiring open or chafed near turbo
P2563.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit
P2563.desc: The position feedback sensor on the variable-geometry or wastegate turbocharger actuator is not communicating or is implausible. Without position feedback, boost control runs in default mode and power is reduced.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2564.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P2564.desc: Position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open reference voltage at the sensor.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2565.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit High
P2565.desc: Position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage in the signal line or open signal return.

causes_en: VTG vanes coked, sticky
Actuator linkage worn
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2566.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Range/Performance
P2566.desc: The turbocharger actuator position sensor reports a value, but it does not track commanded vane or wastegate position within tolerance. Often a sticky VTG mechanism due to soot.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor failed low
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2567.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit Low
P2567.desc: The turbocharger position sensor signal is below the lower limit — short to ground or sensor at zero stop.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to supply
Sensor failed high
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2568.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit High
P2568.desc: The turbocharger position sensor signal is above the upper limit — short to supply, open ground or sensor failed high.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor shorted internally
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2569.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P2569.desc: Direct Ozone Reduction (DOR) catalysts are coated radiator surfaces or dedicated catalysts that decompose tropospheric ozone passing over the radiator — used for low-emissions vehicles. The temperature sensor monitoring the DOR brick reads stuck low — short to ground or sensor short.

causes_en: Open wire or unplugged switch
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P256A.en: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open
P256A.desc: The idle-speed selector input is open. On commercial vehicles this switch lets the operator pick a fast-idle setpoint (for example to keep auxiliary loads supplied). With the input broken, the ECM cannot apply an operator-selected idle speed.

causes_en: Contaminated rotary contact
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P256B.en: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P256B.desc: The idle-speed selector input is electrically intact but the value does not match a valid preset — multiple positions or a non-mappable value. Often a sticky multi-position switch.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P256C.en: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P256C.desc: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P256D.en: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P256D.desc: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal at maximum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Worn rotary contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P256E.en: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P256E.desc: The idle-speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: HVAC module sending inconsistent request B
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P256F.desc: A/C request input B is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — same failure mode as the input A performance fault, applied to the second HVAC channel.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Open signal return
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2570.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P2570.desc: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or open signal return. Without a valid temperature the ECM cannot enable the DOR efficiency monitor.

causes_en: Loose connector
Chafed harness
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P2571.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2571.desc: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator pack.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring
P2572.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit
P2572.desc: General electrical fault on the DOR catalyst deterioration sensor circuit. This sensor estimates the remaining ozone-conversion capacity of the DOR coating — coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by salt or grime, or thermally aged. Without a valid signal the deterioration monitor is disabled.

causes_en: Aged sensor with offset drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P2573.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2573.desc: The DOR deterioration sensor is electrically intact but its readings drift or do not match the model — for example a deterioration value that does not move with km/h driven, or moves implausibly fast.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2574.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Low
P2574.desc: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2575.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit High
P2575.desc: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes_en: Loose connector
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P2576.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2576.desc: The DOR deterioration sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator.

causes_en: DOR coating worn off the radiator
Coating contaminated by salt and grime
P2577.en: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
P2577.desc: The DOR catalyst no longer reduces tropospheric ozone with the required efficiency, based on the deterioration sensor and operating-time model. Coating worn off the radiator surface, contaminated by road salt and grime, or thermally aged after many heat cycles. Replacing the affected radiator/coating restores function.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring
Aged sensor with reduced output amplitude
P2578.desc: General electrical fault on the turbocharger/supercharger shaft speed sensor A — a high-frequency Hall or eddy-current sensor on the compressor shaft. The ECM uses turbo speed for overspeed protection (typically 200,000+ rpm) and for closed-loop boost on VGT systems. With no valid speed the ECM limits boost.

causes_en: Oil-contaminated sensor tip
Aged Hall element
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2579.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2579.desc: Turbo speed sensor A is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the model — for example a speed that does not climb when boost rises, drifts away from the air-mass-flow estimate, or jumps. Often blade-fouling, a contaminated sensor tip or aged element.

causes_en: Open control wire
Failed driver in the control module
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P257A.desc: The control circuit that drives the vacuum reservoir control valve (or vacuum pump motor) is open. The ECM cannot energise the actuator, so vacuum is no longer maintained on demand and consumers like brake booster, EGR or HVAC dampers may run out of vacuum.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P257B.desc: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The actuator may be energised continuously when it should be off.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P257C.desc: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve/motor.

causes_en: Worn switch with contact bounce
Misaligned hood actuator
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P257D.desc: The hood switch is electrically intact, but its state is implausible — for example reporting hood-open while vehicle speed is rising, or rapid toggles. Usually a worn switch with high contact bounce or a misaligned hood actuator.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P257E.desc: The hood switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed switch. The body controller may treat the hood as permanently open and refuse to arm the alarm or close the HV interlock.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P257F.desc: The hood switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. The body controller cannot detect when the hood is opened.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Open supply at the sensor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2580.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P2580.desc: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open supply.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2581.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P2581.desc: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes_en: Oil mist on the sensor tip
Chafed harness near the turbo
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P2582.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2582.desc: Turbo speed sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist on the sensor tip, or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

causes_en: Dirty sensor surface (radar emblem / camera lens)
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact
Failed sensor module
P2583.en: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Single Sensor or Center
P2583.desc: General fault on the radar/lidar/camera distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise control. On systems with a single sensor or three sensors with a center unit, this code refers to the central sensor — without it, ACC distance control is disabled and the system falls back to plain cruise.

causes_en: Internal fault in the fuel additive module — read its DTCs
P2584.en: Fuel Additive Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2584.desc: The fuel additive control module — typical for diesel cars with a separate Eolys/Cerine additive tank that aids DPF regeneration — has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. The original fault is in the additive module itself.

causes_en: Additive tank low — service refill required
P2585.en: Fuel Additive Control Module Warning Lamp Request
P2585.desc: The fuel additive control module asks for the additive-low warning lamp to be illuminated — the additive tank (Eolys/Cerine, used to lower DPF regen temperature) is approaching empty or has reached a service threshold. Continued driving without refilling will eventually disable DPF regeneration.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring to the position sensor
Failed Hall element
P2586.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit
P2586.desc: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor B — second position sensor on the same actuator (redundant Hall) or on a second turbo (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage). With B invalid the ECM cannot cross-check actuator A and falls back to limited boost control.

causes_en: Sensor mounting misaligned after service
Aged Hall element
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2587.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2587.desc: Position sensor B is electrically intact, but the reading does not track sensor A or the actuator-command model. Often a misaligned redundant sensor or aged element on a second turbo.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2588.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P2588.desc: Position sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2589.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit High
P2589.desc: Position sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes_en: Open control wire to the pump
Failed driver in the control module
P258A.desc: The control circuit driving the electric vacuum pump (used to maintain brake-booster vacuum on direct-injection or hybrid powertrains where the engine is not always running) is open. The ECM cannot run the pump on demand — booster vacuum drops, pedal feel hardens, brake assist may be reduced.

causes_en: Aged motor brushes or dry vanes
Leaking vacuum line
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P258B.en: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P258B.desc: The vacuum pump control circuit is electrically intact, but the pump response does not match the model — pump runs longer than expected to reach setpoint, current draw rises (mechanically tight) or vacuum does not build at all. Aged motor brushes, dry vanes or a leaking line are typical causes.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
P258C.en: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Low
P258C.desc: The electric vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The pump may run continuously, drawing current and overheating, until the ECM disables the channel.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open pump motor winding
P258D.en: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A High
P258D.desc: The vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. The driver cannot pull the line low to start the pump.

causes_en: Switch contact bounce
Switch operated while vehicle is moving
P258E.desc: The PTO enable switch is electrically intact but its state does not match operating conditions — for example asserted while the vehicle is rolling above the PTO speed limit, or asserted/de-asserted in fast succession. The ECM rejects the request to avoid unsafe PTO engagement.

causes_en: Open or shorted output line
Downstream consumer not loading the line
P258F.desc: The ECM/PCM produces a torque-management output signal for downstream consumers (TCM during shifts, hybrid module, transfer case) and detects a fault on this output — open, short, or feedback voltage outside expected range. Without it, downstream modules cannot synchronise their behaviour with the engine.

causes_en: Vibration-induced chafing of the harness
Oil mist on the sensor
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P2590.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2590.desc: Position sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration on the actuator, oil mist contamination or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

causes_en: Dirty sensor surface
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact
P2591.en: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Left
P2591.desc: General fault on the left-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise. Multi-sensor radar arrays use left/center/right sensors for wider field-of-view and lane discrimination — without left, ACC may degrade to single-target tracking.

causes_en: Dirty sensor surface
Sensor misaligned after a frontal impact
P2592.en: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Right
P2592.desc: General fault on the right-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise. Same role as the left sensor but covering the right field-of-view.

causes_en: Open or shorted wiring
P2593.desc: General electrical fault on the second turbocharger speed sensor B — used on twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage installations to read the second compressor shaft speed. Same role as sensor A on the second turbo.

causes_en: Oil-contaminated sensor tip
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping
P2594.en: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2594.desc: Turbo speed sensor B is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the boost or air-mass model — same failure mode as sensor A performance fault, applied to the second turbo.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P2595.en: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2595.desc: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes_en: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2596.en: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P2596.desc: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

causes_en: Oil mist on the sensor tip
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P2597.en: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2597.desc: Turbo speed sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist or chafed wiring at the second turbo.

causes_en: Actuator mechanically stuck near low end
Sensor pegged low
P2598.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck Low
P2598.desc: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the low end of its travel even when the actuator is commanded to move. Either the actuator is mechanically stuck closed (wastegate jammed shut, VGT vanes seized at minimum opening) or the sensor itself is pegged low. Boost is uncontrolled — overboost on diesels with VGT, underboost on wastegate-stuck systems.

causes_en: Actuator mechanically stuck near high end
P2599.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck High
P2599.desc: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the high end of its travel — actuator stuck open (wastegate held wide open, VGT vanes seized at maximum opening) or sensor pegged high. Boost suffers — typically underboost on VGT, overboost-protection-off on wastegate.

causes_en: Actuator mechanically stuck near low end
P259A.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck Low
P259A.desc: Same condition as the A-side stuck-low fault, but on the second sensor / second turbo. Position sensor B reads stuck near the low end while the actuator is commanded.

causes_en: Actuator mechanically stuck near high end
P259B.en: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck High
P259B.desc: Same as the A-side stuck-high fault, applied to sensor B / turbo B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes_en: Carbonised VGT vanes
Leaky pneumatic actuator
P259C.en: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger A Boost Control
P259C.desc: After start-up the boost-control loop on turbo A takes longer than the calibration limit to transition from open-loop to closed-loop control. Typically a slow-warming actuator (VGT vanes carbonised), a sluggish position sensor or a leaky pneumatic actuator that cannot follow setpoints quickly enough.

causes_en: Carbonised VGT vanes
P259D.en: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger B Boost Control
P259D.desc: Same condition as the turbo A excessive-warm-up fault, applied to the second turbo. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes_en: Boost leak in the charge-air path
Failing turbocharger that cannot produce target boost
P259E.en: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P259E.desc: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the low end of its travel for too long — the closed-loop controller is saturated against the lower stop trying to reach the boost setpoint. Indicates either a leak (wastegate held closed but boost still escapes) or commanded boost above what the engine can produce.

causes_en: Wastegate stuck closed
P259F.en: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At High Limit
P259F.desc: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the high end of its travel — the controller is saturated against the upper stop trying to bleed off boost. Indicates either a wastegate stuck closed, oversized turbo for the calibration, or commanded boost limits being exceeded by ambient conditions (cold dense air).

causes_en: Boost leak in the charge-air path
P25A0.en: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P25A0.desc: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes_en: Wastegate stuck closed
P25A1.en: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit
P25A1.desc: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

causes_en: Internal fault in the brake module — read its DTCs
P25A2.en: Brake System Control Module A Requested MIL Illumination
P25A2.desc: The primary brake system control module (ABS/ESC/iBooster) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side — for example a regenerative braking fault on a hybrid that affects driveline torque flow. The original fault is in the brake module.

causes_en: Hood not properly latched
Failed hood latch sensor
P25A3.desc: After plausibility checks the body controller has concluded that the engine hood is genuinely open while the vehicle is operating. Used to suspend HV operation on hybrids/EVs (HV interlock), block remote engine start, and trigger the alarm if armed.

causes_en: Open or shorted switch wire
P25A4.desc: General electrical fault on the fuel mode select switch — used on bi-fuel vehicles (CNG/LPG/H2/gasoline) so the driver can pick the active fuel. With the input invalid, the ECM falls back to the default fuel and disables operator-selectable switching.

causes_en: Switch contact bounce
P25A5.desc: The fuel mode select switch is electrically intact, but its state does not match operating conditions — switched to gas while gas tank is empty, or fast toggling. The ECM rejects the request to avoid stalling.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P25A6.en: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Low
P25A6.desc: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P25A7.en: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit High
P25A7.desc: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Worn switch contact
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
Harness routed against vibrating component
P25A8.en: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25A8.desc: Fuel mode switch signal jumps or drops out — worn contact or vibration. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Open control wire to the solenoid
Open solenoid coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P25A9.desc: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit is open. Modern engines with under-piston oil jets switch them on under high load to cool the piston crown — controlled by a solenoid valve in the oil gallery. With the circuit broken, jets cannot be commanded on or stay locked off, raising piston temperatures under load.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P25AA.en: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Low
P25AA.desc: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The jets may be enabled continuously, raising oil pump load and lowering oil pressure to other consumers.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P25AB.en: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit High
P25AB.desc: Control circuit stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Solenoid stuck closed by oil sludge
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P25AC.en: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P25AC.desc: The control circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid valve does not open when commanded — confirmed by oil-pressure or oil-temperature feedback that does not change after the activation pulse. Piston cooling does not engage under high load — risk of piston-crown overheating and ring-land cracks.

causes_en: Solenoid stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P25AD.en: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Stuck On
P25AD.desc: The piston cooling solenoid does not close when commanded off — jets remain active when not needed. Oil pressure to top-end consumers may sag, and warm-up takes longer because the cooling jets remove heat from the pistons during cold start.

causes_en: Low engine oil level
Sludge-clogged oil gallery
Worn oil pump
P25AE.en: Piston Cooling Oil Pressure Too Low
P25AE.desc: With the piston-cooling jets commanded on, the dedicated oil-pressure sensor in that gallery reads below the safe threshold. Insufficient flow to the jets means real piston cooling is not happening — the ECM warns the driver and may reduce torque to protect the pistons.

causes_en: Internal fault — read the module DTCs
P25AF.en: Coolant Temperature Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P25AF.desc: A dedicated coolant-temperature control module (used on engines with electric coolant pumps and electronic thermostats to keep the cylinder head and block at independent setpoints) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side. Original fault is in that module.

causes_en: Stuck float
Bent float arm catching the tank wall
P25B0.desc: Fuel level sensor A (typically the float in the main fuel tank section) reports a value that does not change over a long driving distance — the float is mechanically stuck against the tank wall, baffle or pump module. Without level changes the EVAP monitor cannot run and remaining-range estimates are wrong.

causes_en: Stuck float
P25B1.desc: Same condition as sensor A stuck, applied to the second fuel level sensor B. Saddle tanks (often AWD vehicles) and large trucks use two sensors — one per tank chamber — averaged for total level. A stuck B leaves only A and reduces accuracy.

causes_en: One stuck float — inspect both
P25B2.en: Fuel Level Sensor A or B Stuck
P25B2.desc: The ECM detects that one of the two level sensors is stuck but cannot identify which from the available signals — for example because the saddle-tank algorithm sees implausible delta only intermittently. Both sensors should be inspected.

causes_en: Seized wastegate linkage
Broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P25B3.desc: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck open. Exhaust gas bypasses the turbine even at low load — turbo cannot reach target speed, boost is permanently low and the engine feels asthmatic. Common causes are seized linkage, broken return spring or carbon-locked wastegate flap.

causes_en: Carbon-locked wastegate flap
Seized linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P25B4.desc: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck closed. The turbo cannot bleed off exhaust at high load — boost overshoots the setpoint, risking overboost cut-off and damage to the turbo bearing. Carbon-locked flap, seized linkage or aged actuator are typical causes.

causes_en: Seized wastegate linkage
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P25B5.desc: Same as wastegate A stuck open, applied to the second wastegate (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage). Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes_en: Carbon-locked wastegate flap
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P25B6.desc: Same as wastegate A stuck closed, applied to the second wastegate. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

causes_en: Open or shorted wire
P25B7.en: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
P25B7.desc: General electrical fault on the auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input. Used on commercial vehicles or upfit applications where a second ignition switch (in a sleeper cab, work platform or crew compartment) can crank the engine.

causes_en: Wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P25B8.en: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P25B8.desc: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P25B9.en: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P25B9.desc: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Open switch wire
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P25BA.desc: The DPF/SCR forced-regeneration request switch — used on commercial vehicles to let the operator force a parked regeneration when the automatic regen has been postponed too often — is open. The ECM cannot honour an operator request for forced regen.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation
P25BB.desc: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. The ECM may see a constant regen request which it cannot service while the vehicle is moving.

causes_en: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P25BC.desc: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Turbocharger oil seal leak feeds engine oil into the intake
Oil collected in the intercooler is sucked into the engine on load
Failed PCV / crankcase breather floods intake with oil mist
P25BD.desc: The engine controller commanded a forced shutdown after detecting unmetered fuel reaching the combustion chambers. Common on diesels with leaking turbo seals or cracked intercoolers that drip oil into the intake — the engine then runs on the oil and can overspeed.

causes_en: Broken wire or corroded connector on the disable control line
Open coil in the alt-fuel disable relay
Output driver in the alt-fuel control module faulty
P25BE.en: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit / Open
P25BE.desc: The controller cannot drive the alternative-fuel disable line that switches a bi-fuel vehicle (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) back to gasoline. An open detected on the control side blocks the safety shutoff for the gas system.

causes_en: Disable control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Output driver stuck on inside the control module
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25BF.en: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit High
P25BF.desc: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is above the expected window. Often a short to battery upstream of the relay or a stuck-on driver in the control module.

causes_en: Disable control wire shorted to ground
Low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25C0.en: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit Low
P25C0.desc: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a failed driver pulling the line low.

causes_en: Open feedback wire between relay and control module
Feedback contact in the disable relay corroded or stuck
P25C1.desc: The feedback signal that confirms the alt-fuel disable command was carried out is missing or out of range. The fuel system cannot verify that the gas circuit is shut.

causes_en: Feedback wire shorted to a B+ supply
Pull-up resistor in the input stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25C2.en: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit High
P25C2.desc: The disable feedback signal sits above its valid window. Typical cause is a short to battery on the feedback wire or a failed pull-up in the input stage.

causes_en: Feedback wire shorted to ground
Open pull-up resistor in the controller input
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25C3.en: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit Low
P25C3.desc: The disable feedback signal sits below its valid window. Usually a short to ground or an open pull-up that lets the input float low.

causes_en: Open sensor element or broken sensor wire
Corroded connector on the booster sensor pigtail
P25C4.en: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P25C4.desc: The temperature sensor monitoring the electric brake booster (iBooster, eBooster) returns no usable signal. Without temperature feedback the controller derates booster assist to protect the motor.

causes_en: Sensor drift or contamination on the temperature element
Sensor not seated properly against the booster motor housing
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P25C5.en: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P25C5.desc: The booster temperature sensor reading is implausible relative to commanded assist or coolant temperature. The signal moves too slowly, sticks, or never reaches expected values during operation.

causes_en: Internal short in the sensor element
Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25C6.en: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
