P25C6.desc: The booster temperature signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Typical causes are a shorted sensor element or a short to ground in the harness.

causes_en: Open sensor element
Sensor signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25C7.en: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P25C7.desc: The booster temperature signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to a 5 V reference in the harness.

causes_en: Sensor connector not fully seated or pin tension lost
Harness chafed against booster housing or pedal bracket
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P25C8.en: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25C8.desc: The booster temperature signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during vibration or thermal expansion.

causes_en: Active DTC stored in the secondary brake module
Communication loss interpreted as MIL request
P25C9.en: Brake System Control Module B Requested MIL Illumination
P25C9.desc: A second brake system control module (typically the redundant secondary unit on by-wire or AV-grade brake systems) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

causes_en: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid
P25CA.en: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25CA.desc: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25CB.en: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25CB.desc: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25CC.en: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25CC.desc: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes_en: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid
P25CD.en: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25CD.desc: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25CE.en: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25CE.desc: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25CF.en: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25CF.desc: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes_en: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid
P25D0.en: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25D0.desc: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25D1.en: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25D1.desc: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25D2.en: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25D2.desc: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes_en: Open coil in the park-lock solenoid
Broken control wire between ECU and solenoid
P25D3.en: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25D3.desc: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off. Without the lock, the next start can suffer poor combustion or rough idle until the phaser builds oil pressure.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
ECU low-side driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25D4.en: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25D4.desc: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window. Usually a short to ground or a low-side driver shorted internally.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
ECU output driver stuck on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25D5.en: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25D5.desc: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window. Typical causes are a short to battery or a stuck-on driver in the controller.

causes_en: Soot or carbon deposits prevent valve from reaching the stop
Worn linkage between actuator and valve flap
Position sensor not aligned with valve shaft
P25D6.en: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop Performance
P25D6.desc: During self-calibration of the exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A, the position sensor never reached the expected mechanical stop. The controller cannot zero the position reference, so commanded openings will be inaccurate.

causes_en: Open sender resistor or broken float
Corroded tank pump module connector
P25D7.desc: A third fuel level sensor (C) used on multi-tank trucks, dual-saddle SUVs, or auxiliary fuel systems returns no usable signal. Without it, calculated fuel level and EVAP monitor enabling will be off.

causes_en: Float arm stuck on baffle or fuel pump module
Worn spot on the resistor track at common fill level
P25D8.desc: The third fuel level sensor reading does not change as expected with consumption or refuelling. Float may be sticking, or the resistor track has localised wear.

causes_en: Internal short in the sender resistor
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25D9.en: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Low
P25D9.desc: The third fuel level sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sender or a short to ground in the harness.

causes_en: Open sender resistor
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25DA.en: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit High
P25DA.desc: The third fuel level sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sender or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes_en: Tank module connector not fully seated
Harness chafed near tank straps
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P25DB.en: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P25DB.desc: The third fuel level sensor signal jumps or drops out for short moments. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire that opens during driving vibration.

causes_en: Float arm jammed against tank wall, baffle or pump module
Resistor wiper seized by varnish from old fuel
P25DC.desc: The third fuel level sensor reads a constant value across known consumption or refuelling events. Float arm or resistor wiper is mechanically stuck.

causes_en: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris
P25DD.en: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25DD.desc: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes_en: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally
P25DE.en: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25DE.desc: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes_en: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response
P25DF.en: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25DF.desc: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes_en: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris
P25E0.en: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E0.desc: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes_en: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally
P25E1.en: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E1.desc: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes_en: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response
P25E2.en: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E2.desc: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes_en: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris
P25E3.en: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25E3.desc: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes_en: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally
P25E4.en: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25E4.desc: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes_en: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response
P25E5.en: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25E5.desc: Camshaft phaser B on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes_en: Park-lock pin stuck in the locked groove
Low oil pressure cannot push the lock pin out
Oil control valve blocked by debris
P25E6.en: B Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E6.desc: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position. The phaser stays at the park-lock angle and cannot be advanced or retarded as commanded.

causes_en: Worn vanes or housing inside the phaser
Sludge or contaminated oil prevents return to base
Oil control valve leaks internally
P25E7.en: B Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E7.desc: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages. Next cold start may run rough until oil pressure builds.

causes_en: Oil control valve spool sticks under varnish
Stretched timing chain shifts cam reference
Wrong oil viscosity slows phaser response
P25E8.en: B Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 2
P25E8.desc: Camshaft phaser B on bank 2 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance. Closed-loop control of cam timing is degraded.

causes_en: Open electromagnetic clutch coil
Worn friction surfaces leave the air gap too large to attract
Corroded armature plate stuck open
P25E9.desc: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not close. The supercharger stays disengaged so boost from this stage is unavailable, which limits torque and may also affect cooling pump drives shared with the same belt.

causes_en: Armature plate seized to the pulley face
Driver stuck on keeps clutch energised
Failed pulley bearing welds clutch surfaces
P25EA.desc: The clutch that engages the mechanical supercharger to the engine drive will not open. The supercharger remains coupled at all loads, increasing parasitic loss and fuel consumption when boost is not needed.

causes_en: Coil resistance increased due to thermal damage
High-resistance contact in the clutch connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P25EB.desc: The supercharger clutch control current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Either coil resistance has drifted or the driver feedback is implausible.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25EC.desc: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted clutch coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open clutch coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25ED.desc: Voltage on the supercharger clutch control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open coil that lets the driver float high.

causes_en: Open pump motor winding or worn brushes
Broken control wire between ECU and pump
P25EE.en: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B / Open
P25EE.desc: The controller cannot drive the secondary electric vacuum pump (B). Brake servo or HVAC actuators that depend on engine vacuum may not get enough vacuum during low-load operation or with engine off in stop-start mode.

causes_en: Worn diaphragm or vanes inside the pump
Cracked vacuum hose or loose connection
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P25EF.en: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Range/Performance
P25EF.desc: The secondary vacuum pump does not produce the expected vacuum within the commanded run time. Leak in the pump line or worn pump diaphragm reduces output.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor winding
P25F0.en: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B Low
P25F0.desc: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open motor winding or worn brushes
P25F1.en: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B High
P25F1.desc: Voltage on the secondary vacuum pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor that lets the driver float high.

causes_en: Open sensor element or broken signal wire
Corroded connector at sensor pigtail
P25F2.desc: A third boost pressure sensor (C) used on twin-stage or sequential boost systems returns no usable signal. Without it, boost control of the third stage runs open-loop or is disabled.

causes_en: Sensor drift after thermal aging
Sensing hose blocked by oil residue
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P25F3.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P25F3.desc: The third boost pressure sensor reading is implausible compared with manifold pressure or commanded boost. Either drift, leak in the sensing line, or contamination on the sensor diaphragm.

causes_en: Internal short in the sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25F4.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit Low
P25F4.desc: The third boost pressure sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor element or a short to ground.

causes_en: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25F5.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor C Circuit High
P25F5.desc: The third boost pressure sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes_en: Failed AIR pump motor or impeller
Check valve seized by exhaust soot
Corroded or cracked air injection pipe
P25F6.desc: A general fault in the second secondary air injection (AIR) circuit. Detected by the O2 sensors which expect a lean swing during cold-start AIR pump operation but do not see one.

causes_en: Air pipe partially blocked by carbon
Worn pump impeller reduces flow
Leak between pump and check valve
P25F7.en: AIR System B Incorrect Flow Detected
P25F7.desc: The second AIR system delivers measurably more or less air than expected. Often a partially blocked pipe, a worn pump, or a leak between pump and check valve.

causes_en: Open solenoid coil
Open or shorted wiring to the valve
P25F8.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit
P25F8.desc: A third bypass (recirculation or wastegate) valve used in three-stage charging systems is not responding to control commands. Boost balancing across stages can no longer be achieved.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25F9.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Low
P25F9.desc: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P25FA.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit High
P25FA.desc: Voltage on the third bypass valve control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes_en: Coil resistance changed by thermal stress
High-resistance contact in the valve connector
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P25FB.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Control Circuit Range/Performance
P25FB.desc: The third bypass valve current does not match the commanded value within tolerance. Drifted coil resistance or high-resistance contact in the connector.

causes_en: Carbon buildup blocks the valve flap
Actuator linkage seized by corrosion
P25FC.desc: The third bypass valve is mechanically jammed. Solenoid is energised correctly but the valve flap or disc does not move as expected.

causes_en: Sustained high duty cycle from charge balancing strategy
Cooling air channel blocked by debris
P25FD.en: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Temperature Too High
P25FD.desc: The third bypass valve has reached over-temperature. Either coil duty cycle is too high for too long, or cooling air flow around the valve is restricted.

causes_en: Worn friction surfaces or air gap drift
Oil or debris on the clutch face
P25FE.desc: A general performance fault in the supercharger disconnect clutch. Engagement or release is slow, sticky, or out of tolerance without a clear electrical-side cause.

causes_en: Aged smoothing capacitors lose capacitance
Battery condition causes input voltage to drop too far
Internal fault in the converter switching stage
P25FF.en: Electrical System Voltage Stabilizer Control Module Performance
P25FF.desc: The voltage stabiliser module (DC/DC converter for stop-start engine cranking events) does not maintain the regulated 12 V output during high transient loads. Sensitive electronics may reset during cranking.

causes_en: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump
P2600.en: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit / Open
P2600.desc: The controller cannot drive the electric coolant pump A control line. Without circulation, engine and aftertreatment can overheat or warm up incorrectly.

causes_en: Pump motor seized by debris or sediment
Cracked rotor magnet decouples drive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2601.en: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P2601.desc: The electric coolant pump A is commanded on but does not run. Coolant temperature climbs faster than expected with no flow detected.

mfr.Audi: Coolant Heat Storage (CHS) water pump failure, Coolant Heat Storage (CHS) water pump relay, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Pump motor open
Drive line open
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2602.desc: The ECU detects an open circuit on the electric coolant pump control line. Without pump control the engine cannot actively manage warm-up and cool-down phases.

causes_en: Drive line shorted to ground
Driver stage failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2603.desc: The electric coolant pump drive line reads below the lower threshold — typically a short to ground or a failed driver stage.

causes_en: Drive line shorted to positive
Driver stage shorted on
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2604.desc: The electric coolant pump drive line reads above the upper threshold — usually a short to positive or a stuck-on driver stage.

causes_en: Open heater grid element
Failed heater relay or open coil
P2605.en: Intake Air Heater B Circuit / Open
P2605.desc: The controller cannot drive the secondary intake air heater (heater grid B) used on diesel engines for cold-start support. The grid stays cold so cold-start emissions and white smoke increase.

causes_en: Partial element failure raises grid resistance
Burned relay contacts
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2606.en: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Range/Performance
P2606.desc: The secondary intake air heater current does not match expected resistance. Either the grid is partially open or the relay contacts have high resistance.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2607.en: Intake Air Heater B Circuit Low
P2607.desc: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted relay coil.

mfr.Audi: Intake air heater, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open relay coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2608.en: Intake Air Heater B Circuit High
P2608.desc: Voltage on the secondary intake air heater control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open relay coil.

causes_en: High-resistance battery feed to the heater
Intake air temperature sensor reads with offset
P2609.desc: The intake air heater system did not raise intake temperature by the expected amount during cold-start support. Suggests low current draw, poor connection to the grid, or a failed temperature feedback path.

mfr.Audi: Intake air heater, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Open coil in the PTO engagement solenoid
Broken wire to the PTO solenoid
P260A.desc: The controller cannot drive the power take-off (PTO) engagement line on commercial vehicles. The PTO will not engage even when commanded by the body controller or operator switch.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P260B.desc: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P260C.desc: Voltage on the PTO engagement control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes_en: Burnt-out indicator bulb
Open or shorted wire between cluster and ECU
P260D.desc: The dashboard PTO engaged lamp control circuit is faulty. Driver may not see whether the PTO is currently driving an external accessory.

causes_en: Burnt-out indicator bulb
Open or shorted wire to the cluster
P260E.en: Particulate Filter Regeneration Lamp Control Circuit
P260E.desc: The DPF regeneration warning lamp circuit is faulty. The driver may not be alerted to a required highway run that supports passive regeneration.

causes_en: Internal fault in the monitoring processor
Software memory corruption
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P260F.desc: The dedicated EVAP monitoring processor (often a small auxiliary CPU inside the engine controller or a separate module) does not pass its self-test or runs out of step with the main monitor logic.

causes_en: ECU internal timer fault
Keep-alive memory power intermittent
P2610.en: ECM/PCM Internal Engine Off Timer Performance
P2610.desc: The engine controller's internal soak-time/engine-off timer fails its plausibility check — for example readings claim instant cool-down or never-cooled. Cold-start enrichment, EVAP and catalyst monitors depend on this timer; a fault freezes those readiness monitors.

mfr.Audi: An internal PCM problem, A problem with the PCM power or ground circuit

causes_en: Open coil in the valve solenoid
Broken control wire
P2611.en: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit / Open
P2611.desc: The A/C refrigerant distribution valve A (used to switch refrigerant flow between front and rear evaporators or between cabin and battery cooling on EVs) cannot be driven by the controller.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in the valve solenoid
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2612.en: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Low
P2612.desc: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to a B+ supply
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2613.en: A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit High
P2613.desc: Voltage on the A/C distribution valve A control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes_en: Open output wiring
Internal ECU output driver fault
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2614.desc: The camshaft position output signal sent from the ECU to other modules is interrupted. Other systems that rely on the cam reference (e.g. transmission, hybrid module) do not receive a valid signal.

mfr.Audi: Broken tone ring, Camshaft Position Sensor (CMP) failure, Powertrain Control Module (PCM) failure, Wiring issue

causes_en: Output wire shorted to ground
Output buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2615.en: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Low Bank 1
P2615.desc: The buffered camshaft A position output that the engine controller sends to other modules (transmission, body, ignition module) is below the expected level on bank 1. Other modules cannot use the cam phase reference for synchronisation.

causes_en: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2616.en: Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit High Bank 1
P2616.desc: The buffered camshaft A position output is above the expected level on bank 1. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes_en: Open wire between ECU and downstream module
Output buffer internally open
P2617.en: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit / Open
P2617.desc: The buffered crankshaft position output that the engine controller sends to ignition modules and the transmission cannot drive its line. Open detected on the output side.

causes_en: Output wire shorted to ground
Buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2618.en: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit Low
P2618.desc: The buffered crankshaft position output is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground on the output line or a failed buffer.

causes_en: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2619.en: Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit High
P2619.desc: The buffered crankshaft position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes_en: Open pump motor winding
Broken control wire to the pump
P261A.en: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P261A.desc: The controller cannot drive the second electric coolant pump (B). Often used for aftertreatment, turbo cool-down, or hybrid battery loops — fault stops circulation in that loop.

causes_en: Pump motor seized by sediment
Cracked rotor magnet decouples drive
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P261B.en: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P261B.desc: The second electric coolant pump is commanded on but does not run. Cooling demand of the connected loop is not satisfied.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Motor winding short
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P261C.en: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P261C.desc: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P261D.en: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P261D.desc: Voltage on the second coolant pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes_en: ECU output driver stuck on
Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P261E.en: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Stuck On
P261E.desc: The second coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes_en: ECU output driver stuck on
Control wire shorted to a permanent B+ supply
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P261F.en: Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Stuck On
P261F.desc: The first coolant pump runs even when no command is active. Driver is stuck on or the wire is shorted to a permanent supply.

causes_en: Output wire open or shorted
ECU output stage failed
P2620.desc: A general electrical fault on the ECU output that broadcasts the throttle position signal to other modules — for example to the transmission control or hybrid drive controller.

causes_en: Output wire shorted to ground
Output buffer transistor failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2621.desc: The buffered throttle position output that the engine controller sends to the transmission and body modules is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or a failed output stage.

causes_en: Output wire shorted to B+
Output buffer open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2622.desc: The buffered throttle position output is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open output stage.

causes_en: Open coil in the pressure regulator
Broken control wire
P2623.en: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit / Open
P2623.desc: The Injector Control Pressure (ICP) regulator on hydraulically actuated injectors (HEUI diesel) or the high-pressure regulator on common-rail systems cannot be driven. Injection pressure cannot be controlled, engine may not start.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in regulator coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2624.en: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit Low
P2624.desc: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted regulator coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Open regulator coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2625.en: Injector Control Pressure Regulator Circuit High
P2625.desc: Voltage on the ICP regulator control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open regulator coil.

causes_en: Trim wire open
Internal sensor fault
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2626.en: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2626.desc: The ECU detects an open in the pumping current trim circuit of the wide-band oxygen sensor on bank 1 sensor 1. Without trim correction, the lambda value reported by the sensor is not accurate.

causes_en: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2627.en: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2627.desc: On a wide-band (broadband) O2 sensor, the trim resistor circuit that calibrates the pumping current is reading low on bank 1 sensor 1. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes_en: Open calibration trim resistor
Corroded sensor connector
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2628.en: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2628.desc: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 1 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain is wrong, causing offsets that the controller cannot compensate.

causes_en: Open calibration trim resistor
Open sensor connector pin
P2629.en: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit / Open Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2629.desc: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 is open. Air-fuel feedback for bank 2 cannot be calibrated, fuel control runs degraded.

causes_en: Injector flow drift outside learning window
Unstable rail pressure during learning cycle
P262A.en: Fuel Injector - Pilot Injection Not Learned
P262A.desc: The pilot (pre) injection learning routine on a common-rail diesel did not complete successfully. Without learned pilot quantity, combustion noise increases and NOx may rise.

causes_en: Intermittent main relay opens early
Software timer counter corrupted
P262B.en: Control Module Power Off Timer Performance
P262B.desc: The internal power-down timer of the engine controller does not run as expected. The module either stays awake too long after key-off (battery drain) or shuts down too early (no aftertreatment cool-down or learn-write).

causes_en: Open wire on the reference rail
Open inside the ECU reference output
P262C.en: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit / Open
P262C.desc: The 5 V reference G output that the engine controller supplies to a group of sensors is open. All sensors fed from this rail will report invalid readings.

causes_en: Reference wire shorted to ground
Sensor on the rail shorted internally to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P262D.en: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Low
P262D.desc: The 5 V reference G voltage is below the expected level. Usually a short to ground or excessive load from a downstream sensor pulling the rail down.

causes_en: Reference wire shorted to a B+ supply
Internal 5 V regulator failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P262E.en: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit High
P262E.desc: The 5 V reference G voltage is above the expected level. Typical causes are a short to battery or an internal regulator failure.

causes_en: High-resistance ground for the reference rail
One sensor draws excessive current and shifts the rail
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P262F.en: Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Range/Performance
P262F.desc: The 5 V reference G voltage is within range but unstable or offset against expected. Loose ground or marginal regulator load.

causes_en: Short in the calibration trim resistor
Water intrusion in the sensor connector
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2630.en: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2630.desc: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads low. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, causing rich or lean offsets.

causes_en: Open calibration trim resistor
Corroded sensor connector
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P2631.en: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2631.desc: The wide-band trim resistor circuit on bank 2 sensor 1 reads high. Air-fuel feedback gain on bank 2 is wrong, the controller cannot compensate the offset.

causes_en: Open pump motor winding
Failed pump relay
P2632.en: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit / Open
P2632.desc: The controller cannot drive the secondary fuel pump (B). Common on dual-tank trucks, GDI lift-pump systems, or alt-fuel installations — fault stops fuel delivery from this stage.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in pump motor
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2633.en: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit Low
P2633.desc: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted motor winding.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Open motor winding
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2634.en: Fuel Pump B Control Circuit High
P2634.desc: Voltage on the second fuel pump control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open motor winding.

causes_en: Worn fuel pump
Clogged fuel filter
Pressure regulator fault
P2635.en: Fuel Pump A Low Flow / Performance
P2635.desc: The ECU detects insufficient fuel flow from fuel pump A. Either the pump is worn out, the supply line is restricted, or the pressure regulator does not allow proper flow.

causes_en: Worn impeller reduces volumetric efficiency
Restricted in-tank or in-line fuel filter
Pressure regulator leaks back to tank
P2636.desc: The second fuel pump runs but does not deliver expected volume or pressure. Worn pump, restricted filter, or leaking pressure regulator.

causes_en: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault
P2637.desc: The torque feedback signal A from the transmission or other torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot reduce torque on shift requests, which can cause harsh shifts.

causes_en: Sender calibration drift
Bus value corrupted by EMI
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2638.en: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Range/Performance
P2638.desc: The torque feedback signal A is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes_en: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus
P2639.en: Torque Management Feedback Signal A Low
P2639.desc: The torque feedback signal A reads below its valid range. Either the source reports a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Bulb driver internally shorted
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P263A.desc: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted bulb driver.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Burnt-out MIL bulb
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P263B.desc: Voltage on the malfunction indicator lamp control line is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open lamp.

causes_en: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour
Current feedback loop noisy
P263C.desc: The glow plug control driver does not respond to commands within tolerance. Cold-start glow function is degraded so cold starting can be delayed and white smoke increases.

causes_en: Aged driver shows degraded switching behaviour
Heater element resistance drifted out of range
P263D.desc: The reductant (AdBlue) tank or line heater driver does not switch as expected. AdBlue may freeze in cold weather, blocking SCR dosing.

causes_en: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris
P263E.en: Glow Plug Control Module 1 Over Temperature
P263E.desc: The first glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes_en: One glow plug shorted to ground forces module overcurrent
Cooling air channel blocked by debris
P263F.en: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Over Temperature
P263F.desc: The second glow plug control module reports over-temperature. Sustained current draw or insufficient cooling has driven the module above its rated temperature.

causes_en: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus
P2640.en: Torque Management Feedback Signal A High
P2640.desc: The torque feedback signal A reads above its valid range. Source module sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes_en: Required CAN message not received in time
Source module reports an internal fault
P2641.desc: The torque feedback signal B from a second torque user is missing or invalid. The engine controller cannot coordinate torque reduction with this user.

causes_en: Sender calibration drift
Bus value corrupted by EMI
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P2642.en: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Range/Performance
P2642.desc: The torque feedback signal B is present but its value is implausible against measured engine load and speed. Sender calibration or sensor offset is suspected.

causes_en: Source module sends invalid low value
Signal stuck low on the bus
P2643.en: Torque Management Feedback Signal B Low
P2643.desc: The torque feedback signal B reads below its valid range. Source sends a value below physical possibility or the bus signal is stuck low.

causes_en: Source module sends invalid high value
Signal stuck high on the bus
P2644.en: Torque Management Feedback Signal B High
P2644.desc: The torque feedback signal B reads above its valid range. Source sends an implausibly high value or the bus signal is stuck high.

causes_en: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire
P2645.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P2645.desc: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator A on bank 1 (used in cylinder deactivation systems such as VTEC, AFM, MDS). The valve lift mode cannot be switched.

causes_en: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2646.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P2646.desc: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 1 is commanded to engage (high lift or all-cylinder mode) but does not switch. Engine stays in low-lift or deactivated mode under load, causing reduced power.

causes_en: Insufficient oil pressure / level
Stuck VVL solenoid
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2647.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 1
P2647.desc: On variable valve lift systems (e.g. Honda VTEC) the ECU detects that the bank 1 rocker arm actuator is stuck in the engaged (high lift) position. Idle quality and fuel economy are affected.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2648.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2648.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2649.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2649.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes_en: Open sensor element
Corroded sensor connector
P264A.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P264A.desc: The position sensor that confirms the A rocker arm switching state on bank 1 returns no usable signal. Closed-loop control of valve lift cannot verify the state.

causes_en: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P264B.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P264B.desc: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes on bank 1. Sensor drift or mechanical wear leaves the signal between expected values.

causes_en: Internal short in sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P264C.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P264C.desc: The position sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Usually a shorted sensor or short to ground in the harness.

causes_en: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P264D.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P264D.desc: The position sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Common causes are an open sensor or a short to the 5 V reference.

causes_en: Sensor connector not fully seated
Harness chafed against valve cover or cam carrier
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P264E.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
P264E.desc: The position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire in the harness.

causes_en: Replacement ECU not programmed at install
Non-volatile memory corruption
P264F.en: Engine Serial Number Not Programmed or Incompatible
P264F.desc: The engine controller cannot read a valid engine serial number from its non-volatile memory, or the stored value does not match the expected pattern. Calibration sets keyed to the serial number cannot be applied.

causes_en: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire
P2650.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P2650.desc: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator B on bank 1. The second valve lift mode cannot be commanded.

causes_en: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2651.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P2651.desc: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 1 is commanded to engage but does not switch. Engine stays in the wrong lift or cylinder mode under load.

causes_en: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2652.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 1
P2652.desc: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 1 stays in the activated state when commanded off. Engine cannot return to the alternate lift or cylinder mode.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2653.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P2653.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 1 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2654.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 1
P2654.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 1 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes_en: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire
P2655.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P2655.desc: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator A on bank 2. The valve lift mode cannot be switched on this bank.

causes_en: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2656.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P2656.desc: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 2 is commanded to engage but does not switch. Engine stays in the wrong lift mode under load on this bank.

causes_en: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2657.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 2
P2657.desc: The rocker arm actuator A on bank 2 stays in the activated state when commanded off.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2658.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P2658.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 2 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2659.en: A Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 2
P2659.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator A control line on bank 2 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes_en: Open sensor element
Corroded sensor connector
P265A.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P265A.desc: The position sensor that confirms the B rocker arm switching state on bank 1 returns no usable signal.

causes_en: Sensor signal drift after thermal aging
Worn lock pin reduces travel between modes
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P265B.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P265B.desc: The position sensor reading does not transition cleanly between the two valve lift modes for actuator B on bank 1.

causes_en: Internal short in sensor element
Signal wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P265C.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1
P265C.desc: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Open sensor element
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P265D.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P265D.desc: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes_en: Sensor connector not fully seated
Harness chafed against valve cover
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P265E.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
P265E.desc: The position sensor signal for actuator B on bank 1 jumps or drops out intermittently. Usually a loose connector or a chafed wire.

causes_en: Control valve spool sticky from oil residue
Solenoid coil resistance drift
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P265F.en: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit Range/Performance
P265F.desc: The variable-displacement A/C compressor control valve does not respond to commands within tolerance. Refrigerant flow regulation is degraded so cabin temperature varies or efficiency drops.

causes_en: Open coil in oil control valve
Broken control wire
P2660.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P2660.desc: The controller cannot drive the rocker arm switching actuator B on bank 2.

causes_en: Low oil pressure cannot move the actuator
Mechanical lock pin stuck in unactivated position
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2661.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P2661.desc: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 2 is commanded to engage but does not switch.

causes_en: Mechanical lock pin stuck in activated position
Oil control valve spool stuck open
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2662.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator System Stuck On Bank 2
P2662.desc: The rocker arm actuator B on bank 2 stays in the activated state when commanded off.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2663.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P2663.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 2 is below the expected window. Usually a short to ground or a shorted solenoid coil.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to B+
Open solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2664.en: B Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit High Bank 2
P2664.desc: Voltage on the rocker arm actuator B control line on bank 2 is above the expected window. Typical causes are a short to battery or an open solenoid coil.

causes_en: Open coil in shutoff valve
Broken control wire
P2665.en: Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit / Open
P2665.desc: The controller cannot drive the secondary fuel shutoff valve. Engine cannot be commanded off through this path during a safety event.

causes_en: Control wire shorted to ground
Internal short in solenoid coil
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

U0001.desc: A general fault on the high-speed CAN bus has been detected. This bus typically connects powertrain modules (ECM, TCM, ABS) at 500 kbit/s and a fault disables communication between them, often triggering multiple secondary DTCs in other modules.

causes_en: Sensor failed
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
U3572.en: Stack Outlet Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit
U3572.desc: Generic fault on coolant temperature sensor 2 at the fuel cell stack outlet (used to monitor stack thermal output).

causes_en: Valve actuator failed
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
U3573.desc: Generic electrical fault on the coolant mixing valve control. The valve blends hot and cold coolant streams to maintain stack temperature.

causes_en: Valve electrical or mechanical failure
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
U3574.desc: Generic fault on the coolant mixing valve — combines circuit and mechanical issues. A communication loss with this module breaks any function relying on its data — diagnostic tools may show ''no response'' and dependent modules can fall into limp mode.

causes_en: Position sensor failed
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
U3575.en: Coolant Mixing Valve Position Sensor Circuit
U3575.desc: Generic fault on the position sensor of the coolant mixing valve. A communication loss with this module breaks any function relying on its data — diagnostic tools may show ''no response'' and dependent modules can fall into limp mode.

causes_en: Sensor failed
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
U3576.desc: Generic fault on the differential pressure sensor across the fuel cell stack — measures the pressure drop between cathode and anode (used to detect membrane damage or flooding).
